xa: **Chandragupta** followed **Bhadrabahu** (Jainism) to Shravanabelagola.
**Ashoka and Dasaratha** gave caves to the **Ajivikas**.
**Brahmanism** continued — Kautilya was a Brahmana, **'dvijarshabh'**.

38.s: By which epithet was Kautilya, a Brahmana of the Mauryan period, described?
38.x: Brahmanism continued under the Mauryas, and Kautilya was a Brahmana called 'dvijarshabh'.
xa: Policy was **liberal and tolerant**, with the state protecting **varna and ashrama**.
Tradition: Ashoka redistributed the relics into **84,000 stupas**.
**Chandragupta** followed **Bhadrabahu** (Jainism).

38.s: Which Mauryan ruler followed Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola?
38.x: Chandragupta, a follower of Jainism, went with Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola.

38.s: Which Ashokan edict names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas separately?
38.x: PE VII names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas (Jainas) separately.

38.s: Balirajgarh fort, excavated by the ASI and yielding punch-marked coins, is in which district of Bihar?
38.x: Balirajgarh is in Madhubani district, Bihar; its habitation runs from the Mauryan to the Pala period.
xa: It was in the news in **Apr 2026**.
**Vaishya Tekri** (Ujjain) may hold a Mauryan stupa larger than Sanchi.
Punch-marked silver panas go back to the **Mahajanapada** age.

38.s: What may the site of Vaishya Tekri at Ujjain contain?
o: A third-century BCE stupa larger than Sanchi, along with punch-marked and cast Avanti coins
The earliest known Iron Age settlement of South India
A Kushana palace containing only gold coins
A Gupta-period university at the Uttarapatha junction
38.x: Vaishya Tekri may contain a third-century BCE stupa larger than Sanchi and has yielded punch-marked and cast Avanti coins. Excavation is expected to resume after about 90 years.

xs: **Vaishya Tekri** (Ujjain) may hold a **3rd-century BCE Mauryan stupa, possibly larger than Sanchi**, and has yielded **punch-marked and cast Avanti coins** — option **(1)**.
MP is to resume excavation after **~90 years** (**23 Aug 2026**).
xa: **Ujjain** was the capital of **Avantirashtra**.
**Balirajgarh** (Madhubani) also yielded **punch-marked coins**.
**Sanchi** is called India's **largest stupa**.

39.s: Which inscription is related to Kharavela?
39.x: The Hathigumpha inscription is Kharavela's. Nasik and Nanaghat are Satavahana records and Amaravati a Buddhist site.

39.s: How is the Krishna river referred to in the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela?
39.x: The Hathigumpha inscription calls the Krishna river Kannabenna (Kanhabemna). Kanna and Karna are distractors.

39.s: King Kharavela is related to –
39.x: Kharavela is known from the Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri. Girnar and Junagadh relate to Ashoka and Rudradaman, and Sarnath to Ashoka.

39.s: Who among the following kings had heavily leaned towards Jainism?
39.x: Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jaina who gave caves to Jain monks. Dasharatha gave caves to the Ajivikas, Brihadratha was the last Maurya and Huvishka a Kushana.

39.s: What is/are correct in reference to Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves? (i) It has both natural and artificial caves (ii) Udayagiri has 18 and Khandagiri has 15 caves (iii) Khandagiri caves are famous for Hathigumpha inscription
39.x: Udayagiri and Khandagiri have natural and artificial caves, 18 on Udayagiri and 15 on Khandagiri. Statement iii is wrong: the Hathigumpha inscription is on Udayagiri.

39.s: The inscription of Hathigumpha is the source of information about which king?
39.x: The Hathigumpha inscription is the main source for Kharavela of Kalinga. It has no link with Ashoka, Harsha or Kanishka.

39.s: Kalinga's King Kharvel was associated with:
39.x:
Both names are correct for Kharavela's line (Mahameghavahana family of the Chedis); the printed key takes Mahameghavahana.
Kharavela was the third ruler of the Mahameghavahana family of the Chedi line, and the key takes Mahameghavahana. 'Chedi' names the same line, so it is the tempting near-correct option.

39.s: Whose reign does the Hathigumpha inscription record year by year?
39.x: The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri, near Bhubaneswar, records Kharavela's reign year by year; it belongs to the 2nd century BC.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about Kharavela:
1. He raided Magadha and brought back the Jina image taken by the Nandas.
2. He sent an army west only after an alliance with Satakarni.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela raided Magadha and recovered the Jina image the Nandas had taken. Statement 2 is wrong: he sent an army west ignoring Satakarni, not in alliance with him. So '1 only'.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela **raided Magadha** and brought back the **Jina image** the **Nandas** had taken.
Statement 2 is wrong: he sent an army west **ignoring Satakarni**, not in alliance — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: His deeds are in the **Hathigumpha** inscription (Udayagiri-Khandagiri, Odisha).
He was a **Jaina** king of the **Chedi** line.
⚠ **Nanaghat** = **Naganika**.

39.s: Which one of the following pairs of ruler and inscription is correctly matched?
39.x: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription is at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar. The Nanaghat inscription belongs to the Satavahana queen Naganika, so pairing it with Rudradaman or Kharavela is wrong, and Naganika has nothing to do with Hathigumpha.
39.tq: Hathigumpha = Kharavela; Nanaghat = Naganika; Junagadh = Rudradaman.

39.s: Kharavela of Kalinga belonged to which line?
39.x: Kharavela, a Jaina ruler, belonged to the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) line.

39.s: Which river is called Kannabenna in the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela?
39.x: The Hathigumpha inscription calls the Krishna river Kannabenna (Kanhabenna).

39.s: According to the Hathigumpha inscription, which ruler did Kharavela ignore when he sent an army to the west?
39.x: Kharavela sent his army west ignoring the Satavahana king Satakarni.

39.s: Who among the following post-Mauryan kings was a follower of Jainism?
39.x: Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jaina; he brought back the Jina image taken by the Nandas.

39.s: Which of the following dynasties succeeded the Mauryan Empire in the Deccan region?
39.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
39.x: In the Deccan the Mauryas were succeeded by the Satavahanas, former Mauryan feudatories. The Sungas succeeded them in Magadha, and the Kushanas and Guptas came later in the north.

39.s: Who came to power in Magadha after the Mauryas?
39.x: Pushyamitra Sunga killed the last Maurya Brihadratha and founded the Sunga dynasty in Magadha. The Satavahanas rose in the Deccan, not Magadha.

39.s: Who were the immediate successors of the Mauryas in Magadha ?
39.x: The Sungas founded by Pushyamitra were the immediate successors of the Mauryas in Magadha. The Satavahanas and Kushanas ruled elsewhere.

39.s: Brihadratha, the last Mauryan king, was which king after Ashoka?
39.x: Brihadratha was the 7th king after Ashoka.

39.s: What do the Puranas call the Satavahanas?
39.x: The Satavahanas, earlier Mauryan feudatories, are called Andhra-bhrityas in the Puranas.
xa: Founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.
They **defeated the Sunga-Kanva line**, ending **Susharman**.
Other Deccan feudatory chiefs: **Bhojas, Maharathis, Rashtrikas**.

39.s: Under whom did the Andhra or Deccan region break away from Mauryan control?
o: Satavahanas, who had earlier been Mauryan feudatories
39.x: The Satavahanas, earlier Mauryan feudatories, emerged as the breakaway power in the Andhra or Deccan region.
39.tq: Distinguish the Deccan breakaway power from the powers of Kalinga and the north-west.
xs: **Andhra/Deccan** broke away under the **Satavahanas**, earlier **Mauryan feudatories** — option **(2)**.
**Kharavela** (Chedi) led **Kalinga**; the **Kanvas** ruled Magadha; **Menander** was Indo-Greek in the north-west.
xa: The Puranas call the Satavahanas **Andhra-bhrityas**.
Founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.
Ashokan edicts at **Erragudi** and **Rajula Mandagiri** (Kurnool) show Mauryan rule in Andhra.

39.s:
Consider the following about the Pushyamitra Sunga persecution debate:
1. The Divyavadana describes Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists.
2. Sanchi and Bharhut grew under Sunga rule, which complicates this claim.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
39.x: The Divyavadana calls Pushyamitra a persecutor of Buddhists, but the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut under Sunga rule points the other way.
xa: Against the **Brahmanical-reaction** theory: Pushyamitra was a **Mauryan general**, and **Buddhist art thrived** under the Sungas.
The Sungas **stone-cased** Ashoka's brick stupa at Sanchi.
Pushyamitra led a **Brahmanical revival** (two Ashvamedhas).

39.s: Who founded the Sunga dynasty in Magadha?
39.x: Pushyamitra Sunga founded the Sunga dynasty after overthrowing the Mauryas.
xs: The Sunga dynasty was founded by **Pushyamitra Sunga**, the Mauryan **commander-in-chief (senani)** — option **(3)**.
**Brihadratha** was the last Maurya; **Vasudeva Kanva** founded the **Kanva** dynasty.
xa: The Sungas were the **immediate successors** of the Mauryas in Magadha (APPSC G2 **2003**).
Pushyamitra was a **Brahmana** of the **Bharadvaja gotra**.
He performed **two Ashvamedhas**.

39.s: How did Pushyamitra Sunga seize power from the Mauryas?
o: defeating the Indo-Greeks in the north-west
obtaining the throne through a council of ministers
assassinating Brihadratha during an army review
marrying into the Mauryan royal family
39.x: Pushyamitra, the Mauryan commander-in-chief, killed Brihadratha during a military review, thereby carrying out a military coup.
39.tq: Identify the actor, occasion and manner of accession.
xs: Pushyamitra **assassinated Brihadratha at a military review** of the army — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023**; BPSC **2008**).
It was a **military coup** by the Mauryan **commander-in-chief**.
xa: The army-review detail comes from **Bana's Harshacharita**.
Year: **187 BC** (UPSC); some notes say c. **185 BCE**.
⚠ BPSC **2008** key — the king killed was **Brihadratha**.

39.s: In which year, approximately, was the Sunga dynasty founded?
39.x: The Sunga dynasty is generally dated to 187 BC, though some accounts give approximately 185 BCE.
39.tq: Distinguish the close alternative dates by placing the key in the chronological sequence.
xs: The Sungas came to power in **187 BC** (UPSC) — option **(3)**.
Some notes and the AP History PYQ book give c. **185 BCE**.
**232 BC** is Ashoka's death; **206 BC** Antiochus III; **180 BC** the Indo-Greek takeover in the west.
xa: The coup: **Pushyamitra** killed **Brihadratha** at a military review.
Order in Magadha: **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas**.
The Kanvas ruled c. **73-28 BC**.

39.s: Pushyamitra Sunga belonged to which gotra and held which position before founding the Sunga dynasty?
39.x: Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmana of the Bharadvaja gotra and served as a senapati.
39.tq: Test the identity of a ruler through the paired details of lineage and office.
xs: Pushyamitra was a **Brahmana senapati** of the **Bharadvaja gotra** — option **(4)**.
He was the Mauryan **commander-in-chief (senani)** who killed Brihadratha.
xa: He led a strong **Brahmanical revival** with **two Ashvamedhas**.
**Patanjali** is linked with his court.
The Sunga core: **Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha, Narmada valley**.

39.s: Which inscription refers to the two Ashvamedha sacrifices of Pushyamitra Sunga?
39.x: Pushyamitra performed two Ashvamedhas, referred to in the Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva.
xa: He was a **Brahmana** of the **Bharadvaja gotra**.
⚠ **Divyavadana** calls him a **persecutor of Buddhists** — disputed.
His grandson **Vasumitra** beat a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu**.

39.s: According to Malavikagnimitram, who defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river?
39.x: Malavikagnimitram records that Vasumitra, the grandson of Pushyamitra, defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river.
39.tq: Distinguish the commander who won the battle from the ruler whose dynasty was involved.
xs: **Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram** says **Vasumitra**, Pushyamitra's grandson, defeated a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu** — option **(4)**.
**Menander** and **Demetrius** were the Indo-Greek (Yavana) side.
xa: The same play names **Yajnasena** of **Vidarbha**.
Pushyamitra held the Ganga heartland against **Demetrius** and **Menander**.
Menander debated **Nagasena** in the **Milindapanho**.

39.s: Which last Sunga ruler was killed by Vasudeva Kanva, the founder of the Kanva dynasty?
39.x: Vasudeva Kanva, a Brahmana minister, killed Devabhuti, the last Sunga, and seized power. Vasumitra and Agnimitra were earlier Sungas, and Brihadratha was the last Maurya, killed by Pushyamitra.
39.tq: Devabhuti (last Sunga) killed by Vasudeva Kanva; Brihadratha (last Maurya) killed by Pushyamitra.
xs: **Vasudeva Kanva**, a Brahmana minister, killed the last Sunga **Devabhuti** — option **(3)** (UPSC **2003**).
**Vasumitra** was Pushyamitra's grandson; **Brihadratha** was the last Maurya, killed by **Pushyamitra**.
xa: The Kanvas ruled c. **73-28 BC**.
The last Kanva **Susharman** fell to the **Satavahanas**.
Order: **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas**.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Mauryan dynasty:
1. Brihadratha was killed by his senani Pushyamitra at a military review.
2. Vasudeva Kanva, a minister, founded the dynasty that directly followed the Mauryas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Pushyamitra, a senani, killed Brihadratha at a military review; the Sungas, not the Kanvas, directly followed the Mauryas.

39.s:
Consider the following about the end of the Kanva dynasty:
1. Susharman was overthrown by Menander.
2. Its last ruler was Susharman.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
39.x: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was ended by the Andhras (Satavahanas), not by Menander.
xa: Kanva kings: **Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, Susharman** (c. **73-28 BC**).
The Satavahanas **defeated the Sunga-Kanva line**.
Satavahana founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.

39.s: Who was regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
39.x: Simuka, also known as Srimukha, is regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.
39.tq: Distinguish the dynasty's founder from rulers and founders of neighbouring post-Mauryan houses.
xs: The Satavahana founder was **Simuka (Srimukha)** — option **(3)**.
**Vasumitra** was a Sunga; **Vasudeva Kanva** founded the Kanvas; **Satakarni** was the king Kharavela ignored.
xa: The Puranas call the Satavahanas **Andhra-bhrityas**.
They were **feudatories of the Mauryas** before independence.
They were the **first to unite the Krishna-Godavari region**.

39.s: How many kings ruled in the Kanva dynasty?
39.x: The Kanvas had four kings – Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana and Susharman (c. 73–28 BC).

39.s: Who gave the financial crisis theory of the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
39.x: Kosambi gave the financial crisis theory; H. P. Shastri gave the Brahmanical reaction theory, Raychaudhuri the pacifism theory and Romila Thapar stressed over-centralisation.
xa: Raychaudhuri: after **Kalinga**, non-violence **dulled the army's fighting spirit**.
Kosambi: army, bureaucracy and **Dhamma** spending emptied the treasury; **debased** coins.
**Divyavadana** evidence: revolts at **Taxila** against wicked officials.

39.s: Which of the following is cited as evidence of the financial crisis of the later Mauryas?
o: Increase in the purity of silver coins
Debasement of later punch-marked silver coins with more alloy
39.x: The higher alloy content of later punch-marked silver coins is read as evidence of fiscal strain and debasement.
xa: Other evidence: heavy spending on the **Dhamma mission** and donations to the **Sangha**.
**New taxes on everything**, even actors and prostitutes → revenue hunger.
Kosambi: a huge **army** and **bureaucracy** emptied the treasury.

39.s: Ashoka's expenditure on which of the following was regarded as a strain on the Mauryan treasury?
o: Dhamma missions and donations to the Sangha
39.x: Spending on Dhamma missions and donations to the Buddhist Sangha was considered a burden on the treasury.
xa: This supports **Kosambi**'s **financial crisis** theory.
Coins were **debased** — more alloy in the silver.
⚠ **Raychaudhuri** blamed Ashoka's **pacifism**, not his spending.

39.s: Which historian linked the decline of the Mauryas to a Brahmanical reaction against Ashoka's pro-Buddhist policy?
39.x: H.P. Shastri held that Ashoka's pro-Buddhist policy and ban on sacrifices angered the Brahmins.

39.s: Which historian held that over-centralisation and dependence on the king caused the Mauryan collapse?
39.x: Romila Thapar stressed over-centralisation, with rule depending on the king and weak successors.

39.s: Which of the following pairs of theory of Mauryan decline and historian is INCORRECTLY matched?
39.x: The financial crisis theory is D.D. Kosambi's; H.P. Shastri gave the Brahmanical reaction theory.

39.s: The Divyavadana's evidence of revolts against wicked officials at Taxila supports which theory of Mauryan decline?
39.x: Revolts at Taxila against wicked officials are cited for the oppressive provincial rule theory.

39.s: Which historian blamed Ashoka's pacifism for the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
39.x: H.C. Raychaudhuri held that Ashoka's non-violence after Kalinga weakened the army.

39.s: Which rulers were associated with the western part of the later Mauryan Empire after its division?
39.x: Kunala and later Samprati were associated with the western part, while Dasharatha through Brihadratha ruled the eastern part.
xa: The **Vishnu Purana** lists **seven successors** of Ashoka.
Usual list: **Kunala, Dasharatha, Samprati, Shalishuka, Devavarman, Shatadhanvan, Brihadratha**.
The **Indo-Greeks** virtually replaced the western rulers by **180 BC**.

39.s: By about which year did the Indo-Greeks virtually supplant the western later Mauryan territories?
39.x: The Indo-Greeks had virtually replaced the western later Mauryas by about 180 BC.
39.tq: Distinguish the date of western displacement from the dates of Mauryan succession.
xs: The **Indo-Greeks** virtually replaced the western later Mauryas by **180 BC** — option **(4)**.
**232 BC** is Ashoka's death; **187 BC** is the Sunga coup.
xa: The western rulers were **Kunala** and later **Samprati**.
Indo-Greek leaders: **Demetrius**, later **Menander**.
**Antiochus III** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.

39.s: Samprati, a later Mauryan ruler, was a patron of which faith?
39.x: Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, was a Jain patron who ruled c. 230–215 BCE.

39.s: With the breakaway of which region was Yajnasena, mentioned in Malavikagnimitram, associated?
39.x: Yajnasena is associated with Vidarbha in the account of the regions that broke away after Ashoka.
xs: **Yajnasena** (Malavikagnimitram) is linked with the breakaway of **Vidarbha** — option **(2)** (UPSC).
**Kalinga** broke away under the **Chedis (Kharavela)**; **Kashmir** under **Jalauka**.
xa: **Malavikagnimitram** is by **Kalidasa**.
It also records **Vasumitra** defeating a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu**.

39.s: How did the construction of the Great Wall of China around 220 BC affect the Mauryan north-west?
o: diverted Scythian tribes westward and southward towards India
forced the Indo-Greeks to migrate to Egypt
ended all contact between China and India
enabled the Mauryas to control Bactria
39.x: The Great Wall diverted Scythian tribes towards the west and south, increasing pressure on regions near India while Mauryan frontier defence weakened.
39.tq: Trace the stated cause–effect chain in an external-threat question.
xs: The **Great Wall of China** (c. **220 BC**) **diverted Scythian tribes westward and south towards India** — option **(1)**.
This added to the pressure on a north-west frontier the Mauryas had **neglected**.
xa: **Antiochus III** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.
**Bactrian (Indo-Greek)** invasions under **Demetrius** and **Menander**.
Indo-Greek raids **drained resources**.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a factor in the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
o: Weak and oppressive successors after Ashoka
A permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks

39.s: Which Bactrian (Indo-Greek) rulers threatened the north-west of the Mauryan Empire after Ashoka?

xa: **Antiochus III (Seleucid)** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.
The **Great Wall of China** (c. **220 BC**) diverted **Scythian** tribes towards India.
**Menander (Milinda)** had his capital at **Sakala (Sialkot)**.

39.s: From whom did Antiochus III obtain tribute after crossing the Hindu Kush around 206 BC?
39.x: Antiochus III crossed the Hindu Kush around 206 BC and took tribute from the local ruler Subhagasena.
39.tq: Match the foreign ruler, approximate date and local ruler.
xs: **Antiochus III** took tribute from the local ruler **Subhagasena** — option **(4)**.
He was a **Seleucid** king who crossed the **Hindu Kush** c. **206 BC**.
**Demetrius** and **Menander** were Indo-Greek invaders; **Jalauka** ruled **Kashmir**.
xa: The **Great Wall** (c. **220 BC**) pushed **Scythian** tribes towards India.

42.x: Heliodorus, who set up the Besnagar Garuda pillar, calls himself a Bhagavata from Takshashila (Taxila), envoy of Antialcidas to Bhagabhadra. Sakala was Menander's capital, not his home.

42.x: Hora means horoscope, showing Greek influence on Indian astronomy; Yavanika is the theatre curtain.

The earliest inscription entirely in Tamil

44.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evidence for Kushana-period ports and trade?

44.s: Who among the following first issued gold coins on a large scale?

44.s: The largest number of copper coins in northern and northwestern India were issued by?
44.x: The Kushanas issued the largest number of copper coins in north and north-west India, besides plentiful gold. The Indo-Greeks issued mainly silver.

xa: The **gold dinara** followed the **Roman** weight standard, about **8 g (120 grains)**.

45.x: Dhyana mudra, hands resting in the lap, stands for meditation.

45.x: Bhumisparsha marks the Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, with the earth as witness against Mara.

45.x: The Abhaya mudra (raised right palm) shows fearlessness and is linked with subduing Nalagiri.

45.x: Amaravati is famous for its Buddhist stupa and the Amaravati school of Buddhist sculpture, not Jain, Hindu or Indo-Islamic works.

45.x: In the Agama-Shilpa tradition the sthapati is the master craftsman-architect who designs and directs the making of temples and images, i.e. the master who makes sculptures. xa: ⚠ **Schist** = Gandhara; **red sandstone** = Mathura; **white limestone** = Amaravati.

Southern names and the practice of marrying a maternal uncle’s daughter

Merchant's daughter **Rathavasya** built the **Nodageshwara** temple.

51.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bhatti Mahadevi — Maha Vihara and Maha Chaitya for the Bahushrutiya sect
Upasika Bodhisri — Vihara for the Aparamahavinaseliya sect
Rudradhara Bhattarika — Ayaka pillar for the Maha Chaitya

The **Aparamahavinaseliya** pillar was **Harmyasri's**.

51.x: Kodabalisri, daughter of Virapurushadatta, built a vihara for the Mahishasaka monks; Bhatti Mahadevi's vihara was for the Bahushrutiya.

51.s: Which of the following donor–gift pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bhatti Mahadevi – Vihara and chaitya for the Bahushrutiya
Harmyasri – Vihara for the Mahishasaka monks

51.s: Whose daughter was Queen Rudradhara Bhattarika, who donated an ayaka pillar?
51.x: Rudradhara Bhattarika was the daughter of Rudrasena of Ujjain; Bodhisri was the daughter of Revanta of Amaravati.

51.s: How many dinari-masakas did Chamtisri donate at Nagarjunakonda?
51.x: Chamtisri, the first woman donor, gave 170 dinari-masakas along with 9 ayaka pillars.

51.s: For whom did Harmyasri, sister of Santamula, set up a pillar at the Aparamahavinaseliya chaitya?
51.x: Harmyasri, a sister of Santamula, gave a pillar for her mother at the Aparamahavinaseliya chaitya.

51.s: How was Chamtisri, the first woman donor at Nagarjunakonda, related to Virapurushadatta?
51.x: Chamtisri was the sister of Sri Santamula and so the paternal aunt of Virapurushadatta.

51.s: Which of the following describes most donative inscriptions at Nagarjunakonda?
o: Sanskrit royal edicts dated by regnal decades
Tamil merchant records dated to the reign of Sri Santamula
Greek inscriptions issued by Roman officials
Prakrit Ayaka-pillar records dated to the sixth regnal year of Virapurushadatta
51.x: Most records are Prakrit Ayaka-pillar inscriptions dated in Virapurushadatta's sixth regnal year.
51.tq: Combine language, record type and regnal-date clues.
xs: Most are **Prakrit Ayaka-pillar** records dated in **Virapurushadatta's 6th regnal year** — option **(4)**.
Each names the donor by her **tie to the king** (aunt, sister, queen, daughter).
xa: The Ikshvakus were first to date inscriptions by **year, month and day**.
**Chamtisri's** inscription prays for the king's **long life, victory and prosperity**.
**Chamtisri** used **9 Ayaka pillars** at the Maha Chaitya.

51.s: How were Bapisri and Chatisri, who gave pillars at the Mahachaitya, related to Virapurushadatta?
51.x: Bapisri and Chatisri were queens of Virapurushadatta and daughters of his aunt.

51.s: How is Adavi Chamtisri related to Virapurushadatta in the donative inscriptions?
51.x: Adavi Chamtisri was the sister of Virapurushadatta and gave an ayaka pillar at the Maha Chaitya.

51.s: Which dynasty was the first to date its records by year, month and day?
51.x: The Ikshvakus were the first to date their records by year, month and day.

51.s: What does the inscription of Upasika Bodhisri at Nagarjunakonda show?
51.x: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, so her record shows non-royal patronage of Buddhism.

51.s: In which language are most ayaka-pillar donative inscriptions at Nagarjunakonda written?
51.x: Most donative records at Nagarjunakonda are Prakrit ayaka-pillar inscriptions of Virapurushadatta's 6th regnal year.

51.s: The third Madhava Verma of the Vishnukundina dynasty gave Mruthukali as Agrahara. Agraharas, a grant of land and royal income from it, were mainly given to ____.

51.x: Agraharas – land grants with the royal income from them – were given mainly to Brahmins for Vedic learning, as in the Vishnukundin Mruthukali grant.

51.src: APPSC Junior Assistants in Labs / Panchayat Raj 2012
51.x: Agraharas were donated mostly to Brahmins, especially from the Satavahana period onward.

51.s: Which Ikshvaku king tried to make the intelligentsia partners in agricultural development?
51.x: Sri Chantamula (Vasishthiputra Santamula) donated land, ploughs and cattle to Brahmins, involving the intellectual class in agricultural development.

51.s: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula brought Brahmins from which region and granted them what kind of land grants?
51.x: Santamula brought Brahmins from the north and granted them agraharas.
51.tq: Pair the person with both the direction and the specific grant to avoid location–institution swaps.
xs: Santamula brought **Brahmins from the north** and gave them **agraharas** — option **(1)**.
Brahmins also rose through **Brahmadeya** grants (exempt from **18 taxes**).
xa: The period moved Andhra to an **agrarian, agrahara-based** early medieval order.
Revenue also went to **poets + scholars** and **gifts to religious bodies**.
Preventing **Varnasankara** was the king's duty.

51.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices?
51.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma; an Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Titles: **Goshatasahasra Halashatasahasra**, **Mahadanapati**.
He brought **Brahmins from the north** with **agraharas**.
Romans were said to have built a **stadium** under him.

51.s: According to the recorded four-way division of state revenue, which one of the following was NOT one of the specified major allocations?
51.x: The four specified allocations were administration and army, temples and festivals, poets and scholars, and gifts to religious bodies. Expansion of overseas colonies was not listed; some revenue also went to tanks and canals.
51.tq: Find the option outside the four stated revenue heads rather than choosing a merely less familiar allocation.
xs: **Expansion of overseas colonies** was not an allocation — option **(1)**.
The **four** shares: **administration + army**, **temples + festivals**, **poets + scholars**, **gifts to religious bodies**.
xa: Some revenue also went to **tanks and canals**.
Land tax **Bhaga** = **1/6** of produce.
Economy: mainly **agrarian**.

51.s: Which transition in Andhra history does the Ikshvaku period mark?
o: A Buddhist society to a purely Vedic society
An agrarian economy to a maritime empire
A Satavahana trade economy to an agrarian, agrahara-based early medieval order
A feudal economy to an industrial economy

xs: The period marks the move from a **Satavahana trade economy** to an **agrarian, agrahara-based early medieval order** — option **(3)**.
Roman trade fell **lower than under the Satavahanas**; Brahmins received **agraharas**.
xa: One account: villages became **self-sufficient** after Rome's fall.
A new **landlord class** emerged.
Revenue was split **four** ways.

51.s:

51.s: What did Bhaga represent in the Ikshvaku economy?

xs: **Bhaga** was the land tax (**revenue**) of **one-sixth (1/6)** of the produce — option **(2)**.
The other fractions (one-tenth, one-fourth, one-half) are not the **Bhaga** rate in the notes.
xa: Farmers were called **Halikas**.
Economy: mainly **agrarian**.
**Brahmadeya** grants were exempt from **18 taxes**.

51.s: What were farmers called in Ikshvaku records?

xs: Farmers were called **Halikas** — option **(1)**.
**Sale** = weavers; **Telika** = oil pressers; **Kammaru** = blacksmiths.
xa: Land tax **Bhaga** = **1/6** of produce.
Guilds were called **Nigamalu** (Negimalu).
**Parnika Sreni** (betel-leaf traders) was the most prominent guild.

51.s: What were guilds called in the Ikshvaku inscriptions?
51.x: Guilds were called Nigamalu; the spelling Negimalu also occurs. They continued the Satavahana sreni tradition.

xs: Guilds were called **Nigamalu** (also **Negimalu**) — option **(2)**.
They continued the **Satavahana srenis**.
**Varnasankara** = mixing of varnas; **Brahmadeya** = grant to Brahmins; **Halikas** = farmers.
xa: **Parnika Sreni** = betel-leaf traders (most prominent).
**Poosika Sreni** = sweetmeat traders.
**Nagarjunakonda** was home to merchants and artisans in guilds.

51.x: Sale were weavers. Parnika Sreni were betel-leaf traders, Poosika Sreni sweetmeat traders and Telika oil pressers.
xa: **Kammaru** = blacksmiths.

Guild name: **Nigamalu**.

51.s: Whom did the Poosika Sreni of the Ikshvaku inscriptions represent?
51.x: Poosika Sreni were sweetmeat traders; Parnika Sreni were betel-leaf traders.

51.s: Who were called Telika in Ikshvaku records?
51.x: Sale, Telika and Kammaru meant weavers, oil pressers and blacksmiths respectively.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about Roman trade in the Ikshvaku period:

**Roman-style amphitheatre** at **Vijayapuri**.

51.s: Which of the following provides evidence of Roman contact with the Ikshvaku region?
o: Roman gold and silver coins at Nagarjunakonda and a Roman-style amphitheatre at Vijayapuri
Roman ships engraved at Amaravati and Persian coins at Ujjain
Latin manuscripts at Guntur and Roman pillars at Sopara
Roman inscriptions at Motupalli and Greek temples at Ghantasala

xs: **Roman gold and silver coins** at Nagarjunakonda and a **Roman-style amphitheatre** at Vijayapuri — option **(1)**.
Romans were said to have built a **stadium under Sri Santamula**.

Roman trade was **lower than under the Satavahanas**.

51.s: Which of the following was an export from the Ikshvaku region?
51.x: Exports included spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles. Gold, silver, wine and glassware were imported.

xs: **Spices** were exported — option **(4)**.
**Gold, wine, glassware** (and silver) were **imports**.
xa: Other exports: **iron, coconuts, cotton textiles**.
Roman trade was **lower than under the Satavahanas**.
Ports: **Motupalli, Ghantasala**.

51.s: Which of the following was imported into the Ikshvaku region?
51.x: Gold, silver, wine and glassware were imports; spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles were exports.

51.x: A Roman-style amphitheatre stands at Vijayapuri, evidence of Roman contact.

51.s: Of which metals were Ikshvaku coins mainly made?
51.x: Ikshvaku coins were of lead and copper and bore the Ujjain symbol, the elephant and the lion; they are found in Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts.

51.s: Which symbols are found on Ikshvaku coins?
51.x: Ikshvaku lead and copper coins carry the Ujjain symbol, elephant and lion.

**Sati (sahagamana)** was practised.
Children were named after the **grandfather** (Ehuvala Santamula).

51.x: Ikshvaku inscriptions record names derived from the grandfather (Ehuvala Santamula), matronymics such as Vasishthiputra, and sati.

Preventing **Varnasankara** was the king's duty.

o: Records show matronymics such as Vasishthiputra
Records mention the practice of sati
Brahmins lost land under the Brahmadeya system

52.x: Under the Ikshvakus the queens and princesses (Chamtisri, Bodhisri and others) patronised Buddhism, while the kings were Vedic.

52.s: During whose regnal period did Buddhism receive great patronage in the Ikshvaku kingdom?
52.x: Buddhism received its greatest patronage in Virapurushadatta's reign, the golden age of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda; his successors revived Brahmanism.

52.s: Upasika Bodhishri rendered outstanding service to the propagation of Buddhism during whose reign?
52.x: Upasika Bodhisri served Buddhism in the reign of Virapurushadatta – her Chula-Dhammagiri record at Nagarjunakonda is dated in his 14th regnal year; Ehuvala Chantamula came later and revived Brahmanism.

52.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about religious patronage in the Ikshvaku kingdom?
o: Wealthy lay women funded stupas and viharas
Kings were the chief patrons of stupas and viharas
Queens and princesses supported Buddhist monuments
52.x: The Ikshvakus showed dual patronage: kings performed Vedic sacrifices, while royal and wealthy lay women funded Buddhist stupas and viharas.

52.s:
Which of the following flourished under the Ikshvakus?
1. Puranic Shaivism
2. Vaishnavism
3. Shakti worship

o: Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship thrived
Virapurushadatta performed Vedic sacrifices as a Buddhist
Royal women funded stupas and viharas

52.s: Which one of the following statements about Virapurushadatta is NOT correct?
o: His reign was regarded as the golden age of Buddhism.
He was the only Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism.
He rebuilt the Maha Chaitya under Acharya Bhadanta Ananda.

The rebuilding of the Maha Chaitya
The first construction of Hindu temples
The issue of the first Sanskrit inscriptions

52.s: During whose reign did Upasika Bodhisri serve Buddhism?

54.x: Madhava Varma II was the greatest Vishnukundin ruler; his reign is called the golden age and saw a Vedic revival.

54.s:
Arrange the following Vishnukundin rulers in chronological order:

a. Govinda Varma I

b. Indravarma

c. Madhava Varma II

d. Madhava Varma I
54.x: The order is Indravarma (founder), Madhava Varma I, Govinda Varma I and then Madhava Varma II.

54.s: A twelfth-century inscription from Bezawada preserves which legend about Madhava Varma II?
o: He sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed a poor woman’s son.
He founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty at Vengi.
He married his daughter to Ishanavarma of the Maukharis.
He abdicated after losing Vengi to the Salankayanas.
54.x: The Bezawada inscription narrates that Madhava Varma II sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed the son of a poor woman.
54.tq: Identify the ruler through a distinctive justice legend rather than through a military event.
xs: The **12th-c. Bezawada inscription**: MV II **sentenced his own son to death** after the prince's chariot killed a poor woman's son — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** founded the Eastern Chalukyas; **Ishanavarma** is linked to **Indrabhattaraka**.
xa: MV II = **greatest** Vishnukundin, **golden age**.
Title: **Janasraya**.
Bezawada was a Vishnukundin capital for a time.

54.s: Which combination correctly represents the sacrifices attributed to Madhava Varma II?
54.x: Madhava Varma II is credited with performing 11 Ashvamedhas, 16 Rajasuyas and one Purushamedha.
54.tq: Separate the three numerical counts carefully because the figures are deliberately similar.
xs: **MV II**: **11 Ashvamedhas, 16 Rajasuyas and 1 Purushamedha** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the **11** and **16**.
xa: Also **Hiranyagarbha**, **Agnistoma** and about **1,000 other yagas**.
His reign = **Vedic revival**.
Titles: **Parama Brahmanya**, **Trisamudradhipati**.

54.s: The Khanapur plates, found in Satara district of Maharashtra, record the marriage of Madhava Varma II with a daughter of which ruler?
o: Pulakeshin II of the Badami Chalukyas
54.x: The Khanapur plates record Madhava Varma II’s marriage with a daughter of Vakataka ruler Prithvisena II.
54.tq: Use the marriage alliance to distinguish the correct dynasty and ruler from other figures in the political narrative.
xs: The **Khanapur** plates (Satara) record MV II's marriage to a daughter of Vakataka **Prithvisena II** — option **(2)**.
**Pulakeshin II** ended the dynasty; **Ishanavarma** defeated Indrabhattaraka; **Prithvimula** killed him.
xa: Their son **Vikramendra Varma I** was "**Mahakavi**".
**Madhava Varma I** also married a **Vakataka** princess.
**Chikkulla** plates also mention **Vakataka** marriage ties.

54.s: From which dynasty did Madhava Varma II take Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma?
54.x: He took Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma from the Pallavas; Vengi was taken from the Salankayanas.

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title Satyasraya?
54.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma bore the title Satyasraya; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi.
xa: Vikramendra II = **Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya**.
Indrabhattaraka also = **Paramamaheshwara**, **Chaturdhayaka Yuddha Veera**.
MV II = **Janasraya**, **Trisamudradhipati**.

54.s: Madhava Varma II won the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati by defeating which rulers?
54.x: Madhava Varma II acquired the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati after defeating the Anandagotrikas. Trikuta was identified with Kotappakonda in Guntur.
54.tq: Connect a victory-based title with the defeated power.
xs: **Trikuta-Malayadhipati** came from defeating the **Anandagotrikas** — option **(2)**.
**Trikuta** = **Kotappakonda**, Guntur.
xa: Title holder: **Madhava Varma II** (CDX p.**100**, APP); CDX p.**104** gives it to **Madhava Varma III**.
**Anandagotrikas** = **Kandara** kings, capital **Kandarapuram** (Chejerla inscription).
Anandagotrikas were former **Ikshvaku feudatories**.

54.s: In the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati of Madhava Varma II, which place does Trikuta refer to?
54.x: Trikuta is Kotappakonda in Guntur; the title came after he defeated the Anandagotrikas.

54.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
54.x: Shadabhigna was Govinda Varma's title; Mahakavi was Vikramendra I, Satyasraya Indrabhattaraka and Trikuta-Malayadhipati Madhava Varma II.

54.s: Which of the following titles was borne by Madhava Varma II?
54.x: Madhava Varma II bore the title Janasraya. Shadabhigna belonged to Govinda Varma, Mahakavi to Vikramendra Varma I, and Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya to Vikramendra Varma II.
54.tq: Use a title–ruler match and separate similar royal epithets.
xs: **Janasraya** = **Madhava Varma II** — option **(2)** (G2 **2025** key).
**Mahakavi** = **Vikramendra I**; **Shadabhigna** = **Govinda Varma**; **Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya** = **Vikramendra II**.
xa: ⚠ APP also gives **Janasraya** to **Vikramendra I**.
Other MV II titles: **Trisamudradhipati, Devadhideva, Parameshti, Parama Brahmanya**.
**Trikuta-Malayadhipati** = MV II (CDX p.100, APP).

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya'?
54.x: Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya was a title of Vikramendra Varma II.

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Trisamudradhipati'?
54.x: Trisamudradhipati (lord of the three seas) was one of the titles of Madhava Varma II.

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
54.x: NextGen says Madhava Varma II shifted the capital from Amarapuri to Dendulurupura near Vengi to check Pallava invasions. (official final key accepted both Vikramendravarma and Madhavavarma; Vikramendravarma II's Chikkulla plates were issued from Denduluru)

54.x: NextGen says Madhava Varma II shifted the capital from Amarapuri to Dendulurupura near Vengi to check Pallava invasions. (official final key accepted both Vikramendravarma and Madhavavarma; Vikramendravarma II's Chikkulla plates were issued from Denduluru)

54.s: According to most historians, to which social group did the Vishnukundins belong?
o: Only hereditary feudatories of the Pallavas
54.x: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as Brahmins belonging to the Vishnukundina gotra, although alternative caste theories have also been proposed.
54.tq: Identify the mainstream interpretation while distinguishing it from alternative theories.
xs: The majority view: the Vishnukundins were **Brahmins of the Vishnukundina gotra** — option **(4)**.
Other theories: **Agnikula Kshatriyas** (K. Gopalachari); **Shudras** raised through the **Hiranyagarbha** rite.
xa: **B.V. Krishna Rao** = Brahmins; **N. Venkataramanayya** = Brahmins who took up Kshatriya ways.
Name "**Vishnukundi**" = **Vinukonda** (Guntur).
Original home: **Telangana** (Amrabad, Keesaragutta, Indrapalanagara).

54.s: Which region is indicated by the early records and forts as the original home of the Vishnukundins?
o: Telangana, including Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara
The Krishna-Godavari coast after the Pallava wars
The coastal delta around Vengi alone
The southern Tamil region around Kandarapuram
54.x: Early records and forts at Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara point to Telangana as the original home. The Vishnukundins later expanded into coastal Andhra.
54.tq: Infer the original homeland from the distribution of early forts and records.
xs: Early records and forts show **Telangana** — **Amrabad, Keesaragutta, Indrapalanagara** — as the original home — option **(1)**.
They first ruled Telangana **north of the Krishna**, then expanded to **coastal Andhra**.
xa: **Keesaragutta** = possibly their start as **Vakataka feudatories**.
**Indrapalanagara** = **Tummalagudem**, built by **Indravarma**.
**Amarapura** = **Munnanuru** (Amrabad, Nagarkurnool), where **yaga-vedikas** were found.

54.s: Which of the following pairs on the origin of the Vishnukundins is correctly matched?
o: K. Gopalachari – Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways
54.x: B.V. Krishna Rao regarded the Vishnukundins as Brahmins. K. Gopalachari proposed an Agnikula Kshatriya origin and N. Venkataramanayya called them Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways.
xa: Others: **Shudras** raised through the **Hiranyagarbha** rite.
Majority view: **Brahmins of the Vishnukundina gotra**.
⚠ In the Ikshvaku origin debate, **Gopalachari** gave the **Telugu/Andhra** theory — don't mix them up.

54.s: Which historian held that the Vishnukundins were Agnikula Kshatriyas?
54.x: K. Gopalachari called them Agnikula Kshatriyas; B.V. Krishna Rao held they were Brahmins.

54.s: Keesaragutta may mark the beginning of the Vishnukundins as feudatories of which dynasty?
54.x: Keesaragutta may mark their start as Vakataka feudatories; the founder Indravarma was a Vakataka vassal.

54.s: With which place is the name of the Vishnukundin dynasty generally linked?
54.x: Historians generally take 'Vishnukundi' as the Sanskrit form of Vinukonda, a hill-fort town in the Guntur (now Palnadu) region.

54.s: With which place is Indrapalanagara, the early Vishnukundin capital, identified?
54.x: Indrapalanagara (Sukrapuram), built by Indravarma and the capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma, is Tummalagudem in Telangana.
xa: Also called **Sukrapuram**.
**Tummalagudem** plates = **first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana**.

54.s: Which of the following was regarded as the first capital of the Vishnukundins?
54.x: Amarapura was the first capital of the Vishnukundins. The rulers referred to themselves as Amarapurishulu.
xs: The first capital was **Amarapura** — option **(2)**.
The kings called themselves "**Amarapurishulu**".
xa: Identified as **Munnanuru** (Amrabad, Nagarkurnool), where **yaga-vedikas** were found.
**B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao** places it at **Velpuru** (Guntur).
**Bezawada** and **Denduluru** were later capitals.

54.s: After acquiring the Krishna region, the Vishnukundins used which place as a capital for some time?
54.x: Bezawada, or Vijayawada, was used as a capital for a period after the Vishnukundins acquired the Krishna region.
54.tq: Identify the temporary capital from the territorial-expansion context.
xs: After taking the **Krishna** region, they used **Bezawada** (Vijayawada) as capital for a time — option **(2)**.
They carved the **Indrakeeladri** and **Mogalrajapuram** caves there.
xa: **Keesaragutta** = possibly their start as **Vakataka feudatories**.
**Indrapalanagara** = capital of **MV I** and **Govinda Varma**.
**Denduluru** = **MV II's** capital.

54.s: With which place is Amarapura, the first Vishnukundin capital, identified?
54.x: Amarapura is identified with Munnanuru in Amrabad, where yaga-vedikas were found; Tummalagudem was Indrapalanagara.

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler moved the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
54.x: Of these options Vikramendravarma is the one the APPSC G2 Mains 2025 final key accepted (it accepted Vikramendravarma and Madhavavarma). NextGen credits Madhava Varma II, who is not listed here; Vikramendravarma II's Chikkulla plates were issued from Denduluru.
54.tq: Use the capital-shift clue to identify the ruler.

54.s: Constant wars with which dynasty made the Vishnukundins shift their capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
54.x: Constant wars with the Pallavas led to the shift of the capital to Denduluru (credited in the APPSC key to Vikramendravarma, by some texts to Madhava Varma II).

54.s: Who built Indrapalanagara, the early capital of the Vishnukundins?
54.x: The Tummalagudem inscription says the founder Indravarma built Indrapalanagara.

54.s: Who was the editor of Chikkulla plates of Vishnukundins?
54.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
54.x: The Chikkulla plates of Vikramendravarman II were edited by F. Kielhorn in Epigraphia Indica vol. IV (No. 25); Hultzsch was the editor of the volume, not of this article.

54.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
54.x: The Velpuru pillar is associated with Madhava Varma II, not Govinda Varma I. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
54.tq: Find the swapped ruler by checking the inscription or monument against its recorded patron.
xs: **Velpuru pillar — Govinda Varma I** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The **Velpuru** pillar is **MV II's** — **Ganapati** installed in his **33rd** year.
Others are right: **Ramatirtham** = Indravarma; **Polamuru** = Madhava Varma IV; **Khanapur** = MV II.
xa: **Khanapur** plates record MV II's marriage to **Prithvisena II's** daughter.
**Polamuru** plates describe **divine ordeals**.
**Govinda Varma I** = **Tummalagudem** plates.

54.s: Which is regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana?
54.x: The Tummalagudem plates, associated with Govinda Varma I, are regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana.
xa: They also give the **genealogy**.
Tummalagudem = **Indrapalanagara** (Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri/Nalgonda).
Govinda Varma's **Chaitanyapuri** record is in **Prakrit**.

54.s: In which language was Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri inscription written?
54.x: Of the 21 Vishnukundin inscriptions, Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit, so not all were in Sanskrit.
xa: **Tummalagudem** = **first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana**.
**Chikkulla** has the Telugu phrase "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**".
Records span both Telugu states: **Godavari, Guntur, Telangana**.

54.s: To which ruler do the Chikkulla plates, containing the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul', belong?
54.x: The Chikkulla plates (Tuni, East Godavari) are of Vikramendra Varma II and carry the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'.
xa: Vikramendra II also issued the **Tundi** and **Tummalagudem-2** plates.
Godavari-region records: **Chikkulla, Polamuru**.

54.s: To which ruler do the Ipur plates, bearing Lakshmi and conch symbols, belong?
54.x: The two Ipur plates from Tenali belong to Madhava Varma I.

54.s: What do the Polamuru plates of the Vishnukundins describe?
o: A marriage with a Vakataka princess
A grant to a Buddhist vihara
54.x: The Polamuru plates (Ramachandrapuram) describe divine ordeals; the Vakataka marriage is in the Khanapur plates.

54.s: Of the 21 known Vishnukundin inscriptions, how many are copper-plate records?
54.x: The 21 inscriptions comprise 16 copper-plate and 5 stone records.

54.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler issued the Tummalagudem plates granting land to Paramabhattarika's vihara?
54.x: The Tummalagudem plates of Govinda Varma I record the grant to his queen Paramabhattarika's vihara.

Match the following:

List-I (Inscription)
a. Ramatirtham plates
b. Tummalagudem plates

1. Madhava Varma II

54.s: The Vishnukundins formed a link between which two phases of Andhra history?
o: The Pallava age and the Maukhari age
The Satavahana age and the Ikshvaku age
The Ikshvaku age and the Eastern Chalukyas
The Gupta age and the Kushana age
54.x: The Vishnukundins link the Ikshvaku age with the Eastern Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas took over their agrahara system and administration.
54.tq: Test the broader historical transition rather than an isolated ruler or inscription.
xs: The Vishnukundins link the **Ikshvaku age** and the **Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.
The Eastern Chalukyas took over their **agrahara system and administration**.
xa: Dynasty order: Ikshvakus → **Brihatpalayanas** → **Salankayanas** → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas.
Founder of the Eastern Chalukyas: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Their records lie across **both Telugu states**.

54.s: Which Maukhari king defeated the Vishnukundin ruler Indrabhattaraka Varma?
54.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma and was killed in the Kalinga war.
xa: Ishanavarma's son married Indrabhattaraka's daughter (**Jaunpur** inscription).
Killers: **Prithvimula** of the Ranadurjayas + a **Kalinga** king.
Vikramendra I = "**Mahakavi**", **Parama Saugata**.

54.s: In which year did Pulakeshin II defeat Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru), ending Vishnukundin rule?
54.x: Pulakeshin II ended Vishnukundin rule at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE; his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.
xa: **Indrabhattaraka** was defeated by **Maukhari Ishanavarma** (Jaunpur inscription) and killed in the **Kalinga** war.
**Manchana Bhattaraka** was the **last** Vishnukundin ruler.
Founder of the Vishnukundins: **Indravarma**; greatest: **Madhava Varma II**.
Dates differ: **358-569 CE** vs **c. 420-624 CE**.

54.s: Who founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi after the fall of the Vishnukundins?
54.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakeshin II, founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

54.s: Indrabhattaraka Varma was killed in the Kalinga war by Prithvimula of which dynasty?
54.x: Prithvimula of the Ranadurjayas, with a Kalinga king, killed Indrabhattaraka Varma.

54.s: The Jaunpur inscription records the marriage of Indrabhattaraka Varma's daughter to a prince of which dynasty?
54.x: Maukhari Ishanavarma defeated Indrabhattaraka, and his son married Indrabhattaraka's daughter (Jaunpur inscription).

54.s: Who defeated Manchana Bhattaraka and ended the rule of the Vishnukundins?
54.x: The Badami Chalukya Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru) in 624 CE.

54.s: Where did Pulakeshin II defeat the last Vishnukundin ruler Manchana Bhattaraka?
54.x: The battle that ended Vishnukundin rule in 624 CE was fought at Kunala, near Kolleru lake.

55.s: During his rule, Indrabhattaraka Varma of the Vishnukundin dynasty established many Ghatikas. They were ____.
55.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
55.x: Ghatikas were educational institutions – Sanskrit and Vedic colleges; Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions first mention them.

55.s: The Pallava educational institutions were known as
55.x: The Pallava educational institutions were Ghatikas (e.g. the Kanchi ghatika); Mathas, Vidyapithas and Gacchas are other institutions.

55.s: The medium of instruction in the college attached to the larger temples of South India was:
55.x: The temple colleges (ghatikas) of South India taught Vedas, Vedangas and philosophy in Sanskrit.

55.s: Position of 'Ghatikas' during Vishnukundins?
55.x: Ghatikas were Sanskrit educational institutions, first mentioned in Vishnukundin inscriptions.

55.s: Who is associated with the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra inscriptions?
55.x: The inscriptions of Indrabhattaraka Varma provide the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra.
55.tq: Identify the ruler directly associated with the specific epigraphic evidence.
xs: Ghatikas are first mentioned in **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions — option **(3)**.
He is also credited with the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara**.
xa: **Govinda Varma** = "**Shadabhigna**"; **MV II** = "**Vidyadvijaguru**".
**Vikramendra Varma I** is called "**Mahakavi**" in the Indrapalanagara plates.
Ghatikas taught **14 vidyas**; special ones at **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.

55.s: How many vidyas were taught at the special Ghatikas of Amaravati and Vengi?
55.x: The Ghatikas taught fourteen vidyas: four Vedas, six Vedangas, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra and Puranas.
55.tq: Check the numerical total against the component subjects rather than relying on a rounded figure.
xs: Ghatikas taught **14** vidyas — option **(3)**.
**4 Vedas** + **6 Vedangas** + **Mimamsa** + **Nyaya** + **Dharmashastra** + **Puranas** = 14.
xa: Special Ghatikas: **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
First mention in Andhra: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions.
Buddhist teacher **Dasabalabali** knew the **four Vedas**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about Ghatikas under the Vishnukundins:
1. They were higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning.
2. Special Ghatikas existed at Amaravati and Vengi.
3. They are first mentioned in the inscriptions of Madhava Varma II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Ghatikas were Sanskrit-Vedic colleges with special centres at Amaravati and Vengi; their first mention is in Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions.

55.s: Which was the medium of instruction in the Ghatikas under the Vishnukundins?
55.x: Ghatikas were higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning, and Sanskrit was the teaching language.

55.s: Who was the family deity of the Vishnukundin dynasty?
55.x: Sriparvataswami was the family deity, and the kings described themselves as Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata.
55.tq: Direct identification of the dynastic deity.
xs: The family deity was **Sriparvataswami** — option **(1)**.
Kings styled themselves "**Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata**"; the deity is identified with **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was Yama; **Dantamukha Swami** was the Ganapati at Velpuru; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra.
xa: "**Sriparvata**" also appears on Vishnukundin coins.
Royal titles: **Paramamaheshwara** (Indrabhattaraka, Vikramendra), **Parama Bhagavata**, **Parama Brahmanya**.
**Ramalingeswara** temples: Keesaragutta, Velpuru, Ipur, Indrapalanagara.

55.s: At which place was Dantamukha Swami installed during the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II?
55.x: Dantamukha Swami was installed at Velpuru in the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II.
55.tq: Combine the deity, place and regnal-year clues.
xs: **Dantamukha Swami** was installed at **Velpuru** — option **(1)**.
It marks the **beginning of Ganapati worship**, in **MV II's 33rd year**.
**Keesaragutta** had a Ramalingeswara temple; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra; **Indrapalanagara** had a vihara and a Ramalingeswara temple.
xa: **Velpuru** (Guntur) was also a **Rashtra**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was identified with **Yama**.
MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.

55.s: With which deity is Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, identified?
55.x: Sriparvataswami is Srisaila Mallikarjuna; Amareswara is a common trap.

55.s: The queen of which ruler founded the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara?
55.x: The queen of Govinda Varma I founded the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara; Govinda Varma I himself founded the Govinda Vihara.
xa: The Mahadevi Vihara at **Indrapalanagara** housed **Chaturdasharya bhikshus**; Govinda Varma I granted it **Penkapura and Enmadala**.
Govinda Vihara has a **Prakrit inscription on the Musi**.
Buddhism declined from **MV II** onward.

55.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is called a 'destroyer of Buddhism'?
55.x: Buddhism declined from Madhava Varma II onward, and sites like Undavalli and Mogalrajapuram became Hindu shrines. Govinda Varma I and his queen founded viharas, and Vikramendra Varma II granted a village to a vihara.
xa: MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.
⚠ Some notes say royal grants to monasteries stopped entirely — this contradicts the **Tummalagudem** grants.
Jainism declined as **Kapalika** Shaivas rose.

55.s: Which development was associated with the decline of Jainism during the Vishnukundin period?
55.x: Jainism declined as Kapalika Shaivism rose; Jain shrines such as Srisailam were converted, and Kumarilabhatta attacked Jainism.
55.tq: Link the religious decline with its stated historical cause.
xs: Jainism declined as **Kapalika Shaivism** rose — option **(2)**.
Jain shrines such as **Srisailam** were converted, and **Kumarilabhatta** attacked Jainism.
xa: Buddhism too declined from **MV II** onward.
MV II turned Buddhist sites at **Undavalli** and **Mogalrajapuram** into Hindu shrines.
Family deity **Sriparvataswami** = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.

**Jivaka Chintamani** is the Jain epic; **Tolkappiyar** wrote the grammar.
xa: Kovalan is executed by the **Pandya** king; **Kannagi burns Madurai**.

58.s: Who wrote the Jain epic Sivaga Sindamani?

58.s: Which Tamil work is called 'Mana Nool' (Book of Marriages)?
58.x: Sivaga Sindamani is called Mana Nool, the Book of Marriages.

58.s: According to Manimekalai, what did the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi become?

UPPSC 2014 key: Manimekalai = **merchant story**.
Kannagi, not Madhavi, is Kovalan's wife; she **burns Madurai**.

58.s: How are Silappadikaram and Manimekalai generally regarded?

xs: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are **post-Sangam works** — option **(3)**.
The **Tirukkural** too is post-Sangam.
xa: Silappadikaram = **first Tamil epic** (Ilango Adigal).
Manimekalai = **Buddhist epic** (Sittalai Sattanar).
Oldest Tamil work = **Tolkappiyam**.

58.s: Who was the younger brother of Chera king Senguttuvan and the author of Silappadikaram?
58.x: Ilango Adigal, identified as the younger brother of Chera Senguttuvan, composed Silappadikaram.

xs: **Ilango Adigal**, younger brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**, wrote Silappadikaram — option **(1)**.

xa: Silappadikaram = **first Tamil epic**, post-Sangam.

UPPSC 2014 key: Silappadikaram = **love story**.

58.s: Who wrote the Manimekalai?
58.x: Manimekalai, the Buddhist sequel to Silappadikaram, was written by Sittalai Sattanar.

58.s: Ilango Adigal, author of Silappadikaram, was the grandson of which ruler?
58.x: Ilango Adigal was the grandson of Chola Karikala and the younger brother of Chera Senguttuvan.

58.s: In Silappadikaram, the king of which dynasty executed Kovalan?
58.x: Kovalan was executed by the Pandya king, after which Kannagi burnt Madurai.

58.s: In Sangam Literature ‘Tolkappiyam’ is a text of –
58.x: Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar is the earliest Tamil grammar (with poetics); it is not a work on architecture or polity.

58.s: Which one of the following Tamil Texts has been called Laghuveda?
58.x: Tiruvalluvar's Kural is honoured as the Tamil Veda and Laghuveda; Kalingattuparani (Jayangondar) and Periyapuranam (Sekkilar) are later Chola works and Nandikkalambakam is Pallava.

58.s: The Sangam text Tolkappiyam is a work on
58.x: Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar; it is not on astronomy, music or medicine.

58.s: Tolkappiyam text deals with :
58.x: Tolkappiyam deals with grammar and poetics (and incidentally with society, e.g. the tinai and four castes); it is not a work on administration or law, so 'all the above' is wrong.

58.s: Which of the following Tamil text has been called ‘Laghuveda’?
58.x: The Kural of Tiruvalluvar is called Laghuveda and Tamil Veda; Kalingattuparani, Periyapuranam and Nandikkalambakam are later works.

58.x: The Kural of Tiruvalluvar, 1,330 couplets on ethics, is in Tamil, not Pali or Telugu.

58.s: What does the book Porul of the Tirukkural deal with?
58.x: The Tirukkural's 1,330 couplets are in three books: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth) and Inbam (love).

58.x: The Tirukkural of Tiruvalluvar has 1,330 couplets in three books: Aram, Porul and Inbam.

58.x: Tolkappiyam has three parts: Ezhuttu, Col and Porul; Aram, Porul and Inbam are the books of the Kural.

58.x: The Kural is also called Laghuveda, Tamil Veda and Ulaga Podhumarai; Mana Nool is Sivaga Sindamani.

58.s: Which is the oldest extant Tamil grammar?

Tolkappiyam deals with grammar and poetics. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 57-60]
xa: Tolkappiyam is the only survivor of the **Second Sangam** (at **Kapatapuram**).
**Silappadikaram** by **Ilango Adigal** is the **first Tamil epic**.

58.s: Which one of the following statements about Sangam literature in ancient South India is correct?
o: Sangam poems are devoid of any reference to material culture.
The social classification of Varna was known to Sangam poets.
Sangam poems have no reference to warrior ethics.
Sangam literature refers to magical forces as irrational.
58.x: Sangam poets knew the varna classification, although society was not rigidly divided; the poems are rich in material culture and warrior ethic, so the other options are false.

58.s: Name the source that is silent about the trade routes of ancient India
58.x: Sangam poetry describes ports and goods but not the overland trade routes; the Milindapanha and the Jatakas describe routes and caravan travel.

o: Sangam poems are devoid of any reference to material
The social classification of Varna was known to
Sangam poems have no reference to warrior ethic
Sangam literature refers to magical forces as irrational
58.x: The varna classification was known to Sangam poets (UPSC 2022), though Tamil society was not rigidly stratified; Sangam poems are full of material culture and warrior ethic.

58.s: What is the language of the Sangam literature?
58.x: Sangam literature is in old Tamil; the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit, and Pali is the language of the Buddhist canon.

58.s: Which of the following poets of the Sangam age has referred to a Mauryan expedition against a Tamil chieftain?
58.x: The Sangam poet Mamulanar refers to the Mauryas (Vamba Moriyar) advancing into the south against a Tamil chieftain; Avvaiyar and Paranar wrote other poems and Ilango Adigal is post-Sangam.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the chronology of the Sangam corpus?
o: It is generally placed c. 300 BCE–300 CE
It begins around the 3rd century BCE
It extends to about the 3rd century CE
It is generally placed c. 1000–500 BCE

58.s: To which century is the Tamil-Brahmi that supports the early limit of the Sangam age dated?
58.x: Tamil-Brahmi dated to the 3rd century BCE supports the early limit of the c. 300 BCE–300 CE span.

58.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Sangam chronology?
o: The three-Sangam account is traditional, not historical
Pathinenkilkanakku belongs to the earliest Sangam layer
58.x: Pathinenkilkanakku is post-Sangam, like the Tirukkural and the twin epics; the three-Sangam account is traditional.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Aham — Love, personal emotion and nature
58.x: Aham, meaning interior, deals with love, personal emotion and nature. Puram, meaning exterior, concerns war, valour, royal deeds and ethics.

xs: **Aham — love, personal emotion and nature** — option **(3)**.

58.s: What do Puram poems in Sangam poetry mainly deal with?
58.x: Puram (exterior) poems deal with war, valour, royal deeds and ethics; Aham poems deal with love and emotion.

58.s: About how many poems does the Sangam corpus contain?
58.x: The Sangam corpus has about 2,400 poems by several hundred poets, including women.

2. It has about 2,400 poems, including some by women poets.
3. It has no reference to material culture.

58.x: Sangam poems are in old Tamil and number about 2,400, some by women; they are rich in material culture, so statement 3 is wrong.

58.s: Which of the following belongs to the Ettuthogai (eight anthologies)?
58.x: Padirruppattu, on the Chera kings, is one of the Ettuthogai; Pattinappalai, Mullaippattu and Tirumurugarruppadai belong to Pattupattu.

Ettuthogai = **8 anthologies** of **short poems**.
Pattupattu = **10 idylls**, longer poems.

58.s: Which group of Tamil works, the eighteen minor works on ethics, is largely post-Sangam?
58.x: Pathinenkilkanakku (eighteen minor works on ethics) is largely post-Sangam; Ettuthogai and Pattupattu form the older Melkanakku.

58.s: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu poems are divided into aham and which other category?

One of the earliest bodies of **secular** literature in India.
Puram covers **war, valour, deeds of kings, ethics**.

58.s: Pattinappalai of the Pattupattu describes Puhar and which ruler?
58.x: Pattinappalai is a Pattupattu idyll on Puhar and the Chola king Karikala.

58.s: Which works make up the Melkanakku (18 major works)?
58.x: Melkanakku = Ettuthogai (8) + Pattupattu (10) = 18 major works; Pathinenkilkanakku is the 18 minor works.

58.x: Tamil was the language of Sangam literature, while the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit.

58.x: Sangam means an assembly (academy) of Tamil poets held under Pandya patronage; it has nothing to do with the Buddhist Sangha or the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara.

58.x: Tradition places the first Sangam at Then Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram and the third at Madurai, all under Pandya patronage.

Presiding scholars: **Agastya** (First), **Agastya / Tolkappiyar** (Second), **Nakkirar** (Third).

Presiding scholar of the Third Sangam: **Nakkirar**.
⚠ First and Third Sangams at **Madurai**; Second at **Kapatapuram**.

58.x: Of the Second Sangam at Kapatapuram only Tolkappiyam survives; most of the extant corpus belongs to the Third.

58.x: Sangam means a conference of poets or forum of scholars; all three were held under Pandya patronage.

58.x: Tradition says Agastya presided over the First Sangam at Then Madurai, which was later submerged.

58.x: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription says he broke a Tamil confederacy that had existed for 113 years.

58.x: Pliny links spices with the Cheras, pearls with the Pandyas and muslin with the Cholas, and notes the Roman gold drain.

58.x: Pliny's Natural History mentions spices, pearls and muslin from the Tamil kingdoms and the drain of Roman gold.

58.x: Ashoka's Rock Edict II names the Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras and Keralaputras.

The first Gupta capital in the Tamil region
South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation
The exclusive use of Sanskrit in the Pandya country

59.x: Ma'bar was the Arab name for the Pandya kingdom on the Coromandel coast; it does not denote the Pallava, Chola or Hoysala kingdoms.

too many divisions in the social structure.
the absence of vast areas of fertile land.

61.s: The Allahabad Pillar inscription is associated with which one of the following?
61.x: The Allahabad Pillar inscription is Harisena's eulogy of Samudragupta. It stands on an Ashokan pillar, but the inscription it is named for is Samudragupta's.

61.s: The Allahabad Pillar inscription is associated with which one of the following?
61.x: The Allahabad Pillar is associated with Samudragupta through Harisena's prashasti; Ashoka's edicts are also on it, but the famous inscription is the Gupta eulogy.

61.s: Which of the following the pillar inscriptions has recorded the achievements of Samudragupta, who was known as the ‘Napoleon of India’ for his conquests?
61.x: Samudragupta, whom V.A. Smith called the Napoleon of India, has his conquests on the Allahabad Pillar; the Mehrauli Iron Pillar belongs to Chandragupta II.

61.s: Which one of the following statements about Allahabad Prashasti is correct?
o: It clearly present the Gupta empire as the epicentre of a complex web of varied political relationship.
Line 15 of it refers to the capturing a king of the Kota family.
Line 23 refers to Samudragupta violently exterminating a number of kings of Aryavarta.
Line 20 refers to rulers offering tribute, obeying the orders of the Gupta king.
61.x: Upinder Singh reads the prashasti as presenting the Gupta empire as the centre of a complex web of varied political relationships, so (a). The line references in the other options are wrong: the Kota king and the Aryavarta exterminations come in other lines.

61.s: The military conquests of Samudragupta are recorded in which inscription?
61.x: Samudragupta's conquests are recorded in the Allahabad Pillar (Prayaga) prashasti by Harishena (APPSC 2025 key). The Mehrauli pillar concerns Chandragupta II; the Junagadh inscription records Skandagupta's governor repairing the Sudarshana lake; the Nasik prasasti belongs to the Satavahanas.
61.tq: Samudragupta = Allahabad Pillar; Chandragupta II = Mehrauli.
xs: Samudragupta's conquests are in the **Allahabad Pillar inscription** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
**Mehrauli** = Chandragupta II; **Junagadh** = Parnadatta's lake repair under Skandagupta; **Nasik** is not a Gupta record.
xa: Composer **Harishena**; also called **Prayaga-prashasti**.
It sorts opponents into **four groups**: annexed, frontier, southern, distant.
Southern policy: **grahana-moksha-anugraha**.

61.s: The Allahabad Prasasti of Samudragupta mixes prose and verse in which style?
61.x: The Allahabad (Prayaga) Prasasti is a Sanskrit eulogy in the champu style, mixing prose and verse.
xa: Composer: court poet **Harishena**.
It is inscribed on an **Ashokan pillar**.
The same pillar carries **Ashoka's edicts**, the **Queen's edict** and **Jahangir's** inscription.

61.s: Besides Kumaramatya and Mahadandanayaka, which office did Harisena of Samudragupta's court hold?
61.x: Harisena was Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka; he is not to be confused with the later Jain author of the Brihatkatha Kosha.
xa: He composed the **Prayaga prashasti** in **Sanskrit**.
The prashasti is in **champu** style.
Samudragupta's minister was the Buddhist **Vasubandhu**.

61.s: Who shifted the Allahabad Pillar from Kaushambi to Allahabad/Prayagraj?
61.x: Mughal emperor Akbar moved the Ashokan pillar from Kaushambi to the Allahabad (Prayagraj) fort. Jahangir later added his own Persian inscription to it, which is the common trap.

n: The Allahabad Pillar was originally located at Kaushambi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]

xs: **Akbar** shifted the Allahabad Pillar from **Kaushambi** to **Allahabad (Prayagraj)** — option **(2)**.
The pillar was **originally associated** with **Ashoka**, so Ashoka did not move it.
**Jahangir** only added a **Persian inscription**; **Samudragupta's** prashasti was composed on it by **Harisena**.
xa: The pillar also carries the **Queen's Edict** of **Karuvaki**.
The Prashasti is a **Sanskrit** eulogy in **champu** style (prose + verse).
Harisena held the posts **Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika** and **Mahadandanayaka**.
⚠ Not the Jain **Harisena** of the **Brihatkatha Kosha**.

61.s: Harisena's Prayag Prashasti was written in Sanskrit in which script?
61.x: Harisena wrote the Prayag Prashasti in Sanskrit, in Brahmi script, as a panegyric of Samudragupta.
n: Harisena authored the Prayag Prashasti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Prayag Prashasti is written in Sanskrit. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]

Style: mixed **prose + verse** (**champu**).
Harisena was **Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika** and **Mahadandanayaka** at once.

61.s: With reference to the Allahabad pillar, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: The Queen's Edict concerns Karuvaki. Samudragupta's prashasti was by Harisena and Jahangir's inscription is in Persian.
n: The Allahabad Pillar contains an Ashokan inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Allahabad Pillar contains the Queen's Edict of Karuvaki. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]

xa: The pillar was originally at **Kaushambi**; **Akbar** shifted it to **Allahabad**.
Other name: **Prayaga-prashasti**.
Its war glorification contrasts with **Ashoka's** message of **peace** on the same pillar.
Samudragupta's conquests are recorded on the **Allahabad Pillar**, not Mehrauli, Junagadh or Nasik (APPSC 2025).

61.s: The Allahabad Prashasti of Samudragupta has how many lines?
61.x: The Prashasti is a 33-line Sanskrit eulogy in Brahmi.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Harisena of the Allahabad Prashasti?
o: He was the court poet of Samudragupta
He held the office of Sandhivigrahika
He held the office of Kumaramatya
61.x: The Brihatkatha Kosha is by a later Jain author also named Harisena, not Samudragupta's court poet.

61.s: To which queen does the Queen's Edict on the Allahabad Pillar refer?
61.x: The Queen's Edict on the pillar refers to Ashoka's queen Karuvaki.

61.s: During the period of the South Indian Campaign of Samudragupta, who was the ruler of Vengi?

61.s: Devarashtra is identified with which place of Vishakapatnam district?

61.x: Devarashtra, the kingdom of Kubera in the Allahabad Prasasti, is the Yelamanchili area of Visakhapatnam district (NextGen). The old app note placing it at S. Kota (Vizianagaram) is not supported here.

61.s: The Allahabad Pillar Inscription of Samudragupta mentions a conflict between the Guptas and the Vengi king of the Salankayana dynasty. Who is the Salankayana king mentioned in that inscription?
61.x: The Allahabad Prasasti names Hastivarman of Vengi, a Salankayana, among the southern kings; Nandivarman and Chandravarman are other Salankayanas.

61.s:
Consider the following statements:

II. Samudragupta's South Indian conquest did not lead to any permanent annexation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
61.x: Statement I is false: the Saka (Western Kshatrapa) conquest was Chandragupta II's, not Chandragupta I's (one NextGen page wrongly credits Chandragupta I). Statement II is true: the southern kings were captured and reinstated (grahana-moksha-anugraha), so II only.

61.s: Which Pallava king was defeated by Samudra Gupta?
61.x: Samudragupta defeated Vishnugopa of Kanchi, a Pallava; Kubja Vishnuvardhana is the Eastern Chalukya founder of the 7th century.

61.s: What was the name of the ruler of Kosal in Samudragupta's "Prayag Prashasti"?
61.x: The Prayag Prashasti names Mahendra as king of (Dakshina) Kosala, first of the twelve southern kings; Mahendragiri ruled Pishtapura.

61.s: Which of the following records is associated with the Samudragupta period in the Andhra region?
o: The Amaravati record of Gautamiputra Satakarni
The Motupalli charter of the Kakatiyas
61.x: A record belonging to the Samudragupta period is noted at Sankaram in the Visakhapatnam region.
61.tq: Use the regional location clue to identify the relevant inscriptional record.
xs: A Samudragupta-period record exists at **Sankaram** in **Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)**.
The campaign hit **coastal Andhra**.
xa: Andhra kingdoms: **Pishtapura**, **Vengi**, **Avamukta**, **Devarashtra**, **Erandapalle**, **Palakka**.
**Hastivarman of Vengi** was a **Salankayana**.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Samudragupta's campaigns?
o: The southern kingdoms were permanently annexed.
Assam, Nepal and Bengal were frontier rulers who paid tribute.
The Ganga-Yamuna region was directly annexed.
The atavika (forest) kingdoms of central India were subdued.
61.x: The southern rulers were defeated and reinstated as tributaries, not permanently annexed; the other three are correct.
xa: **Distant** kings — **Kushanas, Sakas, Sri Lanka**, SE Asia — accepted suzerainty.
The Prashasti sorts opponents into **four groups**.
**12 kings** of Dakshinapatha were reinstated.

61.s: According to Gupta records, which powers paid homage to the Gupta ruler?
61.x: The Kushanas and Sakas were among the distant powers, with Sri Lanka and South-East Asia, that accepted Samudragupta's suzerainty and paid him homage.

61.s: What was Samudragupta's policy towards the twelve defeated southern kings?
61.x: The twelve southern kings were captured, released and reinstated (grahana-moksha-anugraha); there was no permanent annexation in the south.
xa: The route ran along the **east coast** to **Kanchi**, where Pallava **Vishnugopa** accepted suzerainty.
**Hastivarman** (Salankayana) of **Vengi** and Mahendragiri of **Pishtapura** were among the southern kings.
⚠ **Vishnugupta** is a misprint — the Pallava king is **Vishnugopa**.
North (Aryavarta) rulers were **annexed**; **frontier** kings paid tribute.

61.s: Mahendragiri, one of the southern rulers in Samudragupta's campaign, ruled over which kingdom?
61.x: Mahendragiri was associated with Pishtapura, identified with present-day Pithapuram in the Kakinada region.
61.tq: Test the ruler–ancient place association using the Andhra regional clues.
xs: **Mahendragiri** ruled **Pishtapura** — option **(2)**.
Pishtapura = **Pithapuram, Kakinada**.
**Devarashtra** = Kubera; **Palakka** = Ugrasena; **Erandapalle** = Damana.
xa: Some notes call Pishtapura's king "**Mahendra**"; the prashasti says **Mahendragiri**.

Pishtapura is among the **coastal Andhra** kingdoms hit by the campaign.

61.s: The Allahabad Pillar inscription gives information on the fourth-century Andhra kings of which of the following?
61.x: The inscription is a chief source for information about the fourth-century Andhra regions and rulers of Vengi, Pishtapura, Avamukta and Devarashtra.

xs: The Allahabad pillar is the chief source for Andhra's **4th-century** kings of **Vengi, Pishtapura, Avamukta and Devarashtra** — option **(1)**.
The southern campaign hit **coastal Andhra**.
xa: Other Andhra kingdoms: **Erandapalle** (Damana) and **Palakka** (Ugrasena).
**Hastivarman** of Vengi was a **Salankayana**; **Mahendragiri** ruled **Pishtapura**.
A Samudragupta-period record exists at **Sankaram** (Visakhapatnam).

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Samudragupta:

South: **12 kings** reinstated by **grahana-moksha-anugraha**.
**Meghavarman** of Sri Lanka sent a mission for a monastery at **Bodh Gaya**.

61.s: Which of the following southern rulers of Samudragupta's campaign is correctly matched with his kingdom?

Kosala = **Mahanadi region, Odisha**.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
