61.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of ‘Parama Bhagawat’ was
61.x:
Most books and the UPPSC official key give Chandragupta II, who used 'Parama Bhagavata' widely on coins and inscriptions. The NextGen Rocket Sheet gives Samudragupta, styled so in the Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (whose genuineness is doubted).
Samudragupta is the first Gupta styled Paramabhagavata, in his Nalanda and Gaya copper plates (NextGen Rocket); Chandragupta II used it regularly on coins and inscriptions, which is why some keys give him.

61.s: Which one of the following Gupta rulers is referred to as ‘Lichchhavi-Dauhitra’ (Son of the daughter of the Lichchhavis)?

61.x:

n: Samudragupta was titled Param Bhagavata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Param Bhagavata is a Vaishnavite title. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
The recall association for Samudragupta's Param Bhagavata title is Param Bhagavata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]

61.x: Devaputra was a Kushana title; the others were used by Gupta rulers.

61.s: Which Gupta ruler is mainly known by the title 'Vikramaditya'?
61.x: Chandragupta II took the title Vikramaditya; Skandagupta also used it later, but the title is usually linked with Chandragupta II.

61.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title) - List-II (Gupta ruler)
A. Kaviraja - 1. Chandragupta II
B. Mahendraditya - 2. Samudragupta
C. Maharajadhiraja (first to assume) - 3. Chandragupta I
D. Sakari - 4. Kumaragupta I
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: Samudragupta was Kaviraja, Kumaragupta I was Mahendraditya, Chandragupta I was the first Maharajadhiraja and Chandragupta II was Sakari (Saka-conqueror).

61.s: Who founded Gupta Dynasty?
61.x: Sri Gupta founded the Gupta dynasty; Chandragupta I was the first great king and real founder of the empire.

61.s: The Gupta Era was Started at:
61.x: The Gupta era (319-20 CE) began with the accession of Chandragupta I; Sri Gupta founded the dynasty but not the era.

61.s: Who of the following was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins?
61.x: The first Gupta coins are the gold king-queen (Chandragupta I-Kumaradevi) type; no coins of Sri Gupta or Ghatotkacha are known. Some scholars think Samudragupta struck them to honour his parents.

61.s: Who established Gupta Samvat?
61.x: Chandragupta I started the Gupta Samvat in 319-20 CE, the year of his accession; Chandragupta II and Ghatotkacha did not.

61.s: The Gupta Samvat was founded by
61.x: The Gupta Samvat (319-20 CE) was founded by Chandragupta I and marks his accession.

61.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to attain the title of ‘Maharaja Dhiraja’?
61.x: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta to take the title Maharajadhiraja; Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were only Maharaja.

61.s: Of which metal were most Gupta coins, which reveal royal titles, religion and prosperity, made?
61.x: Gupta coins were mostly gold and depict rulers, deities and rituals.
xa: First Gupta gold coins (**dinaras**): Chandragupta I's **king-queen type**.
Samudragupta's types: **Ashvamedha**, **lyrist**, **standard**, **archer**, **battle-axe**, **tiger-slayer**.
The **lyrist** type is the basis of his title **Kaviraja**.

61.s: Who succeeded Sri Gupta in the early Gupta line?
61.x: The early Gupta succession ran Sri Gupta, Ghatotkacha and then Chandragupta I.

61.s: Which Purana describes the early territory of the Guptas?
61.x: Puranas such as the Vayu Purana describe the early Gupta territory.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the caste origin of the Guptas?
o: They are described as originally Vaishyas
They were later treated as Kshatriyas
A Brahmana origin has been argued from the Dharana gotra
The Junagadh inscription settles their caste origin
61.x: The Junagadh inscription does not settle the question; the Vaishya-to-Kshatriya view and the Dharana gotra argument are both put forward.

61.s: Sri Gupta, the founder of the Gupta line, ruled a small area of which region?
61.x: Sri Gupta ruled a small part of North Bengal and South Bihar.

61.s: Besides Magadha and eastern Uttar Pradesh, which area formed part of the early territory of the Guptas?
61.x: The early Gupta territory was Magadha, Prayag and eastern UP.

61.s: Which Gupta ruler is regarded as the real founder of the Gupta Empire and ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE?
61.x: Chandragupta I, who ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE, is regarded as the real founder of the Gupta Empire.
61.tq: Use direct ruler-identification from the title or role associated with the ruler.
xs: **Chandragupta I (c. 319-335 CE)** was the real founder — option **(4)**.
He was the **first important king** and **first Maharajadhiraja**.
**Ghatotkacha** was only a **Maharaja**; **Samudragupta** and **Chandragupta II** came later.
xa: Capital: **Pataliputra**.
Married **Kumaradevi**, a **Lichchhavi** princess.

61.s: Which ruler came immediately after Samudragupta in the Gupta line?
61.x: Samudragupta was followed by Ramagupta, whom Chandragupta II killed.

61.s:
Arrange the following Gupta rulers in chronological order:
1. Samudragupta
2. Ghatotkacha
3. Chandragupta I
4. Sri Gupta
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
61.x: Sri Gupta founded the line, Ghatotkacha followed, then Chandragupta I and then Samudragupta.

61.s: In which year did the Gupta Era begin?
61.x: The Gupta Era (Gupta Samvat) began in 319–320 CE, the date of Chandragupta I's accession. 240 and 280 CE are the approximate starting dates of Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha.
61.tq: Distinguish the beginning of the era from the approximate reign dates of individual Gupta rulers.
xs: The **Gupta Era (Gupta Samvat)** began in **319–320 CE** — option **(4)**.
It marks **Chandragupta I's accession**.
**240** and **280** are the approximate starts of **Sri Gupta** and **Ghatotkacha**.
xa: Chandragupta I ruled **c. 319-335 CE** — the real founder.
He was the **first Maharajadhiraja**.
He married the **Lichchhavi** princess **Kumaradevi**.

61.s: Which was the capital of Chandragupta I?
61.x: Chandragupta I ruled South Bihar and parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Saketa and Prayaga, with Pataliputra as capital.
xa: He was the **first Maharajadhiraja**.
He issued the first Gupta **gold coins (dinaras)**.
⚠ He did **not** defeat the Sakas — that was **Chandragupta II**.

61.s: The marriage of Chandragupta I with Kumaradevi was significant primarily because it:
o: secured control over the western seaboard
gave the Guptas legitimacy and political strength through the Lichchhavis
ended the Gupta conflict with the Sakas
established matrimonial relations with the Vakatakas
61.x: Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess, and the marriage enhanced Gupta legitimacy, prestige and political power.
61.tq: Identify the political consequence of a dynastic marriage rather than merely recalling the name.
xs: Marriage to **Kumaradevi** gave **legitimacy and political strength through the Lichchhavis** — option **(2)**.
She was a **Lichchhavi** princess (**Nepal**): legitimacy, prestige and power.
xa: The **king-queen type** coins show Chandragupta I + Kumaradevi.
Coins were issued in the joint names of **king, queen and Lichchhavis**.
**Samudragupta** called himself **Lichchhavi-dauhitra**.

61.s: Who issued the first Gupta gold coins of the king-queen type?
61.x: Chandragupta I, who married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, issued the first Gupta gold coins of the king-queen type.
xa: He was the first to adopt **Maharajadhiraja**.
His capital: **Pataliputra**.
Gupta Era: **319-20 CE**.

61.s: Kumaradevi, queen of Chandragupta I, was a princess of which family?
61.x: Kumaradevi was a Lichchhavi princess; the marriage gave the Guptas legitimacy and power.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta I:
1. He defeated the Sakas and issued silver coins.
2. His capital was Pataliputra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
61.x: Chandragupta I ruled from Pataliputra; the Saka victory and silver coins belong to Chandragupta II.

61.s: Which type of Samudragupta's coinage portrays him as a poet and musician?
61.x: The lyrist or veena-player type depicts Samudragupta as a poet-musician and supports the association of the title Kaviraja with him.
61.tq: Match a coin type with the distinctive activity depicted on it.
xs: The **lyrist (veena-player)** type shows him as a **poet-musician** — option **(1)**.
It is the basis of his title **Kaviraja**.
**Ashvamedha** type followed the horse sacrifice; **archer** and **battle-axe** are other types.
xa: Other types: **standard**, **tiger-slayer**.
Samudragupta also: **Prithivyah Pratham Veer**, **Lichchhavi-dauhitra**.
**V.A. Smith** called him the **Napoleon of India**.

61.s: Which one of the following sets contains only coin types associated with Samudragupta?
61.x: Lyrist, Ashvamedha and archer are all types of Samudragupta's coinage. The King-Queen type belongs to Chandragupta I, while the other options combine unrelated descriptions.
61.tq: Test the whole set and reject options containing a coin type of another ruler.
xs: **Lyrist, Ashvamedha and archer** are all Samudragupta's coin types — option **(1)**.
The **King-Queen** type belongs to **Chandragupta I**; **silver** Saka-model coins to **Chandragupta II**.
xa: Other Samudragupta types: **standard**, **battle-axe**, **tiger-slayer**.
Lyrist type shows him playing the **veena**.
Gupta coins are mostly **gold**.

61.s: Samudragupta's Ashvamedha-type coins were issued to:
o: Celebrate his conquests after the horse sacrifice
61.x: The Ashvamedha coins were issued after the horse sacrifice celebrating his conquests.

61.s: Which coin type belongs to Chandragupta I, not to Samudragupta?
61.x: The king-queen type is of Chandragupta I; lyrist, archer and Ashvamedha are Samudragupta's.

61.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title 'Maharajadhiraja'?
61.x: Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used 'Maharaja'; Chandragupta I was the first to assume 'Maharajadhiraja'.
xa: **Vikramaditya** / **Simhavikrama** = **Chandragupta II** (also taken by Skandagupta) — **APPSC-G2 2008**.
**Samudragupta** = **Kaviraja**, **Lichchhavi-dauhitra**.
Common titles: **Parameshvara**, **Paramabhattaraka**.

61.s: The first inscriptional evidence of the Satipratha has been found from –
61.x: The Eran inscription of 510 CE (Bhanugupta's time) records the sati of the wife of commander Goparaja – the first inscriptional evidence of sati; Junagadh, Mandsaur and Sanchi do not.

61.s: The Mandsaur inscription is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Kumaragupta I, feudatory Bandhuvarman and Vatsabhatti
Chandragupta II, Rudrasimha III and Kalidasa
61.x: The Mandsaur record belongs to the period of Kumaragupta I, under the feudatory Bandhuvarman, and was composed by Vatsabhatti. It also refers to a guild of silk-weavers.
61.tq: Start from the distinctive composer–inscription pair and verify the associated ruler.
xs: Mandsaur = **Kumaragupta I**, feudatory **Bandhuvarman**, composer **Vatsabhatti** — option **(1)**.
It refers to a **silk-weavers' guild**.
**Harishena** wrote the Allahabad prasasti; **Virasena** is linked with Udayagiri; **Bhanugupta** with Eran.
xa: Kumaragupta I's title: **Mahendraditya**; queen **Anantadevi**.
**Bhitari** belongs to **Skandagupta**.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** = Chandragupta II.

61.s: Which inscription records the repair of the Sudarshana lake by Parnadatta, the governor of Skandagupta?
61.x: The Junagadh, or Girnar, inscription records that Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake while serving as Skandagupta’s governor.
61.tq: Use the public-works detail to identify the correct inscription.
xs: The **Junagadh (Girnar)** inscription records **Parnadatta's** repair of the **Sudarshana lake** — option **(3)**.
Parnadatta was **Skandagupta's** governor.
**Mehrauli** = Chandragupta II; **Udayagiri** = Virasena; **Bhitari** = Hunas repulsed.
xa: Skandagupta's **Bhitari** record mentions the **Hunas**.
Samudragupta's conquests are **not** in Junagadh but in the **Allahabad Pillar** (**APPSC 2025**).
**Mandsaur** records a silk-weavers' guild.

61.s: Which inscription provides evidence regarding Chandragupta II's conquests in the north-west and Bengal?
61.x: The Mehrauli iron pillar inscription is associated with Chandragupta II and refers to his conquests in the north-west and Bengal.
61.tq: Use the ruler–inscription association to distinguish similar Gupta epigraphic sources.
xs: The **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** ('Chandra') records **Chandragupta II's** conquests in **NW India** and most of **Bengal** — option **(4)**.
The **Allahabad** pillar is Samudragupta's; **Eran** names Lokapala governors; **Bhitari** is Skandagupta's.
xa: **Udayagiri** cave: Chandragupta II's minister **Virasena** records conquests.
Chandragupta II = **Vikramaditya**, **Simhavikrama** (**APPSC-G2 2008**).
Chandragupta II, not Chandragupta I, defeated the **Sakas**.

61.s: The Eran inscription, the first epigraphic evidence of sati, records the sati of the wife of which commander?
61.x: The Eran inscription of 510 AD records that the wife of the commander Goparaja burned herself on his pyre.
n: The Eran Inscription provides the first inscriptional evidence of Sati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The woman associated with the Sati evidence was the wife of the military commander Gopraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Eran Inscription links Sati with 510 AD and Gopraj's wife. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xa: The 510 CE record is **Bhanugupta's**.
Eran names governors called **Lokapala**.
**Bhitari Pillar** — **Skandagupta** and the **Huna** war.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** — king **Chandra** (**Chandragupta II**).

61.s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is correctly associated with which of the following sets of details?
61.x: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar was set up as a Vishnu Dhvaja (standard of Vishnu) on the hill called Vishnupada, so it is dedicated to Vishnu.
61.tq: Recall the deity of the pillar.
n: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is devoted to Vishnu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Mehrauli Iron Pillar was established as a Vishnu Dhvaja. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Mehrauli Iron Pillar is associated with Vishnupada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xs: The **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** is linked with **Vishnu, Vishnu Dhvaja and Vishnupada** — option **(1)**.
It was **devoted to Vishnu**, **established** as a **Vishnu Dhvaja** and **associated** with **Vishnupada**.
It names a king **Chandra**, identified as **Chandragupta II**.
xa: It claims conquests in **NW India** and most of **Bengal**.
**Udayagiri** cave (near **Vidisha**) has a **Varaha** image and **Virasena's** record.
**Bhitari Pillar** — **Skandagupta**, **Huna** war.
Chandragupta II's title **Sakari** = Saka-conqueror.

61.s: Who wrote both the Mudrarakshasa and the Devichandraguptam?
61.x: Vishakhadatta wrote both plays; the Devichandraguptam tells the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi-Chandragupta II story.
xa: Other literary sources: **Narada, Vishnu, Brihaspati, Katyayana smritis** and Kamandaka's **Nitisara**.
**Fa-Hien's** account and **Kalidasa's** works are also Gupta sources.
**Puranas** (e.g. **Vayu**) describe early Gupta territory.
Gupta **coins** were mostly **gold**.

61.s: Who composed the Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta I's time?
61.x: Vatsabhatti composed the Mandsaur inscription; Harisena wrote the Allahabad Prashasti.

61.s: With which minister of Chandragupta II is the Udayagiri cave inscription associated?
61.x: Virasena, minister of Chandragupta II, is linked with the Udayagiri cave record.

61.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
61.x: The Bhitari Pillar records Skandagupta's war with the Hunas; Mehrauli is Chandragupta II, Junagadh is Skandagupta and Eran is Bhanugupta.

61.s: Where does the Mehrauli Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II stand today?
o: In the yard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Delhi
61.x: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar of king Chandra (Chandragupta II) stands in the yard of Delhi's Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

61.s: In which district of Uttar Pradesh is the Bhitari Pillar of Skandagupta located?
61.x: The Bhitari Pillar, recording Skandagupta's war with the Hunas, is in Saidpur tehsil of Ghazipur district.

61.s: The Eran inscription of 510 CE, the first inscriptional evidence of sati, belongs to the reign of which Gupta ruler?
61.x: The Eran record of 510 CE is of Bhanugupta's time; it records the sati of the wife of his commander Goparaja.

61.s: In which present-day state is Eran, the site of the first inscriptional evidence of sati, located?
61.x: Eran is in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh.

61.s: What is the subject of Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa?
61.x: Mudrarakshasa is a political drama on Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya; the Ramagupta story is in Devichandraguptam.

61.s: Which of the following city was not the capital of the Guptas?
61.x: Gupta capitals were Pataliputra, with Ayodhya, Prayaga and Ujjayini (Chandragupta II's second capital) also named; Varanasi was never a Gupta capital.

61.s: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
61.x: A Chinese source records that Meghavarman of Sri Lanka sent a mission to Samudragupta for permission to build a Buddhist monastery at Bodh Gaya.

61.s: Who of the following Chinese pilgrims to India, gave us some information about the first Gupta ruler ?
61.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary /
61.x: I-Tsing (late 7th century) records that Maharaja Sri Gupta built a temple for Chinese pilgrims near Mrigasikhavana – the only Chinese mention of the first Gupta ruler. Fa-Hien named no king and Hiuen Tsang wrote of Harsha.

61.s: Where did Meghavarman of Sri Lanka send a mission to Samudragupta to build a monastery?
61.x: Meghavarman's request to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya is known from a Chinese source.
xa: Meghavarman wanted a **monastery and rest house** at **Bodh Gaya**.
Chandragupta II's sea trade reached **Europe via Egypt**.
Samudragupta's minister: **Vasubandhu**.

62.s: Which Gupta ruler assumed the throne after killing his elder brother?
62.x: Chandragupta II killed his elder brother Ramagupta and married his widow Dhruvadevi (Devichandraguptam). Samudragupta and Skandagupta came to the throne without such a story, and Sri Gupta was the founder.

62.s: The second capital of the Gupta ruler, Chandragupta-II was
62.x: After conquering the Western Kshatrapas, Chandragupta II made Ujjain his second capital. Malwa and Saurashtra are regions, and Mehrauli is the site of his iron pillar.

62.s: After conquering the Shakas, which of the following metal coins were introduced by Chandragupta II?
62.x: After the Saka conquest Chandragupta II issued silver coins on the Western Kshatrapa model for the conquered west. The Guptas' usual gold coins existed before, so gold is the tempting wrong option.

62.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to issue silver coins?
62.x: Chandragupta II was the first Gupta to issue silver coins, copying Western Kshatrapa coins after the Saka conquest. NextGen 03 p.2 wrongly credits Chandragupta I, whose coins were gold (king-queen type).

62.s: Who is known as ‘Saka-conqueror’?
62.x: Chandragupta II ended Western Kshatrapa (Saka) rule by defeating Rudrasimha III and took the title Sakari, 'Saka-conqueror'. Samudragupta only received homage from the Sakas.

62.s: Who among the following Gupta Kings had another name Devagupta ?
62.x: Devagupta (also Devaraja, Devashri) was another name of Chandragupta II, known from Sanchi and Vakataka records. Samudragupta and Kumaragupta did not bear it.

62.s:
With reference to Chandragupta – II, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The strongest evidence in the context of Saka Victory is the silver coins of this King.
2. The weight of these coins used to be about 33 grains.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
62.x: Chandragupta II's silver coins, copied from the Western Kshatrapas, are the strongest evidence of his Saka victory, and they weigh about 30-33 grains like the Saka drachms, so both statements are right.

62.s: Fa-hien (Faxian), the Chinese pilgrim, travelled to India during the reign of
62.x: Fa-hien was in India c. 399-412 CE, in the reign of Chandragupta II. Samudragupta ruled before him and Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta after.

62.s: In which dynasty did Chandragupta II marry his daughter Prabhavati and strengthen his position?
62.x: Chandragupta II married his daughter Prabhavati to the Vakataka Rudrasena II and, through her regency, controlled the Vakataka kingdom. The Lichchhavi marriage was Chandragupta I's; the Naga link was his own marriage to Kuberanaga.

62.s: The famous Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of -:
62.x: Fa-hien came to India c. 399-412 CE, within the reign of Chandragupta II (c. 380-415). Chandragupta I and Srigupta were too early and Ramagupta's reign was brief.

62.s: Fa-hien (Faxian), the Chinese pilgrim, travelled to India during the reign of
62.x: Fa-hien travelled in India c. 399-412 CE, in the reign of Chandragupta II, though he never named the king. Samudragupta, Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta do not fit those dates.

62.s: Prabhavati Gupta was the ruler of
62.x: Prabhavati Gupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, was the Vakataka queen of Rudrasena II and ruled the Vakataka kingdom as regent. She was born a Gupta but ruled the Vakatakas.

62.s: What was Chandragupta-II also known as?
62.x: Chandragupta II was known as Vikramaditya, a title linked with his victory over the Sakas. Samudragupta and Skandagupta are other rulers, not his titles.

62.s: Which Chinese pilgrim travelled in India during the reign of Chandragupta II?
62.x: Fa-Hien travelled in Chandragupta II's empire, though he never named the king; Xuan Zang and I-Qing came in the 7th century.

62.s: Which city became the second capital of Chandragupta II?
62.x: Ujjain became Chandragupta II's second capital after the Saka conquest.

62.s: To which Vakataka prince did Chandragupta II give his daughter Prabhavatigupta in marriage?
62.x: Prabhavatigupta married the Vakataka prince Rudrasena II, giving an ally for the Saka war.

62.s: Which title did Chandragupta II take after his victory over the Western Kshatrapas?
62.x: Chandragupta II defeated the Sakas and took the title Sakari.

62.s: Whom did Chandragupta II kill before marrying Dhruvadevi?
62.x: Chandragupta II killed Ramagupta and married Dhruvadevi.

62.s: Kuberanaga was the queen of which Gupta ruler?
62.x: Kuberanaga was the queen of Chandragupta II; Kumaradevi, Duttadevi and Anantadevi were queens of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Kumaragupta I.
xa: Chandragupta II also married **Dhruvadevi** after killing **Ramagupta**.
Exam angle: king-queen matching (**UPPSC 2019**).
Kumaradevi was a **Lichchhavi** princess.

62.s: Which Gupta ruler came immediately before Chandragupta II?
62.x: The order is Ramagupta, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta; Ramagupta's brief reign preceded Chandragupta II.

62.s: The title 'Vikramaditya' was used by which pair of Gupta rulers?
62.x: The title Vikramaditya was used by both Chandragupta II and Skandagupta. When a question asks for the principal Gupta ruler associated with Vikramaditya, it commonly refers to Chandragupta II, but both rulers used the title.
62.tq: Separate a shared title from the ruler most commonly associated with it.
xs: **Vikramaditya** was used by both **Chandragupta II and Skandagupta** — option **(4)**.
⚠ When one ruler is asked, the question usually wants **Chandragupta II** (APPSC-G2 **2008**).
**Kumaragupta I's** titles were **Shakraditya** and **Mahendraditya**.
xa: Chandragupta II's other title: **Simhavikrama**; other names **Devagupta / Devaraja**.
Skandagupta took the title after **repulsing the Hunas**.
Founder **Sri Gupta** bore the title **"Maharaja"**.

62.s: Which of the following gives the correct chronological order of the Gupta rulers?
o: Ramagupta - Samudragupta - Chandragupta II - Kumaragupta I
Samudragupta - Chandragupta II - Ramagupta - Kumaragupta I
Samudragupta - Ramagupta - Chandragupta II - Kumaragupta I
Samudragupta - Ramagupta - Kumaragupta I - Chandragupta II
62.x: Ramagupta briefly ruled after Samudragupta; Chandragupta II killed him and was followed by Kumaragupta I.

62.s: Chandragupta II's title Vikramaditya is linked with his victory over which people?
62.x: Chandragupta II took the title Vikramaditya, linked with his victory over the Sakas.
n: Chandragupta II is associated with Vikramaditya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Chandragupta II is associated with the Saka conquest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Chandragupta II is associated with Fa-Hien. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xa: Fa-Hien **never named the king** — his focus was Buddhism.
**Navaratnas** tradition: **Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Dhanvantari, Varahamihira**, Vararuchi and others.
⚠ Fa-Hien was a **pilgrim**, not a member of the court.
He took the throne **after killing his elder brother Ramagupta** (Devichandraguptam).

62.s: By defeating which Saka ruler did Chandragupta II annex western Malwa and Gujarat?
62.x: Chandragupta II defeated Rudrasimha III, annexed western Malwa and Gujarat and made Ujjain his second capital.
xa: The silver coins weighed about **33 grains** (MPPSC 2023, UPPSC 2022 keys).
The **Udayagiri cave inscription of Virasena** records his campaign.
Rudrasimha III was the **last Saka ruler**; Chandragupta II took the title **Sakari**.
⚠ Crediting **Chandragupta I** with the first silver coins and Saka victory is wrong.

62.s: Which Vakataka ruler did Chandragupta II's daughter Prabhavati Gupta marry?
62.x: Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II; the alliance extended Gupta influence into the Deccan without direct annexation.
xa: The **Vakatakas** (northern Maharashtra, **Vidarbha**) were **Brahmins**, successors of the **Satavahanas** and contemporaries of the Guptas.
He also married **Kuberanaga**, a **Naga** princess, and **Dhruvadevi** after killing Ramagupta.
Vakataka **Harishena** patronised **Ajanta**.

62.s: The title ‘Simhavikrama’ of Chandragupta II is particularly associated with which type of coin?
62.x: Chandragupta II issued lion-slayer coins and used the title Simhavikrama. His father is associated with tiger-slayer coins.
62.tq: Discriminate between the lion-slayer and tiger-slayer coin types.
xs: The title **Simhavikrama** goes with Chandragupta II's **lion-slayer** coins — option **(2)**.
**Tiger-slayer** coins belong to his father (**Samudragupta**), not to him.
xa: His other title: **Vikramaditya**.
His **silver coins** (about **33 grains**) were modelled on **Saka** silver coins.
⚠ Kumaragupta I coins = **Kartikeya** + peacock; Skandagupta coins = **Garuda** + **Lakshmi**.

62.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harishena — minister of Chandragupta II responsible for Udayagiri conquests
62.x: Harishena was the court poet of Samudragupta and composed the Allahabad Prashasti. Virasena, not Harishena, was the minister associated with the Udayagiri inscription and conquests of Chandragupta II.
62.tq: Find the wrong person–office association among otherwise familiar Gupta court figures.
xs: **Harishena — minister for Udayagiri conquests** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**; the **Udayagiri cave inscription** belongs to **Virasena**.
In this topic **Harishena** is the **Vakataka** king who patronised **Ajanta**.
**Vararuchi** wrote **Prakrit Prakasha**; **Amarasimha** and **Kalidasa** are among the **Navaratnas** — all correctly matched.
xa: Other Navaratnas: **Dhanvantari, Varahamihira, Shanku, Ghatakarpara, Kshapanaka, Vetalabhatta**.
⚠ Trap: **Fa-Hien** listed as a court member — he was a **pilgrim**, not a courtier.
Fa-Hien visited India in Chandragupta II's reign, **c. 399–414 CE** (UPSC **2025** key).

62.s: The Udayagiri cave inscription recording the Saka campaign of Chandragupta II is associated with which person?
62.x: The Udayagiri cave inscription of Virasena records the campaign of Chandragupta II against the Sakas.
62.tq: Use inscription–author association rather than ruler recall alone.
xs: The **Udayagiri cave inscription** recording the Saka campaign is that of **Virasena** — option **(2)**.
**Harishena** in this topic is the **Vakataka** patron of **Ajanta**; **Bandhuvarman** appears in the **Mandsaur prashasti** with Kumaragupta I.
xa: The campaign defeated **Rudrasimha III** and annexed **western Malwa and Gujarat**.
The **Mehrauli iron pillar** claims north-west India and **Bengal**.
Saka-model **silver coins** are the **strongest evidence** of the Saka victory.

62.s: What was the approximate weight of the Saka-model silver coins of Chandragupta II?
62.x: The Saka-model silver coins of Chandragupta II weighed approximately 33 grains.
62.tq: Test the precise quantitative detail with close numerical distractors.
xs: The Saka-model **silver coins** of Chandragupta II weighed about **33 grains** — option **(3)**.
They were issued **after the Saka conquest** for the new region (MPPSC **2023**, UPPSC **2022** keys).
xa: They are the **strongest evidence** of his victory over **Rudrasimha III**.
⚠ The Saka-model coins were **silver**, not gold.
His gold coins include the **lion-slayer** type (title **Simhavikrama**).

62.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the traditional Navaratnas of Chandragupta II?
62.x: Fa-Hien was a visiting Buddhist pilgrim, not one of the traditional Navaratnas. Kalidasa, Amarasimha and Varahamihira are included in the traditional list.
62.tq: Find the outsider in a well-known named list.
xs: **Fa-Hien** is not a Navaratna — option **(2)**; he was a **Buddhist pilgrim**, not a courtier.
**Varahamihira, Kalidasa, Amarasimha** are all in the traditional **nine gems**.
xa: Full list: **Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Dhanvantari, Varahamihira, Vararuchi, Shanku, Ghatakarpara, Kshapanaka, Vetalabhatta**.
**Vararuchi** wrote **Prakrit Prakasha**.
Fa-Hien visited **c. 399–414 CE** and never named the king.

62.s: With reference to the marriage alliances of Chandragupta II, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Naga alliance – Prabhavati married Rudrasena II
Vakataka alliance – Prabhavati married Rudrasena II
62.x: His daughter Prabhavati married the Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II. Kuberanaga was a Naga princess, and Dhruvadevi was married after Ramagupta's killing.
xa: The Vakataka marriage gave **indirect control over the Vakataka kingdom**.
The Ramagupta story comes from **Devichandraguptam** of **Vishakhadatta**.
Ramagupta had agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi to a **Saka** king.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about Fa-Hien:
1. He was a Buddhist pilgrim whose focus was Buddhism.
2. He explicitly named Chandragupta II as the reigning king.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
62.x: Fa-Hien was a Buddhist pilgrim and did not name the reigning king, as his concern was Buddhism rather than political history.
xa: UPSC **2025** key: Fa-Hien visited during Chandragupta II's reign.
The **Navaratnas** included **Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Varahamihira**, Vararuchi and others.
Chandragupta II made **Ujjain** his second capital.

62.s: In the Ramagupta episode, which queen did Ramagupta agree to surrender to a Saka king?
62.x: Ramagupta agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi; Chandragupta II killed the Saka king and Ramagupta and married her.
xa: Source: **Devichandraguptam** of **Vishakhadatta**.
BPSC **2022** key: Chandragupta II took the throne after killing his elder brother.
Ramagupta's reign is listed as **brief and disputed**.

62.s: The Ramagupta episode is narrated in which work?
62.x: Vishakhadatta's Devichandraguptam narrates the Ramagupta–Dhruvadevi episode.

62.s: During which period did Fa-Hien visit India?
62.x: Fa-Hien came c. 399–412 CE during Chandragupta II's reign.

62.s: From which records is Chandragupta II's title 'Devagupta' known?
62.x: The name Devagupta appears in the Sanchi and Vakataka inscriptions.

62.s: Besides Devaraja, by which other name was Chandragupta II known?
62.x: Chandragupta II was also called Devagupta and Devaraja; Baladitya was Narasimhagupta.
xa: His titles: **Vikramaditya** and **Simhavikrama**.
He took the throne **after killing his elder brother Ramagupta** (BPSC **2022** key).
Kumaragupta I's titles: **Shakraditya** and **Mahendraditya**.

62.s: Which of the following was a traditional Navaratna of Chandragupta II's court?
62.x: Amarasimha was one of the Navaratnas; Fa-Hien was a pilgrim, not a Navaratna.

62.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prabhavati Gupta ruled the Vakataka kingdom as regent after the death of Rudrasena II.
2. Chandragupta II annexed the Vakataka kingdom to the Gupta empire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: Prabhavati Gupta ruled as regent, giving Gupta influence in the Deccan without annexation.

62.s: The Gupta emperor who defeated the ‘Hunas’ was?
62.x: Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas twice. Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and Ramagupta ruled before the Huna attacks.

62.s: Who among the following Gupta rulers defeated Hunas?
62.x: Skandagupta defeated the Hunas. Kumaragupta faced only the first attack late in his reign, and it was prince Skandagupta who repulsed it.

62.s: Who amongst the following had defeated Huna ruler Mihirakula?
62.x: The Huna king Mihirakula was defeated by the Aulikara king Yashodharman of Malwa (c. 528 CE). Budhagupta, Shashanka and Prabhakaravardhana did not defeat him.

62.s: The Hunas invaded India during the reign of :
62.x: The Huna invasion fell in the reign of Skandagupta, who fought them successfully. Under Kumaragupta I they only attempted an attack, and Budhagupta came later.

62.s: Which dynasty was distracted the most by the Hunas invasion?
62.x: The Huna invasions most troubled the Guptas and hastened their decline. The Mauryas, Kushans and Shungas had passed before the Hunas came.

62.s: Who among the following Gupta rulers conquered Hunas?
62.x: Skandagupta defeated the Hunas, as his Bhitari pillar records. Chandragupta II and Kumaragupta I came earlier, and Bhanugupta was a later king.

62.s: Which one of the following Gupta kings had to face the first Huna invasion?
62.x:
Most books and keys: Skandagupta. Strictly: the first Huna attack came at the end of Kumaragupta I's reign and was repulsed by prince Skandagupta (NextGen Indian History 03 p.5; PMF 03 p.81).
Skandagupta is the king who faced the first real Huna invasion and defeated them. Budhagupta and Purugupta were later, and Kumaragupta I saw only the early attempt at the end of his reign.

62.s: Who among the following had defeated Huna ruler Mihirakula?
62.x: Yashodharman, the Aulikara king of Mandsaur, defeated the Huna Mihirakula in c. 528 CE. Budhagupta, Shashanka and Prabhakaravardhana are not credited with it.

62.s: Tormana was from the racial group of –
62.x: Toramana was a Huna king, father of Mihirakula, who led the second Huna invasion. The Sakas (Scythians) and Yuezhi (Kushanas) were earlier peoples.

62.s: From which inscription is it known that Skandagupta defeated Hunas?
62.x: The Bhitari pillar (Ghazipur) records Skandagupta's victories over the Pushyamitras and Hunas. Allahabad is Samudragupta's, Mandsaur Kumaragupta's and Udayagiri Chandragupta II's.

62.s: Who is the author of the Sondani inscription of Yashodharman?
62.x: Yashodharman's Sondani pillar inscription was composed by Vasula. Ravikirti wrote Pulakeshin II's Aihole inscription.

62.s: Which of the following features is depicted on Skandagupta’s gold coins?
o: A ship, a wheel and a seated Buddha
A tiger, a horse and a sacrificial altar
A bow and arrow, the Garuda standard and Lakshmi
A lion, a trident and Nandi
62.x: Skandagupta’s gold coins depict him with a bow and arrow, the Garuda standard and Lakshmi.
62.tq: Recall the distinctive iconography of a ruler’s coinage.
xs: Skandagupta's gold coins show **bow and arrow, the Garuda standard and Lakshmi** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Don't confuse with **Kumaragupta I** coins: **Kartikeya** + king feeding a **peacock**.
xa: Chandragupta II issued **lion-slayer** coins; his father the **tiger-slayer** type.
Later Gupta gold coins had **less gold, more alloy** — debasement.
**No Gupta coins or inscriptions** appear in western Malwa and Saurashtra after Skandagupta.

62.s: The Bhitari pillar inscription in Ghazipur (Uttar Pradesh) records the victories of which Gupta ruler over the Pushyamitras and the Hunas?
62.x: The Bhitari pillar records Skandagupta's victories over the Pushyamitras and the Hunas; he is the Gupta ruler who defeated the Hunas (UPPSC 2015). The first Huna attack came late in Kumaragupta I's reign, but it was Prince Skandagupta who repulsed it; Chandragupta II defeated the Sakas; Toramana's advance came under Budhagupta and later rulers.
xs: The **Bhitari pillar** (Ghazipur, UP) records **Skandagupta's** victories over the **Pushyamitras** and **Hunas** — option **(2)**.
The first Huna attack came late in **Kumaragupta I's** reign but was repulsed by **prince Skandagupta**.
**Chandragupta II** beat the **Sakas**; **Toramana** advanced under **Budhagupta** and after.
xa: UPPSC **2014**: Bhitari pillar = Skandagupta's victory over the Hunas.
He repulsed the Hunas **twice** and took the title **Vikramaditya**.
The **Eran boar** records **Toramana's** first regnal year; the **Mandasor pillars** record Yashodharman's defeat of **Mihirakula**.

62.s: Which institutional change is associated with Skandagupta’s reign?
o: Governors became hereditary feudatories as central control weakened.
The Gupta Empire became a federation of independent republics immediately.
Provincial offices were transferred exclusively to Buddhist monasteries.
Governors were abolished and all provinces were directly administered from Pataliputra.
62.x: Central control weakened under Skandagupta, and governors increasingly became hereditary feudatories.
62.tq: Infer administrative decentralisation from the change in provincial offices.
xs: Under Skandagupta **central control weakened** and **governors became hereditary feudatories** — option **(1)**.
This fed the feudatory cause of decline: land grants + **hereditary governors** created feudatories.
xa: **Feudatories broke away**: Yashodharman; Bihar, Bengal, MP, **Valabhi**, Gujarat, western Malwa.
Gupta administration rested on feudatories, unlike the **centralised Mauryas**.
**Weak successors** after Skandagupta led to the last ruler **Vishnugupta** (**c. 540–550 CE**).

62.s: Which Gupta ruler's governor Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake, as per the Junagadh inscription?
62.x: The Junagadh inscription records Skandagupta's governor Parnadatta repairing the Sudarshana lake.

62.s: Who repelled the first Huna attack on the Gupta Empire?
62.x: Prince Skandagupta repelled the first Huna attack, which took place during the reign of Kumaragupta I.
62.tq: Discriminate between the attacked ruler and the military defender.
xs: **Prince Skandagupta** repelled the **first Huna attack**, late in **Kumaragupta I's** reign — option **(2)**.
**Yashodharman** and **Narasimhagupta Baladitya** defeated the later leader **Mihirakula**.
**Rudrasimha III** was the **Saka** ruler defeated by Chandragupta II.
xa: The Hunas were **Hephthalites / White Huns** from Central Asia via the **Oxus** valley.
They occupied **Gandhara** in the mid-5th century.
Exam angle (UPPSC **2016**): Kumaragupta I = first attack; Skandagupta = repulsed; Yashodharman = defeated Mihirakula.

62.s: By what other name were the Hunas who entered India in the mid-fifth century known?
62.x: The Hunas were Hephthalites, also called White Huns. They came from Central Asia through the Oxus valley.
62.tq: Distinguish closely associated Central Asian peoples by their alternative names.
xs: The Hunas were the **Hephthalites / White Huns** — option **(4)**.
They came from **Central Asia** via the **Oxus** valley and occupied **Gandhara** in the mid-5th century.
xa: First attack: late **Kumaragupta I**, repulsed by prince **Skandagupta**.
Leaders: **Toramana** and his son **Mihirakula**.
**By 485 CE** Hunas held Punjab, Rajasthan, Kashmir, eastern Malwa, central India.

62.s: To which year are Yashodharman's victory pillars at Sondani near Mandasor generally dated?
62.x: Yashodharman's victory pillars at Sondani are dated to approximately 532 CE. They commemorate his victory over Mihirakula.
62.tq: Separate the date of Yashodharman's victory from the earlier Bilsad, silk-weaver and Eran dates.
xs: Yashodharman's victory pillars at **Mandasor (Sondani)** date to **c. 532 CE** — option **(4)**.
**415 CE** is Kumaragupta I's **Bilsad** inscription; **473** is the silk weavers' migration; **510 CE** is the **Eran** sati record.
⚠ Trap: some notes misread this as "**532 victory pillars**".
xa: The pillars commemorate his defeat of **Mihirakula**.
He was a Gupta **feudatory in Malwa**, of the **Aulikaras** of Mandsaur.
His victory **did not revive** the Gupta Empire.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about Mihirakula:
1. He was the father of Toramana.
2. He persecuted Buddhists.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
62.x: Mihirakula was the son, not the father, of Toramana, and was a tyrant and iconoclast who persecuted Buddhists.
xa: He was defeated by **Yashodharman of Malwa**, **Narasimhagupta Baladitya** and the **Maukharis**.
Mihirakula is dated **c. 515 CE**.
Yashodharman's **Mandasor pillars** record his defeat of Mihirakula.

62.s: Which inference most accurately follows from Yashodharman's victory over Mihirakula?
o: It brought Malwa permanently under direct Gupta administration.
It demonstrated the rise of a regional power and further weakened Gupta authority.
It ended the process of regionalisation in northern India.
It immediately restored the Gupta Empire to its former extent.
62.x: Yashodharman's victory did not revive the Gupta Empire; his own rise as a regional power undermined Gupta authority and reflected the wider process of political fragmentation.
62.tq: Distinguish the immediate military success from its broader political consequence.
xs: Yashodharman's victory showed the **rise of a regional power** and **further weakened Gupta authority** — option **(2)**.
The notes say his victory over the Hunas **did not revive the empire**.
xa: **Feudatories broke away**: Yashodharman; Bihar, Bengal, MP, Valabhi, Gujarat, western Malwa.
Rise of **Maukharis, Maitrakas, Later Guptas, Pushyabhutis** followed.
The break-up marks the move from a **single empire → regional kingdoms** + feudal order.

62.s: Which Huna leader led the second Huna invasion and conquered up to Eran?
62.x: Toramana led the second invasion and reached Eran; Mihirakula was his son.

62.s: During whose reign did the Huna leader Mihirakula invade?
62.x: Mihirakula (c. 515) attacked during Narasimhagupta's reign.

62.s: During whose reign did the first Huna attack on the Gupta Empire come?
62.x: The first attack came late in Kumaragupta I's reign and was checked by prince Skandagupta.

62.s: In which year did Yashodharman defeat Mihirakula?
62.x: Yashodharman defeated Mihirakula in 528 CE; his Sondani pillars are c. 532 CE.

62.s: Yashodharman of Mandasor belonged to which family?
62.x: Yashodharman was an Aulikara king of Malwa.

62.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The first Huna invasion occurred late in Kumaragupta I's reign.
Toramana led the second Huna invasion.
Skandagupta defeated the Hunas associated with the first Huna invasion.
62.x: Option C is incorrect: Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman of Malwa (and Narasimhagupta Baladitya), not Skandagupta. The first Huna attack came late in Kumaragupta I's reign and was checked by prince Skandagupta; Toramana led the second.
62.tq: Recall which ruler defeated each Huna leader.
n: The first Huna invasion occurred during Skandagupta's reign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]
Skandagupta defeated the Hunas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]
Toramana led the second Huna invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]
Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]

62.s: Which of the following inscription–ruler pairs is correctly matched?
62.x: The Gwalior inscription shows Mihirakula's rule over Gwalior. The Sondani (Mandasor) pillars record Yashodharman's defeat of Mihirakula, and the Maukhari copper seal belongs to Sarvavarman, not Yashodharman.
n: The Gwalior Inscription records the territory of Mihirakula. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Sondani Inscription is associated with Yashodharman. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Maukhari Copper-Seal is associated with Sarvavarman. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Devapala was the ruler associated with the Chausath Yogini Temple Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]

62.s: What does the Eran boar inscription record?
o: Huna rule over Eran in the first regnal year of Toramana
The victory of Yashodharman over Mihirakula
The migration of silk weavers from Gujarat to Malwa
The foundation of Nalanda by Kumaragupta I
62.x: The Eran boar inscription was built in Toramana's first regnal year and records Huna rule over Eran.
62.tq: Link a monument with the exact Huna ruler and political circumstance named in the record.
xs: The **Eran boar (Varaha)** inscription records **Huna rule over Eran** in **Toramana's first regnal year** — option **(1)**.
Yashodharman's victory is on the **Mandasor pillars**; the **silk weavers'** guild is in the **Mandsaur prashasti**.
xa: Toramana conquered western India up to **Eran** (near Bhopal).
⚠ A separate **Eran** inscription (**510 CE**) of Goparaja is the **earliest sati** record.
The **Bhitari pillar** records **Skandagupta's** victory over the Hunas.

62.s: Which inscription is a record of the Huna ruler Mihirakula?
62.x: The Gwalior inscription belongs to Mihirakula's reign and shows his rule included Gwalior. Bhitari is Skandagupta's, the Eran boar inscription is from Toramana's first year, and Junagadh is Skandagupta's governor's.

62.s: Arrange the following rulers of Gupta dynasty in chronological order and select the correct answer: 23. W (ii) Skandagupta (i) Chandragupta II am (iii) Samudragupta (iv) Kumaragupta I tec
62.x: The order is Samudragupta (iii), Chandragupta II (i), Kumaragupta I (iv), Skandagupta (ii), i.e. (iii), (i), (iv), (ii).

62.s: Gupta dynasty ruled during :
62.x: Counting from Chandragupta I's Gupta era (319-20 CE), the imperial Guptas ruled till about 500 (the line lingered to c. 550), so 319-500 AD is the best option. The others are far too short or belong to other dynasties.

62.s: The last recognised king of the Gupta line was ……… .
62.x: Vishnugupta (c. 540-550 CE) was the last recognised ruler of the Gupta line. Samudragupta was an early Gupta, and Bimbisara and Ashoka were not Guptas.

62.s: Mandsaur – Prashasti presents the details of the achievements of which ruler?
62.x: The Mandsaur (Dashpur) prashasti by Vatsabhatti records the reign of Kumaragupta I and his governor Bandhuvarman. Skandagupta's record is the Bhitari pillar.

62.s: Who was the founder of Nalanda University?
62.x: Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya), c. 450 CE. Dharmapala, the Pala king, founded Vikramashila; Chandragupta II and Pushyagupta did not found it.

62.s: Who was founder of Nalanda University?
62.x: Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I (c. 450 CE). Chandragupta Vikramaditya, Dharmapala (Vikramashila) and Pushyagupta are not its founders.

62.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
62.x: Samudragupta ruled c. 335–375 CE. Ghatotkacha ruled c. 280–319 CE, Chandragupta I 319–335 CE and Chandragupta II c. 380–415 CE, so the other pairs are wrong.
62.tq: Compare adjacent Gupta date ranges and reject shifted reign periods.

62.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty and bore the title ‘Maharaja’?
62.x: Sri Gupta, who ruled approximately from 240 to 280 CE, is regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty and bore the title ‘Maharaja’.
xs: **Sri Gupta** (**c. 240–280 CE**) was the founder of the Gupta dynasty and bore the title **"Maharaja"** — option **(4)**.
**Ghatotkacha** was his successor (**c. 280–319 CE**), not the founder.
**Chandragupta I** (**c. 319–335 CE**) and **Samudragupta** (**c. 335–375 CE**) came later.
xa: The **Gupta Era** (**319–20**) is linked to **Chandragupta I**.
The last ruler of the main line was **Vishnugupta** (**c. 540–550 CE**).
Exam order: **Samudragupta → Chandragupta II → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta** (APPSC-G1 **2018**).

62.s: Who was the last ruler of the main Gupta line?
62.x: Vishnugupta, ruling c. 540-550 CE, was the last of the main Gupta line.
xa: **Weak successors** after **Skandagupta** are a listed cause of Gupta decline.
**Toramana** advanced under **Budhagupta** and after; **Mihirakula** is linked to **Narasimhagupta's** reign.
⚠ The **Later Guptas** of **Magadha** were a separate successor power, distinct from the later kings of the main line.

62.s: Who started the Gupta era (319-20 CE)?
62.x: Chandragupta I started the Gupta era in 319-20 CE.
n: Chandragupta I was called Maharajadhiraja. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #96 · pp 179-181]
Samudragupta was known as the Napoleon of India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #96 · pp 179-181]
Chandragupta II was known as Vikramaditya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #96 · pp 179-181]
Chandragupta II was known as Sakari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #96 · pp 179-181]
Chandragupta II was known as the Saka Conqueror. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #96 · pp 179-181]
xa: Chandragupta I was the first **Maharajadhiraja**.
Chandragupta II was also **Devagupta, Devaraja, Devashri**.
Kumaragupta I was also **Shakraditya** and founded **Nalanda**.
Order: **Samudragupta → Chandragupta II → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta** (APPSC-G1 2018).

62.s: Besides Mahendraditya, which title did Kumaragupta I bear?
62.x: Kumaragupta I was Shakraditya and Mahendraditya; Vikramaditya belongs to Chandragupta II and Skandagupta.
xa: Kumaragupta I founded **Nalanda** University.
He was a devotee of **Kartikeya** and performed the **ashvamedha**.
His gold coins show **Kartikeya** + the king **feeding a peacock**.

62.s: Which title did Narasimhagupta, a later ruler of the main Gupta line, bear?
62.x: Narasimhagupta was called Baladitya.

62.s: During which period did Chandragupta II rule?
62.x: Chandragupta II ruled c. 380–415 CE; 415–455 CE is Kumaragupta I.

62.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gupta rulers:
1. Skandagupta is regarded as the last great Gupta ruler.
2. Vishnugupta ruled c. 540–550 CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: Both are correct: Skandagupta was the last great Gupta, and the last ruler Vishnugupta ruled c. 540–550 CE.

62.s: Which Mauryan ruler extended Mauryan power into the Deccan?
62.x: Bindusara pushed Mauryan power into the Deccan; Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire.

64.s: On which coast did the Gupta-period ports Kalyan and Chaul lie?

64.s: Where was the port of Tamralipti located?
64.x: Tamralipti (Tamluk) in Bengal was the chief port for North Indian trade with South-East Asia.

64.s: Under which Andhra dynasty did the ports of Motupalli and Koduru serve trade with South-East Asia?
64.x: Motupalli and Koduru served South-East Asian trade under the Vishnukundins.

64.s: By which name was Ghantasala, a port in Krishna district, known to classical writers?
64.x: Ghantasala was Kontakossylla; Kadura was Koddura.

64.s: Of which metal was the Gupta rupaka made?

64.s:
Consider the following statements about Gupta coinage:

2. Later dinaras contained less gold and more alloy.
3. Silver rupakas were issued after the defeat of the Kushanas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Dinaras were the most numerous and declined in purity; rupakas followed the defeat of the Western Satraps, not the Kushanas.

64.s: In Gupta-period sources, what does 'Chinansuka' refer to?

64.s:

64.x: Ghantasala and Kadura in Krishna district were Andhra's east-coast ports, and the Satavahana weavers' guild was Kolika Shreni.

**Motupalli and Koduru** served Southeast Asian trade under the **Vishnukundins**.

64.s:

64.x: The decline of sites like Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti and Kaushambi and the paucity of coins are true (b, c). The decline was marked from the 6th-7th century, not only by the mid-9th, so a is false.

64.s: The decline of trade and commerce in North India between 7th and 10th centuries was partly due to the

64.s: The gradual decline of towns was an important feature of which period?
64.x: The gradual decline of towns is a feature of the Gupta period: Mathura, Hastinapur, Shravasti declined and Pataliputra became a village by Hiuen-Tsang's time. The other eras are not marked by it.

64.s: From the third century AD when the Huna invasion ended the Roman Empire, the Indian merchants relied more and more on the :
64.x: With the Roman market lost, Indian merchants turned more to South-East Asian trade. African, West European and Middle Eastern trade did not replace it.

64.s: The gradual decline of towns was a important feature of which period?
64.x: The gradual decline of towns is a recognised feature of the Gupta period, with Mathura, Hastinapur and Kaushambi declining. The Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Satavahana eras are not characterised this way.

64.s: Vishti and feudal obligations on peasants form the basis of which interpretation of the Gupta economy?
64.x: Peasant obligations, including vishti or forced labour, form the basis of the urban decay and feudalism critique of the Gupta economy.
xa: **Vishti** = forced labour.
Declining towns: **Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, Kaushambi**.
**c. 750–1000 CE** = stagnation in North India.

64.s: The decline in Indian silk exports to the Eastern Roman Empire was principally associated with which development?
o: The Sassanids prohibited the silk trade.
The Gupta rulers banned the export of silk.
The Romans learnt to rear silkworms.
64.x: Indian silk exports suffered after the Romans learnt to rear silkworms themselves.
64.tq: Identify the cause directly linked to the decline rather than a nearby political event.
xs: Silk exports to the **Eastern Roman Empire** fell once **the Romans learnt to rear silkworms** — option **(4)**.
That trade continued until about **550 CE**.
xa: **Collapse of the West Roman Empire** = standard cause (APPSC-G2 **2017** key).
**Sassanid** decline after the rise of Islam hurt overland trade.
Trade shifted to **South-East Asia** via **Tamralipti**.

64.s: The decline of trade in North India after the Guptas reduced the inflow of which of the following?
64.x: Losing the north-western route and western India cut trade revenue and the inflow of gold and silver.
xa: **Eastern Roman** silk and spice trade lasted until about **550 CE**, until the Romans learnt to **rear silkworms**.
**Collapse of the West Roman Empire** = standard cause of North India's trade decline (APPSC-G2 2017 key).
Decaying towns: **Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, Kaushambi** (APPSC-GS 2023 key).
c. **750-1000 CE** = stagnation in North India.

64.s: With which historian is the 'urban decay' interpretation of the post-Gupta period associated?
64.x: R.S. Sharma's urban decay thesis links shrinking towns, rural self-sufficiency and scarce gold coins.
xa: Declining towns: **Sanghol, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, Kaushambi** (APPSC-GS **2023**).
Peasants bore **vishti** + feudal obligations — basis of the **urban decay / feudalism** critique.
Later dinaras were **debased** — less gold, more alloy.

64.s: Until about which year did Indian trade with the Eastern Roman Empire continue?
64.x: Eastern Roman trade continued until about 550 CE, before the post-Gupta decline and the stagnation of c. 750-1000 CE.
xa: **West Roman collapse** = standard cause of trade decline (APPSC-G2 **2017** key).
**Sassanid decline** after the rise of Islam hurt overland trade.
**Hunas** disrupted the north-western route.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about urban decay after the Guptas?
o: Pataliputra had become a village when Hiuen-Tsang came
Sanghol and Hastinapur were among the declining towns
Stagnation lasted from about 750 to 1000 CE
Towns declined only by the mid-9th century
64.x: Gradual decline of towns was already a feature of the Gupta period and visible in the 7th century.

64.s: The decline of which empire after the rise of Islam hurt India's overland trade?
64.x: The Sassanid decline after the rise of Islam hurt overland trade.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:

64.x: The Hunas blocked the north-western route, and the loss of western India cut the inflow of gold and silver.

64.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the caste system during the post Gupta period?

a. Abhira tribe fragmented into Abhira Brahmanas, Abhira Kshatriyas and Abhira Shudras

b. Brahmanas were not further divided in subcastes during this period

c. Peasants with unequal access to the economic powers were included in Shudra varna

64.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
64.x: Tribes like the Abhiras split into Abhira Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Shudras, peasants were placed in the Shudra varna and Kayasthas emerged as scribes (a, c, d). Brahmanas themselves split into many subcastes, so b is wrong.

64.s: "Kayastha" is the caste of?
64.x: Kayasthas were a caste of scribes who kept records and accounts. They were not traders or physicians.

64.s: A new sort of social structure known as the Jajmani system became prevalent in India during:
64.x: The jajmani system, linking service castes to landholding patrons, is traced to the post-Gupta period. It does not belong to the Satavahana, Gupta or Mauryan periods.

64.s: Which of the following lawgivers of the post Gupta period declared that Sudras were not slave by nature?
64.x: Medhatithi, the post-Gupta (9th c.) commentator on the Manusmriti, held that Shudras were not slaves by nature. Vijnaneshvara (Mitakshara), Narada and Jimutavahana (Dayabhaga) are other jurists.

64.s: Why did castes multiply into numerous sub-castes during the Gupta period?
o: Chandalas were admitted into the four varnas
foreigners and tribes were absorbed into the caste structure
64.x: Foreigners and tribes absorbed into the caste structure, particularly through land grants, multiplied the jatis.
xa: **Kayasthas** rose as a new caste group from the land-grant bureaucracy.
**Untouchability intensified** for Chandalas.
The **Shudras'** status improved.

64.s: The Kayasthas emerged primarily from which occupational and administrative background?
o: Scribes and record-keepers connected with land grants
64.x: Kayasthas emerged as scribes and record-keepers of land grants and became a new caste or class.
64.tq: Match the social group with its distinctive occupational origin.
xs: **Kayasthas** were **scribes and record-keepers of land grants** — option **(3)**.
They rose as a new caste group from the **land-grant bureaucracy**.
xa: They sat in town councils as the **prathama kayastha**.
The **Damodarpur** plates list the town council: nagarashreshthi, sarthavaha, prathama kulika, prathama kayastha.
**Bronze Buddha images** were a craft of the period, unrelated to Kayasthas.

64.s: How many types of slaves does the Narada Smriti list?
64.x: The Narada Smriti lists 15 types of slaves; Chandalas lived outside the varnas and settlements.
xa: Castes **multiplied into sub-castes (jatis)** by absorbing **foreigners** and **tribes**.
**Kayasthas** rose as scribes and record-keepers of land grants.
**Brahmanas** gained through **brahmadeya** land grants.
The Gupta rulers were originally **Vaishyas**, later regarded as **Kshatriyas**.

64.s: What was the jajmani system?
o: Hereditary service castes serving landowning patrons for a share of produce
Guilds receiving deposits and giving loans
Grants of tax-free villages to temples
64.x: Under the jajmani system, service castes served landowning patrons (jajmans) for a share of produce; it became common in the post-Gupta period.

64.s: Which form of marriage of girls did the Gupta-period Dharmashastras advocate?
64.x: The Dharmashastras advocated pre-puberty marriage; widows were to remain celibate, svayamvara gave way to arranged marriages and women were generally denied education.
xa: Women had no general property rights but controlled **stridhana**.
**No purdah** (per art).
**Earliest sati inscription**: **Eran, 510 CE**.

64.s: In the Gupta period, what did the stridhana controlled by women consist of?
64.x: Women lacked general property rights but controlled stridhana, their marriage gifts.
xa: Dharmashastras advocated **pre-puberty marriage**; svayamvara gave way to arranged marriages.
Widows were expected to stay **celibate**.

**Ganikas** (courtesans) lacked respectability; lower-varna women were freer to earn a living.

64.s: Whose wife does the Eran inscription of 510 CE, the earliest inscriptional evidence of sati, refer to?
64.x: The Eran inscription (510 CE) records the sati of the wife of Goparaja, a general of Bhanugupta.
xa: ⚠ Eran 510 CE = a **general's** wife, **not a king's** wife.
Sati was **rare** under the Guptas.
**Widows** were expected to stay **celibate**.

64.s: In the Gupta period, what did svayamvara give way to?
64.x: Svayamvara gave way to marriages arranged by parents, and pre-puberty marriage was favoured.

64.s: Which of the following pairs of land types is correctly matched?
64.x: Maru meant desert. Urvara was fertile, usara barren and aprahata fallow land.

xa: Also **shadvala** (grassy) and **pankila** (muddy).

64.s: In the Amarakosha's land types, what did 'Usara' mean?
64.x: Usara was barren land; Urvara was fertile and Maru desert.

64.s: Which of the following was NOT the feature of the Guilds during the Gupta Period ?
64.x: Gupta guilds were autonomous bodies with their own laws, judicial powers and even armed bodies. So 'non-autonomous bodies' is the feature they did not have.

64.s: In relation to the Dashpur inscription of Kumaragupta and Bandhuvarman, which statement is incorrect?
o: The inscription mentions the construction of the Sun
It is oldest example of the advertisement tradition in
The inscription also refers to Dashpur as Pashchimapur
The inscription was composed by Bhavabhuti
64.x: The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti, not Bhavabhuti, so option 4 is incorrect. It does record the Sun temple, praises silk cloth (oldest advertisement) and calls Dashpur Pashchimapur.

64.s: Which of the following inscription reveals information about Silk Weavers Guild?
64.x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription records the silk weavers' guild that built and repaired a Sun temple. The Prayag, Eran and Hathigumpha records do not.

64.s: Which of the following inscriptions is known as the first advertisement of the World?
64.x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription of Kumaragupta I's time, praising silk cloth, is called the first advertisement. Sohgaura, Supia and Eran are other records.

64.s: What did some Gupta-period guilds maintain for their protection?

Gupta and Vakataka **seals** name artisans, merchants and guilds.

64.s: In the Gupta period, what was the head of a guild called?
64.x: The head of a guild was the Sreshthi or Setti; a Sarthavaha was a caravan trader in long-distance trade.
xa: **Shreni** = guild.
In the town council the **Sarthavaha** sat beside the **nagarashreshthi**, **prathama kulika** and **prathama kayastha** (Damodarpur plates).
**Damodarpur copper plates** show guilds acting as **banks**.
Guilds settled internal disputes and regulated trade.

64.s: The Indore copper plate records an endowment with which guild for maintaining a temple lamp?
64.x: The Indore plate concerns the oil-men's guild and a temple lamp; the Dashpur inscription concerns the silk-weavers' guild and the Damodarpur plates guild banking.
xa: Mandsaur = **world's first advertisement**, composed by **Vatsabhatti**.
Indore plate: guild of oil-men of **Indrapura**, under **Skandagupta**.
Damodarpur plates belong to **Kumaragupta I**.

64.s: Which Gupta records show guilds acting as banks?
64.x: The Damodarpur copper plates of Kumaragupta I show guilds acting as banks; the Indore plate records the oil-men's lamp endowment.

64.s: From where did the silk-weavers' guild of the Mandsaur (Dashpur) inscription migrate to Dashpur?

xa: Temple built **436–37 CE**, repaired **473 CE**.
Composed by **Vatsabhatti**, not Bhava.
Called the **oldest advertisement** in Indian tradition.

64.s: Who composed the Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription, called the oldest advertisement in the Indian tradition?
64.x: The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti, not Bhava (the MPPSC trap).
xa: It records a **silk weavers' guild** from **Lata (Gujarat)** that migrated to Dashpur and built a **Sun temple**.
It dates to **Kumaragupta I** and **Bandhuvarman**; the repair is dated **473 CE**.
Several weavers changed professions — a sign of **falling silk demand**.
⚠ **Indore** plate = oil-men + lamp; **Damodarpur** = guild banks + town council.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about guilds in the Gupta period?
o: They received public deposits and gave loans
They framed their own rules and used their own seals
Some of them kept their own armed bodies
They were controlled by royal officials and had no autonomy
64.x: Gupta guilds were autonomous bodies with their own rules, seals, banking work and sometimes armed bodies.

64.s: The Indore copper plate, recording an endowment with the guild of oil-men, belongs to the reign of which Gupta ruler?
64.x: The Indore copper plate of Skandagupta records an endowment with the oil-men of Indrapura to keep a lamp burning in a Sun temple.

64.s: In his travels through India, Fahhien has mentioned a hospital, it was located at
64.x: Fa-hien described a free hospital at Pataliputra endowed by citizens, where the poor got doctors, food and medicine. Tamralipti was only his port of departure.

64.s: Fa-hien’s mission to India was to
o: learn about the administrative system of the Gupta kings.
understand the social position of women during the Gupta period.
visit the Buddhist institutions and to collect copies of Buddhist manuscripts.
get full knowledge about the condition of peasants during the period of Gupta kings.

64.s: In travel through India Fa-hien has mentioned a hospital, it was located at
64.x: Fa-hien recorded a free hospital at Pataliputra funded by citizens, giving poor patients doctors, food and medicine. Tamralipti was only his port of departure.

64.s: During which age did women enjoy equality with men?
64.x: No period gave women equality with men; in the Gupta age their status fell (early marriage, no property rights), so 'None of these'.

64.s: How did Fa-Hien come to India and how did he return?
o: by sea via Sri Lanka; overland via Central Asia
overland via Central Asia and Gandhara; by sea via Sri Lanka
overland via Central Asia; overland via Central Asia
64.x: Fa-Hien travelled overland through Central Asia and Gandhara and returned by sea through Sri Lanka, via Tamralipti.

64.s: By what name is the account of the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien known?

64.s: According to Fa-Hien, how did the Chandalas announce their approach?
64.x: Fa-Hien noted that Chandalas lived outside villages and towns and struck wood to warn others.

His account: **Fo-kwo-ki** ("Record of Buddhist Kingdoms").
He saw **free hospitals** at **Pataliputra** and **20 viharas at Mathura**.
**Cowrie shells** were used in daily exchange; he returned by sea via **Tamralipti and Sri Lanka**.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about society as described by Fa-Hien?
o: Chandalas followed the same food restrictions as everyone else.
Cowrie shells were used in daily exchange.
Hindus and Buddhists lived in harmony.
The people were peaceful and prosperous.

xa: Government was **mild** with **few taxes**.

**Free hospitals** at Pataliputra; **rest houses** on highways.

64.s: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of which Gupta ruler?
64.x: Fa-Hien was in India c. 399–412 CE, in the reign of Chandragupta II, though he never named the king. Samudragupta ruled before this; Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta ruled after it.

64.s: According to Fa-Hien, how many viharas were there at Mathura?
64.x: Fa-Hien recorded 20 viharas at Mathura.

64.s: Which of the following places did Fa-Hien NOT describe as a centre of Buddhist decay?
64.x: Fa-Hien saw decay at Kapilavastu, Gaya and Kushinagar, but found 20 viharas flourishing at Mathura.

64.s: In Gupta times, with what was ordinary daily exchange mainly carried on?
