65.s: The ornament in the chest of Lord Vishnu
65.x: The Kaustubha gem, which rose from the churning of the ocean, adorns Vishnu's chest. Marakatham (emerald), Manikyam (ruby) and Pagadam (coral) are ordinary gems.

65.s: Who were the first to worship Vasudeva Krishna :
65.x: The Bhagavatas (Vasudevakas) were the first worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna, known from Panini's time. Vedic Aryans worshipped nature gods, and the Tamils and Abhiras are not credited with it.

65.s: Who contributes the most in the development of Bhagavata sect?
65.x: Bhagavatism peaked under the Guptas, who made it virtually the state religion and styled themselves Parama Bhagavata with Garuda as emblem. Indo-Greeks like Heliodorus were only early patrons.

65.s: The earliest known epigraphic evidence of Bhagvatism is :
65.x: The Besnagar Garuda pillar of Heliodorus (2nd c. BCE) is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. The Prayag prashasti, Nasik and Ayodhya records are later.

65.s: Which incarnation of Vishnu is depicted as saving the Earth from the Sea?
65.x: In the Varaha (boar) avatar Vishnu killed Hiranyaksha and lifted the Earth from the cosmic ocean on his tusks. Matsya saved Manu from the flood, Kurma bore Mount Mandara and Narasimha killed Hiranyakashipu.

65.s: The earliest known epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism is
65.x: The Garuda column at Besnagar, set up by the Greek envoy Heliodorus, is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism. Samudragupta's Prayag prashasti is much later.

65.s: The originator of Bhagavata Religion was –
65.x: The Bhagavata religion goes back to Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan, son of Devaki. Janaka and Yajnavalkya are Upanishadic figures and Surdas a medieval poet.

65.s: Bhagavatism centred on the worship of Vasudeva-Krishna of which clan?
65.x: Bhagavatism centred on Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan; its foundations were karma, bhakti and ahimsa.
xa: It preached the **Avatara** theory of Vishnu (ten incarnations).
**Heliodorus**, envoy of Indo-Greek king **Antialcidas**, set up the **Garuda pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha)** and called himself a **Bhagavata**.
**Panini** refers to Vasudeva worship.
⚠ First **'Parama Bhagavata'**: many notes = **Chandragupta II**; UPPSC keys (2009, 2015) = **Samudragupta**.

65.s: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of which Indo-Greek king?
65.x: Heliodorus, envoy of Antialcidas at the court of the Sunga ruler Bhagabhadra, set up the Garuda pillar to Vasudeva.
xa: **Garuda** was later the Gupta **dynastic emblem**.
The **Bhagavatas** first worshipped Vasudeva-Krishna (UPPSC **1997**).
**Panini** refers to Vasudeva worship.

65.s: Gupta-period Vaishnavism preached the theory of how many incarnations of Vishnu?
65.x: The avatara theory of ten incarnations of Vishnu was preached during the Gupta period.
xa: Colossal **Varaha** panel at **Udayagiri** under **Chandragupta II**.
Vaishnava symbols: **chakra, shankha, Garuda**; centre **Mathura**.
Text: **Bhagavad Gita**.

65.s: Under whose patronage was the colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri carved?
65.x: The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri was carved under Chandragupta II, and the cave functioned as his personal temple.
xs: The colossal **Varaha** panel at **Udayagiri** was carved under **Chandragupta II** — option **(1)**.
The cave was his **personal temple**.
xa: It is read as his **rescue of the land**, e.g. from the **Sakas**.
Udayagiri (MP) has **1 Jain cave** among **20**.
**Udayagiri Cave 4** holds an **Ekamukhalinga**.

65.s: The Gupta kings, who called themselves 'Parambhagavata', used which emblem?
65.x: The Gupta kings called themselves Parambhagavata and used the Garuda emblem, marking them as Vaishnavas.
n: The Guptas were associated with Vaishnavism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Guptas were called Parambhagavatas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Guptas used Garuda symbolism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Vaishnavism** developed from the **Bhagavata religion**.
The **Besnagar Garuda Pillar** of **Heliodorus** is associated with the Bhagavata religion.
**Skandagupta**'s coins carry the **Garuda standard**.
Colossal **Varaha (boar) Vishnu** panel at **Udayagiri** was carved under **Chandragupta II**.

65.s: Nandivarman II's Pedavegi inscription is regarded as the first inscription in Andhra Pradesh relating to which of the following?
65.x: The Pedavegi inscription of Nandivarman II is regarded as the first inscription in Andhra Pradesh concerning Vishnu temples.
xa: Salankayanas also used Shaiva **Parama Mahesvara** titles.
**Gudimallam's Parasurameswara** temple = oldest Shiva linga (APPSC G2 **2008**).
**Kapalikas**: **Bhairavakonda** caves.

65.s: The Vaishnava Salankayana rulers also used which Shaiva title?
65.x: The Salankayanas followed Vaishnavism, but their rulers also used Shaiva titles such as Parama Mahesvara.
xa: **Nandivarman II's Pedavegi** inscription = first in AP on **Vishnu temples**.
**Gudimallam** = oldest Shiva linga in AP.
**Kalamukha** and **Pashupata** flourished under the **Kakatiyas**.

65.s: Which Gupta ruler was the first to take the title 'Parama Bhagavata'?
65.x: Samudragupta was the first Gupta to take the title Parama Bhagavata; Chandragupta II's coins also carry it.

65.s: In which form does the colossal Udayagiri panel of Chandragupta II's time show Vishnu?
65.x: The Udayagiri panel shows Varaha, the boar incarnation of Vishnu, in Chandragupta II's personal cave temple.

65.s: Who were the first worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna?
65.x: The Bhagavatas (Vasudevakas) were the first worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna; Vaishnavism grew from them.

65.s: Which is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism?
65.x: The Garuda pillar of Heliodorus at Besnagar (Vidisha) is the earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism.

65.s: At the court of which Sunga king did Heliodorus, who set up the Besnagar Garuda pillar, serve as envoy?
65.x: Heliodorus, envoy of Antialcidas, was at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.

65.s: Which religion did the Gupta kings generally patronise?
65.x: The Guptas patronised Bhagavatism, yet Samudragupta allowed Meghavarman to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.
xa: **Sanchi**: Chandragupta II's officer **Amrakardava** granted to the Buddhist vihara.
**Kahaum pillar** (Skandagupta era) records **Jain images**.
Fa-Hien noted **cordial Hindu-Buddhist relations**.

65.s: With which religion is Kalika Purana associated ?
65.x: The Kalika Purana is an upapurana of the Shakta (goddess) tradition, probably composed in Assam. It is not Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain.

65.s: Kalika Purana is associated with which of the following religion?
65.x: The Kalika Purana belongs to Shaktism, the worship of the goddess. It is not a Vaishnava, Buddhist or Jain text.

65.s: Who are the worshippers of Kapalini?
65.x: Kapalini, the skull-bearing form of the goddess consort of Kapali-Bhairava, was worshipped by the Kapalikas. Kalika is a goddess, not a sect, and the Shaktas and Vaishnavas are broader traditions.

65.s: The Kapalikas emerged from the school of:
65.x: The NextGen APPSC fact list states that the Kapalikas emerged from the Misra Saivam school, which is the APPSC key. Pashupata is the oldest Shaiva sect, and Vaishnavam is a different tradition.

65.s: Which one of the following was a Shaiva sect in ancient India?
65.x: Mattamayura was a Shaiva sect known from Chedi (Kalachuri) inscriptions. The Ajivikas were a heterodox sect, Mayamata is an architecture text and Isanasivagurudeva Paddhati a ritual manual.

65.s: Ardhanarishvara, a figure of half Shiva and half Parvati, represents
o: Union of God with his Shakti
65.x: Ardhanarishvara, half Shiva and half Parvati, shows the god united with his Shakti. 'Union of male and female' and 'god and goddess' are looser versions of the same idea.

65.s: Who was the founder of Pashupata Shaivism?
65.x: Pashupata Shaivism was founded by Lakulisha.
n: Bauddha is a Nastika school. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Jain is a Nastika school. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Ajivika is associated with Niyativada or determinism (fate). [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Pashupata is associated with Lakulisha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
xa: Astika schools **accept Vedic authority**; Nastika: **Charvaka, Buddhism, Jainism, Ajivika**.
**Niyati** is linked with **Makkhali Gosala**.

65.s: How many Mahapuranas are traditionally recognised, the corpus that took its final shape in the Gupta period?
65.x: There are 18 Mahapuranas (APPSC G2 2011 key), among them Vishnu, Bhagavata, Matsya, Vayu, Brahmanda, Markandeya, Shiva and Kurma. 12, 16 and 24 are wrong; 12 is the number of land types in the Amarakosha.
xs: There are **18 Mahapuranas** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 **2011** key).
⚠ **12** is the number of land types in the **Amarakosha** (another topic) — not here.
xa: Principal: **Vishnu, Bhagavata, Matsya, Vayu, Brahmanda, Markandeya, Shiva, Kurma**.
Final shape in the **Gupta period** (c. 4th–6th c. CE).
Five topics: creation, re-creation, genealogies, **manvantaras**, dynastic history.

65.s: The five traditional subjects of the Puranas include which of the following?
o: Trade, taxation, diplomacy, warfare and agriculture
Creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history
Ritual, pilgrimage, music, dance and sculpture
Grammar, logic, medicine, astronomy and architecture
65.x: The pancha-lakshana of the Puranas consists of creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras and dynastic history.
65.tq: Recall the five-part classification as a complete group.
xs: **Pancha-lakshana**: **creation, re-creation, genealogies, manvantaras, dynastic history** — option **(2)**.
These are the Puranas' **five topics**.
xa: **18 Mahapuranas** (APPSC-G2 **2011**).
Final shape in the **Gupta period** (c. 4th–6th c. CE).
**Smriti** texts: **Yajnavalkya, Narada, Brihaspati, Katyayana**.

65.s: In which period did the Mahapuranas take their final shape?
65.x: Compiled over centuries, the 18 Mahapuranas took final shape in the Gupta period (c. 4th-6th century CE).

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalika Purana:
1. It is one of the 18 Mahapuranas.
2. It was likely written in Assam.
3. It is associated with Shaktism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: The Kalika Purana is a Shakta upapurana, likely written in Assam, not a Mahapurana.

65.s: Who founded the Pashupata sect, the oldest Shaiva sect?
65.x: Pashupata, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by Lakulisha (Nakulisha); in it pashu is the individual soul and pati the Supreme soul.
xa: Lakulisha is placed in the **1st c. CE** per some notes.
**Kalamukhas** followed **Kalanana**, a disciple of Lakulisha.
Pashupata and Kalamukha later flourished under the **Kakatiyas**.

65.s: Which pair of sects later flourished under the Kakatiyas?
65.x: The Kalamukha and Pashupata sects later flourished under the Kakatiyas.
65.tq: Start from the sure pair and reject combinations formed by mixing unrelated religious traditions.
xs: **Kalamukha and Pashupata** later flourished under the **Kakatiyas** — option **(2)**.
**Pashupata** = oldest Shaiva sect (founder **Lakulisha**); **Kalamukhas** followed **Kalanana**.
xa: Kalamukha: **Simha Parishat** (Andhra), **Shakti Parishat** (Karnataka).
**Kapalikas**: **Bhairavakonda** caves (AP).
**Gudimallam** (Tirupati district) = oldest Shiva linga.

65.s: For what is the Parasurameswara temple at Gudimallam (Tirupati district) known?
o: The earliest known Shiva linga, bearing a standing figure of Shiva
The earliest Buddhist stupa in Andhra
The earliest Jain cave shrine in Andhra
The earliest image of Vishnu as Varaha
65.x: Gudimallam near Renigunta has the oldest known Shiva linga, which carries a standing figure of Shiva.
xa: **Ekamukhalinga** (one face of Shiva) is a **Gupta** form — **Udayagiri Cave 4**, **Khoh**.
**Nandivarman II's Pedavegi** inscription = first in AP on **Vishnu temples**.
Saivism symbol: **Linga** (APPSC G2 **2025**).

65.s: The Kapalikas, an extremist skull-bearing sect, belonged to which tradition?
65.x: Kapalikas were an extremist, skull-bearing Shaiva sect that emerged from the Misra Saivam (mixed Shaivism) school.
xa: ⚠ APPSC keys differ: **Pashupata Shaivism** (G2 **2019**) vs **Misra (mixed) Shaivism** (GS **2018**).
**Bhairavakonda caves** (AP) belong to the Kapalikas.
**Kalamukhas** were the other extreme sect.

65.s: The Gupta 'Ekamukhalinga' is a linga bearing which of the following?
65.x: Ekamukhalinga has a single face of Shiva, as at Udayagiri Cave 4 and Khoh.

65.s: Kalanana, whom the Kalamukhas followed, was a disciple of which teacher?
65.x: Kalanana was a disciple of Lakulisha, founder of the Pashupata sect.

65.s: To which Shaiva sect do the Bhairavakonda caves in Andhra Pradesh belong?
65.x: The Bhairavakonda caves in Andhra belong to the Kapalikas, the skull-bearing Shaiva sect.

65.s: With whom is the Nathpanth associated?
65.x: The Nathpanth of Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath worships Shiva as Adinath.

65.s: The Simha Parishat in Andhra and the Shakti Parishat in Karnataka were branches of which Shaiva sect?
65.x: The Kalamukhas were strong in medieval Andhra (Simha Parishat) and Karnataka (Shakti Parishat).

65.s: In the Gupta period, in what form were Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi worshipped?
65.x: Durga, Amba, Kali and Chandi were worshipped as mother goddesses during the Gupta period.
xa: **Gaja-Lakshmi** appears on **seals**.
**Tantrism** spread from the **5th c.**, centred on **shakti**.
Surya and Shakti already appear in **Hala's Gathasaptasati**.

65.s: Tantrism, open to women and Shudras, began to spread from about which century CE?
65.x: Tantrism spread from about the fifth century, centred on shakti, and influenced Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Buddhism and Jainism.
xa: Mother goddesses: **Durga, Amba, Kali, Chandi**.
Surya and Shakti appear in **Hala's Gathasaptasati**.
**Gaja-Lakshmi** appears on seals.

65.s: Ardhanarishvara represents the union of which deities?
65.x: Ardhanarishvara unites Shiva and Parvati, joining Shaivism and Shaktism.

65.s: During the reign of which Gupta ruler did the silk-weavers' guild build a Sun temple at Mandsaur?
65.x: The Mandsaur inscription of Kumaragupta I's time records the Sun temple built by the silk weavers from Lata.

65.s: At which place out of the following a Gupta era temple is not found?
65.x: Gupta-period temples survive at Bhitargaon (brick temple, Kanpur), Deogarh (Dashavatara) and Bhitari (Ghazipur, Skandagupta's excavated Vishnu temples). Rajgir is known for Buddhist and earlier Magadhan sites, not a Gupta temple.

65.s: The Dasavatara Temple at Deogarh belongs to which period?
65.x: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is a Gupta temple (c. 6th c. CE) of the early Nagara style, depicting Vishnu's ten avatars. The Pallavas, Cholas and Vijayanagara built in the south and later.

65.s: With reference to the cultural history of India, the term 'Panchayatan' refers to
65.x: Panchayatana is a style of temple construction with the main shrine and four subsidiary shrines. It is not a village assembly, sect or office.

65.s: With reference to the cultural history of India, the term 'Panchayatan' refers to –
65.x: Panchayatana is a temple plan with a central shrine and four subsidiary shrines, as at Deogarh. It is not an assembly, a sect or a functionary.

65.s: The temple of Deogarh near Jhansi and the sculptures in the temple at Garhwa near Allahabad are the important remains of the
o: More than one of the above
65.x: The Deogarh temple near Jhansi and the Garhwa sculptures near Allahabad are remains of Gupta art. The Mauryas built no such temples and the Rashtrakutas worked in the Deccan.

65.s: What is the raised platform on which Gupta temples stood called?
65.x: Gupta temples established the square garbhagriha, pillared mandapa, pradakshina path and raised jagati platform.
xa: These mark the beginning of the **Nagara style**.
**Panchayatana** plan first at **Deogarh**.
No free-standing Hindu temple survives **before the Guptas**.

65.s: To which period do the earliest surviving free-standing Hindu temples belong?
65.x: No free-standing Hindu temple survives from a period earlier than the Guptas.
xa: Stages: **Sanchi 17, Tigawa** → **Nachna, Bhumara** → **Deogarh, Bhitargaon**.
Gupta age = **Golden Age of art and architecture**.
Iconography of Brahmanical, Jain and Buddhist deities was **standardised**.

65.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
65.x: Bhitargaon is a Gupta-period Hindu temple associated with the third stage of temple evolution; it is not identified as a Buddhist chaitya in this classification.
65.tq: Find the wrong monument–religious structure pair among nearby architectural examples.
xs: **Bhitargaon — Buddhist chaitya** is wrong — option **(2)**; Bhitargaon is a **third-stage** Gupta temple with Deogarh.
**Deogarh = Dashavatara**, **Bhumara = Shiva**, **Nachna = Parvati** — correct.
xa: Third stage: **low square shikhara**, **Panchayatana** plan.
**Deogarh** = earliest Panchayatana.
Gupta age = **Golden Age** of art and architecture.

65.s: Which of the following temple – stage pairs is NOT correctly matched?
65.x: Deogarh belongs to the third stage, like Bhitargaon; Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa are first stage and Nachna second.

65.s: Which is the earliest example of the Panchayatana plan?
65.x: The Panchayatana plan (main shrine plus four corner shrines) first appears at the Deogarh Dashavatara temple; Bhumara has only two flanking shrines.
xa: Deogarh and **Bhitargaon** = third stage.
Third stage replaced the flat roof with a **low square shikhara**.
Basic elements: **garbhagriha, mandapa, pradakshina path, jagati**.

65.s: To which deity is the Gupta temple at Nachna dedicated?
65.x: Nachna, a second-stage temple, is dedicated to Parvati; Bhumara is a Shiva temple.

65.s: The shikhara first appears in which stage of Gupta temple architecture?
65.x: Third-stage temples such as Deogarh and Bhitargaon dropped the flat roof for a low square shikhara.

65.s: Which Gupta temple has only two flanking shrines, not a full Panchayatana?
65.x: Bhumara has two flanking shrines; Deogarh is the earliest full Panchayatana with four subsidiary shrines.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhitargaon temple:
1. It is a Buddhist chaitya.
2. It belongs to the third stage of Gupta temple architecture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: Bhitargaon is a third-stage Gupta Hindu temple, not a Buddhist chaitya.

65.s: In which district of Uttar Pradesh is the Dashavatara temple of Deogarh located?
65.x: The Dashavatara temple, the earliest Panchayatana temple, is at Deogarh in Lalitpur district near Jhansi.

65.s: What was the name of weapon which was made from Dadhichi's back bone?
65.x: Indra's thunderbolt, the Vajrayudha, was made from the backbone of sage Dadhichi to kill Vritra. Pashupata was Shiva's weapon, Brahmastra Brahma's and Gandiva Arjuna's bow.

65.s:
Match the following.
List I
List II

A. Nandi
1. Divine white elephant

B. Kalpvriksha
2. Holy cow

C. Airawat
3. Shiva’s bull

D. Kamdhenu
4. Divine tree
Codes A B C D A B C D
65.x: Nandi is Shiva's bull (3), Kalpavriksha the divine tree (4), Airavata the divine white elephant (1) and Kamadhenu the holy cow (2), giving 3-4-1-2.

65.s: Which of the following symbols appeared as sectarian symbols on Gupta coins and seals?
65.x: The linga, trident and bull appeared as sectarian symbols on Gupta coins and seals.
65.tq: Test a symbolic group by direct identification.
xs: **Linga, trident (trishula) and bull** appear on Gupta coins and seals — option **(4)**.
These are **Shaiva** sectarian symbols.
xa: **Gaja-Lakshmi** also appears on seals.
The Gupta emblem was **Garuda**; Skandagupta's coins show the **Garuda standard**.
Buddhism's principle: **Ashtanga Marga**.

65.s: With which religion are the chakra, shankha and Garuda associated as symbols?
65.x: Chakra, shankha and Garuda belong to Vaishnavism; the linga to Saivism.
xa: APPSC G2 **2025** match also had **Animism → Nature Worship**.
Gupta dynastic emblem = **Garuda**, Vishnu's mount.
Saiva symbols on Gupta coins and seals: **linga, trident, bull**.

65.s:
With reference to the temple of Bhitargaon, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, which of the following statements is/ are correct?
(1) This temple was constructed during 5th century A.D. to 6th century A.D.
(2) It is one of the oldest brick temples of India.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-
65.x: Both are correct: the Bhitargaon temple (Kanpur) is a Gupta brick temple of the 5th–6th century with terracotta panels, one of the oldest brick temples of India.

65.s: Which one of the following best describes a major religious change during the Gupta period?
o: Temple worship was replaced entirely by Vedic fire sacrifices.
Idol worship was prohibited in public temples.
Theistic and devotional Hinduism increasingly replaced sacrificial Brahmanism.
Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh ceased to be regarded as supreme deities.
65.x: Hinduism became increasingly theistic and devotional, while temple-based idol worship became common and the earlier dominance of sacrificial Brahmanism declined.
65.tq: Choose the comprehensive description of a religious transition.
xs: **Theistic and devotional** religion replaced **sacrificial Brahmanism** — option **(3)**.
**Idol worship in temples** became common — shift from Vedic fire altar to temple.
**Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh** were the supreme deities.
xa: Comparative: Mauryan = **Vedic + Shramana**; Gupta = **sacrifice → temple and bhakti**.
**Smarta** practices spread.
**Six schools** of philosophy took final shape.

65.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Moksha — one of the three components of Trivarga
65.x: The four Purusharthas are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. The first three together are called Trivarga.

xs: **Trivarga = Dharma, Artha, Kama** — option **(2)**.
The four **Purusharthas** are Dharma, Artha, Kama, **Moksha**; Moksha is **not** in trivarga.
xa: Supreme deities: **Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh**.
**Smarta** practices spread.
**Six schools** of philosophy took final shape.

65.s: What are the first three Purusharthas - Dharma, Artha and Kama - together called?
65.x: Dharma, Artha and Kama form the trivarga; Moksha is the fourth Purushartha.

65.s: Who is associated with the foundation of Nalanda during the Gupta period?
65.x: Kumaragupta I, also known as Shakraditya, is credited with founding Nalanda.
65.tq: Use the founder–institution trap among Gupta rulers and Buddhist centres.
xs: **Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya)** founded **Nalanda** — option **(3)**.
**Mihirakula**, the Huna, **persecuted** Buddhism.
xa: **Mahayana** images flourished in Gupta art.
Buddhism **lost royal patronage and declined**.
Buddhist centres: **Nalanda, Sarnath**.

65.s: Whose teachings did the Lingayat sect follow?
65.x: Lingayats followed Basava; Pashupata was founded by Lakulisha and the Nathpanth led by Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath.
n: Pashupata is associated with Shaivism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]

65.s: Who wrote the Visuddhimagga?
65.x: Buddhaghosa wrote the Visuddhimagga; Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa and Dinnaga founded Buddhist logic.
xa: Asanga and Vasubandhu: **4th c.**; Dinnaga and Buddhaghosa: **5th c.**
Visuddhimagga is in **Pali** (**Theravada**).
**Kumaragupta I** founded **Nalanda**.

65.s: Which Huna ruler persecuted Buddhism in the Gupta period?
65.x: Buddhism lost royal patronage and was persecuted by Mihirakula, though Mahayana images flourished in Gupta art.
xa: **Kumaragupta I** founded **Nalanda**.
Scholars: **Asanga, Vasubandhu, Dinnaga, Buddhaghosa**.
**Sanchi**: **Amrakardava's** grant to the Buddhist vihara.

65.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Buddhist logic?
65.x: Dinnaga (5th century) founded Buddhist logic; Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa.

65.s: Who is the author of the Abhidharmakosa?
65.x: Vasubandhu (4th century) wrote the Abhidharmakosa.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about Jain art in the Gupta period:
1. Mathura was a major centre of Jain art.
2. Mathura was especially noted for images of the Tirthankaras.
3. Kushinagar was the leading centre of Tirthankara images.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: Mathura was the major centre of Jain art, particularly for Tirthankara images; Kushinagar was not.

65.s: With which event is the Vallabhi council of the fifth century CE associated?
o: The compilation and writing down of the Svetambara canon
The composition of the Tripitaka by Buddhist monks
The foundation of Nalanda by Kumaragupta I
The beginning of the Pashupata sect
65.x: The Vallabhi council, held under Devarddhi Kshamashramana, compiled and committed the Svetambara Jain canon to writing.
xs: The **Vallabhi council** (**5th c. CE**) compiled and wrote down the **Svetambara canon** — option **(1)**.

Jain symbol: **Triratna** (APPSC G2 **2025**).

65.s: Under whom was the Vallabhi council of the 5th century CE held?
65.x: Devarddhi Kshamashramana presided over the Vallabhi council, which wrote down the Svetambara canon.

65.s: Amrakardava, who recorded a grant to a Buddhist vihara at Sanchi, was an officer of which Gupta ruler?
65.x: Amrakardava, an officer of Chandragupta II, recorded the Sanchi grant; the Kahaum pillar of Skandagupta's time records Jain images.
xa: **Samudragupta** allowed **Meghavarman**'s monastery at **Bodh Gaya**.
**Vallabhi council** (**5th c. CE**) under **Devarddhi Kshamashramana** wrote down the **Svetambara** canon.

⚠ **Dhruva**'s opponent was **Vatsaraja**, not Nagabhata II or Nagabhata I — a UPSC-notes trap.

xa: Govinda III also defeated **Dharmapala**, then retreated after a **Himalayan** campaign.
The **Sanjan plates** describe Govinda III's campaign.
Indra III sacked Kannauj c. **916 CE**.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs: King Dynasty
1. Nannuka Chandela
2. Jayashakti Parmara
3. Nagabhata II Gurjara-Pratihara
4. Bhoja Rashtrakuta How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: Only two pairs are right: Nannuka – Chandela and Nagabhata II – Gurjara-Pratihara. Jayashakti was a Chandela, not a Paramara, and Bhoja was a Paramara (or Pratihara) king, not a Rashtrakuta.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs : King Dynasty
1. Nannuka – Chandela
2. Jayashakti – Paramara
3. Nagabhata II – Gurjara Pratihara
4. Bhoja – Rashtrakuta How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: Only two pairs are right: Nannuka (Chandela founder) and Nagabhata II (Gurjara-Pratihara). Jayashakti was a Chandela and Bhoja a Paramara, so pairs 2 and 4 are wrong.

68.s: The struggle for Kannauj is historically significant because it illustrates which broader development in early medieval India?
o: The disappearance of dynastic competition in northern India
The complete centralisation of power under one pan-Indian emperor
The shift of political power towards regional kingdoms
The replacement of agriculture by maritime trade as the main economic base
68.x: The struggle demonstrates the shift of power to regional kingdoms during early medieval India.
68.tq: Identify the broad historical interpretation supported by the political pattern.
xs: The struggle shows the **shift of power to regional kingdoms** — option **(3)** is correct.
No power held Kannauj permanently, and all three ended **exhausted**.
xa: New Rajput states followed: **Chandelas**, **Chauhans**.
Kannauj stood for the title of **Samrat** of North India.
AP angle: Rashtrakuta pressure on the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi** ran in parallel.

68.s: Which power finally held Kannauj at the end of the tripartite struggle?
68.x: Kannauj was finally held by the Pratiharas under Bhoja and Mahendrapala I, though no power retained it permanently for long.
xa: Duration: nearly **two centuries**, **8th-10th c.**
Pratihara decline after **Indra III**'s raid → **Chandelas**, **Chauhans**.
All three powers were **exhausted**.

68.s: What was one important consequence of the exhaustion of all three powers involved in the struggle for Kannauj?
o: The permanent Rashtrakuta annexation of Bengal
The abolition of regional kingdoms in northern India
The immediate restoration of Harsha's empire
The emergence of new Rajput states such as the Chandelas and Chauhans
68.x: The exhaustion of the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas, along with Pratihara decline after Indra III's raid, opened the way for new Rajput states such as the Chandelas and Chauhans.
68.tq: Trace the political consequence of weakening major powers to the rise of regional states.
xs: Exhaustion of all three led to new Rajput states — **Chandelas** and **Chauhans** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Pratiharas** declined after **Indra III**'s raid.
xa: The overall significance: a shift of power to **regional kingdoms**.
Indra III defeated Pratihara **Mahipala I** c. **916 CE**.
**Chauhans** were not a party to the struggle itself.

68.s: Jayashakti, in the list of early medieval kings, belonged to which dynasty?
68.x: Jayashakti was a Chandela, not a Paramara; Bhoja of Dhar was the Paramara.

68.s: Which Rajput dynasty began as Pratihara feudatories and rose after the tripartite struggle?
68.x: The Chandelas began as Pratihara feudatories in the early 9th century and rose as the three powers weakened.

68.s: The Sanjan plates, dated to 871 CE and associated with Amoghavarsha I, provide information about which event?
o: Dharmapala's installation of Chakrayudha at Kannauj
68.x: The Sanjan plates, issued during the reign of Rashtrakuta ruler Amoghavarsha I in 871 CE, describe Govinda III's Himalayan campaign.
68.tq: Combine the source, date and dynasty clues before identifying the event.
xs: The Sanjan plates describe **Govinda III's Himalayan campaign** — option **(2)** is correct.
They are **Rashtrakuta** plates of **Amoghavarsha I** (**871 CE**).
**Chakrayudha's installation** is in the **Khalimpur plates**; **Indra III's sack** came c. **916 CE**.
xa: Quote: his horses "drank the icy waters of **Himalayan** streams, his elephants tasted the **Ganga**".
⚠ **Sanjan** = Rashtrakuta; **Gwalior** = Pratihara; **Khalimpur** = Pala.

68.s: Which source records the victories of Nagabhata II over Chakrayudha and Dharmapala?
68.x: The Gwalior prashasti of Mihira Bhoja records Nagabhata II's victories over Chakrayudha and Dharmapala.
68.tq: Use the source–ruler–victory association rather than the dynasty name alone.
xs: The **Gwalior prashasti** records **Nagabhata II**'s victories over **Chakrayudha** and **Dharmapala** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **Pratihara** record of **Mihira Bhoja**.
**Sanjan plates** = Govinda III's campaign; **Khalimpur plates** = Chakrayudha's installation.
xa: ⚠ **Sanjan** = Rashtrakuta; **Gwalior** = Pratihara; **Khalimpur** = Pala.
Nagabhata II was in turn defeated by **Govinda III**.

68.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Matsya Nyaya – Law of the jungle
Param Saugat – Law of the jungle
68.x: Matsya Nyaya means the law of the jungle. The Khalimpur inscription records Gopala's selection, Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Param Saugat means a devout Buddhist.
n: The Khalimpur Inscription is associated with Dharmapala. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Khalimpur Inscription mentions the selection or election of Gopala. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Matsya Nyaya means the Law of the Jungle. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Dharmapala held the title Param Saugat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The title Param Saugat indicates Buddhist affiliation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Khalimpur Inscription links Dharmapala with Gopala and Matsya Nyaya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xa: The Khalimpur plates also say **Chakrayudha** was installed at **Kannauj** with the approval of northern kings.
⚠ **Sanjan** = Rashtrakuta; **Gwalior** = Pratihara; **Khalimpur** = Pala.
Dharmapala removed Pratihara nominee **Indrayudha** and installed puppet **Chakrayudha**.
**Dhruva** defeated both **Vatsaraja and Dharmapala**.

68.s: What do the Khalimpur plates of Dharmapala record?
o: Sack of Kannauj by Indra III
68.x: The Pala Khalimpur plates record Gopala's election and Chakrayudha's installation.

68.s: Gopala was elected Pala king to end which condition?
68.x: Gopala's election ended Matsya Nyaya, the law of the jungle, as the Khalimpur plates say.

68.s: The Gwalior prashasti, recording Nagabhata II's victories, belongs to which dynasty?
68.x: The Gwalior prashasti of Mihira Bhoja is a Pratihara record; Sanjan is Rashtrakuta and Khalimpur Pala.

68.s: Which university was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala?
68.x: Dharmapala, titled Param Saugat, founded Vikramashila.

68.s: Which Pala king took the title 'Param Saugat'?
68.x: Dharmapala took the title Param Saugat (devout Buddhist) and founded Vikramashila.

69.s: The founder of Nalanda University was:
69.x: Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya) in the 5th century AD; the Palas later patronised it.

69.s: Nalanda University was founded during the dynasty of
69.x: Nalanda was founded in the Gupta period by Kumaragupta I; the Palas revived and patronised it but did not found it.

69.s: Nalanda is located in –
69.x: Nalanda lies in Bihar (ancient Magadha), south-east of Patna.

69.s: ‘Nava Nalanda Mahavihara’ is famous for –
69.x: Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, founded by Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap (foundation stone 20 November 1951), is a Pali and Buddhist research centre, not a museum or a memorial.

69.s: In which among the following state 'Odantipur' Education Centre was situated?
69.x: Odantapuri (Uddandapura), founded by Gopala, stood at present Bihar Sharif in Bihar.

69.s: Which one of the following rulers established Vikramshila university?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala; Gopala founded Odantapuri, while Devapala and Mahipala I founded neither.

69.s: Who among the following had build the Sompura Mahavihara?
69.x: Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur, Bangladesh) was built by the Pala king Dharmapala; Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda and Vijayasena was a Sena king.

69.s: Who founded the Vikramshila University?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala; Kumarila Bhatta, Madhvacharya and Pulakesin II have nothing to do with it.

69.s: Who established the Odantapuri University?
69.x: Odantapuri was founded by Gopala, the first Pala king, not by Dharmapala (Vikramashila) or Ramapala (Jagaddala).

69.s: The Vikramshila University was established by
o: More than one of the above
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala alone; Gopala founded Odantapuri, so 'more than one' is wrong.

69.s: Who among the following was the founder of Vikramshila University?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala, not Gopala (Odantapuri), Devapala or Mahipala.

69.s: Which of the following Universities was founded by Dharmapala?
69.x: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila; Taxila and Nalanda are older, and Valabhi was a Maitraka centre.

69.s: Who founded the Vikramshila University ?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala, not Devapala, Ramapala or Gopala.

69.s: Which one of the following rulers established Vikramashila University?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala; Gopala founded Odantapuri, and Devapala and Mahipala I did not found it.

69.s: Vikramshila Mahavihara, a great center of education in ancient India, was established by
69.x: Vikramashila Mahavihara was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala, not by Kumaragupta I (Nalanda), Harsha or Lakshmanasena.

69.s: The most ancient monastery in India is
69.x:
Most books and keys: Nalanda. Strictly: the Bhaja rock-cut vihara (2nd century BCE) is older than Nalanda (5th century CE) (Wikipedia, Bhaja Caves).
Of the three great monastic universities offered, Nalanda (5th century, Kumaragupta I) is the oldest; Odantapuri and Vikramashila are 8th-century Pala foundations.

69.s: Under the Palas, which centre became associated with translating books into Tibetan?
69.x: Jagaddala was associated with translations into Tibetan, while Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala.
xa: **Sakya Sri Bhadra** of Jagaddala took **Tantric Buddhism** to Tibet.
**Dharmapala's seal** was found at Nalanda.
Jagaddala was sacked in the early **13th c.**

69.s: Where is the Somapura Mahavihara located at present?
69.x: Somapura Mahavihara is at Paharpur in Naogaon district, Bangladesh. Antichak is Vikramashila, Varendra is Jagaddala and Bihar Sharif is Odantapuri.

69.s: Nalanda University in Bihar was founded in which century AD?
69.x: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century AD by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I.
n: Nalanda University was located in Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University was founded in the 5th century AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University had a Gupta foundation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University was a major Buddhist centre of learning. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xa: It **attracted students** from **China, Tibet, Greece, Persia** and other regions.
**Nava Nalanda Mahavihara** — **Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap**; foundation stone laid on **20 November 1951**.
⚠ **Nalanda** is Gupta-founded; the other four mahaviharas are **Pala** foundations.
**Vikramashila** was founded by **Dharmapala**; **Odantapuri** by **Gopala**.

69.s: Vikramashila Mahavihara, at Antichak, lies in which district of Bihar?
69.x: Vikramashila is at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka (BPSC 2023 trap).
xa: It stood on the **Ganga**; its walls had **terracotta panels**.
**Atisha Dipankara Shrijnana** of Vikramashila revived Buddhism in Tibet.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the destruction of Pala-period centres of learning:
1. Their destruction by Bakhtiyar Khilji is generally placed around 1193–1200.
2. One tradition gives 1194 for the destruction of Nalanda.
3. Jagaddala was sacked in the early eleventh century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: The destruction is placed around 1193–1200, with 1194 for Nalanda in one tradition. Jagaddala was sacked in the early thirteenth century, not the eleventh.

69.s: Where is the Odantapuri Mahavihara located at present?
69.x: Odantapuri, built by Gopala, was at Bihar Sharif in Bihar.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about Vikramashila Mahavihara:
1. It was founded by Dharmapala.
2. It lies in Banka district of Bihar.
3. It was a centre of Tantric (Vajrayana) Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala and was a Vajrayana centre. It lies at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka.

69.s: Who founded the Nalanda Mahavihara?
69.x: Nalanda was founded by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I in the 5th century AD; the Palas only patronised it.

69.s: In which year was the foundation of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara laid?
69.x: Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap laid the foundation of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara on 20 November 1951.

69.s: Which mahavihara was founded by Gopala, the first Pala king?
69.x: Gopala built Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif); Vikramashila and Somapura were founded by Dharmapala and Jagaddala by Ramapala.

69.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Mahavihara) - List-II (Founder)
A. Nalanda - 1. Ramapala
B. Odantapuri - 2. Dharmapala
C. Vikramashila - 3. Kumaragupta I
D. Jagaddala - 4. Gopala
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
69.x: Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I, Odantapuri by Gopala, Vikramashila by Dharmapala and Jagaddala by Ramapala.

69.s: In which region was the Jagaddala Mahavihara, founded by Ramapala, located?
69.x: Jagaddala, founded by Ramapala, was in Varendra, now in Naogaon, Bangladesh.

69.s: Who laid the foundation of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1951?
69.x: The Nava Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap (foundation 20 November 1951).

69.s: By what name do Tibetan sources call the five great monasteries of the Pala period together?
69.x: Nalanda, Odantapuri, Vikramashila, Somapura and Jagaddala together are called the Panchamahavihara.

69.s: Which mahavihara, founded by Gopala, became a model for the monasteries of Tibet?
69.x: Odantapuri at Bihar Sharif, founded by Gopala, with about 12,000 monks, was a model for Tibetan monasteries.

69.s: Which one of the following places was not the center of learning during early medieval period?
69.x: Taxila (Gandhara, now Rawalpindi district, Pakistan) belongs to the early historic period and had declined long before; Nalanda, Vikramashila and Uddandapura (Odantapuri) flourished in the early medieval Pala age.

69.s: In the time of Harsha, of which tradition was Valabhi a centre?
69.x: Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in Harsha's time, distinct from the Pala Mahaviharas.
xa: **Taxila** = ancient **Gandhara** centre — also not Pala-era.
Nalanda was the **Mahayana** counterpart.
**Balaputradeva** built a monastery at **Nalanda**, not Valabhi.

69.s: Taxila, the odd one out among early medieval centres of learning, was the capital of which region?
69.x: Taxila was an early Buddhist centre and the capital of Gandhara, in present Rawalpindi district of Pakistan.

69.s: Which of the following studied at Taxila?
69.x: Taxila's students included Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya, Charaka and Jivaka. Atisha, Shilabhadra and Dharmakirti belong to the Pala-era mahaviharas.

69.s: Which of the following was NOT a mahavihara of the Pala period?
69.x: Somapura, Jagaddala and Vikramashila were Pala mahaviharas; Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in western India in Harsha's time.

69.s: Who was the founder of Pala dynasty?
69.x: Gopala, elected by the chiefs around 750 CE to end anarchy (matsyanyaya), founded the Pala dynasty; Dharmapala and Devapala were his successors.

69.s: How did Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, come to power?
o: Defeating the Sena ruler of Bengal
Inheritance from the later Guptas of Magadha
Election by notables to end matsyanyaya
69.x: Gopala was elected by regional notables in the mid-eighth century to end matsyanyaya, a period of anarchy.
xa: UPPSC 2021: kings chosen by the people = **Gopala** and **Nandivarman II Pallavamalla**.
Gopala built **Odantapuri** (APPSC GS 2018).
He also displaced the **Khadgas** of east Bengal.

69.s: The Pala founder Gopala displaced the Khadgas of which region?
69.x: Gopala displaced the later Guptas in Magadha and the Khadgas in eastern Bengal, and built Odantapuri.
xa: Odantapuri is at **Bihar Sharif**, Nalanda district; about **12,000** monks.
Odantapuri was a **model for Tibetan monasteries**.
Gopala was **elected** c. mid-**8th c.**

69.s: Which inscription records the election of Gopala as king?
69.x: The Khalimpur inscription of Dharmapala records Gopala's election. The Nalanda copper plate records Devapala's grant of five villages.

69.s: Gopala was elected by the notables to end a state of anarchy. What was it called?
69.x: Gopala was elected in the mid-8th century to end matsyanyaya, the 'law of the jungle'. The Kaivarta revolt came under Ramapala.

69.s: Near which place was Dharmapala defeated by Nagabhata II?
69.x: Dharmapala (c. 770-810) was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.
xa: Dharmapala ruled c. **770-810**.
**Somapura** (Paharpur, Bangladesh) is also credited to Dharmapala.
Buddhist texts were compiled at **Nalanda** under Dharmapala; his **seal** was found there.

69.s: Which Pala ruler is associated with the revival of Pala power and was defeated by Rajendra Chola?
69.x: Mahipala I, whose reign is placed around c. 977–1027, revived Pala power and was defeated by Rajendra Chola.
69.tq: Use the paired achievement to distinguish one ruler from the other Palas.
xs: **Mahipala I** (c. **977-1027**) revived Pala power and was defeated by **Rajendra Chola** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Gopala** was the elected founder; **Devapala** made the Nalanda grant; **Ramapala** was the last strong ruler.
xa: **Ramapala** (c. **1072-1126**): Kaivarta revolt, **Jagaddala**.
**Dharmapala** (c. **770-810**) founded **Vikramashila**.
The **Senas** succeeded the Palas in Bengal.

69.s: In the reign of which Pala ruler did the Kaivarta revolt take place?
69.x: Ramapala (c. 1072-1126), the last strong Pala ruler, faced the Kaivarta revolt and is associated with Jagaddala.
xa: **Ramacharita** by **Sandhyakar Nandi** is about Ramapala and the Kaivarta revolt.
**Vikramashila** reached its **zenith under Ramapala**.
Jagaddala (Varendra, Bangladesh) **translated books into Tibetan**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the grant to Balaputradeva's monastery at Nalanda:
1. The five villages were granted by Devapala.
2. The grant is recorded in the Nalanda copper plate.
3. The grant was made by Dharmapala, founder of Vikramashila.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Devapala granted the five villages, as the Nalanda copper plate records. Dharmapala founded Vikramashila but did not make this grant.

69.s: Which Pala ruler installed Chakrayudha on the throne of Kannauj?
69.x: Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj. Devapala is known for the Nalanda grant and Mahipala I for reviving Pala power.

69.s: Besides Nagabhata II, the Pala king Dharmapala was also defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
69.x: Dharmapala was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

69.s: Which Pala ruler founded both Vikramashila and Somapura?
69.x: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Somapura; Gopala built Odantapuri and Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I.
xa: ⚠ Trap (BPSC 2023): Vikramashila is in **Bhagalpur (not Banka)**.
**Jagaddala** was founded by **Ramapala**.

69.s: Who founded the Jagaddala Mahavihara?
69.x: Jagaddala in Varendra was founded by Ramapala, the last strong Pala ruler. Gopala built Odantapuri and Dharmapala Vikramashila.

69.s: A Buddhist monk who went to Tibet in the eleventh century to propagate Buddhism was:
69.x: Atisha Dipankara Srijnana of Vikramashila went to Tibet in the 11th century and revived Buddhism there; Nagarjuna and Vasubandhu were much earlier and Pujyapada was a Jain grammarian.

69.s: The ruler of Suvarnabhumi, who founded a Buddhist monastery at Nalanda and requested Devapala through his ambassador to grant five villages for its maintenance, was
69.x: Balaputradeva, the Shailendra king of Suvarnadvipa (Sumatra–Java), built a monastery at Nalanda and Devapala granted five villages for it (Nalanda copper plate).

69.s: The ruler of Suvarnabhumi, who founded a Buddhist Monastry at Nalanda and requested Devapala through his ambassador to grant five villages for its maintenance, was
69.x: Balaputradeva, the Shailendra ruler of Suvarnabhumi, built a monastery at Nalanda and his envoy obtained five villages from Devapala.

69.s: Which of the following acharya – association pairs is correctly matched?
o: Shantarakshita – Founded Samye monastery in Tibet
Sakya Sri Bhadra – Head of Nalanda in Harsha's time
69.x: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded Samye monastery in Tibet. Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time, Atisha was linked with Vikramashila and Sakya Sri Bhadra with Jagaddala.
xa: Sakya Sri Bhadra took **Tantric Buddhism** to Tibet.
⚠ Trap (BPSC 2025): **Kautilya** was not a Nalanda acharya.
Vikramashila trained monks for **Tibet**.

69.s: Which one of the following was NOT an acharya associated with the Buddhist mahaviharas such as Nalanda and Vikramashila?
69.x: Kautilya was not a Nalanda acharya (BPSC 2025 trap). Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time, Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded Samye monastery in Tibet, and Atisha of Vikramashila revived Buddhism in Tibet.
69.tq: Kautilya is the odd one out among Nalanda acharyas.
xs: **Kautilya** was not a Nalanda acharya — option **(2)** is the answer (BPSC 2025 trap).
**Shilabhadra** and **Shantarakshita** were Nalanda acharyas; **Atisha** was of **Vikramashila**.
xa: **Sakya Sri Bhadra** belonged to **Jagaddala**.
Andhra's **Dharmakirti** taught at Nalanda.
Nalanda was founded by **Kumaragupta I** (Gupta).
69.fixed: Shilabhadra (Harsha's time) is not Pala-era, so 'Pala-era' made option 1 also correct

69.s: Under whom did Andhra's Dharmakirti, who taught at Nalanda, study?
69.x: Dharmakirti studied under Dharmapala of Kanchi, the head of Nalanda (not the Pala king Dharmapala).
xa: Dharmapala of Kanchipuram was an **earlier head** of Nalanda; **Shilabhadra** headed it in Harsha's time.
**Ramacharita** is by **Sandhyakar Nandi**.

69.s: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded which monastery in Tibet?
69.x: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded the Samye monastery in Tibet.

69.s: With which mahavihara was Sakya Sri Bhadra, who took Tantric Buddhism to Tibet, associated?
69.x: Sakya Sri Bhadra belonged to Jagaddala. Atisha was from Vikramashila and Shantarakshita from Nalanda.

69.s: Who was the head of Nalanda in Harsha's time?
69.x: Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time.

69.s: With which mahavihara was Atisha Dipankara Srijnana, who went to Tibet in the eleventh century, associated?
69.x: Atisha Dipankara Srijnana of Vikramashila went to Tibet in the 11th century and revived Buddhism there.

69.s: Of which region was Balaputradeva, who set up a monastery at Nalanda, the ruler?
69.x: Balaputradeva was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa or Suvarnabhumi. His envoy requested Devapala to grant five villages for maintaining the monastery at Nalanda.
69.tq: Match the foreign ruler with his geographical and dynastic identity.
xs: **Balaputradeva** was the **Shailendra** ruler of **Suvarnadvipa/Suvarnabhumi** — option **(2)** is correct.
He built a **monastery at Nalanda**.
xa: At his envoy's request **Devapala granted five villages** (BPSC 2018; **Nalanda copper plate**).
**Pala-style bronzes** in Southeast Asia show maritime cultural exchange (UPSC).
**Kamarupa** and **Kalinga** came under Pala influence under **Ramapala**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about Balaputradeva:
1. He was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa.
2. His envoy obtained five villages for his Nalanda monastery from Dharmapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Balaputradeva was the Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa. The five villages were granted by Devapala, not Dharmapala.

69.s: Who among the following is credited with initiating a new Samvat :
69.x: The Sena king Lakshmanasena is credited with the Lakshmana Samvat (Lakshmana era); the Pala kings Dharmapala and Devapala started no era.

69.s: The Lakshman Era was started (in AD 1119) by which of the following dynasty?
69.x: The Lakshmana era (Lakshmana Samvat, reckoned from c. 1119 AD) is named after the Sena king Lakshmanasena of Bengal; the Pratiharas, Palas and Chauhans started no such era.

69.s: Who was the last Sena ruler, whose court poet was Jayadeva and who was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji?
69.x: Lakshmanasena was the last Sena ruler; Jayadeva was at his court and he was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji.
xa: Sena founders: **Samantasena** / **Vijayasena**, then **Ballalasena**.
Bakhtiyar Khilji also destroyed Pala-era centres c. **1193-1200**.

69.s: Who founded the Sena dynasty of Bengal?
69.x: Samantasena, from Karnataka and a Pala feudatory in Rarh, founded the Sena line. Vijayasena founded independent Sena rule.

69.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
69.x: The scholar king Ballalasena wrote Danasagara and Adbhutasagara. Jayadeva was Lakshmanasena's poet, and Lakshmanasena was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji.

69.s: Who founded independent Sena rule in Bengal?
69.x: Samantasena founded the line as a Pala feudatory; Vijayasena made Sena rule independent.

69.s: Nalanda University was destroyed by –
69.x: Nalanda was sacked by the army of the Turkish (Muslim) general Bakhtiyar Khalji at the end of the 12th century. The Kushans and Scythians were far earlier and the Mughals far later.

69.s: Which of the following sites have been introduced in UNESCO's heritage list in 2016?
69.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
69.x: Nalanda Mahavihara (Bihar) was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in July 2016. Jantar Mantar Jaipur was listed in 2010, the Goa churches in 1986 and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus in 2004.

69.s: On which material were the illustrated Buddhist manuscripts of the Pala period written?
69.x: Pala art includes bronze and black-stone sculpture and illustrated palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.
xa: Artists: **Dhiman** and his son **Vitapala** (per **Taranatha**).
**Pala-style bronzes** reached Southeast Asia.
Somapura: grand scale, rich **terracotta** ornamentation.

69.s: Who were Dhiman and his son Vitapala of the Pala period, mentioned by Taranatha?
69.x: Dhiman and his son Vitapala were noted artists of Pala art, as recorded by Taranatha.
xa: Pala sculpture: **bronze** and black-stone (**basalt**).
Manuscripts: **palm-leaf illustrated** Buddhist manuscripts.
Pala-style bronzes in **Southeast Asia** show maritime exchange.

69.s: Who wrote Ramacharita, a work dealing with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt?
69.x: Ramacharita was written by Sandhyakar Nandi and deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.
69.tq: Match the literary work with its author and subject.
xs: **Sandhyakar Nandi** wrote **Ramacharita** — option **(3)** is correct.
It deals with **Ramapala** and the **Kaivarta** peasant revolt.
**Jayadeva** was **Lakshmanasena**'s poet; **Taranatha** recorded the artists **Dhiman** and **Vitapala**.
xa: Ramapala (c. **1072-1126**) was the last strong Pala.
Ramapala founded **Jagaddala**.
**Atisha Dipankara** of Vikramashila revived Buddhism in Tibet.

69.s: In which materials was Pala sculpture chiefly made?
69.x: Pala sculpture is known for bronze and black-stone (basalt) images.

69.s: Where is the grand-scale Pala terracotta decoration best seen?
69.x: Somapura shows Pala terracotta on a grand scale; Vikramashila has terracotta wall panels.

69.s: Sandhyakar Nandi's Ramacharita deals with which Pala ruler?
69.x: Ramacharita by Sandhyakar Nandi deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.

70.s: Which of the following rulers does not belong to Gurjara- Pratihara dynasty?
70.x: Bhartripatta (Bharatrabhatta) I was a Guhila ruler of Mewar, not a Pratihara. Nagabhata II, Mahendrapala I and a later Devapala (c. 948–954) were all Gurjara-Pratihara kings.

70.s: The Gurjar-Pratihara dynasty was founded by :
70.x: Nagabhata I (c. 730–760), who repulsed the Arabs, founded the imperial Gurjara-Pratihara line; Vatsaraja and Mihira Bhoja came later and Harsha was a Pushyabhuti.

70.s: Which one of the following ruler is not related to Gurjar-Pratihara dynasty?
70.x: Bhartripatta (Bharatrabhatta) I was a Guhila of Mewar; Nagabhata I, Mahendrapala I and a later Devapala (c. 948–954) were Pratihara kings.

70.s:
Arrange the names of the following historical personalities in correct chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below:
1. Nagabhatta II
2. Mahipala
3. Mahendrapala
4. Vatsaraja
Codes :
70.x: Vatsaraja (c. 780–800), Nagabhata II (800–833), Mahendrapala I (885–910), Mahipala (912–944): 4, 1, 3, 2.

70.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kannauj around 916 CE — Mahipala I defeated Indra III
Bundelkhand campaign — Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II
Early ninth-century Kannauj — Nagabhata II defeated Chakrayudha
70.x: Around 916 CE, Indra III defeated Mahipala I and sacked Kannauj. The other three pairs correctly identify the campaigns and victors.
70.tq: Find the reversed victor–defeated pair in the battle table.
xs: "**Mahipala I** defeated **Indra III**" is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer.
Around **916**, **Indra III** sacked Kannauj, defeating Mahipala I.
**Govinda III** beat **Nagabhata II** (Bundelkhand); Nagabhata II ousted **Chakrayudha** and beat **Dharmapala** near **Monghyr**.
xa: **Mahmud of Ghazni** attacked Kannauj in **1018**.
⚠ **Vatsaraja** lost to Dhruva; **Nagabhata II** to Govinda III.
Rajashekhara served **Mahipala I** as well as Mahendrapala I.

70.s: The Pratihara king Vatsaraja, after taking Kannauj and defeating Dharmapala, was defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
70.x: Vatsaraja took Kannauj and defeated Dharmapala but was later defeated by the Rashtrakuta Dhruva, marking the beginning of the tripartite struggle.
xa: Vatsaraja ruled c. **780-800**.
Some notes say he made Kannauj capital; others say he only conquered it.

70.s: Near which place did the Pratihara king Nagabhata II defeat the Pala ruler Dharmapala?
70.x: Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha, defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital.
xa: Govinda III's defeat of him came in a **Bundelkhand** campaign.
His grandson **Mihira Bhoja** was the son of **Ramabhadra**.
The **Gwalior prashasti** records his victories.

70.s: Which Pratihara ruler came immediately after Vatsaraja?
70.x: The order is Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihira Bhoja, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala, so Nagabhata II followed Vatsaraja.
n: Vatsaraja preceded Nagabhata II in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Nagabhata II preceded Mahendrapala I in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mahendrapala I preceded Mahipala in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]

70.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated the Pratihara king Nagabhata II?
70.x: Nagabhata II was defeated by Govinda III, while his predecessor Vatsaraja lost to Dhruva.

70.s: Which Pratihara ruler bore the title 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'?
70.x: Mahendrapala I (c. 885–910) was styled Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta and patronised Rajashekhara.

70.s: 'Aadi Varaha' was the title of which Gurjar Pratihara ruler?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja, a Vaishnava, took the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa; Adivaraha appears on his coins.

70.s: The greatest Pratihara King was –
70.x: Mihira Bhoja (836–885) was the greatest Pratihara king. Dharmapala was a Pala, Harsha a Pushyabhuti, and Mahendrapala I was Bhoja's son.

70.s: What is/are not true about King Mihir Bhoja? (i) He was the son of Nagabhatta-II (ii) Kannauj was the capital of his kingdom. (iii)Arab traveller Al-Masudi gave him name of King Baura.
70.x: Only (i) is false: Mihira Bhoja was the son of Ramabhadra and grandson of Nagabhata II. Kannauj was his capital, and Al-Masudi called the king 'Baura'.

70.s: Mihira Bhoja was the grandson of Nagabhata II. Who was his father?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja was the son of Ramabhadra and therefore the grandson of Nagabhata II.
xa: Bhoja's capital: **Kannauj (Mahodaya)**.
Title **Adivaraha** — a devotee of Vishnu.
Bhoja ruled c. **836-890**, the dynasty's zenith.

70.s: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around which year?
70.x: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD and made it the Pratihara capital. 629 AD relates to Hiuen Tsang's journey.
70.tq: Place Mihir Bhoja in the early 9th century.
n: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
xs: **Mihir Bhoja** captured **Kannauj** around **836 AD** and made it his capital — option **(1)**.
His reign: c. **836-890**, the **zenith** of the dynasty.
**916** is when **Indra III** sacked Kannauj under **Mahipala I**.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say **Nagabhata II** made Kannauj the capital.
Titles: **Adivaraha** (UPPSC 2017) and **Prabhasa**; he followed **Vaishnavism**.
The **Barah copper plate** mentions a skandhavara at **Mahodaya**.
He built **Teli-ka-Mandir, Gwalior**.

70.s: Which ruler of Kashmir checked the expansion of the Pratihara king Mihira Bhoja?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja's expansion was checked by Sankaravarman of Kashmir, along with the Rashtrakuta Krishna II and the Pala Devapala.
xa: Bhoja's title: **Adivaraha**.
Sulaiman called him "**Juzr**".

70.s: Which of the following pairs about the Pratiharas is correctly matched?
70.x: Mihir Bhoja took the title Adivaraha. The Pratiharas first ruled from Ujjain, later from Kannauj, and Mihir Bhoja followed Vaishnavism.
n: Ujjain was the first capital of the Pratiharas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Kannauj was the later capital of the Pratiharas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja was known by the title Adivaraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja was known by the title Prabhasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja followed Vaishnavism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja made Kannauj his capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
xa: The dynasty was **founded** by **Nagabhata I**.
⚠ Other notes give an earlier capital at **Bhinmal** (Rajasthan), before Ujjain.
"Pratihara" = door-keeper; they claimed descent from **Lakshmana**.
Mihira Bhoja was the **grandson of Nagabhata II** (son of **Ramabhadra**).

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Mihira Bhoja:
1. He was the son of Ramabhadra.
2. He was the grandson of Nagabhata II.
3. His coins carry a Shaiva legend.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja was Ramabhadra's son and Nagabhata II's grandson. His coins carry the Vaishnava legend Adivaraha, not a Shaiva one.

70.s: Besides Adivaraha, which title did Mihira Bhoja bear?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja bore the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa. Nripatunga and Viranarayana were Amoghavarsha I's, Prabhutavarsha Govinda III's.

70.s: Which title of Mihira Bhoja reflects his devotion to Vishnu and also appears as a legend on his coins?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja bore the title Adivaraha, reflecting his devotion to Vishnu; Adivaraha also appeared on his coins.
70.tq: Match the ruler with the title and its numismatic association.
xs: **Adivaraha** reflects Bhoja's devotion to Vishnu and appears on his coins — option **(3)** is correct (UPPSC 2017).
**Juzr** was Sulaiman's name for him; **Aryavarta** is in Mahendrapala I's title; **Mahodaya** = Kannauj.
xa: Al-Masudi called him "**Baura**".
Bhoja built the **Teli-ka-Mandir**, Gwalior.

70.s: The Arab traveller Suleman visited India in the reign of Pratihar King –
70.x: The Arab merchant Sulaiman (c. 851) wrote of the Pratihara kingdom in the reign of Mihira Bhoja (Bhoja I), praising his cavalry.

70.s: By what name did the Arab merchant Sulaiman (mid-9th century) refer to Mihira Bhoja?
70.x: Sulaiman called Mihira Bhoja 'Juzr' or 'Al-Juzr'; 'Baura' was Al-Masudi's name for him and Adivaraha was Bhoja's own title on his coins.
xa: Sulaiman came in the mid-**9th c.**, in **Bhoja I**'s reign (RPSC 2023).
Sulaiman named **Amoghavarsha** one of the four great kings of the world.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arab traveller Sulaiman:
1. He praised the Pratihara cavalry.
2. He named Amoghavarsha I one of the four great kings of the world.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
70.x: Sulaiman praised the Pratihara cavalry and named the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I one of the four great kings of the world.
xa: Sulaiman came in the mid-**9th c.**, in **Bhoja I**'s reign.
Al-Masudi called Bhoja "**Baura**".
⚠ **Juzr** = Sulaiman's name; **Baura** = Al-Masudi's.

70.s: By what name did the Arab writer Al-Masudi call the Pratihara king?
70.x: Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king Baura; Juzr is Sulaiman's name for the kingdom, and Balhara was the Arab term for Rashtrakuta kings.

70.s: The great Sanskrit poet and dramatist Rajashekhara was in the court of:
70.x: Rajashekhara (Karpuramanjari, Kavyamimamsa) was the court poet of the Pratihara Mahendrapala I and also of his son Mahipala I; Mahendrapala I is the standard answer.

70.s: The great Sanskrit poet and dramatist, Raj Shekhara was in the court of
70.x: Rajashekhara was the court poet of Mahendrapala I (and later Mahipala I), not of Raja Bhoja of Dhar or the Rashtrakuta Indra III.

70.s: Rajashekhara was associated with the courts of which of the following rulers?
70.x: Rajashekhara was the court poet of Mahendrapala I and was also associated with the court of Mahipala I.
70.tq: Match the court poet with both of his recorded patrons.
xs: Rajashekhara served **Mahendrapala I** and **Mahipala I** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Indra III** and **Krishna II** were Rashtrakutas, not his patrons.
xa: Works: **Kavyamimamsa**, **Karpuramanjari**, **Viddhasalabhanjika**.
Mahendrapala I ruled c. **890-910**.
Kannauj was sacked by **Indra III** under Mahipala I.

70.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Rajashekhara?
70.x: Prabandhachintamani was written by Merutunga, whereas Kavyamimamsa, Karpuramanjari and Viddhasalabhanjika were works of Rajashekhara.
70.tq: Use the author–work distinction to identify the wrongly attributed work.
xs: **Prabandhachintamani** is not Rajashekhara's — it is by **Merutunga** — option **(3)** is the answer (MPPSC 2025).
Rajashekhara wrote **Kavyamimamsa**, **Karpuramanjari** and **Viddhasalabhanjika**.
xa: **Kavyamimamsa** is on poetics; **Karpuramanjari** is a **Prakrit play**.
Rajashekhara was court poet of **Mahendrapala I** (and **Mahipala I**).

70.s: Who wrote the Prabandhachintamani?
70.x: Prabandhachintamani is Merutunga's work, not Rajashekhara's.

70.s: What does the term 'Pratihara' traditionally mean?
70.x: Pratihara means door-keeper. The dynasty claimed descent from Lakshmana, who was regarded as Rama's door-keeper brother.
70.tq: Distinguish the literal meaning of the dynastic name from its origin legend.
xs: "Pratihara" means **door-keeper** — option **(1)** is correct.
The dynasty claimed descent from **Lakshmana**, Rama's door-keeper brother.
"Fire-born" refers to the separate **Agnikula legend** of **Mount Abu**.
xa: "**Gurjara**" is read as a tribe/people or as the region **Gurjaratra**.
Capitals: **Bhinmal → Ujjain/Avanti → Kannauj (Mahodaya)**.
Founder **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) resisted the Arabs.

70.s: According to the Agnikula legend in Prithviraj Raso, which group of dynasties was born from the fire-pit at Mount Abu?
70.x: The Agnikula legend associates the Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras and Chauhans with birth from the fire-pit at Mount Abu.
70.tq: Recall the complete legendary group rather than a partial pair.
xs: The Agnikula clans are the **Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras and Chauhans** — option **(1)** is correct.
The legend, from **Prithviraj Raso**, has them born from the fire-pit at **Mount Abu**.
xa: **Chauhans**, **Paramaras** and **Chaulukyas** later broke away from the Pratiharas as feudatories.
"Pratihara" = **door-keeper**.
Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho**.

70.s: Besides the Harshacharita, in which source are the Gurjaras first mentioned?
70.x: The Gurjaras are first mentioned in the Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II and Banabhatta's Harshacharita.

70.s: From whom did the Pratiharas claim descent?
70.x: 'Pratihara' means door-keeper; they claimed descent from Lakshmana, Rama's door-keeper brother.

70.s: Where was the early seat of the Gurjaras?
70.x: Bhinmal in Rajasthan was the early Gurjara seat; Ujjain and then Kannauj (Mahodaya) came later.

70.s: What was the capital of the Pratihara founder Nagabhata I?
70.x: Nagabhata I ruled from Ujjain (Avanti). Kannauj became the capital from Nagabhata II.

70.s: By what other name was Kannauj, the Pratihara capital from Nagabhata II's time, known?
70.x: Kannauj was also called Mahodaya; the Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions a camp there.

70.s: Which copper plate of Mihira Bhoja mentions a camp (skandhavara) at Mahodaya?
70.x: The Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions his camp at Mahodaya (Kannauj).

70.s: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the main power that kept Arab rule confined to which region?
70.x: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the principal power that helped keep Arab rule confined to Sindh.
xa: Sulaiman praised Pratihara **cavalry** as the best in India.
He also praised their **army, wealth and security**.
Hiuen Tsang had described the **Sun temple of Multan**.

70.s: Which ruler of Sindh was defeated and killed by Muhammad bin Qasim?
70.x: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion of Sindh, defeated and killed Raja Dahir, and his conquest stayed largely within Sindh and Multan.
n: Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s invasion was an Arab invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Dahir was defeated and killed by Muhammad-bin-Qasim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s conquest was largely confined to Sindh and Multan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
xa: The date is also given as **711–12 CE**.
The Pratiharas were the main power that kept Arab rule confined to **Sindh**.
Founder **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) **resisted the Arabs**.
**Mahmud of Ghazni** attacked Kannauj in **1018**.

70.s: In which year did Muhammad bin Qasim take Sindh?
70.x: Muhammad bin Qasim took Sindh in 712, defeating and killing Raja Dahir.

70.s: The Gwalior inscription of Mihira Bhoja credits whom with repulsing the mleccha (Arab) army?
70.x: The Gwalior inscription says Nagabhata I repulsed the mleccha army.

70.s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni attack Kannauj, hastening the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas?
70.x: Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Kannauj in 1018, one of the blows (with Indra III's raid and the secession of feudatories) that weakened Pratihara power.
xa: The **Chandelas** were based at **Khajuraho**.
Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho** (UNESCO site).
Indra III's sack is dated c. **916**.

70.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler looted Kannauj around 916, defeating the Pratihara Mahipala I?
70.x: Indra III raided Kannauj c. 916, defeating Mahipala I.

70.s: Which breakaway Pratihara feudatory is associated with Khajuraho?
70.x: The Chandelas of Khajuraho were among the feudatories that broke away as Pratihara power declined.

71.s: The magnificent temple of Kailasa was erected by
71.x: The monolithic Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16) was carved under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I, not Govinda II, Krishna II or Dantidurga.

71.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched with respect to Rashtrakutas?
o: Amoghavarsha: the first Kannada book writer
Dantidurga: the founder of Rashtrakuta kingdom
Krishna-III: the famous rock-cut temple of Shiva at Ellora
71.x: The wrong pair is Krishna III – Ellora: the Kailasa rock-cut Shiva temple was carved under Krishna I. Amoghavarsha's Kavirajamarga is the earliest available Kannada book, Dantidurga founded the dynasty, and Al-Masudi (915–16) wrote of the 'Balhara' (Vallabharaja).

71.s: Which among the following Rashtrakuta ruler built the Kailas temple of Ellora?
71.x: The Kailasa temple of Ellora was built by Krishna I; Govinda II, Amoghavarsha and Indra III are known for other things.

71.s: Who among the following was born in a military camp in the course of his father’s campaign?
71.x: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD in a military camp at Shribhavan on the Narmada while his father Govinda III was returning from the north.

71.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler built the famous Shiva temple of Ellora?
71.x: Krishna I built the rock-cut Shiva (Kailasa) temple at Ellora, not Dantidurga, Krishna II or Govinda III.

71.s: Kailasa temple of Ellora was constituted by
71.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I; Krishna III is the usual trap.

71.s: In which battle did the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III defeat the Cholas?
71.x: Krishna III defeated the Cholas at Takkolam (949 CE).
xa: Takkolam (**949 CE**): Chola **Parantaka I** defeated, prince **Rajaditya** killed.
Krishna III patronised the poet **Ponna**.
The Kailasa is a **monolithic** temple.

71.s: Who was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to march into northern India?
71.x: Dhruva was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to move north; he defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala.
xa: Against Vengi he acted through **Vemulavada Arikesari I**, beating **Vishnuvardhana IV**.
Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter **Shila Mahadevi** to Dhruva.
His successor **Govinda III** reached the **Himalayas**.

71.s: Which one of the following was a military achievement of Govinda III?
o: Sacking Kannauj in the reign of Indra III
Defeating Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reaching the Himalayas
71.x: Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and is said in the Sanjan plates to have reached the Himalayas.
71.tq: Separate the military achievements of successive Rashtrakuta rulers instead of matching all northern campaigns together.
xs: **Govinda III** defeated **Nagabhata II** and **Dharmapala** and **reached the Himalayas** — option **(2)** is correct.
His Himalayan march is recorded in the **Sanjan plates**; defeat of Nagabhata II: UKPSC 2021.
**Takkolam** was **Krishna III**'s victory; **Tailapa II** overthrew the Rashtrakutas.
xa: Govinda III reigned **793-814**.
His title: **Prabhutavarsha**.
He was followed by **Amoghavarsha I** (**814-878**).

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the order of Rashtrakuta rulers:
1. Dantidurga ruled from 753 to 756.
2. Dhruva ruled before Govinda III.
3. Amoghavarsha I ruled before Govinda III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: The order is Dantidurga (753-756), Dhruva (780-793), Govinda III (793-814) and Amoghavarsha I (814-878). Amoghavarsha I came after Govinda III.

71.s: Amoghavarsha I is particularly associated with which of the following combinations?
71.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, was associated with Kavirajamarga, and is described as a Jain ruler or patron.
71.tq: Use a cluster of contributions to identify the ruler rather than relying on a single isolated fact.
xs: Amoghavarsha I = **Manyakheta**, **Kavirajamarga** and **Jainism** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kailasa** = Krishna I; **Takkolam** = Krishna III; **Gadayuddha** = **Ranna**; **Hiranyagarbha** = Dantidurga.
xa: Amoghavarsha won at **Vingavalli** (title **Viranarayana**); also titled **Nripatunga**.
He also wrote the Sanskrit Jain text **Prashnottara Ratnamalika**.
**Sulaiman** called him one of the **four great kings** of the world.

71.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD.
Amoghavarsha I was born in a military camp.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Manyakheta.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Shribhavan.

Were the first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition in the Deccan

xs: The **Durga temple**, Aihole, has an **apsidal (gajaprishtha) plan** with a **pillared gallery** round the shrine — option **(1)**.

xa: Durga temple carries a **Nagara** shikhara on its apsidal plan.
Aihole = "**Cradle of Indian temple architecture**" (Nilakanta Sastri).

A rekha shikhara on an apsidal plan

Ravana Phadi — Aihole — rock-cut cave with a tower

**Huchimalligudi** (Aihole) is **Nagara** (UPSC 2026).
**Lad Khan** is one of the earliest temples, dedicated to **Shiva**.

75.s: Which of the following pairs of temples both have a Nagara shikhara?

xs: **Huchimalligudi (Aihole)** and **Dashavatara (Deogarh)** both have a **Nagara** shikhara — option **(2)** (UPSC 2026 key).
**Malegitti Shivalaya**, **Virupaksha**, **Meguti** and **Sangameshvara** are **Dravida**, so every other pair fails.
xa: Pattadakal Nagara temples: **Papanatha**, **Kashi Vishwanatha**, **Galaganatha**.
**Durga** temple, Aihole: Nagara shikhara on an **apsidal** plan.
**Lad Khan** has **no shikhara** at all.

75.s: Which Jain temple at Aihole is built in the Dravida style and bears the Aihole inscription?

**Virupaksha** copies the Pallava **Kailasanatha**; the Rashtrakuta **Kailasa (Ellora)** continues the line.

75.s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal copies the tradition of which temple?
75.x: The Dravida-style Virupaksha temple copies the Pallava Kailasanatha tradition of Kanchi, a line continued by the Rashtrakuta Kailasa at Ellora.

Its architects: **Gunda Anivaritachari** and **Sarvasiddhi Acharya**.

75.x: Pattadakal served as the royal coronation site of the Badami Chalukyas.

o: Pattadakal – UNESCO site with Nagara and Dravida temples side by side

75.x: Queen Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple for Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

76.x: Manchikallu (Simhavarman) and Mayidavolu (Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja, Prakrit) are early Pallava records from the Guntur region.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about Narasimhavarman I:

2. Mahabalipuram is called Mamallapuram after him.
3. Vichitrachitta was one of his titles.

76.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mamalla and Vatapikonda were his titles. Statement 2 is correct: Mamallapuram is named after him. Statement 3 is wrong: Vichitrachitta was a title of his father Mahendravarman I. So B; A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
76.tq: Mamalla/Vatapikonda = Narasimhavarman I; Vichitrachitta/Chitrakarapuli = Mahendravarman I.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Narasimhavarman I** bore the titles **Mamalla** ("great wrestler") and **Vatapikonda**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram)** is named after him.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Vichitrachitta** was **Mahendravarman I**'s title — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Reign **630-668**; took **Vatapi (642)**.
He built the monolithic **rathas** at Mahabalipuram; staunch **Shaivite**.
**Nandivarman II**'s title: **Pallavamalla**.

He was Pulakesin II's enemy, not his supporter.
xa: He killed **Pulakesin II** at **Manimangala (642)** and sacked **Vatapi**.
Titles **Mamalla** and **Vatapikonda**.

77.s: During whose reign was the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram built?

77.s: Besides two Shiva shrines, the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram has a shrine of which deity?
