Of the above, the correct statements are
78.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(B) VRO/Village Surveyor
78.x: Both are correct: Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI) built Rajamahendravaram, and the Rajahmundry district of the Madras Presidency was created in 1823 (split into Godavari and Krishna districts in 1859).

78.s: What was the name of the new city built by Ammaraja I (921-927), believed to be the cultural capital of the Andhras?
78.x: Ammaraja I (921-927) built Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry), later the cultural capital of the Andhras.

78.s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was developed under which dynasty?
78.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

78.s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was built during whose reign?
78.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

78.s: Which region formed Venginadu, the core territory of the Eastern Chalukyas?
78.x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab (Venginadu), with capitals at Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.
xa: Pithapuram = first capital (**Kubja**); Vengi/Pedavegi = **Jayasimha I**; Rajahmundry = **Ammaraja I**, beautified by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Dandin called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".

78.s: Who shifted the capital of the Eastern Chalukyas to Vengi?
78.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.
78.tq: Match a capital change with the ruler responsible for it.
xs: **Jayasimha Vallabha I** shifted the capital to **Vengi** (Pedavegi, near Eluru) — option **(4)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** ruled from **Pithapuram**; **Amma I** made **Rajamahendravaram** capital.
xa: Jayasimha I issued the **Vipparla inscription** (G2 2017 key).
Title: **Samastha Bhuvanashraya**.
Core territory: **Venginadu** (Krishna-Godavari doab).

78.s: Arrange the capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas in chronological order:
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana ruled from Pithapuram, Jayasimha Vallabha I moved to Vengi, and Rajamahendravaram is linked with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: another sequence is **Vengipura (Pedavegi) → Rajahmundry → Pithapuram → Vengi** again.
Vengi = **Pedavegi, near Eluru**.
APPSC G2 2008 key: Rajaraja Narendra "**built Rajahmundry**".

78.s: By what name is Vengi referred to in Dandin's Dashakumaracharita?
78.x: Dandin calls Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'. Mangalapura is Mangalagiri in the Kopparam inscription, Pishtapura is Pithapuram, and Rajamahendra is a title of Ammaraja I.
78.tq: Dandin: Vengi = Andhra Nagaram.
xs: **Dandin**'s **Dashakumaracharita** calls Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**" — option **(2)**.
**Mangalapura** = Mangalagiri (Kopparam inscription); **Pishtapura** = Pithapuram; **Rajamahendra** = Ammaraja I's title.
xa: Vengi = **Pedavegi**, near **Eluru**.
Capital moved to Vengi by **Jayasimha Vallabha I**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura.
2. The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
78.x: Both are correct: the Marturu inscription calls Mangalagiri Mangalapura, and the Vipparla inscription was issued by the Eastern Chalukya Jayasimha Vallabha.
n: The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]

**Magallu** inscription of **Danarnava** gives the **first mention** of the **Kakatiyas**.
**Nandampudi** grant of Rajaraja Narendra was **written by Nannaya**.
⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** = first Telugu inscription.

78.x: Bezawada came to be called Vijayawada after Vijayaditya.

78.x: Ammaraja I bore the title Rajamahendra; Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) is named after it.

78.x: The capitals moved from Pithapuram to Vengi and then to Rajamahendravaram, which Ammaraja I made the capital.

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital of the Eastern Chalukyas.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital, and Rajaraja Narendra later ruled from it and made it famous.

78.s: With which present place is Vengi, the second capital of the Eastern Chalukyas, identified?
78.x: Vengi is Pedavegi near Eluru; Jayasimha I shifted the capital there from Pithapuram.

78.s: Which dynasty gave prominence to Jain religion and worked for its propagation in Telugu land?
78.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
78.x: The Vemulawada Chalukyas (Karimnagar), patrons of Pampa and Somadeva Suri, did most to propagate Jainism in Telugu land; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya. The Eastern Chalukyas only patronised Jainism alongside Shaivism.

78.s: The great Vishnu temple of Kunti Madhava at Pithapuram was constructed by
78.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
78.x: The first Eastern Chalukya king, Kubja Vishnuvardhana, a Vaishnava, built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

78.s: Who built the 'Nedumbasadi' for the Jains?
78.x: Ayyana Mahadevi, Jain queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana, built the Nedumbasadi at Bezawada for the Kavaruragana Jains (Musinikonda inscription).

78.x: Ayyana Mahadevi, who built the Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada, was the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana.

78.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler promoted Jainism?
78.src: APPSC Junior Assistants in Labs / Panchayat Raj 2012
78.x: Vimaladitya was the only Eastern Chalukya king who converted to Jainism (guru Trikalayogi Siddhanti; Ramatirtha cave).

78.s: Who built the great Vishnu temple called Kunti Madhava Temple in Pithapuram?
78.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
78.x: The first Eastern Chalukya king, Kubja Vishnuvardhana, a Vaishnava, built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

78.s: Which of the following ruling dynasties gave great importance to Jainism and worked tirelessly to spread that religion in andhra desa?
78.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
78.x: The Vemulawada Chalukyas (Karimnagar), patrons of Pampa and Somadeva Suri, did most to propagate Jainism in Telugu land; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya. The Eastern Chalukyas only patronised Jainism alongside Shaivism.

78.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
78.x: Bhima – Draksharama (3); Eastern Chalukyas – Pancharama kshetras (4); Rajaraja Narendra – Chalukya-Chola architecture (2); Kakatiyas – Shaivism almost destroyed Jainism (1).

78.s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
78.tq: Use the temple–builder pair rather than confusing it with later Vengi temples.
xs: The **Kunti Madhava** temple at **Pithapuram** is credited to **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
**Rajaraja Narendra** built the **Rajaraja temple**, Bikkavolu; **Chalukya Bhima I** the **Bhimeswara** temples.
xa: Pithapuram (**Pishtapura**) was Kubja's **first capital**.
Kubja = founder; brother of **Pulakesin II**; independent in **624 CE**.
⚠ "108 Shaivalayas" → **Vijayaditya II**, not Kubja.

78.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler granted Mushikonda village to the Jains?
78.x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.
xa: He took the throne back from **Kokkili**, who then set up the **Yalamanchili** kingdom.
APP gives him the titles **Tribhuvanankusa, Samasta Bhuvanashraya** (with Jayasimha I).
**Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre of the period.

78.s: Who issued the Maliyapundi grant to a Jain temple at Dharmapuri?
78.x: Ammaraja II issued the Maliyapundi grant at the request of his vassal Durgaraja.

78.s: Which grant records Queen Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati?
78.x: The Musinikonda grant of Vishnuvardhana III records Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati.

78.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Vengi school of Eastern Chalukya architecture)?
o: Name of the style – Vesara or Chalukya
Vimana – Dravidian form with Buddhist influence
Base of the temple – raised jagati
78.x: The Vengi school used local sandstone, not granite; the Vesara/Chalukya name, Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence and raised jagati are correct.
xa: The Vengi school is described as **Dravida** style.
Key temples: **Pancharamas** (Bhimarama, Draksharama).
**Bikkavolu** temples: Gunaga Vijayaditya III; **Rajaraja temple**: Rajaraja Narendra.

78.s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
78.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
78.tq: Start from the sure temple group and match it to its builder.
xs: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** built the **Bikkavolu** Shiva temples — **Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara, Chandrashekhara** — option **(1)**.
**Kunti Madhava** = Kubja; **Bhimeswara** = Chalukya Bhima I; **Rajaraja temple**, Rajahmundry **Vishnu** temple and **Kalidindi** = Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: **Vijayeshwara** has carved **Ganga and Yamuna** figures.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III = **greatest** king (APHQ 2011).
He developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada**.

78.s: Who built the Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot?
78.x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
78.tq: Distinguish the Bhimeswara temples from the separate 108-temple tradition.
xs: The **Bhimeswara** temples at **Draksharama** and **Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram)** are attributed to **Chalukya Bhima I** — option **(2)**.
**Vijayaditya II** = **108 Shiva temples**; **Kubja** = **Kunti Madhava**; **Rajaraja Narendra** = Rajaraja temple.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I built the **Pancharamas** (Bhimarama, Draksharama).
He ruled **30 years**; **360 battles** per Mallappadeva's Pithapuram inscription.
Title: **Kollabhiganda**.

78.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
78.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
78.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.
xs: **Bhimarama** is one of the **Pancharamas** — option **(4)**; **Draksharama** is another.
**Vijayeshwara** and **Chandrashekhara** are Bikkavolu temples; **Kunti Madhava** is at Pithapuram.
xa: The Pancharamas were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
**Bhimeswara** temples: **Draksharama** and **Samalkot**.
Dominant faith: **Shaivism**.

78.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
78.x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.
78.tq: Test an unusual person–grant association, a common source of identity traps.
xs: **Chamekamba**, courtesan under **Ammaraja II**, won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant for a Jain temple — option **(4)**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati** near Vijayawada; **Kundavva** was the Chola mother of Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: ⚠ Ayyana Mahadevi = queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** per G2 2025 key (some notes: Gunaga Vijayaditya III).
**Vishnuvardhana III** granted **Mushikonda** to Jains; **Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre.
Mother goddess: **Kushmandini** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

78.s: Ayyana Mahadevi built the Jain Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati near Vijayawada. Whose queen was she?
78.x: The standard view (Musinikonda grant) makes Ayyana Mahadevi the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana; note that the APPSC 2025 key gave Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Ammaraja II is linked to Chamekamba and the Kaluchumbarru grant, and Vimaladitya married Kundavai.
78.tq: Nedumba Vasati = Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of Kubja (key).

78.s: Kokkili belongs to which dynasty?

78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana I, founder of the Eastern Chalukyas, bore the title Vishamasiddhi (also Makaradhwaja).

78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesin II, founded the Eastern Chalukya line of Vengi in 624.

78.x: Kollabhiganda was the title of Vijayaditya IV, son of Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled six months and died near Virajapuri fighting Kalinga.

78.s: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They initially ruled as subordinates to the Badami Chalukyas.
They were defeated and annexed by the Rashtrakutas.

78.x: The Vengi Chalukyas began as subordinates of Badami, promoted early Telugu literature and lasted 624-1075; they fought the Rashtrakutas for two centuries but were never annexed - they merged into the Chola line.

78.s: Which one of the following were the contemporaries to the Eastern Chalukyas in the south?
78.src: Social and Cultural History of AP and Welfare Programmes 201
78.x: The Pallavas of Kanchi were the southern contemporaries of the early Eastern Chalukyas (Jayasimha I clashed with them); the Ikshvakus were earlier, the Mughals later and the Palas in Bengal.

78.x: The Cholas had close political and marriage ties with the Chalukyas of Vengi: Kundavai–Vimaladitya, Ammanga Devi–Rajaraja Narendra, Madhurantaki–Kulottunga I.

78.x: Nivartana, kharidika and khari were Eastern Chalukya units of land area, based on the seed sown.

78.s: In which year did Kubja Vishnuvardhana declare his independence and found the Eastern Chalukya line?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana became viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.

xs: The matronymic "**Hariti Putra**" was used like the **Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas** — option **(4)**.

Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**.

78.s: After 973 CE, who was the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas?

78.s:
Assertion (A): The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

78.x: Both are true: the Eastern Chalukyas branched from the Badami line because Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakeshin II's brother, founded their rule in Vengi.

Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, later became an important centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]

79.x: Bhattavamana was Kavi Vrishabha; the other titles belonged to Vishnuvardhana III, Ammaraja II and Rajaraja Narendra.

79.s: Who had the title 'Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu'?
79.x: Vishnuvardhana III was Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu; Ammaraja II was Kavigayaka Kalpataru.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s: Chellavva of the Eastern Chalukya court is known by which title?
79.x: Chellavva, court singer of Chalukya Bhima I, had the title Gandharva-vidya-visarada. Kavi Vrishabha was Bhattavamana's title.

79.s: Who was the father of Chellavva, compared to Tumburu in the Attili inscription?
79.x: The Attili inscription compares Mallappa, Chellavva's father, to Tumburu.

79.s: What is the subject of Ugradityacharya's Kalyanakaraka?
79.x: Kalyanakaraka is a Jain Ayurvedic book on diagnosis and treatment, written by Ugradityacharya.

79.s: Ugradityacharya, author of the Kalyanakaraka, was a Jain scholar of which place?
79.x: Ugradityacharya was a Jain scholar of Ramatirtha.

79.s: In whose court was Bhattavamana, author of the Kavyalankara Sutras?
79.x: Bhattavamana (title Kavi Vrishabha) was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I.

79.s: Which Agama is common for Ramanuja and Madhva Philosophers?
79.x: Both Ramanuja (Sri Vaishnavism) and Madhva follow the Pancharatra Agama; Vaikhanasa is the other Vaishnava agama, used at Tirumala, and Shaakta/Jangama are non-Vaishnava.

79.s: Which agama tradition is followed to perform rituals in Srivari temple Tirumala?
79.x: Worship at the Srivari (Venkateswara) temple, Tirumala, follows the Vaikhanasa Agama, a Vaishnava tradition founded by Vikhanasa; Pancharatra is the other Vaishnava agama but not Tirumala's.

79.s: The early Chalukyas worshipped this mother goddess?
79.x: The Chalukyas called themselves Hariti-putras (sons of Hariti) of the Manavya gotra, nourished by the Seven Mothers; Rocket lists Hariti as the mother goddess worshipped by the early Chalukyas. Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi, not the Chalukya family goddess (printed key: Cushmandini).

79.s: Nayanmar's belongs to the convention of
79.x: The Nayanars (63 Tamil saints) were devotees of Shiva, i.e. the Saiva tradition; the Alvars were the Vaishnava saints.

79.s: Which development is associated with Jayasimha II?
o: The Boyas founded the merchant headquarters at Penugonda.
The Koya Kottalu were drawn into the Brahmanical fold.
The Venginadu was divided into eighteen offices.
79.x: Under Jayasimha II, groups such as the Koya Kottalu were assimilated into the Brahmanical fold.
79.tq: Identify the ruler associated with tribal assimilation rather than with religious construction or administration.
xs: Under **Jayasimha II**, the **Koya Kottalu** and others were drawn into the **Brahmanical fold** — option **(2)**.
**Penugonda** was the merchant guild HQ; the **Pancharamas** were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**, not Jains.
xa: **Panduranga** subdued the **Boyas**.
Society: **varna-based**, Brahmin privilege.

79.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have performed the Ashvamedha?
79.x: Jayasimha I performed the Ashvamedha, while royal prashastis also boast of several Ashvamedhas.
79.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a specific Vedic ritual.
xs: **Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayaditya II** built **108 temples**; **Vimaladitya** became a Jain; **Danarnava** was Vaishnava.
xa: Royal prashastis boast of many Ashvamedhas.
Danarnava built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple, **Samalkot**.
**Chalukya Bhima I**: **Pancharamas**.

79.s: Which of the following were the Shaiva sects prevalent under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Shaiva sects of the period were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata. Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions, and Virashaiva persecution came later in the Kakatiya age.
79.tq: Shaiva trio: Kapalika, Kalamukha, Pasupata.
xs: The Shaiva sects were **Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata** — option **(1)**.
**Virashaiva** persecution of Jains came later, in the **Kakatiya** age; **Pancharatra** and **Vaikhanasa** are not Shaiva sects.
xa: Shaivism was **dominant**; custom of a **temple for each battle**.
Kapalikas emerged from the **Misra Saivam** school.
Royal title **Parama Maheshwara** reflects Shaiva faith.

79.s: Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa were traditions of which faith?
79.x: Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions; the Shaiva sects were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s: Which Vaishnava Eastern Chalukya ruler built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot?
79.x: Danarnava, a Vaishnava, built the Mandavya Narayana temple; Kubja Vishnuvardhana built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s: What was the Nellore region called in ancient times?
79.x: Pakanadu was the Nellore region (NextGen lists Palnadu = Macharla-Gurajala, Kammanadu = Bapatla-Ongole-Narasaraopet, Venginadu = Krishna-Godavari). Venginadu and Palnadu are other nadus.

79.s: What did the word 'Udranga' refer to during the ancient Chalukya period?
79.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Fixed (principal) land tax); it is added as option 5.
No option is right: D.C. Sircar's Indian Epigraphical Glossary explains udranga as the fixed or principal land tax (tax on permanent tenants), paired with uparikara (minor taxes); it is not a toll, salt, water or shop tax. The older app key 'tax on water' has no source support.

79.s: What were the Ashtadasa Tirthas in Eastern Chalukya administration?
79.x: The kingdom followed the Saptanga idea and had Ashtadasa Tirthas, meaning eighteen offices.
79.tq: Discriminate between an administrative number and similarly structured territorial or religious lists.
xs: **Ashtadasa Tirthas** = **18 offices** — option **(1)**.
They went with the **Saptanga** idea of the state; the territorial units were **Vishaya / Mandala** and the **Nadus**.
xa: **Tirthulu** = council of ministers; **Samaharta** = chief.
**Vishayapati / Mandaleswara** headed a Vishaya / Mandala.
**Vanneyus** = toll collectors.

79.s: What was the council of ministers called under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Eastern Chalukya council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.
xa: The king was assisted by the **Yuvaraja**.
**Ashtadasa Tirthas** = 18 offices.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples.

79.s: Which of the following Nadus was associated with the Nellore region?
79.x: Pakanadu was associated with Nellore. Venginadu covered parts of Krishna and Godavari, while Kammanadu included Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet.
79.tq: Use the geographical association to distinguish the named territorial units.
xs: **Pakanadu** = **Nellore** — option **(4)**.
**Venginadu** = Krishna, Godavari; **Kammanadu** = **Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet**; **Palnadu** is listed without a region.
xa: The **Asanapura** Ghatika, headed by **Mandasharma**, was in **Kammanadu**.
Core territory of the dynasty = **Venginadu**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vishaya or Mandala — Vishayapati or Mandaleswara
79.x: The state was organised into Vishayas or Mandalas under a Vishayapati or Mandaleswara.
79.tq: Match the territorial level with its officer while rejecting officers belonging to other institutions.
xs: **Vishaya / Mandala — Vishayapati / Mandaleswara** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **village** head was **Grameyaka / Gramani / Urgavunda**; **Samaharta** was chief of the ministers; **Sthanadhipati** managed temples.
xa: Nadus: **Venginadu** (Krishna, Godavari), **Kammanadu** (Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet), **Pakanadu** (Nellore).
**Vanneyus** = toll collectors.

79.s: Who were the Vanneyus under the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: Members of the council of ministers
79.x: Vanneyus collected tolls; Grameyaka/Urgavunda was the village head and the Sthanadhipati managed temples.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s: Who was the chief member of the Tirthulu (council of ministers) of the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Samaharta was the chief of the Tirthulu; the Vishayapati/Mandaleswara headed a province and the Grameyaka a village.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s: Which region did Kammanadu of the Eastern Chalukya period cover?
79.x: Kammanadu covered Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet; Pakanadu was Nellore and Venginadu parts of Krishna and Godavari.
79.tq: one-liner

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya administration:
1. Grameyaka or Urgavunda was the village head.
2. The Sthanadhipati collected tolls.
3. Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen administrative offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: 1 and 3 are correct. The Sthanadhipati managed temples and their land endowments; tolls were collected by the Vanneyus.
79.tq: statements

79.s: In Eastern Chalukya grants, Udranga was a tax on what?
79.x: Udranga is explained in epigraphy as the fixed or principal land tax (tax on permanent tenants), paired with uparikara; it was not a water tax.

79.s: How many limbs of the state does the Saptanga idea, followed by the Eastern Chalukyas, name?
79.x: Saptanga means seven limbs of the state; eighteen was the number of offices (Ashtadasa Tirthas).

79.s: Who was the king's adviser on judicial matters under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Pradvivaka was the king's adviser on judicial matters (chief judge).

79.s: What were 'jayapatras' under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: Disputes were settled with local elders, and written verdicts were called jayapatras.

79.s: Which officer managed temples and their land endowments under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Sthanadhipati managed temples and their land endowments.

79.s: Which was the central location of trade guilds in medieval Andhra?
79.x: Penugonda (West Godavari) was the headquarters of the merchant guilds of medieval Andhra and seat of goddess Vasavi; Bejwada was a trade centre but not the guild headquarters.

79.s: Brahmins who received agraharas are stated to have performed which rituals?
79.x: Brahmins receiving tax-free agraharas performed Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna rituals.
79.tq: Match the social beneficiaries with the rituals associated with their privilege.
xs: Brahmins of the **agraharas** performed **Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna** rituals — option **(4)**.
**Hallisaka (Kolatam)** is a dance; **Tarka** and **Vyakarana** are Ghatika subjects.
xa: Agraharas were **tax-free villages**.
Grants came from the **Badami Chalukya** model.
**Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha**.

79.s: Who subdued the Boyas?
79.x: Panduranga subdued the Boyas, while Jayasimha II is associated with the assimilation of the Koya Kottalu.
79.tq: Separate two related social developments by matching each group with its stated agent.
xs: **Panduranga** subdued the **Boyas** — option **(1)**.
**Jayasimha II** is linked with the assimilation of the **Koya Kottalu**.
xa: Panduranga, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**, also issued the **Addanki** inscription.
Vishnuvardhana III gave **Mushikonda** to Jains; **Ammaraja II** made the **Kaluchumbarru** grant.

79.s: Who were the Panchanamvaru, who appear as an organised body from the Eastern Chalukya period?
o: Five merchant guilds of the ports
79.x: Panchanamvaru were the five artisan groups: blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter and sculptor.

79.s: Which inscription of Chalukya Bhima I names a Setti Shreshthi (chief merchant)?
79.x: Chalukya Bhima I's Kakumanu inscription names a Setti Shreshthi.

79.s: Who sent 72 merchants to China?
79.x: The 72-merchant mission to China is associated with Kulothunga I; Saktivarma's coins have been found in Arakan, Burma.
xa: Merchant guild HQ (medieval Andhra): **Penugonda**.
Saktivarma I had beaten Kalyani Satyasraya's army with Chola help.

79.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched (overseas trade under the Eastern Chalukyas)?
o: Coins found in Arakan (Burma) – Kulothunga I
72 merchants sent to China – Saktivarma I
Trade with the eastern islands – Rajaraja Narendra
Headquarters of the merchant guilds – Pithapuram
79.x: Rajaraja Narendra traded with the eastern islands; Arakan coins belong to Saktivarma I, the 72 merchants were sent by Kulothunga I, and the guild headquarters was Penugonda.

79.s: Which place was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra?
79.x: Penugonda was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra.

79.s: Coins of which Eastern Chalukya ruler have been found in Arakan (Burma)?
79.x: Coins of Saktivarma I found in Arakan show overseas trade.

79.s: During which period did the persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu take place?
79.x: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred in the Kakatiya age, not under the Eastern Chalukyas, who patronised Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.
xa: **Vimaladitya** even became a Jain.
Buddhism survived at **Amaravati** and **Nagarjunakonda**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about religion under the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Potlacheruvu was a famous Buddhist centre.
2. Vimaladitya was the only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain.
3. Amaravati was a centre where declining Buddhism survived.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre, not a Buddhist one.

79.s: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham for whom?
o: His Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
79.x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva, as recorded in the Ramateertham inscription.

xs: **Vimaladitya** built the **Ramakonda** cave temple for his Jain guru **Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva** — option **(1)**.

xa: Vimaladitya was the **only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain**.
Other Jain grants: **Mushikonda** (Vishnuvardhana III), **Kaluchumbarru** (Ammaraja II), **Nedumba Vasati** (Ayyana Mahadevi).

79.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mushikonda grant to Jains – Kubja Vishnuvardhana
79.x: Ammaraja II made the Kaluchumbarru grant at the request of Chamekamba; Mushikonda village was granted to Jains by Vishnuvardhana III.

**Vimaladitya** built the **Ramakonda** cave temple.
Vishnuvardhana III's title: **Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu**.

79.s: At whose request did Ammaraja II renew the Maliyapundi gift to a Jinalaya near Dharmapuri?
79.x: The Maliyapundi grant was made at the request of the vassal Durgaraja; Chamekamba requested the Kaluchumbarru grant.

79.s: In which district is Ramatirtham, where Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple?
79.x: Ramatirtham, with the Jain Ramakonda cave temple, is in Vizianagaram district.

79.s: Gramadevata temples belong to which tradition?
79.x: Gramadevata (village goddess) shrines belong to the Shakta (Sakteya) tradition of mother-goddess worship.

79.s: Who was conferred the title Gandharva-vidya-visarada in the Chalukyan Court?
79.src: Asst. B.C. Welfare Officer, Asst. Social Welfare Officer & A
79.x: Chellavva, court singer and dancer of Chalukya Bhima I, received the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada and the village Attili.

79.s: Which religious sect enjoyed great popularity under eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
79.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
79.x: Saivism dominated under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: kings built Shiva temples (Biccavolu, Draksharama), and Buddharamas became Saiva shrines. Jainism and Buddhism declined.

79.s: Which one of the following religions was not prevalent at the time of Chalukayas?
79.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
79.x: Hinduism (Saivism, Vaishnavism), Buddhism and Jainism all existed under the Chalukyas, but Judaism had no place in their realm. So Judaism was the religion not prevalent.

79.s: What were Ghatikas in the Eastern Chalukya period?
o: Military cantonments attached to royal forts
Jain cave temples used for royal burials
Advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples
Merchant guilds situated at coastal ports
79.x: Ghatikas were advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples.
79.tq: Apply the institutional definition while rejecting misleading associations with military, commercial and temple structures.
xs: **Ghatikas** were **advanced Sanskrit schools** attached to **agraharas or temples** — option **(3)**.
Merchant guilds were headquartered at **Penugonda**, a separate institution.
xa: Heads: **Ghatika Samanyulu** — e.g. **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura**, Kammanadu.
Subjects: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.

79.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT included among the subjects taught in Ghatikas?
79.x: Ghatikas taught subjects such as Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda and Ayurveda. Hallisaka was a popular dance, not an academic subject.

xs: **Hallisaka** was not a Ghatika subject — option **(4)**; it is a popular dance (**Kolatam**).
Subjects taught: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.
xa: Ghatikas were **advanced Sanskrit schools**.
Jain pupils began with "**Om Namah Siddham**".

79.s: What were the heads of Ghatikas called?
79.x: The heads of Ghatikas were called Ghatika Samanyulu.
79.tq: Match the educational institution with its specialised headship title.
xs: Ghatika heads were the **Ghatika Samanyulu** — option **(3)**.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples; **Vanneyus** collected tolls; **Vishayapati** headed a Vishaya.
xa: Example: **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura** Ghatika, Kammanadu.
His son **Katikasharma** appears in the **Nidamarru** inscription.

79.s: Mandasharma was the head (Ghatika Samanyulu) of which Ghatika?
79.x: Mandasharma headed the Asanapura Ghatika in Kammanadu.

79.s: With which words did Jain pupils begin their studies in this period?
79.x: Jain pupils began their studies with 'Om Namah Siddham'.

79.s: What were the Ashtadasha Tirthas in the Eastern Chalukya administration of Vengi?
79.x: The Ashtadasha Tirthas were the 18 departments; the Yuvaraja was a partner in governance and councils were called Varagoshti.
xa: The Chola Vengi viceroys (**Rajapratinidhi**) were **Kulottunga I's sons**.
Chola kings also named a **yuvaraja** in their own lifetime.
Eastern Chalukya Vengi also had **Nakaras** headed by **Shreshthis**.

79.s: What were the councils of the Eastern Chalukya administration called?
79.x: The Eastern Chalukyas had 18 departments (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and councils called Varagoshti.

80.s: Draksharama temple, a part of Pancharama shrines, is a fine example of the fine architectural style of:
80.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
80.x: The Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama was built by the Eastern Chalukya king Chalukya Bhima I, in the Vengi Chalukya (Vesara-influenced) style; it is not a Pallava or Satavahana work, and 'Chalukyas' alone means the Badami line.

80.s: Among the Vengi Chalukya rulers in Andhra, who built many temples?
80.x: Chalukya Bhima I, who fought 360 battles, is said to have built 360 temples, including the Pancharamas and the Bhimeswara temples of Draksharama and Samalkot.

80.s: Founder of famous Draksharama temple?
80.x: Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama; Gunaga Vijayaditya built the Bikkavolu group and Vijayaditya II the 108 Narendreswara temples.

80.s: In which place Chalukya Bhimavaram founded by Chalukya Bhima is situated in Andhra?
80.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
80.x: Chalukya Bhimavaram is Samalkot (Samarlakota), seat of Kumararama, built by Chalukya Bhima I in memory of his son; Pithapuram and Draksharama are separate towns and Gunupudi is Somarama.

80.s: Which one of the following is not in Pancharama?
80.x: The Pancharamas are Draksharama, Kumararama (Samalkot = Chalukya Bhimavaram), Somarama (Gunupudi), Ksheerarama (Palakollu) and Amararama (Amaravati); Simhachalam is a Narasimha shrine, not a Pancharama.

80.s: Amaravati is one of the following?
80.x: Amaravati is the seat of Amararama, one of the five Pancharamas built by Chalukya Bhima I; it is not a Shakti Peetha.

80.s: Who built the Pancharamas in Andhra?
80.x: The Eastern Chalukya king Chalukya Bhima I built the Pancharamas; Kubja Vishnuvardhana built the Kunti Madhava temple and Rajaraja Narendra temples at Rajahmundry.

80.s: During whose period were the Pancharamas built?
80.x: The Pancharamas were built under the Vengi (Eastern) Chalukyas by Chalukya Bhima I, long before the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara.

80.s: Sapta Godavari associated with?
80.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
80.x: Sapta Godavari is the sacred tank (pushkarini) of the Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama, whose water, said to be brought by the Seven Sages, is used for the abhisheka; it is not at Ksheerarama or Amararama.

80.s: Who built the twin Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot?
80.x: Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara (Samalkot). Prola Raju II and Rudra Deva were Kakatiyas and Anavema Reddy a Reddi king.
n: Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples of Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Kumararama Bhimeswara is located at Samalkota. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xa: He also built **Somarama** at Gunupudi and the Kumaraswamy temple at **Chebrolu**.

Draksharama is one of the **Trilinga kshetras**.

80.s: Who is associated with building the Pancharamas or making them Shaiva kshetras?

80.tq: Use the builder–religious foundation association rather than the place-based clues.
xs: **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas** or made them Shaiva kshetras — option **(1)** is correct.
**Danarnava** built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple at Samalkot; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** built **Kunti Madhava** at Pithapuram.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I also built **Bhimeswara (Draksharama)**, **Kumararama (Samalkot)** in memory of his son, and **Someswara (Somarama)** at Gunupudi.
He also built the **Kumaraswamy temple** at **Chebrolu**.
His commander **Bhattupu** built the **Parvateswara** temple on **Indrakeeladri**, Bezawada.

80.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
80.x: Bhimeswara is at Draksharama. Kumararama is at Samalkot, Kumaraswamy at Chebrolu and Someswara at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram.
xa: All four were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Kumararama (**Kumara Bhimeswara**) was built in memory of his son.

80.s: Which town was anciently called 'Chalukya Bhimavaram'?
80.x: Chalukya Bhimavaram is Samalkot (Kumararama), not Palakollu, which is Ksheerarama.

80.s: In whose memory did Chalukya Bhima I build the Kumararama temple at Samalkot?
80.x: Kumararama (Kumara Bhimeswara) at Samalkot was built by Chalukya Bhima I in memory of his son.

80.s: Where is Ksheerarama, one of the Pancharamas, located?
80.x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu (West Godavari); Kumararama is at Samalkot, Amararama at Amaravati and Draksharama at Draksharama.
xa: The fifth: **Somarama** at **Gunupudi, Bhimavaram** (West Godavari).

80.s: Where is Somarama, one of the Pancharamas, located?

xa: The five: **Draksharama, Kumararama, Ksheerarama, Somarama, Amararama** (Amaravati).

**Chalukya Bhima I** built / made the Pancharamas Shaiva kshetras.

80.s: The architectural structure of which of the following temples exemplifies the independent style of the Chalukya-Cholas, incorporating Pallava and early Chalukya influences?

80.s: Which statement correctly compares the Badami Chalukya and Vengi architectural developments?
o: The Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka, while the Vengi line carried a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase.

xs: The **Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka**, while the **Vengi line carried a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Vengi line did not reject Badami influence: Badami Chalukya features are part of its base style.
Neither was exclusively Buddhist; the Vengi style used local **laterite and limestone** in the **Krishna-Godavari delta**.

xs: The **Alampur Navabrahma** temples were built by the **Badami Chalukyas** — option **(2)** is correct.

The **Eastern Chalukyas (Vengi)** followed a Dravida-based style leading to the **Chalukya-Chola** phase.

80.x: The Bhimeswara temples on the Godavari (Draksharama, Samalkot) were built by Chalukya Bhima I ('Chalukya-I' = Chalukya Bhima I). 81.s: The Kalamalla inscription is associated with which ruler and date?

**Punyakumara** (**625-650 CE**) left Potladurthi, Malepadu and Erragudipadu records.

81.x: The Renati Cholas made Telugu a royal and legislative language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, and from 575 to 848 CE Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.

xa: The **Kalamalla** inscription (**575 CE**) is the first Telugu inscription.
The Renati Cholas made Telugu a **royal and legislative language**.

81.x: The Renati Cholas were the first to make Telugu a royal and legal language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, about five centuries before Nannaya.

81.x: The Renati Cholas were the first to make Telugu a royal and legal language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit.

81.s: Who among the following was regarded as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line?
81.x: Nandivarma is identified as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line.
81.tq: Separate the progenitor from the founder and the last ruler.
xs: **Nandivarma** was the **progenitor** of the Renati Cholas — option **(1)** is correct.
**Dhanunjaya Varma**, his son, was the **founder**; **Satyaditya** bore the title Chola Maharaja; **Elachola Maharaja** was the last ruler.
xa: ⚠ Progenitor = **Nandivarma**; founder = **Dhanunjaya Varma**.
**Mahendra Vikramavarman**, grandson of Nandivarma, had the title **Muditha Silakshara Navarama**.
⚠ For the Nellore Chodas, the progenitor is **Bijjana**.

81.s: Who is regarded as the greatest ruler of the Renati Cholas?
81.x: Punyakumara (625-650 CE), with titles such as Pormukharama and Prithvivallabha, was the greatest Renati Chola ruler. Nandivarma was the progenitor, Dhanunjaya Varma the founder and Elachola Maharaja the last ruler.
81.tq: Progenitor Nandivarma, founder Dhanunjaya, greatest Punyakumara, last Elachola.
xs: **Punyakumara** (**625-650 CE**) was the greatest Renati Chola ruler — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nandivarma** was the progenitor, **Dhanunjaya Varma** the founder, **Elachola Maharaja** the last ruler.
xa: Titles: **Pormukharama**, **Purushashardula**, Uttamottama, **Prithvivallabha**; wife **Vasantapori**.
His inscriptions: **Potladurthi**, **Malepadu** and **Erragudipadu**.

81.s: Which of the following was NOT a title of Punyakumara?
81.x: Pormukharama, Purushashardula and Uttamottama were titles of Punyakumara. Chola Sthapanacharya was the title taken by Tikkana Choda.

xs: **Chola Sthapanacharya** was not Punyakumara's title — option **(3)** is correct.
It was taken by **Tikkana Choda** (Nellore Chodas) after putting **Rajendra Chola** on the Chola throne.
Punyakumara's titles: **Pormukharama**, **Purushashardula**, **Uttamottama**, **Prithvivallabha**.
xa: Punyakumara (**625-650 CE**) was the greatest Renati ruler; wife **Vasantapori**.
⚠ **Tikkana Choda** (king) ≠ **Kavi-Brahma Tikkana** (poet-minister).

81.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Renati Chola dynasty?
81.x: Dhanunjaya Varma, son of Nandivarma, was the founder; Nandivarma was only the progenitor.

81.s: Who was the last ruler of the Renati Cholas?
81.x: Elachola Maharaja was the last Renati Chola ruler.

81.s: Who had the title 'Muditha Silakshara Navarama'?
81.x: Mahendra Vikramavarman, grandson of Nandivarma and father of Punyakumara, bore this title.

81.x: Punyakumara ruled from 625 to 650 CE.

81.x: The Nellore Choda line begins with (Tenungu) Bijjana, a vassal of the Kalyani Chalukya Someshvara I, named as progenitor; Tikka (Tikkana Choda) was a later, greater ruler.

81.s: With which place were the Nellore Chodas associated?

**Nannuru** was another branch.

Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola

81.x: The Konidena Chodas ruled Kammanadu from Konidena (Kotyadona) near Narasaraopet.

81.s: Which of the following statements about Tikkana Choda is correct?
o: He was the court poet of Manumasiddhi II and wrote Purushartha Saramu.

81.x: Manumasiddhi II sought the help of Kakatiya Ganapati against Vijayaganda Gopala.

81.x: Bijjana was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas; Manumasiddhi I was their first king.

81.s: Who went as envoy to Kakatiya Ganapatideva when Manumasiddhi II was restored to the Nellore throne?
81.x: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II, with the poet Tikkana as envoy.

81.x: The ASI survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve (Yerragondapalem) copied 25 inscriptions of the 2nd-16th centuries.

82.s: Who among the following dynasties founded the Kingdom of Berar?

82.s: Who founded the Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar, and what was its capital?

82.x: Golconda was earlier called Mankal or Mangalavaram; Mangalapura was Mangalagiri.

83.x: The Gona Haihayas were associated with Vardhamanapuram; the Palnadu Haihayas with Gurajala and the Panchadhara Haihayas with the Visakhapatnam-Yelamanchili region.

Palnadu Haihaya founder: **Betaraju I** (**Satrasala** inscription).
**Kona Haihayas**: Konaseema, **Rakuduru**.

83.s: Who founded the Kota line, and where was its seat?
o: Bhimaraju II; Vardhamanapuram in South Telangana
83.x: Betaraju I was the founder of the Kota line, whose seat was Dhanyakatakam in Kammanadu.

xs: **Betaraju I** founded the Kota line, seat **Dhanyakatakam in Kammanadu** — option **(4)** is correct.

83.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
83.x: The Kota kings ruled Kammanadu and had Dhanyakatakam as their seat. The Vatsavayis were associated with Peddapuram, the Pusapatis with Vizianagaram, and the Bana kings with Rayalaseema and part of Karnataka.

83.s: From where did the Palnadu Haihayas rule?
83.x: The Palnadu Haihayas ruled from Gurajala; Rakuduru was the Kona Haihaya capital.

83.s: From where did the Chagis rule the Natavadi and Vijayavati vishayas?
83.x: The Chagis, raised to Mandaleswara rank by Kulottunga I, ruled from Gudimetta (later also Vinukonda).

83.s: From which creature did the Matsyas of Oddadi claim descent?
83.x: The founder of the Matsyas of Oddadi claimed descent from a fish (matsya); their emblem was a double fish.

83.s: Whose daughter did Satyamartanda, founder of the Matsyas of Oddadi, marry?

83.s: From whom did the Palnadu Haihayas claim descent?
83.x: The Palnadu Haihayas of Gurajala claimed descent from Kartavirya Arjuna.

83.s: Which was the capital of the Bana kings?
83.x: The Bana kings, who claimed descent from Bali, ruled from Parivipuram (Hindupur).

83.s: What was the emblem of the Matsyas of Oddadi?
83.x: The Matsyas of Oddadi (c. 1200-1470) had the double fish as emblem.

83.s: Which zamindars claim descent from the Matsyas of Oddadi?
83.x: After Singaraja (1471) the line was replaced by zamindaris; the Madgole zamindars claim Matsya descent.

83.s: A Kota chief married Ganapamba. Whose daughter was she?
83.x: A Kota chief married Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva; some sources name him Bhimaraju II. This marriage reflects the Kotas becoming Kakatiya vassals.

xs: A Kota chief married **Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva** — option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Kota overlords: **Chalukya-Cholas → Velanati Chodas → Kakatiyas**.

83.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the overlords of the Kota chiefs?
o: They were first subordinate to the Chalukya-Cholas.

The Kakatiyas were their final overlords.
The Kakatiyas were their first overlords.

83.s: Which Kota ruler (1108-1127) led Kalinga campaigns with the Velanati Chodas?
83.x: Kota Bhimaraju I (1108-1127) backed the Chalukya-Cholas and joined the Velanati Chodas in Kalinga campaigns.

83.x: The Chagis served the Chalukya-Cholas, then the Kakatiyas, then the Gajapatis; the Velanati stage belongs to the Kota chiefs.

83.s: Kakatiya Ganapatideva's sister Melambika married into which family?
83.x: Melambika married a son of the Natavadi chief Chagi Buddharaja.

83.x: The Pusapatis ruled from Vizianagaram (APPSC GS 2022); Peddapuram was the seat of the Vatsavayis.

84.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. Mitakshara was the civil law for upper castes and Dayabhaga was the civil law for lower castes.

3. The Mitakshara system deals with the matters related to the property held by male members only of a family, whereas the Dayabhaga system deals with the matters related to the property held by both male and female members of a family.

84.s: In which of the following castes does the father's property not inherit equally to all the sons?
84.x: Among the Nambudiri Brahmins of Kerala only the eldest son married within the caste and held the family property (primogeniture), so sons did not inherit equally; the Nayars were matrilineal (marumakkathayam).

84.x: Dayabhaga recognises the sons' right in ancestral property only after the father's death, whereas Mitakshara gives it by birth.

o: Smriti Chandrika is associated with Devana Bhatta.

Dayabhaga is associated with Jimutavahana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Parashar Madhav is associated with Madhvacharya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Smriti Chandrika deals with Hindu law. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]

The others are correct: **Dayabhaga** — **Jimutavahana**; **Smriti Chandrika** — **Hindu law**.
xa: **Mitakshara** — **Vijnanesvara**, a commentary on **inheritance**.
**Chaturvarga Chintamani** — **Hemadri**; **Daan Sagar** — **Ballal Sena**.

o: It is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti
Under it sons acquire a right in ancestral property by birth
It applied only to the upper castes

84.x: Dayabhaga, by Jimutavahana, prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara covers most of India.

84.x: Daan Sagar was written by Ballal Sena; Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika.

84.x: Madhavacharya's Parasara Madhaveeyam, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was the main law book of Vijayanagara justice.

84.x: Parashar Madhav is a commentary on the Parashara Smriti; the Mitakshara is the commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

84.s: Who is the author of the Chaturvarga Chintamani?
84.x: Hemadri, a minister of the Yadavas of Devagiri, wrote the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

84.s: The Kalyani Chalukyas flourished approximately during which period?

84.s: Why are the Kalyani Chalukyas significant in Indian history?
o: abolished hereditary rights in ancestral property
checked Chola expansion northwards and contributed to the development of Hindu legal tradition through Mitakshara
unified all of northern India under one empire
ended the Gupta Empire and introduced Persian administration

xs: They **checked Chola expansion northwards** and gave Hindu law the **Mitakshara** — option **(2)** is correct.

84.x: Kalyani is present Basavakalyan in Karnataka; Badami was the earlier Chalukya capital.

founded by Tailapa II in 973 CE after defeating the Rashtrakutas

84.s: Which one of the following statements about Bilhana is correct?
o: He was a Bengal jurist who wrote the Dayabhaga.
He was a Kashmiri poet at Vikramaditya VI’s court and compared the ruler’s reign with Ramarajya.
He was a Virashaiva saint who composed Vachana literature.
He was a Yadava minister who wrote Chaturvarga Chintamani.
84.x: Bilhana was a Kashmiri poet at Vikramaditya VI’s court and likened the ruler’s reign to Ramarajya. The other descriptions refer to different persons or traditions.
84.tq: Apply the wrong-author-for-the-work and wrong-origin traps.
xs: Bilhana was a **Kashmiri poet at Vikramaditya VI's court** who likened his rule to **Ramarajya** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Dayabhaga** is **Jimutavahana**'s (Bengal); vachanas are **Basavanna**'s; **Chaturvarga Chintamani** is **Hemadri**'s.
xa: His work: **Vikramankadevacharita**.
Bilhana claims the Chalukyas originated at **Brahmachulakam**.

84.s: By what other name is the 100-chapter Sanskrit encyclopaedia Manasollasa known?
84.x: Manasollasa, also called Abhilashitartha Chintamani, covers statecraft, agriculture, medicine, astronomy, music, dance and cuisine.
xa: Author: **Someshvara III** (**1126-1138**).
⚠ Not to be confused with **Vikramankadevacharita** (**Bilhana**) or **Mitakshara** (**Vijnaneshwara**).

84.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
84.x: Nagavarma II wrote Kavyavalokana. Manasollasa is by Someshvara III, Mitakshara by Vijnaneshwara and Vikramankadeva Charita by Bilhana.
n: Someshvara III authored the Manasollasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Bilhana authored the Vikramankadeva Charita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Vijnaneshwara authored the Mitakshara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Nagavarma II authored the Kavyavalokana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
xa: ⚠ Bilhana = poet; Vijnaneshwara = jurist; both at **Vikramaditya VI**'s court.
Bilhana likened Vikramaditya VI's rule to **Ramarajya**.
Mitakshara is a commentary on the **Yajnavalkya Smriti**.
Hemadri (Yadava minister) wrote **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.

84.s:
Consider the following statements about the Manasollasa:
1. It is a 100-chapter encyclopaedia.
2. Its subjects include agriculture, medicine and cuisine.
3. It was written by Vikramaditya VI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
84.x: The Manasollasa is a 100-chapter encyclopaedia covering statecraft, agriculture, medicine, music and cuisine; it was written by Someshvara III, not Vikramaditya VI.

84.s: Whose life is described in Bilhana's Vikramankadevacharita?
84.x: Bilhana's Vikramankadevacharita is a biography of his patron Vikramaditya VI, whose reign it likens to Ramarajya.

84.s: Over which region were the wars between the Kalyani Chalukyas and the Cholas mainly fought?
84.x: The Chola-Chalukya wars were fought mainly over Vengi (coastal Andhra) and the Raichur doab.

84.s: At the confluence of which rivers was the battle of Kudalasangamam (c. 1062) fought?
84.x: Kudalasangamam lies at the Krishna–Tungabhadra confluence, where the Cholas heavily defeated Someshvara I.

84.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler was heavily defeated by the Cholas at Kudalasangamam (c. 1062)?
84.x: At Kudalasangamam, at the Krishna-Tungabhadra confluence, the Cholas heavily defeated Someshvara I.

84.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Kalyani Chalukya architecture used ornate pillars.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured undecorated doorways.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture included intricate wall motifs.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture included stepped superstructures.
84.x: Option B is incorrect: Kalyani Chalukya temples have richly decorated doorways, not plain ones. Ornate pillars, intricate wall motifs and stepped superstructures are all correct features.
84.tq: Check the feature in each statement.
n: Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured ornate pillars. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured stepped superstructures. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured decorated doorways. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured intricate wall motifs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
xs: The incorrect statement is that Kalyani Chalukya architecture had **undecorated doorways** — option **(2)**.
Their temples had **decorated doorways**.
The others are correct features: **ornate pillars**, **intricate wall motifs**, **stepped superstructures**.
xa: Style: mature **Vesara (Gadag style)** in **chloritic schist (soapstone)**.
**Star-shaped (stellate)** plans, later used by the **Hoysalas**.
**Mahadeva** temple at **Itagi** — "Emperor among temples".
Other temples: **Kasivishveshvara** (Lakkundi), **Doddabasappa** (Dambal).

84.s: Which stone was mainly used for Kalyani Chalukya temples of the mature Vesara (Gadag) style?
84.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas built mainly in chloritic schist (soapstone), not granite; their stellate plans later became a model for the Hoysalas.
xa: **Mahadeva** temple at **Itagi** = "Emperor among temples".
**Kasivishveshvara** is at **Lakkundi**.

84.s: How is the Itagi Mahadeva temple popularly described?
84.x: The Itagi Mahadeva temple is popularly known as the “Emperor among temples.”
84.tq: Recall the distinctive epithet attached to the monument.
xs: The **Itagi Mahadeva** temple is the "**Emperor among temples**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It is in mature **Vesara (Gadag style)**.
xa: Others: **Kasivishveshvara** (Lakkundi), **Doddabasappa** (Dambal), **Kedareshwara** (Balligavi).
Material: **chloritic schist (soapstone)**.

84.s: Where is the Mahadeva temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
84.x: The Mahadeva temple is at Itagi; Kasivishveshvara is at Lakkundi, Doddabasappa at Dambal and Kedareshwara at Balligavi.
xa: Itagi Mahadeva = "**Emperor among temples**".
**Stellate plans** were later used by the **Hoysalas**.

84.s: Where is the Kasivishveshvara temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
84.x: The Kasivishveshvara temple is at Lakkundi; Itagi has the Mahadeva temple and Dambal the Doddabasappa temple.

84.s: For which dynasty did the star-shaped (stellate) temple plans of the Kalyani Chalukyas later become a model?
84.x: The stellate plans of the Gadag style were later taken up as a model by the Hoysalas.

84.s: Where is the Doddabasappa temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
84.x: The Doddabasappa temple is at Dambal; the Kedareshwara temple is at Balligavi.

84.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas vassals before seizing over the kingdom?
84.x: Before Rudradeva declared independence (1163) the Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas, who had earlier replaced their first overlords, the Rashtrakutas; they were never Hoysala or Yadava vassals.

84.s: According to the Khazipet inscription, with which event was the early rise of the Kakatiyas connected?
o: the conquest of Devagiri from the Yadavas
the founding of Dwarasamudra by the Hoysalas
the seizure of Kalyani by Bijjala
a grant of Hanamkonda with hereditary rights
84.x: The Khazipet inscription records Hanamkonda being granted with hereditary rights, reflecting the Kakatiyas’ rise as feudatories.
84.tq: Use an inscriptional clue to identify the political basis of a dynasty’s rise.
xs: The **Khazipet inscription** records a **grant of Hanamkonda with hereditary rights** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Kakatiyas rose as **Kalyani feudatories**.
xa: **Someshvara I** granted Hanamkonda to Kakatiya **Prola I**.
**Beta I and Prola I** were Kalyani feudatories.

84.s: From which capital did the Yadavas (Seunas) rule after the weakening of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
84.x: The Yadavas or Seunas ruled from Devagiri; the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra, the Kakatiyas from Hanamkonda-Warangal and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.
xa: **Beta I and Prola I** of the Kakatiyas were **Kalyani feudatories**.
**Bijjala** seized the Kalyani throne c. **1156**.
The dynasty ended c. **1189 CE**.

84.s: Who seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE?
84.x: Kalachuri ruler Bijjala seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE.
84.tq: Match the seizure of the central throne with the correct successor power.
xs: **Bijjala of the Kalachuris** seized Kalyani c. **1156** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Prola I** was a Kakatiya feudatory; **Hemadri** was a Yadava minister.
xa: The Kalyani Chalukya dynasty ended c. **1189 CE**.
Successors: **Hoysalas, Yadavas (Seunas), Kakatiyas, Kalachuris**.

84.s: In which year did the Kalyani Chalukya dynasty come to an end?
84.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ended around 1189 CE, and the Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Yadavas emerged as successor powers.
xa: **Bijjala** seized the throne c. **1156**.
Kakatiyas rose as Kalyani feudatories (**Khazipet inscription**).

84.s: Which was the capital of the Hoysalas, a successor power of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
84.x: The Hoysala capital was Dwarasamudra; the Yadavas ruled from Devagiri.

84.s: Which of the following pairs of successor powers and capitals is correctly matched?
84.x: The Kakatiyas ruled from Hanamkonda–Warangal; the Hoysalas ruled from Dwarasamudra, the Yadavas from Devagiri and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.

85.s: Which one of the Chola kings conquered Ceylon?
85.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of the whole of Ceylon by defeating and capturing Mahinda V. Rajaraja I had taken only the northern part (Anuradhapura).

85.s: Name the Chola King who conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka?
85.x: Rajaraja I defeated Mahinda V and conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka, including Anuradhapura; his son Rajendra I later took the whole island.

85.s: One of the following Chola rulers, forced the Sri Vijaya empire of South-East Asia to accept his Suzerainty
85.x: Rajendra I's 1025 naval expedition defeated Srivijaya (Sailendra rulers) and took Kadaram, forcing it to accept Chola power. Rajaraja I, Rajendra II and Rajadhiraja did not lead it.

85.s: Who among the following carried out a naval invasion of Southeast Asia?
85.x: Rajendra I sent the naval expedition of 1025 against Srivijaya in South-East Asia (Malay Peninsula, Sumatra). Rajaraja I's naval wars were against the Cheras, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

85.s: Which Chola king defeated the Sailendra king by sending a naval expedition to the Srivijaya Empire?
85.x: Rajendra I's navy defeated the Sailendra ruler of Srivijaya in 1025 and took Kadaram. Kulottunga II and Rajaraja III were later, weaker Cholas.

85.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Cholas defeated Pandya and Chera rulers and established their domination over peninsular India in early medieval times.
2. The Cholas sent an expedition against Sailendra empire of South‑east Asia and conquered some of the areas. Which of these statements is/are correct?
85.x: Both are correct: the Cholas defeated the Pandyas and Cheras and dominated peninsular India, and Rajendra I's 1025 expedition against the Sailendra empire of Srivijaya conquered Kadaram and places in Malaya and Sumatra.

85.s: Who among the following led a successful military campaign against the kingdom of Srivijaya, the powerful maritime State, which ruled the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and the neighbouring islands?
85.x: Rajendra I (Chola) led the successful naval campaign of 1025 against Srivijaya, ruled by the Sailendras over the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and nearby islands. Amoghavarsha, Prataparudra and Vishnuvardhana never sent overseas expeditions.

85.s: Who among the following led a successful military campaign against the kingdom of Srivijaya, the powerful maritime State, which ruled the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and the neighbouring islands?
85.x: Rajendra I (Chola) led the successful naval campaign of 1025 against Srivijaya, ruled by the Sailendras over the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and nearby islands. Amoghavarsha, Prataparudra and Vishnuvardhana never sent overseas expeditions.

85.s: The Chola monarch who conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka and made it a province of his empire was
85.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
85.x: Rajaraja I conquered northern Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura) and made it the Chola province Mummudicholamandalam.

85.s: Which of the following is a South Indian dynasty that was known for its extensive maritime trade and connections with Southeast Asia?
85.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
85.x: The Cholas were the South Indian dynasty famed for maritime trade with South-East Asia (Srivijaya, Kadaram) and China. The Ahoms, Khasis and Jaintias are north-eastern.

85.s: Which Sri Lankan king was defeated and captured by Rajendra I when he completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon?
85.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Ceylon by taking its southern part and capturing Mahinda V, building on Rajaraja I's conquest of the north.
n: Rajendra I completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I captured the southern part of Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I defeated Mahinda V. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: He seized the royal insignia; the Cholas held the island for about **five decades**.
Sri Lanka's **Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas around **1070**.
Rajendra I's titles: **Gangaikondachola, Kadaramkondan**, Pandita Chola.
Northern Sri Lanka was named **Mummadichola Mandalam**.

85.s: Which Chola ruler conquered the whole of Sri Lanka, defeating Mahinda V and seizing his royal insignia?
85.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Sri Lanka by defeating Mahinda V and seizing the royal insignia; the island stayed under the Cholas for about five decades. Rajaraja I had taken only the north, Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam, and in Kulottunga I's time Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas (c. 1070).

xs: **Rajendra I** conquered the whole of Sri Lanka, defeating **Mahinda V** and seizing the royal insignia — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajaraja I** had taken only the **north**; **Rajadhiraja I** was killed at **Koppam**.
In **Kulottunga I**'s time, **Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas (around **1070**).
xa: Chola hold on the island lasted about **five decades**.
Northern Sri Lanka was named **Mummadichola Mandalam**.

85.x: Rajaraja I destroyed the Chera fleet at Kandalur Salai (Trivandrum) and captured Quilon.

85.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajaraja I — Kadaram conquest in 1025 CE
85.x: The 1025 CE Kadaram conquest was conducted by Rajendra I. Rajaraja I is associated with the Maldives and the attack on the Chera fleet at Kandalur Salai, while Kulottunga I campaigned in Kalinga.

85.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajendra I – Naval expedition against Kadaram and Srivijaya
Kulottunga I – Defeat of Pallava Aparajita
Aditya I – Loss at Thakkolam to the Rashtrakutas
85.x: Rajendra I sent the naval expedition to Kadaram and Srivijaya. Aditya I defeated Pallava Aparajita, Parantaka I lost at Thakkolam and Kulottunga I abolished tolls.
n: Aditya I defeated the Pallava ruler Aparajita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Parantaka I lost the Battle of Thakkolam to the Rashtrakutas in 949 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I led a naval expedition against Kadaram in 1025 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I led a naval expedition against Srivijaya in 1025 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I abolished tolls. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: The Srivijaya expedition was in **1025 CE**.
Rajendra I defeated Pala **Mahipala I** in the **Ganga** expedition (**1022 CE**).
⚠ "Victor of the Ganges" = **Rajendra I**, not Aditya I.
**Rajadhiraja I** was killed at **Koppam (1053)**.

85.s: Against which kingdom was the naval expedition of Rajendra I in 1025 CE directed?
85.x: Rajendra I's 1025 CE naval expedition was against the revived Srivijaya empire: he defeated the Sailendra king and took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra. Anuradhapura was destroyed by Rajaraja I, and Kalinga was conquered by Kulottunga I.
85.tq: Anchor the expedition to its year and destination before considering the distractors.
xs: Rajendra I's **1025 CE** naval expedition was against **Srivijaya** — option **(2)** is correct.

**Anuradhapura** was destroyed by **Rajaraja I**; **Kalinga** was **Kulottunga I**'s.
xa: Srivijaya covered **Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java**.
Exam angle: "Who led the campaign against Srivijaya?" — **Rajendra I** (UPSC **2025**).

85.s: Which historian said the Cholas turned the Bay of Bengal into a 'Chola Lake'?
85.x: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri described the Bay of Bengal as a 'Chola Lake'; the 1025 CE Srivijaya expedition was led by Rajendra I.
xa: It is called "**India's first overseas expedition**".
Cholas = first Indian power with **overseas naval campaigns**.

85.s: Chola overseas naval activity helped spread which art tradition to Southeast Asia?
85.x: The Cholas, described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.
xa: **K.A. Nilakanta Sastri**: the Bay of Bengal became a "**Chola Lake**".
The **1025** Srivijaya expedition = "India's first overseas expedition".

85.s: What was the main cause of the Chola expedition against Srivijaya?
o: blocked Indian traders on the China route
85.x: Chola-Sailendra ties, once cordial, soured when Srivijaya blocked Indian traders on the China route; Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition cleared these obstacles and widened Chola trade with China.

xs: Srivijaya **blocked Indian traders on the China route** — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: The expedition (**1025 CE**) was led by **Rajendra I**.

85.s: Who were the first Indian power to carry out overseas naval campaigns?
85.x: The Imperial Cholas were the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, reaching Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Srivijaya.

85.s: Who expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070?
85.x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070.

Vijayabahu I established Chola rule over the whole island for about five decades

85.x: Rajaraja I gave his daughter Kundavai in marriage to the Eastern Chalukya Vimaladitya. Rajendra I's daughter Ammanga married Rajaraja Narendra.

85.s: Which Chola ruler placed Saktivarman and Vimaladitya as Eastern Chalukya princes in Vengi?
85.x: Rajaraja I arranged Vengi by placing Saktivarman and Vimaladitya there; he also captured Quilon, annexed Madurai and conquered the Maldives.
xa: Rajaraja I also hit the Chera fleet at **Kandalur Salai** and destroyed **Anuradhapura**.
⚠ **Whole Sri Lanka** and complete subjugation of Pandyas and Cheras = **Rajendra I**.

85.s: Whose Kalinga conquest is celebrated in Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani?
85.x: Kulottunga I conquered Kalinga, a campaign sung in Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani.

85.s: Whom did the Chola princess Madhurantaki marry?
85.x: Madhurantaki married Rajendra Chalukya, who became Kulottunga I. Kundavai married Vimaladitya, Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra, and Saktivarman I was Vimaladitya's elder brother who ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I's help.
85.tq: Her father is given as Virarajendra or Rajendra I — the APPSC 2025 key rejected 'daughter of Rajendra II'.
xs: **Madhurantaki** married **Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vimaladitya** married **Kundavai**; **Rajaraja Narendra** married **Ammanga Devi**.
xa: Her father: some notes **Virarajendra**, another **Rajendra I**.
⚠ "Daughter of **Rajendra Chola II**" was marked **incorrect** in the **APPSC 2025** key.

85.s: Who married Vimaladitya, according to the Chola–Eastern Chalukya matrimonial alliances?
o: Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I
85.x: Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja I, married Vimaladitya. Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra.
85.tq: Discriminate between similarly named Chola princesses and their spouses.
xs: **Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja I**, married **Vimaladitya** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2025**).
⚠ Not **Saktivarman**; **Ammanga Devi** (daughter of **Rajendra I**) married **Rajaraja Narendra**.
xa: **Madhurantaki** married **Rajendra Chalukya = Kulottunga I**.
**Saktivarman I** was Vimaladitya's elder brother.

85.s: After whose ouster did Saktivarman I rule Vengi with the help of Rajaraja I?
85.x: Saktivarman I, the elder brother of Vimaladitya, ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I’s help after Jatachoda Bhima was ousted.
85.tq: Use the political sequence of ouster, assistance and rule to identify the correct figure.
xs: **Saktivarman I** ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I's help after **Jatachoda Bhima** was ousted — option **(1)** is correct.
**Someshvara II** was defeated by Virarajendra; **Mahinda V** by Rajendra I; **Pallava Aparajita** by Aditya I.
xa: Saktivarman I was **Vimaladitya's elder brother**.
**Rajaraja I** placed **Saktivarman and Vimaladitya** in Vengi.

85.s: Whose daughter was Madhurantaki, the wife of Kulottunga I?
85.x: Madhurantaki was the daughter of Rajendra II and married Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I).
85.tq: one-liner

85.s: Whom did Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I, marry?
85.x: Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra in 1022. Their son was Rajendra Chalukya, who later became Kulottunga I.
85.tq: Test the matrimonial alliance through the bride–groom pair.
xs: **Ammanga Devi** married **Rajaraja Narendra** (**16 Aug 1022**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Rajendra Chalukya** was their son; **Vimaladitya** married **Kundavai**.
xa: Their son became **Kulottunga I**.
The **Kundavai** and **Ammanga Devi** marriages made Kulottunga I heir to both thrones.

85.s: Who was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi?
85.x: Parantaka Chola was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya before the merger under Kulottunga I.
85.tq: Distinguish the last ruler of the line from the last ruler of the earlier Eastern Chalukya branch.
xs: The last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi was **Parantaka Chola** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajaraja Chola Ganga** was a Vengi viceroy (Tekkali inscription); **Rajendra Chalukya** became **Kulottunga I**, the first of the line.
**Vijayaditya VII** died in **1075**, after which Kulottunga I merged Vengi.
xa: Viceroys (sons of Kulottunga I): **Rajaraja III (Mummadi Chola)** and **Vira Chola**, at **Jagannathapuram**.
Vira Chola was viceroy **twice** and **crowned at Jagannathapuram**.

85.s: What did Kulottunga I do after the death of Vijayaditya VII in 1075?
o: merged Vengi with his Chola dominions
abandoned the Chola kingdom and returned to China
transferred the Chola capital to Uraiyur
85.x: After Vijayaditya VII’s death in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with his Chola dominions and ruled both regions, giving rise to the Chalukya-Chola association.
85.tq: Follow the succession event to determine its political consequence.
xs: After **Vijayaditya VII**'s death (**1075**), Kulottunga I **merged Vengi** with his Chola dominions — option **(2)** is correct.
Ruling both = **"Chalukya-Chola"**.
xa: First king of the Chalukya-Chola line (APPSC G2 **2011**).
**Mandalika Yugam** (**1076** to about **1210**) followed.

85.s: The Chola viceroy Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), son of Kulottunga I, installed whom in Kalinga?
85.x: Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola) installed Anantavarman Chodaganga in Kalinga; Gonka I was his commander.
85.tq: one-liner

85.s: With which place is Jananathapura, where the Chola viceroy Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned, identified?
85.x: Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama); his Tekkali inscription records his rule.
85.tq: one-liner

85.s: Who was the last Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi?
85.x: Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya; Parantaka Chola was the last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi.
85.tq: one-liner

85.s: Which ruler united the Tamil (Chola) and Andhra (Vengi) kingdoms?
85.x: Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; Vengi had been a prize in the Chola-Chalukya wars, and the Mandalika Yugam followed (1076 to c. 1210).
xa: The **Kundavai** and **Ammanga Devi** marriages made Kulottunga I heir to both thrones.
After **Koppam**, Someshwara took the title **Vengi Purveshwara**.

85.s: Which period of Andhra history followed the merger of Vengi with the Chola dominions and is known as the Mandalika Yugam?
85.x: After the Chalukya-Chola merger, the Mandalika Yugam lasted from 1076 to about 1210.

85.s: The Tekkali inscription belongs to which Chola viceroy of Vengi?
85.x: Rajaraja Chola Ganga, crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama), is known from the Tekkali inscription.

85.s: Who was the commander of Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), the son of Kulottunga I and viceroy of Vengi?
85.x: Gonka I was the commander of the viceroy Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), who ruled from Jagannathapuram.

85.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas after Kulottunga I?
o: Complete withdrawal of the Cholas from Vengi before Kulottunga I
Strengthening of the central bureaucracy and disappearance of local chiefs
Abolition of local authority by the Pandyas
Weakening of the central bureaucracy and growth of local chieftains
85.x: After Kulottunga I, the central bureaucracy weakened and local chieftains grew in power. The Chalukya-Cholas subsequently declined with the rise of the Pandyas.
85.tq: Identify the cause–effect chain and reject the option that reverses the administrative trend.
xs: After Kulottunga I, the **central bureaucracy weakened** and **local chieftains grew** — option **(4)** is correct.
The opposite (stronger centre, chiefs gone) is wrong.
xa: The Chalukya-Cholas declined with the **rise of the Pandyas**.
Last ruler **Rajendra III** was gone by **1279**.
Kulottunga I ruled **1070-1120**.

85.s: What did the Chola king Kulottunga I (1070-1122 CE) abolish?
85.x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls and married his daughter to a Sinhala prince; the Brihadeeswara temple was built by Rajaraja I.
n: Kulottunga I ruled from 1070 to 1122 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I abolished tolls. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I gave complete freedom to Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I married his daughter to a Sinhala prince. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: ⚠ Other notes give his reign as **1070-1120**.
He was born **Rajendra Chalukya**, son of **Rajaraja Narendra** and **Ammanga Devi**.
He sent **72 merchants to China** (UPPSC 1992).
Title **Sungam Tavirtta Chola** (abolisher of tolls); built **Kulottunga Cholapuram**.

85.s: Who was the mother of Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I), son of Rajaraja Narendra?
85.x: Kulottunga I, also called Rajendra Chalukya, was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi and took the Chola throne in 1070 CE.
xa: He merged **Vengi** in **1075**.
Ammanga Devi was the daughter of **Rajendra I**.

85.s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send in his embassy to China?
85.x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China as part of the diplomatic and commercial contact recorded for his reign.
85.tq: Treat the merchant count as a direct numerical recall point and compare the close alternatives.
xs: Kulottunga I sent **72 merchants to China** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is recorded as a **72-member merchant mission** (UPPSC **1992**).
xa: He conquered **Kalinga** (Jayamkondar's **Kalingattuparani**).
He built **Kulottunga Cholapuram** (Visakhapatnam).

85.s: In which year did Kulottunga I send 72 merchants to China?
85.x: Kulottunga I sent a goodwill mission of 72 merchants to China in 1077.
85.tq: one-liner

85.s: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the Cholas: B. C.
o: The Chola Empire was founded by Parantaka-I
