85.s: Who among the following laid the foundation of the Chola Empire in the IXth century AD?
85.x: Vijayalaya founded the imperial Chola empire in the 9th century (850 CE, capture of Thanjavur). Parantaka and Rajaraja were later kings; Krishna I was a Rashtrakuta.

85.s: Which region is called the Granary of South India?
85.x: Thanjavur, in the fertile Kaveri delta, is called the granary (rice bowl) of South India. Madras, Kanyakumari and the Coromandel coast as a whole are not given this name.

85.s: Which of the following statement is CORRECT about Chola kings?
o: The Chola Empire was founded by Rajendra I.
Aditya I succeeded Vijayalaya to become the ruler of the empire.
Aditya I was popularly called the Victor of the Ganges.
85.src: APPSC 2023 Screening test (Online Mode) to the post of Deput
85.x: Aditya I (871-907) succeeded his father Vijayalaya. Rajendra I did not found the empire, and the 'victor of the Ganges' (Gangaikonda) title belongs to Rajendra I, not Aditya I or Vijayalaya.

85.s: In which region was the Chola empire expanded?
o: Coromandel Coast and some region of Deccan
85.x: The Chola empire covered the Coromandel coast (Cholamandalam) and parts of the Deccan up to the Tungabhadra and Krishna. Vijayanagara, Malabar and the Hoysala country were not its core.

85.s: The capital of Cholas was -
85.x: Tanjore (Thanjavur) was the capital of the imperial Cholas from Vijayalaya; Gangaikondacholapuram came later. Kaveripattinam was a Sangam-age port, Kanchi and Mahabalipuram were Pallava.

85.s: Which dynasty assumed dominance in South India under the reign of Rajaraja I during 985-1016 AD?
85.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
85.x: Under Rajaraja I (985-1014) the Cholas became the dominant power of South India; his accession began the golden age of the Chola empire.

85.s: From which of the following is the name 'Coromandel' derived?
85.x: 'Coromandel' comes from Cholamandalam, not Tondaimandalam (the former Pallava country); the Chola core was the Kaveri delta.
xa: **Tondaimandalam** was annexed by **Aditya I** from the Pallavas.
Early capital **Uraiyur**; imperial capital **Thanjavur**.

85.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Imperial Cholas flourished approximately from the 4th to the 6th century CE.
Parantaka I defeated the Pandyas and Sri Lanka.
Rajaraja I ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
Aditya I defeated the Pallava ruler Aparajita and expanded northward.
85.x: Option A is incorrect: the Imperial Cholas, founded by Vijayalaya, flourished from about the 9th to the 13th century CE. Parantaka I did fight the Pandyas and Sri Lanka, Rajaraja I ruled 985–1014 CE, and Aditya I defeated Aparajita.
85.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Imperial Chola period lasted from approximately the 9th to the 13th century CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Parantaka I defeated the Pandyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Parantaka I defeated Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajaraja I ruled from 985 to 1014 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Aditya I defeated the Pallava ruler Aparajita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Aditya I expanded the Chola territory northward. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the Imperial Cholas flourished **from the 4th to the 6th century CE** — option **(1)**.
They flourished from about the **9th to the 13th century CE**.
The others are correct: **Parantaka I** defeated the **Pandyas and Sri Lanka**; **Rajaraja I** ruled **985 to 1014 CE**; **Aditya I** defeated Pallava **Aparajita**.
xa: Parantaka I lost the **Battle of Thakkolam** to the **Rashtrakutas** in **949 CE**.
Parantaka I took **Madurai** — title **Madurai-konda**.
**Uttaramerur inscriptions** belong to Parantaka I.
Chola inscriptions are the **most voluminous** in South India.

85.s: Where was Vijayalaya a feudatory of the Pallavas before he founded the imperial Chola line?

85.s: From whom did Vijayalaya capture Thanjavur in 850 CE?

85.s: Who founded the Imperial Chola dynasty by capturing Tanjavur?
85.x: Vijayalaya founded the Imperial Chola line in the mid-9th century by taking Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars. Aditya I, Parantaka I and Rajaraja I were later rulers.

n: Vijayalaya Chola founded the Imperial Chola dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Vijayalaya Chola captured Tanjavur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xs: **Vijayalaya Chola** founded the Imperial Chola dynasty by **capturing Tanjavur** — option **(2)**.

**Aditya I** succeeded him; **Parantaka I** and **Rajaraja I** came later.

Imperial Cholas: c. **850-1279 CE**, rising from the **Kaveri delta**.
Last ruler **Rajendra III** was gone by **1279**.

85.s: Who succeeded Vijayalaya, the founder of the imperial Chola line?
85.x: Vijayalaya founded the line by taking Thanjavur in 850 CE; his successor was Aditya I, not Parantaka I.

Consider the following statements:

85.x: Vijayalaya took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE, but he was succeeded by Aditya I; Parantaka I came after Aditya I.

85.s: Who among the following was killed at Koppam while mounted on an elephant?
85.x: Rajadhiraja I was killed at Koppam on the back of an elephant and was known by the title Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar.
85.tq: Link the unusual death description with the correct ruler.
xs: **Rajadhiraja I** was killed at **Koppam (1053)** on an elephant's back — option **(1)** is correct.
Hence his title **Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar**.
**Rajendra II** was crowned on the battlefield and claimed victory.
xa: His opponent: Western Chalukya **Ahavamalla Someshwara I**, who then took the title **Vengi Purveshwara**.
Rajadhiraja I ruled from **1044**; other title **Vijaya Rajendra**.

85.s: By what other name was the Chola king Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) known?
85.x: Rajaraja I, also known as Arumolivarman, ruled 985-1014 CE and made the Chola state the largest in South India.
xa: Titles: **Ulakalanda Perumal** (land survey) and **Mummudi Chola** (northern Sri Lanka = **Mummadichola Mandalam**).
Built **Brihadeshvara (Rajarajeshwara)** temple, **1010**.

85.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with which Chola ruler?
85.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with Parantaka I. He was defeated at Takkolam in 949 CE.

xs: The **Uttaramerur inscriptions** belong to **Parantaka I** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vijayalaya** was the founder; **Rajaraja I** built Brihadeshvara; **Kulottunga I** began the Chalukya-Chola line.
xa: Parantaka I took **Madurai** → title **Madurai-konda**.
His forces were beaten at **Takkolam (949)** by Rashtrakuta **Krishna III**.

85.s: Who was the last ruler of the Imperial Chola dynasty?
85.x: Rajendra III (1246–1279) was the last Imperial Chola; the Pandyas rose after him.

85.s: Which Chola ruler was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam?
85.x: Rajendra II was crowned on the field at Koppam after Rajadhiraja I was killed; he set up a victory pillar at Kolhapur.

85.s: Which statement correctly describes Kulottunga I?
o: He was killed at Koppam while riding an elephant.
He was the founder who captured Thanjavur in 850 CE.
He defeated Pallava Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.
He was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line and ruled from 1070 to 1122 CE.
85.x: Kulottunga I was the first ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line (1070-1122 CE). Rajadhiraja I died at Koppam, Vijayalaya took Thanjavur, and Aditya I defeated Aparajita and annexed Tondaimandalam.

85.x: Rajendra II, crowned on the battlefield of Koppam, set up a victory pillar at Kolhapur.

85.x: Uraiyur was the early Sangam Chola capital. Thanjavur became important under the Imperial Cholas, while Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I.

85.s: Who built Visakhapatnam city?
85.x: Kulottunga Chola I built Visakhapatnam, named Kulottunga Cholapatnam after himself. Arikesari II, Narasimha II and Pandurangadu are distractors.

85.s: Brihadeeshwara Temple of Thanjavur was built during the reign of Chola emperor –

85.s: Who among the following Chola rulers is credited to have built a huge artificial lake known as Chola Gangam?
85.x: Rajendra I dug the huge Chola Gangam (now Ponneri) lake at Gangaikondacholapuram to mark his Ganga expedition; it was not the work of his father Rajaraja I.

85.s: Who was the founder of ‘Gangai Konda Cholapuram’ ?
85.x: Rajendra I founded Gangaikondacholapuram as his new capital to commemorate his victorious north-Indian (Ganga) campaign.

85.s: In which year was Gangaikondacholapuram founded as the new Chola capital?

85.s: Under which dynasty was the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur built?

85.x: Rajaraja I completed the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) temple in 1010 CE.

85.x: Amma I made Rajamahendravaram the capital; Rajaraja Narendra later made it famous.

Consider the following statements about Rajamahendravaram:

85.s: Which of the following is the title of Rajendra Chola?
85.x: Gangaikonda Chola ('the Chola who took the Ganga') is Rajendra I's best-known title, taken after the Ganga expedition of 1022. Kadaram Kondan (option d) was also his title, so the question has two right options; Singalantaka and Telinga-kula-kala were titles of Rajaraja I.

85.s: Who assumed the title of ‘Gangaikondachola’?
85.x: Rajendra I took the title Gangaikonda Chola after his northern (Ganga) campaign of 1022, in which he defeated the Pala king Mahipala I.

85.s: Which of the following was not one of the titles assumed by the Chola king Rajendra?
85.x: Rajendra I's titles were Mudikonda Cholan, Gangaikonda Cholan, Kadaramkondan and Pandita Cholan. Tyagasamudra is not one of them, so it is the exception.

85.s: Who was the Chola king to have conquered Bengal?
85.x: Rajendra I's northern expedition (1022) crossed the Ganga and defeated the Pala king Mahipala I of Bengal, earning him the title Gangaikonda Chola. (Options b and c repeat Rajendra I.)

85.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
85.x: Maduraikonda was the title of Parantaka I, not Kulottunga I. Rajaraja I was known as Mummadi Chola, Rajendra I as Gangaikondachola, and Rajadhiraja I as Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar.
85.tq: Find the swapped title–ruler pair among closely related Chola rulers.
xs: **Kulottunga I — Maduraikonda** is wrong — option **(1)**; Maduraikonda was **Parantaka I**'s title.
Correct pairs: **Rajadhiraja I — Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar**; **Rajendra I — Gangaikondachola**; **Rajaraja I — Mummadi Chola**.

85.s: Which Chola ruler took the title 'Ulakalanda Perumal', reflecting a land survey and revenue reorganisation?
85.x: Ulakalanda Perumal and Mummudi Chola were titles of Rajaraja I; Madurai-konda was Parantaka I's and Gangaikonda Chola Rajendra I's.
xa: Rajendra I's other titles: **Kadaram Kondan** (Kedah) and **Pandita Chola** (patron of learning).

91.s: Among the following who established Devagiri as an independent Yadava Kingdom?

91.s: Which Yadava king defeated Rudradeva?
91.x: Yadava Jaitugi (Jaitrapala) defeated and killed Kakatiya Rudradeva and held the young Ganapatideva captive (Hemadri; Paithan plate). Rudradeva is the victim, not the victor.

91.x: The Bidar fort inscription records Rudramadevi's victory over the Yadava king Mahadeva. Chandupatla records her death, Bayyaram is Mailamba's tank record and Hanumakonda is Rudradeva's 1163 record.

91.s: Who was the ruler of Devgiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion?

92.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?

92.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before taking over the kingdom?

92.x: The Kakatiyas were first subordinates of the Rashtrakutas, and only later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them.

92.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba traces the Kakatiyas from Venna (Venna Bhupati) as the first of the line. The Kazipet inscription names Beta I; Junagarh and Vijayawada are unrelated.

92.x: The Kakatiya rulers, as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, bore the title Mahamandaleswara (Beta II took it). It is a feudatory title, so the overlord Chalukya and Rashtrakuta kings did not use it as their style.

92.s: Who is the Guru of Ganapati Deva?

92.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.
xs: **Kamasani** belonged to the **Viriyala** family, so option **(3)** is correct.
She made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal (**Gudur** inscription).
xa: **Beta I** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
**Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.
**Recherla** = Rudra; **Kayastha** = Prasadaditya; **Malyala** = Gundiya, Chauda Senani.

92.s: Which Kakatiya feudatory bore the title 'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya'?
92.x: Prasadaditya of the Recherla family bore the titles Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya and Raya Pitamahanka. Recherla Rudra was Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya.

92.s: Chouda Samudram was built by a member of which Kakatiya feudatory family?
92.x: Malyala Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram.

92.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Navabrahma temple complex at Alampur consists of nine temples.
The Thousand Pillars Temple at Anamakonda was built by Rudradeva.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was constructed by Krishnadevaraya.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD.
92.x: Option C is incorrect: the Ramappa Temple at Palampet was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD, not by Krishnadevaraya, who built the Hazara Ramaswamy Temple at Hampi. The other statements are right.
92.tq: Check the builder named in each statement.
n: Navabrahma is a nine-temple complex. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Navabrahma is located at Alampur, also called Alampuram. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Ramappa Temple is located at Palampet in Warangal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Ramappa Temple was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Thousand Pillars Temple is located at Anumakonda, also called Anamakonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Thousand Pillars Temple was built by Rudra Deva. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xs: The incorrect statement is **Ramappa Temple was constructed by Krishnadevaraya** — option **(3)**.
The **Ramappa Temple** at **Palampet** was built by **Recharla Rudra** in **1213 AD**, in **Ganapatideva**'s reign.
The others are correct: the **Navabrahma** complex at **Alampur** has **nine temples**; the **Thousand Pillars Temple** at Anamakonda was built by **Rudradeva**.
xa: Ramappa is an example of **Ekasila architecture**; it also has the **Ramappa tank**.
Ramappa became a UNESCO site in **2021** — star-shaped platform, **floating bricks**.
**Rudreshwara Temple** — built **1163 CE**.
**Palampet** inscription — **Recherla Rudra**, **1213**.

92.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Swayambhu Devalayam and Kesavala – Chalukya Bhima I
92.x: The Jaina Basthi was built by Mailamma. Bhimeswara Temple was built by Chalukya Bhima I, the Thousand-Pillar Temple by Rudra Deva and the Swayambhu Devalayam by Prola Raju II.
n: Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeshwara Temple on the banks of the Godavari. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Rudra Deva built the Thousand-Pillar Temple at Anumakonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prola Raju II built the Swayambhu Devalayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prola Raju II built Kesavala. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Mailamma built the Jaina Basthi at Anamakonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xa: ⚠ Other notes credit the **Kadalalaya Jainavasadi** to Prola II's minister **Chetanamatya** and wife **Mailama**.
⚠ **Kesamudram** = Prola I; **Kesari Samudram** = Rudradeva; **Arikesari Samudram** = Prola II.
**Ramappa** is an example of **Ekasila architecture**.
**Lakkavaram and Ghanapur** tanks — **Ganapatideva**.

92.s: In which year was the Ramappa Temple at Palampet inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
92.x: The Ramappa Temple, noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
xa: It was built in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
Its builder's title was **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'**.
The **Palampet** inscription records it.

92.s: Which minister of Beta I built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram?
92.x: Beta I's minister Naranayya built the Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram.

92.s: The Ramappa temple at Palampet is noted for the use of which material?
92.x: Ramappa, a UNESCO site (2021), stands on a star-shaped platform and is noted for its floating bricks.

92.s: Which of the following Kakatiya pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mahadeva – construction of the Ramappa temple
Durgaraja – donations to the Betesvara temple
Prola II – victory pillar at Srisailam
92.x: The Ramappa temple belongs to Ganapatideva's reign, not Mahadeva's; the other pairs are correct.
xa: Beta II's title: **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva** (**1195-1199**) died in the revenge war against the Yadavas.
Ramappa = UNESCO World Heritage Site, **2021**.

92.s: Where is the Kakatiya inscription that refers to the Ramappa temple?
92.x: The Palampet inscription refers to the Ramappa temple; Sanigaram refers to Juddha Mallajinalaya, Dharmasagara to Jalakaranda and Pithapuram to Kolleru Lake.
xa: Pithapuram is a **Velanati** (Prithvisvara) record.
**Motupalli** (**1244**) = protection for foreign traders.
**Bayyaram** (**1219**) = best early genealogy.

92.s: Whose accession is recorded in the Draksharama inscription (1158) of minister Inangala Brahmi Reddi?
92.x: The Draksharama inscription of 1158 records Rudradeva's accession and calls him Vinaya Bhushan.

92.s: In which year was the Rudreshwara (Thousand Pillar) Temple built by Rudradeva?
92.x: The Rudreswara (Thousand Pillar) Temple is a Kakatiya temple built in 1163 CE by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I.
n: Rudreshwara Temple belongs to the Kakatiya Dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built in 1163 CE. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xa: The **Thousand-Pillar Temple** is credited to **Rudra Deva**; one note credits **Prola II** — follow Rudradeva, **1163**.
**Ramappa Temple**, Palampet — **Recharla Rudra**, **1213 AD**.
**Swayambhu Devalayam** and **Kesavala** — **Prola Raju II**.
Rudradeva shifted the capital from **Hanamkonda** to **Orugallu** (APPSC G2 2019).

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rudra Deva ascended the throne in 1158.
2. Kumaragiri Reddy ascended the throne in 1386.
3. Durga Nripathi ascended the throne in 1296.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
92.x: Rudra Deva came to the throne in 1158 (Draksharama inscription) and Kumaragiri Reddi in 1386, so 1 and 2 are correct. Durgaraja (Durga Nripathi) ruled 1108–1116, not from 1296, so 3 is wrong.
n: Rudra Deva ascended the throne in 1158. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Mahadeva ascended the throne in 1196. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Pratapa Rudra ascended the throne in 1296. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Kumaragiri Reddy ascended the throne in 1386. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]

92.s: Which of the following Kakatiya kings ruled the whole of Andhradesa as a unified sovereign, combining the Andhra, Telangana and Rayalaseema regions of present Andhra Pradesh, from Ganjam in the north to Kanchipuram in the south?
92.x: Ganapatideva (1199-1262) conquered coastal Andhra, Velanadu, Nellore and Kalinga and reached Kanchi, uniting 'Telugudesam' under one sovereign. Prataparudra I (Rudradeva) began the independent kingdom; Beta I was a feudatory.

92.s: Kakatiya king Ganapatideva ruled South India during which year?
92.x: Ganapatideva, the greatest and longest-reigning Kakatiya, ruled 1199-1262 (about 63 years). 1050-1323 spans the whole dynasty and 1411-1530 is unrelated.

92.s: The mighty Kakatiya king who expanded his empire to Kanchi?
92.x: Ganapatideva conquered coastal Andhra, Nellore and Kalinga and his forces marched to Kanchi (Chebrolu 1228, Ganapeswaram 1231 records). Beta I, Prola I and Prola II were early feudatory rulers.

92.s: Who was the successor of Ganapatideva?
92.x: Ganapatideva had no son and nominated his daughter Rudramadevi as successor. Rudradeva was his uncle and predecessor's predecessor; Recherla Rudra was a general.

92.s: After the Satvahanas, which Kakatiya ruler was successful in bringing the whole Telugu under one rule in AD 1199?
92.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
92.x: Ganapatideva, whose inscriptions begin in 1199, united all the Telugu lands ('Telugudesam') under one rule for the first time since the Satavahanas. Rudradeva had only Telangana and part of coastal Andhra.

92.s: The most powerful Kakatiya ruler who expanded the empire upto Kanchi was
92.x: Ganapatideva, the most powerful Kakatiya, extended the empire to Kanchi. Beta I, Prola I and Prola II were early feudatories.

92.s: After the Satvahanas, which Kakatiya ruler was successful in bringing the whole Telugu area under one rule in AD 1199?
92.src: Social and Culture History & Welfare Programmes paper 2019
92.x: Ganapatideva (from 1199) brought the whole Telugu area under one rule, after the Satavahanas. Rudradeva, Mahadeva and Prola II did not.

92.s: Where is the first inscription of Ganapatideva (26 December 1199) found?
92.x: Released from Yadava captivity in 1199, Ganapatideva issued his first inscription at Manthena; he later bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara.
xa: General **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
He married Pinnachodi's daughters **Narama and Perama**; their brother **Jayapa** became Gajasahani.
He ruled **1199-1262** (**63 years**), the greatest Kakatiya.
**Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) protected foreign traders.

92.s: Who bore the title 'Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda'?
92.x: Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka took this title after killing Velanati Prithviswara in 1210.

92.s: In which year did Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore kill Prithviswara, ending the Velanati kingdom?
92.x: Prithviswara was killed in 1210, ending the Velanati kingdom, and both rulers took the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
xa: Final end of the Velanati Chodas: **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** killed in **1257**.
Prithviswara's **Pithapuram** inscription names **Kolleru Lake**.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.

92.s: In 1257, Ganapatideva, allied with Akkana and Bayyana, killed which ruler, finally ending the Velanati Chodas?
92.x: The 1257 alliance killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, the final end of the Velanati Chodas; Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi, not Ganapatideva.
xa: Ganapatideva restored **Manumasiddhi II** to the Nellore throne.
**Tikkana** went as envoy to seek his help.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were enemies of Manumasiddhi.

92.s: Ganapatideva married Narama and Perama and made their brother Jayapa Gajasahani. Whose daughters were they?
92.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, chief of the elephant forces.

92.s: Ganapatideva restored which ruler to the Nellore throne after the poet Tikkana came to him as envoy?
92.x: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne; Tikkana went to him as envoy.
xa: In **1210** Ganapati and **Choda Tikka** killed **Prithviswara** — end of the Velanati kingdom.
**1257**: killing of **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** = final end of the Velanati Chodas.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi** (from **1201**).
Tikkana dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to Manumasiddhi.

92.s: From the reign of which Kakatiya ruler did Telugu replace Sanskrit in inscriptions?
92.x: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions from Ganapatideva's reign, not Rudradeva's.
xa: The Kakatiyas left **1,000+** inscriptions.
**Ramappa temple (Palampet)** became a UNESCO site in **2021**.
First mention = **Magallu 956**; first sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**.
Last ruler = **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara names which lake?
92.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara names Kolleru Lake (APPSC G2 2017).

92.s: To whom did Tikkana dedicate his Nirvachanottara Ramayana?
92.x: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi of Nellore, not to Ganapatideva.

92.s: Who was Ganapatideva's general who took Divi during the coastal campaign from 1201?
92.x: From 1201, Ganapatideva's general Mutyalachaundaraya took Divi in the coastal campaign.

92.s: In which battle did the Pandyas defeat Ganapatideva in 1263?
92.x: In 1263 the Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur (Muthukuru).

92.s: Which part of the Kakatiya kingdom fell to the Pandyas after the battle of Muttukur (1263)?
92.x: After the Pandyas beat Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263, Nellore passed to them.

92.s: For control of which regions did Ganapatideva fight the Eastern Gangas?
92.x: Ganapatideva fought the Eastern Gangas for southern Kalinga and Vengi.

92.s: Who was the mother of Rudrama Devi who guided her training as successor to Ganapatideva?
92.x: Her mother Kupama Devi guided her training; Mailamba was Ganapatideva's sister. Rudrama Devi ruled 1262-1289.
xa: Ganapati's daughters: **Rudramamba** (m. **Veerabhadra**) and **Ganapamba** (m. the **Kota** chief).
Sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
Mailamba issued the **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**).
Rudrama Devi was the **fourth independent ruler**.

92.s: Which of the following powers was NOT defeated by Rudrama Devi?
92.x: Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas, the Eastern Gangas and the Seunas of Devagiri; the Western Chalukyas had declined long before her reign.
n: Kakatiya Rudrama Devi defeated the Seuna rulers of Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Eastern Gangas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
xa: She was the **daughter** of **Ganapati Dev** and the **fourth independent ruler**.
She was a **female ruler** who succeeded as **putrika**.
Her title **Rayagajakesari** is credited for her victory over the **Yadavas** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
⚠ Another APPSC key (2017) gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

92.s: In whose reign did Marco Polo visit the Kakatiya port Motupalli ('Mutfili')?
92.x: Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya port Motupalli (Mutfili) c. 1292–93, in Rudrama's reign, and praised the ruling queen.

92.s: Veerabhadra, the husband of Rudrama Devi, was a prince of which of the following?
92.x: Rudrama Devi married Veerabhadra, a Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukya prince; Ganapamba married the Kota chief.

92.s: Ganapamba, daughter of Ganapatideva, was married to a chief of which family?
92.x: Ganapamba married the Kota chief; Rudrama married the Nidadavolu prince Veerabhadra.

92.s: Ganapatideva's sisters Mailamba and Kundamamba were married to the sons of whom?
92.x: Mailamba and Kundamamba, Ganapatideva's sisters, married sons of Natavadi Buddharaja.

92.s: Which set contains only works or grants of Ganapatideva's reign?
o: Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
92.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks and the grant of Ganapavaram villages belong to Ganapatideva's reign.
xa: **Chouda Samudram** was built by **Malyala Chauda Senani**.
**Betesvaralayam** was built by **Beta II**.
Exam angle: match **tank → builder** and **ruler → temple**.

92.s: Which Kakatiya ruler had the longest reign, of 63 years?
92.x: Ganapatideva ruled 1199–1262, about 63 years, the longest Kakatiya reign.

92.s: Rudrama Devi, daughter of Ganapatideva, was married to which Chalukya prince?
92.x: Rudrama Devi married the Chalukya prince Veerabhadra; her daughter Rudramma married the Yadava prince Ellanadeva.
xa: Another daughter **Ruyyamma** married **Induluri Annayya**.
She ruled as **'Rudradeva Maharaja'** from **1258** (co-regency).
Royal guru: **Visveshwara Shivacharya** (Mandaram agrahara).
She was the second great woman ruler of medieval India after **Razia Sultana**.

92.s: Which of the following statements about the political opposition faced by Rudrama Devi is correct?
o: Nellore remained permanently under Kakatiya control after Muttukur.
The Pandyas supported Rudrama Devi against Kayastha Ambadeva.
She faced only internal opposition and no external attacks.
Her opponents included the Yadavas and Pandyas, while after Muttukur in 1263 Nellore came under the Pandyas.
92.x: Rudrama Devi faced internal rebellions and attacks by the Yadavas and Pandyas. After Muttukur in 1263, Nellore was under Pandya control.
92.tq: Check the direction of political support and the change in territorial control.
xs: Her opponents included the **Yadavas** and **Pandyas**, and after **Muttukur (1263)** **Nellore** was under the **Pandyas**, so option **(4)** is correct.
She also faced internal revolts (**Harihara and Murari**, **Ambadeva**). **Ambadeva** revolted **with Pandya support**, so the Pandyas did not back her.
xa: Ambadeva's victories are in the **Tripurantakam inscription**.
**Kalinga's** Narasimhadeva occupied **Vengi** (**1262**).
She died fighting **Ambadeva** in **1289**.

92.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Thousand Pillar inscription?
o: It records the Kakatiya declaration of independence.
It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
92.x: The Thousand Pillar (Anumakonda) inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva, not Ganapatideva.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bayyaram tank inscription — 1219 — genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Palampet inscription — 1213 — Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam — 1244 — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 concerns protection for foreign traders. Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya is associated with the Sanigaram inscription.
92.tq: Find the one exchanged fact in an inscription–date–content set.
xs: The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) gave **protection to foreign traders**. It is not about the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, so option **(3)** is the wrong pair.
The **Juddha Mallajinalaya** is linked to the **Sanigaram** inscription, built by **Beta I's** minister **Naranayya**.
The other pairs are correct: **Bayyaram 1219**, **Palampet 1213**, **Draksharamam 1158**.
xa: Motupalli was issued by **Ganapatideva**.
**APPSC 2025** key matched Sanigaram to **Rudradeva**.
The **Draksharamam** inscription was issued by minister **Inangala Brahma Reddi**.

92.s: The Kakatiya Dharmasagara inscription mentions which musical instrument?
92.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the musical instrument Jalakaranda (APPSC 2019).

92.s: Who composed the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of Rudradeva?
92.x: The 1163 Anumakonda inscription, which declares Kakatiya independence, was composed by Achitendru.

92.s: Which scholar found the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of 1163?
92.x: The Thousand Pillar inscription of Rudradeva was found by J.S. Fleet.

92.s: Which inscription records the victories of Ambadeva?
92.x: The Tripuranthakam inscription records the victories of Kayastha Ambadeva.

92.s: In June 2026, an ASI survey of which region copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records of the 2nd–16th centuries?
92.x: ASI's Nallamala survey (June 2026) copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records.

92.s: Who defeated Ganapatideva in 1263?
92.x: In 1263 Jatavarman Sundara Pandya defeated the Kakatiya forces at Muttukur (Nellore), and Nellore passed to the Pandyas. The Velanati Chodas had already been destroyed; the Yadavas and Hoysalas did not win this battle.

92.s: Which of the following defeated Ganapatideva in 1263
92.x: The Pandyas under Jatavarman Sundara Pandya defeated Ganapatideva's forces at Muttukur in 1263 and took Nellore. The Velanati Chodas had ended earlier.

92.s: Who shifted the Kakatiya Capital from Hanumakonda to Warangal?
92.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
92.x: Ganapatideva shifted the Kakatiya capital from Hanumakonda (Anamakonda) to Warangal (Orugallu) in 1254.

92.s: According to the Musunuri inscription, how did Pratapa Rudra die?
o: He died while constructing a tank.
He died in a battle at Vijayapuri.
He died jumping into the Narmada.
92.x: The Musunuri (Vilasa) record of the Musunuri Nayakas says Prataparudra, captured by the Delhi army, died by jumping into the Narmada on the way to Delhi.
92.tq: Recall how the last Kakatiya king died.
n: Pratapa Rudra died by jumping into the Narmada. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Pratapa Rudra** **died by jumping into the Narmada** — option **(4)**.
The notes record that he died by jumping into the **Narmada**.
He was not killed at **Motupalli** or **Vijayapuri**; Motupalli is linked with **Ganapatideva**'s **1244** Abhaya Sasanam.
xa: **Motupalli** inscription protected foreign traders.
**Tripuranthakam** inscription records **Ambadeva**'s victories.
**Dharmasagar** inscription names the instrument **Jalakaranda** (APPSC 2019).
**Bayyaram tank** inscription of **Mailamba** (**1219**) gives the best early genealogy.

92.s: Which commander of Prataparudra defeated the Hoysala Ballala III after 1316?
92.x: Prataparudra's commander Pedarudru defeated Ballala III after 1316; earlier, Veera Ballala II's advance had led Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
xa: **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**; **Mahadeva** died in the revenge war.
The Yadava conflict began under **Prola II**.
**Velanati Chodas** killed **Prola II**; Rudradeva avenged him.
Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy in **1159**.

92.s: In whose reign did the Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas (Sevunas) of Devagiri begin?
92.x: The Yadava conflict began under Prola II, who was killed by the Velanati Chodas; Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy in 1159.
xa: Prola II (**1116-1157**) set up a **victory pillar** at **Srisailam**.
He is credited with **Arikesari Samudram** and the **Swayambhu** temple.
Rudradeva made **Vellanki Gangadhara** viceroy of Sabbinadu.
Rudradeva declared **independence** in **1163**.

92.s: Which Yadava ruler killed the Kakatiya Rudradeva?

93.s: The Kakatiya King Pratapa Rudra became a captive at the end of his life to:

93.s: The person who defeated Prataparudra-II and took him captive?

93.s: After the victory in 1323, the Delhi Sultans changed the name of Warangal to?
93.x: After capturing Orugallu in 1323, the Tughlaqs renamed Warangal Sultanpur. The other names are distractors.

93.s: In which year did Kakatiya kingdom fall?
93.x: The Kakatiya kingdom fell in 1323 when Ulugh Khan took Warangal. 1313 and 1318 were tributary treaties; 1336 is the founding of Vijayanagara.

93.s: Which event directly weakened the Kakatiya resistance during the 1323 siege of Orugallu?
o: The revolt of Harihara and Murari
The occupation of Vengi by Ganga Narasimhadeva

xa: After **5 months**, Prataparudra surrendered and was **captured**.
Causes of the fall: **southern disunity**, **weak cavalry**, **internal betrayal**, exhaustion from raids.
Of **75** generals, **Prolaya Nayaka**, **Racherla Singama** and **Prolaya Vema** survived and led the liberation.

93.s: After the Tughlaq conquest of Orugallu in 1323, who was placed in charge of Andhra?

**Malik Maqbul** (the converted **Jagannatha Pandit**) was stationed at Warangal.
The **1323** siege lasted **5 months**.

93.s: How long did the final Tughlaq siege of Warangal in 1323 last?
93.x: Ulugh Khan's final siege lasted five months, after Bobbareddi withdrew his forces.

93.s: Under which Sultan did Ulugh Khan lead the final siege of Warangal in 1323?
93.x: The 1323 conquest of Warangal was led by Ulugh Khan for his father, Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

93.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as a cause of the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom?

xs: A **maritime blockade by European powers** is not among the causes, so option **(3)** is the answer.

xa: The fall of Warangal (**1323**) ended the Kakatiyas.
The **Musunuri** and **Reddi** states rose from the liberation movement.
Andhra was placed under **Malik Burhanuddin**.

93.s: According to the Vilasa copper plate, in which river did the captured Prataparudra drown himself?
93.x: Prataparudra surrendered in 1323 and, while being taken towards Delhi, drowned himself; the Vilasa record names the Narmada (another account names the Kaveri).
xa: He was held captive by **Ulugh Khan**.
Orugallu was renamed **Sultanpur (Sultanpurti)**.

93.s: By what name was the converted Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit, placed at Warangal after 1323, known?
93.x: Malik Maqbul was posted at Warangal; Malik Burhanuddin, vizier of Devagiri, was in charge of Andhra.

93.s: Ulugh Khan, who took Prataparudra captive in 1323, later became which Sultan?
93.x: Ulugh Khan (Juna Khan), the captor of Prataparudra, later ruled as Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

93.s: Under the Nayankara system, who held the principalities into which the kingdom was organised?

93.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the institutional succession mentioned in relation to the Nayankara system?

Village names in **Vishnukundin** grants are pure Telugu.
Nagabu was identified by **Veturi Prabhakara Sastri**.

101.s: In which centuries did the separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs emerge?
101.x: After the Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant and the common Old Kannada–Telugu script, the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.
xa: The Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions are c. **400 BCE**, Guntur.
The separate script has **rounded letters** and vowel signs.
Telugu script derives from **Brahmi**.

101.s: Which of the following describes the Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions?
o: Sanskrit inscriptions in the common Old Kannada script
Tamil inscriptions in the Grantha script
Prakrit inscriptions in a variant of Brahmi carrying early Telugu place and personal names
Telugu inscriptions in the fully developed medieval Telugu script
101.x: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, dated approximately to 400 BCE in Guntur, use a variant of Brahmi and contain early Telugu place and personal names.
101.tq: Use the precise combination of date, place, script and linguistic evidence.
xs: The **Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions** use a **Brahmi variant** carrying **early Telugu place and personal names** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are dated c. **400 BCE**, in **Guntur**.
The fully developed Telugu script came only in the **11th-14th c.**
xa: Telugu script evolved from **Brahmi**.
Next stage: common **Old Kannada-Telugu** script (Kadamba-Chalukya).
The first Telugu word, **"Nagabu"**, is in the **Amaravati** inscription.

101.s: What was the royal language in the Prakrit age of Andhra, whose golden age came under Hala?
101.x: Prakrit was the royal language in this age (APPSC G2 2011 key), with its golden age under Hala. Sanskrit later became the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas; Telugu appears only as words in Prakrit records; Tamil is not the answer.
xs: The royal language of the Prakrit age was **Prakrit** (G2 2011 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its golden age came under **Hala**.
Telugu then appears only as **words inside Prakrit records**.
xa: **Hala's Gatha Saptasati** has Telugu words like atta, addam, potta, pilla.
Later the official language was **Sanskrit** (G2 2008 key), with Telugu as the people's language.
**Mayidavolu** plates (Prakrit, c. **300 CE**) first record "Andhrapatha".

101.s: The Telugu word 'Vepuru' occurs in which inscription?
101.x: 'Vepuru' is from the Myakadoni inscription; 'Nagabu' from Amaravati.

101.s: Which dynasty issued the Chikkulla plates, in which the Telugu plural form '-ambul' appears?
101.x: The Chikkulla plates of the Vishnukundins use the plural '-ambul' (Vijayarajya Samvatsarambul).

101.s: In which script was Telugu written in the early medieval (Kadamba–Chalukya) period?
101.x: In the Kadamba–Chalukya period a common Old Kannada–Telugu script was used; the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.

101.s: Which is regarded as the first Telugu word found in an inscription?
101.x: 'Nagabu' in the Amaravati inscription is the first Telugu word, identified by Veturi Prabhakara Sastri.

101.s: Telugu words such as atta, potta, pilla and pandi are found in which Prakrit work?
101.x: Hala's Prakrit Gatha Saptasati contains Telugu words like atta, addam, potta, tuppu, pilla and pandi.

101.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, belongs to which dynasty?
101.x: The Kalamalla inscription of about 575 CE is associated with the Renati Chola ruler Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya.
101.tq: Identify the dynasty linked with the earliest inscription.
xs: **Kalamalla** (Kadapa, c. **575 CE**) belongs to the **Renati Cholas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Issuer: **Dhanunjaya Varma** (Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya).
It is the **first Telugu inscription**, in **prose** (G2 2012 key).
xa: **Erragudipadu** (Punyakumara, Renati Chola) is the first **fully available** Telugu inscription, in geya style.
**Arumbhaka** is by **Erikal Mutturaju**, the same line as Kalamalla.
⚠ **Kalamalla** = first inscription (prose); **Addanki** = first poetic inscription.

101.s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and is written in a song or geya style?
101.x: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara of the Renati Cholas is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and uses a song or geya style.
101.tq: Distinguish between the earliest inscription and the first fully available inscription.
xs: **Erragudipadu** is the **first fully available Telugu inscription**, in **song (geya) style** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was issued by **Punyakumara**, a **Renati Chola**.
**Kalamalla** is the first Telugu inscription (prose); **Addanki** the first poetic one; **Vipparla** the "first complete early Telugu text".
xa: **Chejarla** (Kubja Vishnuvardhana) has over **50% Telugu** words.
**Vipparla** is credited to **Jayasimha Vallabha I** (APPSC key).

101.s: Which inscription contains the first Madhyakkara poem?
101.x: Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara poem; Addanki is the first Telugu poetic inscription in Taruvoja metre.
xa: Addanki was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
Bezawada was issued by **Yuddhamalla II** (Nagamalleswara temple).
Sataluru, Kandukur and Dharmavaram belong to **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.

101.s: Who issued the Addanki inscription, the first Telugu poetic inscription?
o: Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III
101.x: The Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre was issued by Panduranga (Pandaranga), commander of the Eastern Chalukya king Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Yuddhamalla II issued the Bezawada inscription, Punyakumara the Erragudipadu inscription and Kubja Vishnuvardhana the Chejarla inscription.
101.tq: Addanki = Panduranga (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III), Taruvoja
xs: **Addanki** was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of Eastern Chalukya **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Yuddhamalla II** issued **Bezawada**; **Punyakumara** issued **Erragudipadu**; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** issued **Chejarla**.
xa: Addanki is in **Taruvoja** metre — the **first Telugu verse**.
Bezawada is the **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Sataluru**: Champakamala with prasa; **Kandukur**: Seesa and Ataveladi.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I — first complete early Telugu prose inscription
Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana — more than 50 per cent Telugu words
Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I — first complete early Telugu text
Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first Telugu poetic inscription
101.x: Pitikayagulla is associated with the eighth century and post-Badami Chalukya influence, particularly in relation to early Telugu script; it is not the first Telugu poetic inscription. That distinction belongs to Addanki.
xs: **Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first poetic inscription** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Pitikayagulla** is an **8th c.** early-Telugu-script record with post-Badami Chalukya influence, near **Bestavaripeta, Prakasam**.
The first poetic inscription is **Addanki** (Panduranga).
The others are correct: **Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I**; **Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (over **50%** Telugu); **Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (p.133) credit **Vipparla** to **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Pitikayagulla was reported in **Jun 2026**; some notes place it in **Rayalaseema**.

101.s: Which of the following is NOT among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya?
101.x: Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada show pre-Nannaya written Telugu; the Motupalli epigraph is a later Kakatiya-era record.
xa: Nannaya relied on a written form tested through **five centuries** of inscriptions.
**Kalamalla** (Kadapa) by **Dhanunjaya Varma**, **Renati Chola** = **first Telugu inscription**.
**Bezawada** (**Yuddhamalla II**) = **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Erragudipadu** (**Punyakumara**) = first fully available Telugu inscription.

101.s: Why is the Chebrolu inscription significant?
o: The transition from Sanskrit to Tamil exclusively
The first use of the Madhyakkara metre
101.x: The Chebrolu inscription is noted for showing the Marga and Desi forms.
101.tq: Identify the distinctive linguistic feature associated with an inscription.
xs: The **Chebrolu inscription** shows the **Marga and Desi** forms — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first **Madhyakkara** poem is the **Bezawada** inscription.
The earliest Telugu prose is **Kalamalla**.
xa: Kakatiya-era inscriptions: **Guduru** (Beta II), **Konidena** (Opili Siddhi), **Upparapalle** (Katamaraju), **Karimnagar** (Gangadhara).
The **Desi vs Marga** debate: Bhakti poets brought native Telugu idiom against heavy Sanskrit.

101.s: Who issued the Vipparla inscription?
101.x: Vipparla is Jayasimha Vallabha I's (G2 2017 key); Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's.

101.s: To whose reign does the Chejarla inscription, with over 50% Telugu words, belong?
101.x: Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's inscription with over 50% Telugu words.

101.s: To about which year is the Kalamalla inscription, the first Telugu inscription, dated?
101.x: Kalamalla (Kadapa), by Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, dates to c. 575 CE.

101.s: The first poetic inscription in Telugu, at Addanki, is in which metre?
101.x: Addanki is the first poetic inscription, in Taruvoja; Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara.

101.s: Who issued the Bezawada inscription with the first Madhyakkara poem?
101.x: The Bezawada (Nagamalleswara temple) inscription is Yuddhamalla II's.

101.s: Which metre is used in the Kandukur inscription of Gunaga Vijayaditya?
101.x: Kandukur and Dharmavaram use Seesa and Ataveladi.

101.s: In which language were the grant details written in bilingual Eastern Chalukya records?
101.x: Eastern Chalukya records gave the praise in Sanskrit and the grant details in Telugu.

101.s: Which of the following inscription–metre pairs is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Addanki is in Taruvoja; the first Madhyakkara is in the Bezawada inscription.

101.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic and literary situation during the Kakatiya period?
o: Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed, and Telugu became the main language of inscriptions.
Persian became the principal language of Kakatiya inscriptions.
Only Tamil was used for literary composition and inscriptions.
Telugu literature declined, while Sanskrit disappeared from inscriptions.
101.x: In the Kakatiya era most inscriptions were in Telugu, which grew as an administrative language, and Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed. Persian and Tamil were not the Kakatiya inscriptional languages, and Telugu literature flourished rather than declined.
101.tq: Separate the language of literary development from the language retained in inscriptions.

101.s: Which was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas?
101.x:
Most books and keys: Telugu. Strictly: the prasasti and much of the court record were in Sanskrit.
APPSC keys and NextGen give Telugu as the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas (G2 2008); Sanskrit stayed the language of the grants' prasasti.

101.s: Which Renati Chola ruler issued the Erragudipadu inscription?
101.x: The Erragudipadu inscription, the first fully available Telugu inscription, is of Punyakumara.

101.x: In June 2026 an ASI survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve copied 25 inscriptions (2nd–16th centuries).

101.s: With whom is the line 'Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa' associated?
101.x: The line is associated with Krishnadevaraya, whose period with the Ashtadiggajas was the peak of Telugu literary culture.

101.s: Palkuriki Somana's book?

101.s: Who composed Basava Puranam?

101.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Basava Puranam was composed by Palkuriki Somanatha, not Vemulavada Bhimakavi, so that pair is wrongly matched; Nannechoda - Kumarasambhavam, Somanatha - Panditaradhya Charitra and Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya - Sivatattvasaram are correct.

101.s: Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra?
101.x:
Some keys: Basava (founder of Veerashaivism) or Somanatha (who popularised it in Telugu). Strictly: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya propagated it in Andhra (NextGen Andhra Cholas p.3).
Veerashaivism was spread in Andhra by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya (12th c.); Basava founded it in Karnataka, and Palkuriki Somanatha later popularised it through Telugu literature. The printed key (Basava) contradicts its own explanation.

101.s: Who wrote Vrushadhipa Satakam?
101.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is by Palkuriki Somanatha; Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram.
xa: Vrushadhipa Satakam = **First Telugu Satakam**, **100 verses**.
**Sivatattvasaram** (~**400** kanda poems); Mallikarjuna = originator of the **Sataka** form.
⚠ "First Satakam" claims differ: **Sivatattvasaram** vs **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.

101.s: Palkuriki Somanatha's Basava Puranam was composed in which metre?
101.x: Basava Puranam is in the native dwipada metre, which Somanatha popularised, not in Champu style.
xa: **Champu** (mixed prose + verse) was pioneered by **Nannaya**.
⚠ CDX names **Markandeya Puranam** (**Marana**) as the first Telugu Purana.
**Ranganatha Ramayanam** (**Gona Budda Reddy**) was the first dwipada kavya.

101.s: Palkuriki Somanatha, hailed as Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi, led which literary movement?
101.x: He led the Desi kavita movement against the Sanskritised marga style, popularising dwipada, ragada and other desi metres.
xa: He popularised desi metres: **dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**.
Works: **Basava Puranam**, **Panditaradhya Charitra**, **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.
He wrote **Rudra Bhashyam** in **Sanskrit** and **Ragadas** in **Kannada**.

101.s: With which of the following combinations is Nannechoda associated?
o: Vrushadhipa Satakam and the title Gajasahini
Basava Puranam and the title Prabandha Parameswara

xs: **Nannechoda** wrote **Kumarasambhavam** and bore the title **Kavirajasekhara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gajasahini** was **Jayapa Senani's** office; **Ubhayakavimitrudu** is **Tikkana's**; **Prabandha Parameswara** is **Errana's**.
xa: Kumarasambhavam is **Kannada-influenced** and began the **"eight descriptions"** of prabandha.
He is also called **Kaviraja Shikhamani**.
⚠ Nannechoda is **not** in the Kavitraya.

101.s: Who wrote Sivatattvasaram, of about 400 kanda poems?
101.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram and originated the Sataka form.

101.s: Who wrote Panditaradhya Charitra, called the first Telugu encyclopaedia?
101.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra and Vrushadhipa Satakam.

101.s: What does Palkuriki Somanatha's Basava Puranam deal with?
101.x: Basava Puranam narrates the life of Basava and Veerashaivism.

101.s: Telugu literature was first influenced by which empire?
101.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of

101.s: Who wrote Kavi Vakbandham?
101.x: Tikkana wrote Kavi Vakbandham and Krishna Satakam besides his Bharatam.

101.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani, ascribed to Nannaya, is a Telugu grammar written in Sanskrit. 101.s: Who wrote the Jain work Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu?

xs: **Kavijanasrayam**, the first Telugu work on prosody, is by **Malliya Rechana** — so option **(4)** is correct.

**Ketana** wrote **Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam**.

**Kavi Vakbandham** is by **Tikkana**.

101.s: Who wrote Kavyalankara Chudamani, the first alankara work in Telugu?
101.x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; Kavijanasrayam is by Malliya Rechana.

101.x: Appakaviyam is by Kakunuri Appakavi (17th c.); Appayacharya wrote Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu.

B. Tikkana age

101.s: Who is identified as the first prabandha writer in Telugu?

101.s: Which of the following literary form–example pairs is correctly matched?
