They abolished all forms of taxation and ended state supervision of markets.
107.x: Alauddin’s measures are regarded as the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement system for revenue assessment.
107.tq: Select the option containing both linked historical significances without an exaggerated claim.
xs: They were the **first state-run price control and rationing system** in India and the **first land measurement for revenue** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Land was measured in **biswa**; granaries rationed grain in scarcity.
There was no paper currency and no end of taxation — taxes like **ghari** and **charai** were added.
xa: His reign = **"imperial period"** of the Sultanate.
Despotism and heavy spying hollowed out the state.

107.s:
Consider the following statement connected with Alauddin Khalji :
I. He collected revenue by measuring the cultivated land.
II. He enforced revenue measures in his entire empire.
III. He abolished the powers of provincial Governors.
Select the correct answer from the coding scheme given below :
107.x: I is true – Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure cultivated land. III is accepted in the key – he took revenue under direct state control and curbed the governors' (muqtis') independent powers. II is false – measurement was limited to Delhi and the Doab.

107.s: The term used for measurement of land in the Delhi Sultanate Period was
107.x: Masahat means measurement of land; Alauddin was the first Sultan to assess revenue on it (unit: biswa). Kismat-i-Ghalla and Ghalla-Bakhshi are crop-sharing; Ghazi is a title.

107.s: During the regime of which Sultan was the Khalisa land developed on a large scale?
107.x: Alauddin reclaimed milk, inam and waqf grants and brought much land under khalisa (crown land) to pay his army in cash.

107.s: At what share did Alauddin Khalji fix the state's demand of produce (kharaj)?
107.x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.
xa: New taxes: **ghari** (house) and **charai** (grazing); **jizya** continued.
Resumed **inam** and **waqf** grants enlarged the **khalisa**.

107.s: What was the headman's cess abolished by Alauddin Khalji called?
107.x: Alauddin abolished the kismat-i-khuti and brought khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis under taxation.
xa: The state share (**kharaj**) was **half** of produce.
Land was measured in **biswa**.

107.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, on what was Ghari levied?
107.x: Ghari was the house tax; Charai was the grazing tax and Kharaj 50% of yield.
n: Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Milq lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Waqf lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
The reclamation of Milq and Waqf lands expanded Khalisa land. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was a land tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was fixed at 50% of the yield under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Ghari was a house tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: ⚠ **Ghari** = house; **Charai** = grazing.
**Khalisa** = crown land, grew as **inam, waqf** grants were resumed.
**Jizya** continued; ⚠ some notes give the state share as one-fifth.
State share of **half (50%)**: BPSC **2018**.

107.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Alauddin Khalji's revenue measures?
o: The privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were expanded to strengthen intermediaries.
His measures weakened the role of traditional intermediary tax collectors.
The traditional tax-collection privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were abolished.
Revenue was collected more directly by weakening intermediary tax collectors.
107.x: Option A is incorrect: Alauddin Khalji abolished, not expanded, the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis. This weakened the intermediaries and let the state collect revenue more directly.
107.tq: Check what happened to the intermediaries' privileges.
n: Alauddin Khalji abolished the traditional tax-collection privileges of Khutts, Mukaddams, and Chaudharys. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji collected revenue more directly after abolishing the privileges of Khutts, Mukaddams, and Chaudharys. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji's policy weakened intermediary tax collectors. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the privileges of **Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary** were **expanded** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Alauddin Khalji** **abolished** their **traditional tax-collection privileges**, **weakening intermediary tax collectors**.
Revenue was thus **collected more directly** — options **(2)**, **(3)** and **(4)** are true.
xa: The intermediaries had to pay the **same taxes** as others; **Kismat-i-khuti** (headman's cess) was abolished.
He was the **first Sultan** linked with **systematic land measurement**; standard unit = **biswa**.
**Diwan-i-Mustakharaj** recovered **arrears** from revenue officials.

107.s: On what basis was Alauddin Khalji the first Sultan to assess land revenue?
107.x: Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure land (masahat), with the biswa as the standard unit.

107.s: What was the standard unit of land measurement under Alauddin Khalji?
107.x: Land was measured with the biswa as the standard unit.

107.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, on what was Charai levied?
107.x: Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals; Ghari was the house tax.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms:
1. The privileges of khuts and muqaddams were abolished.
2. Land measurement covered the whole empire.
3. Khalisa land was expanded by reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Intermediaries lost their privileges and khalisa grew; measurement was limited to Delhi and nearby areas.

107.s: Which Sultan had forbidden the nobles to hold banquets and festivities, and make marriage alliance without his permission?
107.x: Alauddin forbade nobles to hold social gatherings and festivities or to make marriage alliances without his permission, to stop conspiracies.

107.s: Barani's causes of revolt perceived by Alauddin were noble wealth, noble marriages and gatherings, drinking and which other?
107.x: Barani's four causes were noble wealth, noble intermarriage and gatherings, a weak intelligence system and drinking.
xa: Answers: confiscated **inam, waqf**; reorganised **spies**; **prohibited liquor**, gambling; royal permission for feasts and marriages.
APPSC G1 **2018**: prohibition + market control + severe punishment = **Alauddin**.

107.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Alauddin Khalji's ordinances?
o: Confiscation of religious grants and free lands
Permission for nobles to form unrestricted marriage alliances
107.x: Noble marriages and gatherings required royal permission; the other three were part of his ordinances.
xa: Offenders got **severe punishment**; rape was punished severely.
The causes come from **Barani**.

107.s: Prohibition of liquor and gambling, control of markets and severe punishment of offenders are associated with which Delhi Sultan?
107.x: All three measures belong to Alauddin Khalji: his ordinances prohibited liquor and gambling, he regulated the markets, and offenders were punished severely. Balban was harsh but did not control markets; Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz did not impose these measures together.
xs: Prohibition, market control and severe punishment = **Alauddin Khalji** (APPSC G1 **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
His ordinances **prohibited liquor**, intoxicants and gambling.
His **market control** fixed prices for a cheap standing army.
xa: Barani's four causes of revolt: **wealth**, **intermarriage**, **weak spies**, **drinking**.
**Mubarak Shah** withdrew the harsh regulations after **1316**.

107.s: Which ordinance of Alauddin Khalji was aimed at nobles' intermarriages and gatherings?
o: Royal permission for feasts and marriage alliances
107.x: To check nobles' gatherings and intermarriage, feasts and marriage alliances needed royal permission.

107.s: The office of Ariz-i-Mamalik under Alauddin Khalji was associated principally with which department?
107.x: Ariz-i-Mamalik was the head of the army department. It was not a ministerial office concerned with law or religious endowments.
107.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to an administrative title.
xs: **Ariz-i-Mamalik** headed the **army department** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes call it "minister of law" — a trap.
Under Jalaluddin, Alauddin held this post along with **Amir-i-Tuzuk**.
xa: The Ariz-i-Mumalik **recruited the standing army**.
**Diwan-i-Riyasat** ran the markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** recovered revenue arrears.

107.s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
107.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.
107.tq: Link the military reform, payment method and identifying administrative terms to one ruler.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** created the first standing army paid in **cash**, with **dagh** and **huliya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was recruited by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (army minister).
xa: Ferishta puts its cavalry at about **4,75,000**.
Dagh = **branding of horses**; huliya = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.

107.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes dagh from huliya or chehra?
o: Dagh was the cash payment of soldiers, whereas huliya was the recruitment of cavalry.
Dagh was a land-revenue assessment, whereas huliya recorded the wealth of nobles.
Dagh was the registration of peasants, whereas huliya was the measurement of land.
Dagh was the branding of horses, whereas huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
107.x: Dagh referred to branding horses and huliya or chehra to the descriptive roll of each soldier. Neither was a land-revenue measure or an assessment of nobles’ wealth.
107.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated military terms.
xs: **Dagh** = **branding of horses**; **huliya / chehra** = **descriptive roll of each soldier** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Both stopped **fraud / false musters**.
⚠ Notes that call dagh a land-revenue measure, or huliya an assessment of nobles' wealth, are wrong.
xa: Alauddin was the **first Sultan** to keep a large **permanent standing army**, paid in **cash**.
The Bahmani minister **Mahmud Gawan** later brought in **dagh and chehra**.

107.s: Which Bahmani minister later copied Alauddin Khalji's dagh and chehra?
107.x: Mahmud Gawan of the Bahmanis brought in dagh, chehra, land measurement and a larger khalisa.

107.s: How were the soldiers of Alauddin Khalji's standing army paid?
107.x: Alauddin was the first Sultan with a large permanent standing army paid in cash.

107.s: The attempt of Alauddin Khalji to control the market prices
107.x: The sources and the keys call Alauddin's market control highly successful: prices stayed fixed even in famine and the army was kept on low pay.

107.s: Which one of the following best explains the contradictory effects of Alauddin Khalji’s reforms?
o: They weakened the army but eliminated all opposition among the nobles.
They raised prices and ended the use of spies, but strengthened provincial autonomy.
They benefited merchants and peasants while weakening the central government.
They kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression generated discontent.
107.x: The reforms helped maintain low prices and a strong army capable of resisting the Mongols, but repression and espionage created widespread discontent.
107.tq: Balance positive and negative consequences instead of selecting a one-sided claim.
xs: The reforms **kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression bred discontent** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The army became strong enough to **beat the Mongols**.
**Rule by espionage + repression** hollowed out the state.
xa: The dynasty **fell soon after his death in 1316**.
Criticism: controls may have been **confined to Delhi**, and they hurt **merchants and peasants**.

107.s: With which dynasty are token currency, transfer of capital and canals associated?
107.x: The Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals; the Khaljis for market control and the Lodis as the first Afghan dynasty.
xa: Khaljis' contribution also included **taxation reforms**.
Alauddin's reign = the **"imperial period"**.

107.s: Who is the main source for Alauddin Khalji's market control measures?
107.x: Barani is the main source; Mubarak Shah later abolished the controls.
xa: UPPSC keys call the market control **"highly successful"**.
Prices stayed **stable** during Alauddin's reign.

107.s: Which Sultan abolished Alauddin Khalji's price controls and restored confiscated lands after ascending the throne?
107.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316–1320) abolished the price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew the harsh regulations.

107.s: In which work is Ziauddin Barani's account of Alauddin Khalji's reforms found?
107.x: Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, the main account of the reforms; Khazain-ul-Futuh is by Amir Khusrau.

107.s: Who wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing Alauddin Khalji's campaigns?
107.x: Amir Khusrau, who went on the 1310 campaign, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.

107.s: Which was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
107.x: The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty; they founded Agra.

107.s: Which pair of Delhi Sultanate dynasty and key contribution is wrongly matched?
107.x: Agra was founded by the Lodis; the Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals.

107.s: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate founded Agra?
107.x: The Lodis, the first Afghan dynasty, founded Agra.

107.s: Alauddin Khalji’s reign is often called the ‘imperial period’ of the Delhi Sultanate mainly because it was marked by:
o: the replacement of the Sultanate by the Bahmani kingdom
the exclusive supremacy of the ulema over state policy
extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions
the abandonment of expansion and the growth of provincial independence
107.x: Alauddin’s extensive conquests, centralised administration, strong army and imperial ambitions led his reign to be described as the imperial period of the Sultanate.
107.tq: Infer the historical label from the cluster of policies and achievements.
xs: The reign shows **extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alauddin dreamed of being **Sikandar-i-Sani** and ran **harsh, centralised** rule.
The **ulema** were overridden, not supreme.
xa: Firsts: **state-run price control**, **rationing**, **land measurement** for revenue.
Kafur's campaigns reached **Madurai** (**1311**).

108.s: The Hindu king that has given shelter to Bahauddin Gurshasp who revolted against Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq in A.D.1326.
108.x: Bahauddin Gurshasp, Muhammad bin Tughlaq's cousin who revolted in 1326, took shelter with Kampila Deva (Kampili); Tughlaq then took Kampili and captured Harihara and Bukka.

108.s: The first Indian ruler to organise Haj Pilgrimage from the state exchequer was
108.x: Akbar was the first Indian ruler to organise the Haj pilgrimage at the state's expense.

108.s: Which of the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq is not true?
o: He had his father Ghiyasuddin killed
His real name was Juna Khan
He ascended the throne in A.D. 1300
After conquering Orugallu in A.D. 1323 he renamed it Sultanpur
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Juna Khan) became Sultan in 1325, not 1300, so option 3 is false. Warangal (Orugallu) fell in 1323 and was renamed Sultanpur.

108.s: Between which years is the Tughlaq period of the Delhi Sultanate generally placed?
108.x: The Tughlaq period began with Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 and ended when Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414.
108.tq: Identify the dynasty's beginning and end points rather than confusing it with neighbouring dynasties.
xs: The Tughlaq period runs **1320 to 1414** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It began with **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq Shah in 1320** and ended when **Khizr Khan** took Delhi in **1414**.
xa: Ghiyasuddin ruled **1320-25**; Firoz **1351-88**.
**Timur's invasion** came in **1398**.

108.s: What was the earlier name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called Juna Khan (also Ulugh Khan) before he became Sultan; Ghazi Malik was his father Ghiyasuddin.

108.s: Which Sultan of Delhi made a rule that, in any given year, the land revenue can be increased only nominally, viz one-tenth or one-eleventh of the fixed revenue?
108.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limited revenue increases to about one-tenth, raised slowly. Alauddin and Firoz are not credited with this rule.

108.s: Which technique was used in times of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq for measurement of Khalisa land?
Whom did Ghazi Malik kill to become Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320?
108.x: Ghazi Malik, earlier governor of Punjab, killed Khusrau Shah and became Sultan in 1320.
xa: He built the **Tughlaqabad** fort.
He was the **first Sultan to start irrigation/canal works**.

108.s: To about what share did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limit any increase in land revenue?
108.x: Ghiyasuddin limited any increase to about one-tenth and raised it gradually, besides drought remission and cultivation of waste land.
xa: He was the **first Sultan to start canal works**; **Firoz** dug the most.
He improved the **postal system** with runners and horsemen.

108.s: During whose reign was Warangal conquered and renamed Sultanpur?
108.x: Warangal fell in 1323 during Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign and was renamed Sultanpur.
108.tq: Link the conquered place, its new name and the ruler responsible for the conquest.
xs: Warangal fell in **1323** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** and was renamed **Sultanpur** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The attack was led by Prince **Juna Khan** (later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**).
xa: Andhra was then run by **Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri, assisted by **Malik Maqbul**.
**Prataparudra II** was taken towards Delhi and died in the **Narmada**.

108.s: In which year did Warangal fall to the Tughlaq forces after a five-month siege?
108.x: Juna Khan first attacked Warangal in 1321-22; it fell after a five-month siege in 1323, before Ghiyasuddin's death in 1325.

108.s: Where did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq die in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed?
108.x: He died at Afghanpur in 1325 (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan); he had built Tughlaqabad.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** suspects a plot by **Juna Khan**.
Cities of Delhi: **Siri** — **Alauddin Khalji**; **Tughlaqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

108.s: Of which province was Ghazi Malik the Governor against the Mongols under Alauddin Khalji?
108.x: Ghazi Malik (later Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) was Governor of Punjab under Alauddin, guarding against the Mongols.

108.s: Which city of Delhi was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
108.x: Ghiyasuddin built Tughlaqabad; Siri was Alauddin's and Firozabad and Hisar were Firoz's.

108.s: In which river did the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II die after the fall of Warangal?
108.x: Prataparudra II was taken towards Delhi and died in the Narmada.

108.s:
Consider the following statements
1.
Assertion (A): Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued a new gold coin which was called Dinar by Ibn Battuta.
2.
Reason (R): Muhammad bin Tughlaq wanted to issue token currency in gold coins to promote trade with West Asian and North African countries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a new gold coin known as the Dinar (called Dinar by Ibn Battuta). He also issued a silver coin called the Adli and undertook important currency reforms during his reign. Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a token currency around 1330 CE to tackle the shortage of silver in the royal treasury. Drawing inspiration from the currency system used in China under Kublai Khan, he issued copper coins (Jitals) and set their value at the same level as silver tankas. However, since the concept of token currency was unfamiliar in India and there was no effective control over minting, counterfeit coins were produced on a large scale. The widespread forgery disrupted the economy and undermined public confidence in the currency. Consequently, the Sultan withdrew the scheme and agreed to exchange the copper coins for silver coins.

108.s: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq had transferred his capital from Delhi to –
108.x: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq had shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devgiri). It was one of the most significant experiments of Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq. Various factors have been identified for this experiment. According to Barani, Devgiri probably was at the center of his empire. According to Ibn Battuta, the people of Delhi used to write undeferential letters to Sultan. To punish them he decided to make Devgiri his capital. Muhammad Tughluq was also the first Sultan of Delhi who tried to establish the administrative and cultural unity of northern and southern India. Probably this was also the main reason behind making Devgiri his capital. According to Dr. K.A. Nizami, Sultan Qutbuddin Mubarak Khalji had changed the name of Devgiri to Qutbabad and Muhammad Tughluq to Daulatabad.

108.s: For the first time the token currency was introduced in India by :
108.x: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq launched different types of coins during his period and also decided on their reasonable prices. But the circulation of token currency was his specialty. According to Barani, due to lack of silver in treasury and policy of expanding the empire, Muhammad Tughluq had to launch the token currency. The token currency was launched in Iran during the regime of Gaykhatu, though, the experiment was unsuccessful. The token currency was successfully launched during the period of Kublai Khan. Innovative Muhammad- Bin- Tughluq was inspired by them. The modern historian also notes that there was a shortage of silver all over the world, and there was a severe shortage of silver in India too. Due to this reason, he launched token currency.

108.s:
Assertion (A): Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq issued a new gold coin which was called Dinar by Ibn Battuta.
Reason (R) : Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq wanted to issue token currency in gold coins to promote trade with West Asian and North African countries.
o: Both ‘A’ and ‘R’ are individually true and ‘R’ is the
Both ‘A’ and ‘R’ are individually true but ‘R’ is not
108.x: Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq issued the new gold coins which were called ‘Dinar’ by Ibn Battuta. He issue the token currency in copper or Bronze coins to promote his military power not for trade with the West Asian and the North African countries in token currency of gold. Thus, Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

108.s:
Consider the following statements-
Assertion (A) : The scheme of the token currency of Muhammad Tughluq proved unsuccessful.
Reason (R) : Muhammad Tughluq did not have the proper control over currency issue.
Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
108.x: Barani describes the five main schemes of Muhammad Tughluq:- (1) Tax increase in Doab, (2) Devgiri (Daultabad) as Capital, (3) Issuing token currency, (4) Attack on Khurasan and (5) Qarachil expedition. The main reason behind the failure of token currency was that the state had no control over the minting of coins. The value of the token currency was equivalent to the silver value currency. As a result, many fraud mints were formed. The Lagan began to be paid by forged coins.

108.s: In which year did Muhammad bin Tughlaq transfer his capital to Devagiri?
108.x: The capital was transferred in 1327; token currency followed around 1329–30.
xa: Khurasan: a huge army raised, then **disbanded unpaid / unused**.
Qarachil (**Kumaon** hills): **army destroyed in the hills**.

108.s: What did the token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1329-30 consist of?
o: Gold and silver coins issued to overcome a gold shortage
Silver and copper coins issued exclusively for the army
Copper and brass coins intended to function as tokens
Lead and potin coins modelled on Satavahana currency
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency in copper and brass because of a shortage of silver. Widespread forgery led to its recall and redemption at heavy cost.
108.tq: Discriminate the metal composition and the economic purpose of the token currency.
xs: The token currency was of **copper and brass**, meant to function as tokens — so option **(3)** is correct.
Cause: a **silver shortage** and the idea of a token coin.
Result: **mass forgery**; the coins were **recalled and redeemed at heavy cost** to the treasury.
xa: It came c. **1329-30**, after the move to Daulatabad (**1327**).
Exam line: "token currency was **copper and brass**".

108.s: What did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's higher taxation of the Doab, coinciding with a famine, lead to?
108.x: Meant to raise revenue, the Doab tax increase coincided with famine and caused peasant revolts and flight.
xa: During the famine the Sultan moved to the **Swarga-dwari** relief camp on the **Ganga** near **Kannauj**.
**Taqavi** (sondhar) loans for seed and wells came from MBT.

108.s: What was the aim of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Qarachil (Kumaon hills) expedition?
108.x: The Qarachil expedition aimed to secure the hill frontier; the Khurasan expedition aimed at Central Asian conquest.
xa: Khurasan army: **disbanded unpaid / unused**; Qarachil army: **destroyed in the hills**.
Barani called MBT a **"mixture of opposites"**.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
108.tq: Find the odd location by separating Firoz Shah's town-building from Muhammad bin Tughlaq's capital transfer.
xs: **Daulatabad** is not a Firoz town — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Daulatabad was **Devagiri**, renamed by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1327**).
Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla), **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** from **Topra** and **Meerut** to Delhi.

108.s: For which of the following is Firoz Shah Tughlaq's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul noted?
o: Paying compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Introducing token currency in copper and brass
Leading the Qarachil expedition into the Kumaon hills
108.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul paid compensation to persons who had suffered during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's rule.
108.tq: Identify the responsible official by matching the administrative action with the correct office-holder.
xs: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** **paid compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Nagarkot texts were translated by **Azizuddin Khalid Khani**; **token currency** and **Qarachil** were **MBT's**.
xa: Maqbul was the Brahmin **Jagannatha Pandit**, converted to Islam.
He had assisted **Malik Burhanuddin** at **Warangal** before becoming Firoz's chief minister.

108.s: How did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Khurasan expedition end?
o: The army being destroyed in the hills

110.s: Who was the first Muslim ruler of Delhi?
110.x: Iltutmish was the first Sultan of Delhi who received the investiture from Caliph. In 1229 A.D., the Caliph of Baghdad, Al-Muntasir Billah, bestowed on Iltutmish the title of “Sultan-i- Azam” or the Sultan The Great. Thus, in this way, he was the first legally independent Sultan of Delhi. He was successful in keeping the throne of Delhi safe from the danger of Mongol invasion as well as from the attacks of both Taj ud-din Yalduz and Qabacha. He broke up the Rajput powers in the north and established his supremacy over them. He made his rule hereditary, issued coins with his name and made Delhi a beautiful capital. He is said to have introduced first Arabic silver (175gm) and copper currency which were two basic coins of the Sultanate period. Iltutmish belonged to the tribe of ‘Ilbari’ in the Eurasian Steppe of Turkestan. Iltutmish was first appointed governor of Badaun in recognition of his services during the campaign of Muhammad of Ghur against the Khokhars in 1205-06 A.D. Amirali Ismail invited Iltutmish for the coronation in Delhi with the approval of Turkish nobles after the death of Aybak. Iltutmish declared himself Sultan in 1211 A.D.

111.x: (i) Balban established an army department ‘Diwan-i-Arz’ to look after a large standing army with a view to potential Mongol threats. 111.s: Which one of the following dynasties saw the heyday of the Wizarat:
111.x: Wizarat was an institution recognized by the Islamic administration. Non-Arabic institutions were being repealed, and nomenclature used for Minister for Council under emperor was used as Wizarat. The idea for adopting Wizarat as an institution was inspired by Persia by Abbasi Caliphs. Abbas Fazal-Bin-Ahmad was first Wazir in the reign of Mahmud Ghaznavi, (during Ghaznavid administration) who was accomplished in conducting the administration. The prime minister of state was known as Wazir. Tughluq era was the golden period of Indian Muslim Wizarat.

111.s: Supreme rural officials of land revenue in Sultanate period?

Hence, Chaudhary was the main revenue collector for villages during the Sultanate period.

xa: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess**.

111.s: Who among the following had established the Diwan-i-Arz department under Delhi Sultanate?
111.x: Balban set up the Diwan-i-Arz (army department) under the Ariz-i-Mumalik to maintain a large standing army against the Mongols. Alauddin is the tempting wrong option, but he did not found it.

o: extra payment made to the nobles
revenue assigned in lieu of salary
excess amount paid to the exchequer by the iqtadars
illegal exactions extracted from the peasants
112.x: Fawazil was the surplus revenue collected by Iqtadars beyond their salary. This extra amount had to be deposited into the state treasury.

112.s: Which medieval king of India introduced the ‘Iqta system’?
112.x: Iltutmish first introduced 'Iqta' system in Delhi Sultanate Period. In the Islamic empire of the Caliph, land was granted to army officials for limited periods in lieu of a regular wage. The Iqta system was introduced in the 9th century A.D. to relieve the state treasury when insufficient tax revenue and little booty from wars made it difficult for the government to pay salaries.

112.s: Which one of the following is NOT the characteristic of 'Iqta System'?
o: Iqta was a revenue collection system
Siyasatnama was the source of information for Iqta
Revenue from Iqta was directly deposited in Sultan's
Muqti was supported to maintain troops out of the
112.x: Iqta system in India was introduced by Iltutmish during Sultanate period. According to this system, the owner of Iqta (Iqtadar or Muqti) was given the responsibility of collecting revenue and taxes in his area. Revenue from Iqta was not directly deposited in Sultan's account, whereas it was used by the Muqti to meet his administrative and military expenditures. Muqti had to maintain troops out of this revenue collected from Iqta for the service of Sultan. Siyasatnama authored by Abu Ali Hasan Ibn Ali Tusi (Nizam-ul-Mulk) is the source of information for primary Iqta system. 5. Given below are two statements one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) The territories of the Sultanate could be broadly divided into two parts – the Khalsa and the Jagirs. Reason (R): The Jagirs comprised of the land under the control of the State. Select the correct answer from the code given below : (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (b) (A) is false, but (R) is true. (c) (A) is true, but (R) is false. (d) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). U.P. P.C.S (Pre) 2025 Ans. (c) In the revenue administration of the Delhi Sultanate, the standard division of territories is accepted as Khalisa and Jagirs (Iqta). Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct. Reason (R) is incorrect, because land under the “direct control of the state” was considered Khalisa, whereas a Jagir was granted to a Mansabdar/Jagirdar

112.s: Which among the following medieval ruler of India introduced Iqta system?
112.x: Iltutmish introduced the iqta as a systematic institution in the Sultanate. Balban and Alauddin only modified it (Balban checked muqtis, Alauddin shifted to cash pay).

112.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, the in-charge of revenue collection was known as ‘Amil’.

II. The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution.

III. The office of ‘Mir Bakshi’ came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statement I is correct as the amil was the pargana revenue officer. Statement II is false because the iqta was a foreign Turkish institution, not an ancient indigenous one. Statement III is not supported, so only I is correct.

112.s: Muhammad Ghori granted first Iqta in India to –
112.x: Soon after the victories of Muhammad Ghori, Iqta system was established in North India. In 1192 A.D., Muhammad Sam of Ghori (Muhammad Ghori) appointed Qutb-ud-din- Aybak, as in charge of his Indian territories. He played an important role in the second battle of Tarain. Pleased with his works, Ghori appointed him the administrator of Kuhram and Samana. He had taken care of the administration of North Indian territories conquered by them as representative of Ghori till 1206. During this period, Aibak also expanded Turkish power in northern India.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): At first, the Turkish administration in India was essentially military.
2.
Reason (R): The country was parcelled out as 'Iqtas' among leading military leaders.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
112.x: In the early Delhi Sultanate period, the Turkish rulers depended heavily on military commanders for administration and control. Large territories were assigned as iqtas to military nobles, who collected revenue and maintained troops on behalf of the Sultan. Thus, the iqta system gave the administration a predominantly military character.

112.s: Which statement regarding the development of the iqta system is correct?
o: Firoz Tughluq abolished the iqta system completely.
Iltutmish built the iqta into a systematic administrative institution.
Alauddin Khalji converted every iqta into private property.
Qutbuddin Aibak first introduced it as a hereditary system in India.
112.x: Iltutmish developed the iqta into a system. Under the Sultanate, it remained a revenue assignment rather than private ownership.
112.tq: Identify the ruler associated with institutional consolidation, not later modification.
xs: **Iltutmish** built the iqta into a **systematic institution** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2010** key: Iltutmish).
**Firoz** did not abolish iqtas — he made them **hereditary**; iqtas were **not ownership of land**, so (3) is wrong.
**Aibak** received the **first iqta** (**Hansi**) from **Ghori**, but it was **transferable**, not hereditary.
xa: Holder = **iqtadar / muqti** (or **wali** for a province).
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution (**UPSC 2019**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.

112.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the responsibilities of a muqti?
o: He was exempt from maintaining law and order
He sent the surplus revenue to the central government
112.x: A muqti maintained troops, collected revenue, preserved law and order and remitted the surplus to the centre, so he was not exempt from maintaining law and order.
xa: The muqti held an **iqta**, a revenue assignment, **not ownership of land**.
Iqtas were **transferable**; muqtis moved periodically until **Firoz** made them hereditary.
**Alauddin** tightened the **audit** of muqtis.

112.s: To whom is the first iqta grant in India, of Hansi, credited?
o: Muhammad Ghori, granted to Qutbuddin Aibak
Alauddin Khalji, granted to Malik Kafur
112.x: Muhammad Ghori granted Hansi (some sources say Kuhram) to Qutbuddin Aibak, the first iqta. Iltutmish later built the iqta into a system; Balban and Alauddin are not linked with the first grant.
112.tq: First iqta: Hansi, Ghori to Aibak.
xs: The first iqta, **Hansi**, was granted by **Muhammad Ghori** to **Qutbuddin Aibak** — option **(2)**.
Some notes say **Kuhram** instead of Hansi.
xa: **Iltutmish** later built the iqta into a system (**UPPSC 2010**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution.

112.s: Which one of the following statements about the nature of the iqta system is correct?
o: It was an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
It was exclusively a religious endowment system.
It was introduced only in the Mughal period.
It was a Turkish, non-indigenous institution.
112.x: The iqta was a Turkish institution and was not an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
112.tq: Discriminate between a foreign administrative institution and an indigenous one.
xs: The iqta was a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution — option **(4)**.
⚠ Trap: "ancient indigenous institution" is **false** (**UPSC 2019**).
It began under **Ghori** (**Hansi** to **Aibak**), long before the Mughals, and was a revenue assignment, not a religious endowment.
xa: **Iltutmish** institutionalised it.
Iqta = ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s: What was the position of iqtas before the policy of Firoz Tughlaq?
o: They were permanently owned by the muqtis.
They were administered exclusively as khalisa lands.
They were granted only to religious leaders.
They were periodically transferable between muqtis.
112.x: Before Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary, muqtis were transferred periodically from one iqta to another.
112.tq: Distinguish a transferable assignment from a hereditary one.
xs: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable** and muqtis were **moved periodically** — option **(4)**.
Iqtas were **not ownership of land**; **khalisa** was the separate crown land; grants to religious men were **inam**.
xa: **Firoz Tughlaq** made iqtas **hereditary**.
Iqta = **land revenue** assigned instead of a **cash salary**.
Muqti sent the **fawazil** (surplus) to the treasury.

112.s: The iqta system is regarded as the ancestor of which Mughal arrangement?
o: Amara Nayankara and Siddha Sainyam system
112.x: The iqta system is considered the ancestor of the Mughal jagir and mansab system; the other pairs belong to different contexts.

112.s: What was the surplus revenue that a muqti sent to the centre called?
112.x: The muqti sent the surplus, called fawazil, to the centre.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about the iqta system:

112.s: Who among the following sultans of Delhi was the first to have paid to his soldiers in cash?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first large standing army paid in cash rather than through iqtas. Iltutmish and Balban paid soldiers through iqtas.

112.s: Which Sultan introduced large-scale cash payment to his standing army?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji paid his standing army in cash, whereas Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas and Firoz Tughlaq returned to assignment-based payment.

112.s: With reference to the iqta system, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the jagir system to improve army efficiency.
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq ordered an inquiry into grants and jagirs.
Unlawful grants were seized during the reign of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
112.x: Firoz Tughlaq revived the jagir system and made iqtas hereditary. This revival adversely affected army efficiency; he did not abolish the system.

xs: "**Firoz abolished the jagir system**" is NOT correct: he **revived** the jagir and made iqtas **hereditary** — option **(2)**.
That revival **hurt army efficiency**, as nobles controlled recruitment, promotion and discipline.
Statements (3) and (4) are correct: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** inquired into **grants/jagirs** and seized **unlawful grants**.
xa: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = back to assignments.

112.s: Which lands did Alauddin Khalji take back to enlarge the khalisa?
112.x: Alauddin enlarged the khalisa and took back Milq, Idrarat and Waqf lands.

112.s: Which of the following is correct about Firoz Tughlaq's policy?
o: He first paid the army in cash

112.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, what was the crown land whose revenue supported the court and royal household called?

Madad-i-Mash was associated with religious institutions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]

112.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; Zabt was the Mughal revenue system, khalisa was crown land and iqta/jagir were revenue assignments.

Khalisa was land under direct state control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]

Sardeshmukhi was an important Maratha revenue claim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]

**Iltutmish** built **Sultan Ghari**, tomb of his son **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.

115.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
115.x: Tughlaqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque is Sher Shah Suri's, the Moth Masjid dates from Sikandar Lodi's reign and the Kirti Stambha is Rana Kumbha's.
n: Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Moth Masjid was built during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Tughluqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Kirti Stambha was built by Rana Kumbha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xa: Qila-e-Kuhna is at **Purana Qila**, Delhi, built in **1541**.
**Tughlaqabad** was massive and rugged, built for security.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** built **Jahanpanah**.

115.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
115.x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque. Aibak built the Adhai Din ka Jhopra, Iltutmish completed the Qutb Minar and Alauddin Khalji built the Alai Darwaza.
n: Adhai Din Ka Jhopara in Ajmer was built by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in Delhi was built by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
The Qutub Minar was completed by Iltutmish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xa: ⚠ **Aibak** began the Minar (first storey), **Iltutmish** completed it, **Firoz Tughlaq** rebuilt the top.
The Qutb Minar is about **72.5 m**, **five** storeys.
"**Qutb Minar and its Monuments**" = UNESCO site, inscribed **1993**.

115.s: Who built the city of Jahanpanah?
115.x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** built the **Tughlaqabad** fort-city — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style: **sloping (battered) walls**, pointed domes, false arches.

115.s: Who founded Siri, one of the cities of Delhi?
115.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji; Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin and Jahanpanah by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

115.s: Which of the following pairs (city of Delhi – founder) is correctly matched?
115.x: Firozabad (Kotla) was founded by Firoz Tughlaq; Siri was Alauddin's, Tughlaqabad Ghiyasuddin's and Jahanpanah Muhammad bin Tughlaq's.

115.s: Who built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541) in the Purana Qila, Delhi?
115.x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in 1541.

115.s: Who built the Jamat Khana Masjid at the Nizamuddin dargah?
115.x: The Jamat Khana Masjid was built by Khizr Khan, son of Alauddin Khalji.

115.s: Which of the following was built after Tughlaqabad Fort but before Fatehpur Sikri?
115.x: The Lodi Garden tombs (1451–1526) come between Tughlaqabad Fort (1320s) and Fatehpur Sikri (1570s).

115.s: Who built the Hazar Sutun palace at Siri?
115.x: Hazar Sutun, like the Alai Darwaza and Hauz-i-Alai, was built by Alauddin Khalji, not Sher Shah.

115.s: Who built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) at Mehrauli?
115.x: Balban built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) and his own tomb at Mehrauli.

115.s: Who added a madrasa and his own tomb at Hauz Khas, on the tank of Alauddin Khalji?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built a madrasa and his tomb at Hauz Khas beside Alauddin's tank.

115.s: In which citadel of Delhi stands the Ashokan pillar brought from Topra?
115.x: Firoz Shah Kotla, the citadel of Firozabad, holds the Topra Ashokan pillar.

115.s: During whose reign was the Moth ki Masjid in Delhi built?
115.x: The Moth ki Masjid was built in Sikandar Lodi's reign, in the Lodi style.

115.s: Who built the Kirti Stambha at Chittor?
115.x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor is credited to Rana Kumbha of Mewar.

115.s: The Qutab Minar was named after: merican
115.x: Khwaja Qutb-ud-din There is historical debate about who the Qutab Minar was named after. It is commonly believed to be named in honour of the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutb-ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki. Construction was started by Qutb-uddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

115.s: Who amongst the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys, making five. Aibak built only the first storey and Iltutmish the 2nd-4th.

115.s: Who among the following sultans built the fifth storey of Qutub Minar?
115.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys, making five. Aibak built only the first storey and Iltutmish the 2nd-4th.

115.s: Which of the following is part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' World Heritage Site?
115.x: The site includes the Qutb Minar, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Iron Pillar, Iltutmish's tomb, Alauddin's tomb and madrasa, and Imam Zamin's tomb; Tughlaqabad Fort is separate.
xa: The site was inscribed by UNESCO in **1993**.
**Iron Pillar**: Gupta era (king "Chandra" = **Chandragupta II**), famous for resisting rust.

115.s: The Iron Pillar standing in the courtyard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque belongs broadly to which period?
115.x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta-era pillar. Its king Chandra is generally identified with Chandragupta II, and it is famous for its resistance to rust.
115.tq: Identify the period from the associated ruler and distinctive material feature.
xs: The **Iron Pillar** belongs to the **Gupta period** (Gupta-era) — option **(3)**.
Its king "**Chandra**" is identified with **Chandragupta II**.
xa: It is famous for **resisting rust**.
It stands in the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque court, part of the **UNESCO** Qutb site (**1993**).
⚠ The **Topra Ashokan pillar** is a different pillar, at **Firoz Shah Kotla**.

115.s: How many tapering storeys does the Qutb Minar have?
115.x: The Qutb Minar has five tapering storeys, is about 72.5 metres high and bears bands of Quranic calligraphy.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Qutb Minar is 180 ft high" is **false** (CGPSC 2023) — actually about **238 ft**.
Some notes give **73 m**.
Dedicated to Sufi saint **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.

115.s: Why does the present Qutb Minar have five storeys although its upper portion was altered?
o: Iltutmish added two storeys after completing the entire monument.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys.
Alauddin Khalji added two marble storeys to the original tower.
Sikandar Lodi added two storeys after rebuilding the monument.
115.x: Lightning damaged the upper portion of the Qutb Minar. Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the damaged top storey with two storeys made of marble and sandstone.
115.tq: Follow the cause-and-repair sequence rather than associating every addition with the original builder.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** replaced the **lightning-damaged top storey** with **two storeys** — option **(2)**; hence **five storeys** today.
The new storeys were in **marble and sandstone**.
**Iltutmish** built storeys 2nd-4th and completed it; **Sikandar Lodi** only **repaired** it.
xa: ⚠ **Aibak** began (first storey) – **Iltutmish** completed – **Firoz Tughlaq** rebuilt the top.
Height about **72.5 m** (some notes **73 m**).

115.s: In which year was 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' declared a World Heritage Site?
115.x: The Qutb complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

115.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Qutb Minar complex World Heritage Site?
115.x: Tughlaqabad Fort is not part of the Qutb WHS; Alai Darwaza, the Iron Pillar and Imam Zamin's tomb are.

115.s: Which Sultan began the Qutb Minar but built only its first storey?
115.x: Aibak began the minar and built the first storey; Iltutmish completed it.

115.s: Who built the second to fourth storeys of the Qutb Minar?
115.x: Iltutmish completed the second to fourth storeys; Firoz Tughlaq later rebuilt the top.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:
1. Sikandar Lodi carried out repairs to it.
2. It is about 180 ft high.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Sikandar Lodi, like Firoz Tughlaq, repaired the minar; it is about 238 ft (72.5 m) high, not 180 ft.

115.s: With whom is the king 'Chandra' of the Iron Pillar in the Qutb complex identified?
115.x: The Gupta-period Iron Pillar's 'Chandra' is Chandragupta II.

115.s: What is the approximate height of the Qutb Minar?
115.x: The Qutb Minar is about 72.5 m (238 ft) high; the 180 ft figure is a trap.

115.s: After which Sufi saint is the Qutb Minar commonly believed to be named?
115.x: The Qutb Minar is commonly believed to be named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (the point is debated).

115.s: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world?
115.x: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur (Vijayapura), Karnataka, is the 17 th-century mausoleum of Sultan Mohammad Adil Shah, renowned for its massive, unsupported dome—the second-largest in the world after St. Peter's Basilica.

115.s: Which of the following rulers got the Jantar Mahal of Mandu constructed?
115.x: Gujari Mahal was constructed by Raja Man Singh Tomar between 1486-1516 A.D. It is a unique piece of architecture.

115.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid
115.x: The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).
115.tq: Identify the complete regional cluster rather than matching only one monument.
xs: **Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid** are all **Bengal** monuments — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is **Bahmani** (Bidar); (2) mixes **Jaunpur**, Daulatabad and **Bijapur**; (3) mixes **Hyderabad**, Bengal and **Mandu**.
xa: Bengal style: **brick** building, **curved roofs**.
**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

115.s: Who built the Chand Minar at Daulatabad in 1435?
o: Alauddin Ahmad Shah of the Bahmani dynasty
115.x: The Chand Minar at Daulatabad was built in 1435 by the Bahmani Sultan Alauddin Ahmad Shah.
115.tq: Match the monument with its correct builder and date while rejecting nearby Sultanate rulers.
xs: The **Chand Minar**, Daulatabad, was built in **1435** by Bahmani Sultan **Alauddin Ahmad Shah** — option **(2)**.
It dates to the **15th century** (statement correct, CGPSC 2023).
**Mahmud Gawan** is linked to his **madrasa at Bidar**, not the Chand Minar.
xa: Bahmani works: **Gulbarga Jama Masjid** (fully covered courtyard), **Bidar Fort** (Gagan Mahal), **Ashtur** tombs.
**Firoz Shah Bahmani's** tomb has a **Sanskrit inscription**.

115.s: A massive propylon screen in front of the prayer hall and the absence of minarets, as seen in the Atala Masjid, mark which provincial style?
115.x: The Sharqi style of Jaunpur is marked by massive gateway facades with a propylon screen and no minarets, as in the Atala Masjid. Bengal used brick and curved roofs, Malwa is known for the Jami Masjid at Mandu, and Gujarat for strong Hindu-Jain carving.
115.tq: Propylon + no minarets = Jaunpur's Atala Masjid.
xs: A massive **propylon** screen and **no minarets**, as in the **Atala Masjid**, mark **Jaunpur (Sharqi)** — option **(3)**.
**Bengal** used brick and curved roofs; **Malwa** = Jami Masjid, Mandu; **Gujarat** = strong Hindu-Jain carving.
xa: ⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal).
Jaunpur's style is known for **massive gateway facades**.

115.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
115.x: The Adina Mosque is associated with Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat. Gol Gumbaz is at Bijapur, Jami Masjid at Mandu and Chand Minar at Daulatabad.
115.tq: Check the region of each monument and locate the swapped regional association.
xs: **Adina Mosque — Gujarat** is wrong: the Adina Mosque is at **Pandua, Bengal** — option **(4)**.
Others are correct: **Chand Minar–Daulatabad**, **Gol Gumbaz–Bijapur**, **Jami Masjid–Mandu** (Malwa).
xa: **Gujarat** style: strong Hindu-Jain carving; **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.
⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal); **Gol Gumbaz** = Bijapur.

115.s: Which Bahmani monument has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome?
115.x: The Gulbarga Jama Masjid has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome; the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is a three-storeyed building with glazed tiles.

115.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
115.x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.
115.tq: Identify the monument through its unusual functional features rather than its dynasty alone.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is known for its **acoustics** and **piped water** — option **(2)**.
A handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
Covered courtyard = **Gulbarga**; curved brick roofs = **Bengal**; propylon = **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers.
Golconda Jami Masjid gateway has fine **Nastaliq** calligraphy.

115.s: The Jami Masjid at Mandu belongs to which provincial style?
115.x: The Jami Masjid, Mandu, is the leading monument of the Malwa style.

115.s: Whose tomb is the Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur?
115.x: Gol Gumbaz is the 17th-century tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur.

115.s: Strong Hindu-Jain carving is a feature of which provincial style?
115.x: Gujarat's provincial style shows strong Hindu-Jain carving, as in the Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad.

115.s: Where is the Adina Mosque located?
115.x: The Adina Mosque is at Pandua in Bengal, not in Gujarat.

115.s: The Charminar is traditionally associated with which event?
o: The completion of the Golconda Fort water system
The founding of the Bahmani kingdom
115.x: The Charminar was built to mark the end of a plague. It has four arches and four minarets and combines Persian arches with Deccani stucco.
115.tq: Link the monument with its commemorative purpose rather than with a general architectural feature.
xs: The **Charminar** was built to mark the **end of a plague** — option **(3)**.
It has **four arches + four minarets** and blends **Persian arches with Deccani stucco**.
xa: Dates differ: some notes say **1591-92**, others **1594**.
Its design is said to be inspired by the minarets of **Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid**, Golconda.
**Hyderabad** was founded in **1591**, planned on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.

115.s: Who planned Hyderabad on the model of Isfahan?
115.x: Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad on the model of Isfahan.
xa: Charminar marked the **end of a plague**.
Capital moved from **Golconda** to Hyderabad in **1592**.

115.s: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh are notable because they:
o: Have no domes and are decorated only with pierced stone screens
Contain the tombs of seven Bahmani rulers and have octagonal domes on circular bases
Were built entirely in the Bengal brick tradition
Contain the tombs of seven Qutb Shahi rulers and have onion domes on square bases
115.x: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh contain the seven rulers of the dynasty and are characterised by onion domes resting on square bases.
115.tq: Combine the number of rulers with the distinctive tomb form to identify the correct description.
xs: The **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers and have **onion domes on square bases** — option **(4)**.
They are **Qutb Shahi**, not **Bahmani**, and their domes are not octagonal on circular bases.
xa: Qutb Shahi architecture = **Indo-Saracenic** blend of Persian and Hindu traditions (AP angle).
**Golconda Fort**: acoustics, handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**.

115.s: In which year was Hyderabad founded?
115.x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591, and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.
xa: The city plan was modelled on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
**Charminar** marked the **end of a plague**.

115.s: Which of the following describes Qutb Shahi architecture?
o: An Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions
A Buddhist-Greek style centred on stupas
A purely Persian style without Indian elements
115.x: Qutb Shahi architecture combined Persian and Hindu traditions and is described as an Indo-Saracenic blend.
115.tq: Distinguish a blended architectural tradition from styles described as purely belonging to one cultural stream.
xs: Qutb Shahi architecture is an **Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions** — option **(1)**.
So it is neither **purely Persian** nor a Dravidian or Buddhist style.
**Charminar** shows the blend: **Persian arches with Deccani stucco**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers, with **onion domes on square bases**.
**Hyderabad** (founded **1591**) was planned on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
⚠ Golconda Jami Masjid: **Nastaliq** on the gateway, **Naskh** around the mihrab.

115.s: In which script is the fine calligraphy on the gateway of the Golconda Jami Masjid?
115.x: The gateway has fine Nastaliq calligraphy (Yazdani); Naskh is used for the Quranic verses around the mihrab.
xa: ⚠ **Nastaliq** = gateway calligraphy; **Naskh** = Quranic verses around the mihrab.
**Golconda Fort** is known for **acoustics** — a handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
**Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers, with **onion domes on square bases**.

115.s: In which year was the Qutb Shahi capital moved from Golconda to Hyderabad?
115.x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.

115.s: In the Golconda Jami Masjid, the Quranic verses around the mihrab are in which script?
115.x: Naskh is used for the Quranic verses around the mihrab; the gateway is in Nastaliq.

115.s: By which building are the minarets of the Charminar said to have been inspired?
115.x: The minarets of Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid at Golconda are said to have inspired the Charminar.

115.s: What is the name of the 16th century stepwell that the Archaeological Survey of India recently conserved in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund India?
o: More than one of the above
115.x: Rajon ki Baoli, located in the Mehrauli Archaeological Park in Delhi, is a four-tiered stepwell built around 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi, during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. It is an excellent example of Lodi-period architecture and traditional water-engineering techniques. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), in collaboration with World Monuments Fund India (WMFI) and the TCS Foundation, has successfully completed the conservation and rejuvenation work of Rajon ki Baoli. 2. A key focus of Viksit Bharat Yatra is to disseminate information and facilitate access to which of the following areas ? (a) Environmental conservation efforts (b) Space exploration advancements (c) Welfare and development schemes (d) Promotion of traditional arts and crafts Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2025 Ans. (c) One of the major objectives of the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra is to disseminate information about government welfare and development schemes among citizens and to ensure easy access to these schemes and their benefits. The yatra was flagged off by PM Narendra Modi on November 15, 2023 from Khunti, Jharkhand. This Yatra focuses on raising awareness about government schemes in both rural and urban areas and on expanding the reach of these schemes to eligible beneficiaries.

115.s: Who built Rajon ki Baoli, the 'stepwell of the masons' in Mehrauli?
115.x: Daulat Khan Lodi built Rajon ki Baoli in 1506 under Sikandar Lodi.
xa: Restored by **ASI**, **World Monuments Fund India** and **TCS Foundation** (May **2025**).
**Sikandar Lodi** also repaired the **Qutb Minar**; his tomb is in **Lodi Garden**.
Lodi style: **octagonal tombs** and the **double dome**.

115.s: Around which year was Rajon ki Baoli in Mehrauli built?
115.x: Rajon ki Baoli was built c. 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi under Sikandar Lodi.

115.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of these monuments?
1. Alai Darwaza
2. Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
3. Sultan Garhi
4. Tughlaqabad Fort

116.s: Who of the following has given a detailed description of the postal system found during the Sultanate period?
116.x: The detailed description of the postal system is obtained from the chronicle journey of Ibn Battuta. He was the resident of Tanzir region of Morocco and came to India during the period of Muhammad Tughluq. ‘Kitab-ul-Rihla’ is his famous book.

116.s: Medieval traveller and writer Ibn Batuta belonged to which country?
116.x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco (1304), so Morocco is correct; Persia and Afghanistan are not his origin.

116.s: Which scholar came to India with Mahmud Ghazni –
116.x: Al-Biruni, a scholar from Khwarizm, came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind. Ibn Battuta, Khusrau and Ferishta belong to other periods.

116.s:
What is the sequence of arrival of these travellers?
1. Ibn Battuta
2. Tavernier
3. Al-Biruni
4. Manucci
116.x: (i) Al-Biruni : Al-Biruni was a resident of Khiva (ancient Khwarizm). He was in the court of the last emperor of Khiva dynasty as a scholar and diplomat before Mahmud Ghazni’s victory over India. He came to India with Mahmud Ghazni during his invasion of India. (ii) Ibn Battuta (1333-1342 A.D. ) : He was Moroccan traveller. He came to India during the Sultanate period in the regime of Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq (1325-1351A.D.). Muhammad Tughluq appointed him as ‘Qazi’ of Delhi. Later, he sent him to China as an ambassador in 1342. He composed his travelling experiences in his book “Rihla.” (iii) Jean-Baptiste Tavernier (17th century A.D.) : A French gem merchant and traveller began his voyage the period of Shahjahan. He made six voyages to the East. He wrote his travel accounts in his book "The Six Voyages of John Baptista Tavernier". (iv) Niccolao Manucci (1653-1708 A.D.) : He was an Italian traveller. He reached India from his hometown Venice while travelling to Turkiye and Asia. He had given his services to Prince Dara Shukoh as a cannoneer. Later, he opted for the medical profession. Manucci is famous for his work. "Storia do Mogor or Mogul India, 1653-1708". 7. Who were called ‘Dastar-Bandan’? (a) SufiSaint (b) Khan (c) Malik (d) Ulema U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014 Ans. (d) During the Sultanate period, high-positioned or designated religious and judicial authorities honourable (Ulema) were collectively known as Dastar-Bandan, because they dressed with an official turban. 8. 116.s: Where did Al-Biruni, who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, come from?
116.x: Al-Biruni was from Khwarizm (Khiva), in present Uzbekistan.

116.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Deva Raya II in 1443, was the envoy of which ruler?
116.x: Abdur Razzaq came from Persia as the envoy of Shah Rukh to Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.

116.s: Where did Marco Polo, who visited Motupalli in 1292 during Rudramadevi's reign, come from?
116.x: Marco Polo was a Venetian (Italy) who visited Motupalli in 1292.

116.s: Which of the following pairs (traveller – origin) is INCORRECTLY matched?
116.x: Marco Polo came from Venice (Italy); Abdur Razzaq was the traveller from Persia.

116.s: To which office did Muhammad bin Tughlaq appoint Ibn Battuta?
116.x: Ibn Battuta came to Delhi in 1333 and was made qazi of Delhi by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

116.s: To which country did Muhammad bin Tughlaq send Ibn Battuta as his envoy?
116.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as envoy to China.

116.s: In which language was Ibn Battuta's travelogue Rihla written?
116.x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla is in Arabic and records the postal system, sati and slave markets.

116.s: Where was the historian Ferishta born?
116.x: Ferishta was born at Astarabad in 1552.

116.s: In which year did Ibn Battuta come to Delhi?
116.x: Ibn Battuta reached Delhi in 1333 and stayed in India till 1342.

116.s: At which place was Ibn Battuta born?
116.x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco in 1304.
