Khusrau is among the prominent composers of **Hindustani** music.

116.s: With whom is the music treatise Man Kautuhal associated?
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
116.x: Man Kautuhal is associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior; Rag Vibodh is by Somnath.
xa: ⚠ Don't swap them: Man Kautuhal is Man Singh's, Rag Vibodh is Somnath's.
**Amir Khusrau** credited with ragas **Aiman, Zilaf, Sazgiri**.

116.s: Which Sufi order popularised sama and institutionalised qawwali in its khanqahs?
116.x: The Chishtis popularised sama, and qawwali was institutionalised in Chishti khanqahs using Indian ragas.
116.tq: Match the musical practice with the Sufi order most closely associated with it.
xs: The **Chishtis** popularised **sama** and institutionalised **qawwali** in their khanqahs — option **(4)**.
Qawwali in Chishti khanqahs used **Indian ragas**.
xa: **Sama** = devotional music to induce **ecstasy**; a core Sufi practice.
**Amir Khusrau**, disciple of Chishti **Nizamuddin Auliya**, is credited by tradition with qawwali.
Persian contributions listed in **PT365**: sitar, santur, **qawwali**, ghazal.

116.s: Who wrote the music treatise Rag Vibodh?
116.x: Rag Vibodh is by Somnath; Man Kautuhal is linked to Raja Man Singh Tomar.

116.s: Who among the following is credited with starting the qaul and tarana forms of music?
116.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with qawwali and with starting qaul, qalbana, tarana and khayal.

116.s: Who among the following had translated Chintamani Bhatt’s Sanskrit text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it the title ‘Tutinama’?
116.x: Khwaza Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi translated Chintamani Bhatt’s text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it title 'Tutinama'. Nakhshabi was a 14th-century Persian Physician and Sufisaint who migrated to Badayun (UP).

116.s: Which ruler is associated with the Persian translation of the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini?
116.x: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir is associated with translating the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini into Persian.
116.tq: Identify the patron from the translated Sanskrit works rather than from the translator’s name.
xs: **Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir** had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian — option **(3)**.
**Firoz Tughlaq** is linked to **Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi**; **MBT's** time to the **Tutinama**; **Man Singh Tomar** to Man Kautuhal.
xa: Later Mughal translation: **Razmnama** = Mahabharata.
**Kalila wa Dimna** = Persian version of the **Panchatantra**.

116.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Razmnama — Persian translation of Suka Saptati
Sringaramanjari — translated into Sanskrit by Shay Akbar
Kalila wa Dimna — Persian version of Panchatantra
Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi — Sanskrit texts from Jwalamukhi temple
116.x: Razmnama was the Persian translation of the Mahabharata, whereas Suka Saptati was translated as Tutinama.
116.tq: Find the one reversed translation relationship among otherwise valid pairs.
xs: **Razmnama — Suka Saptati** is wrong — option **(1)**; Razmnama is the **Mahabharata**.
Suka Saptati became the **Tutinama** (Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi).
Others correct: **Shay Akbar** put **Sringaramanjari** into Sanskrit; **Kalila wa Dimna** = Panchatantra; **Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi** = Jwalamukhi texts.
xa: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi texts came from the **Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot)** temple under **Firoz Tughlaq**.
Sringaramanjari was by **Rangasai** — a Qutb Shahi reverse exchange.

116.s: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi was based on the Sanskrit texts of which temple?
116.x: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi translated Sanskrit texts of the Jwalamukhi temple at Nagarkot under Firoz Tughlaq.

116.s: Who translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit?
116.x: Shay Akbar made the reverse translation of Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit.

116.s: Tutinama of Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi was a Persian translation of which Sanskrit text?
116.x: Nakhshabi rendered Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati into Persian as the Tutinama in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's time.

116.s: What is the Razmnama?
o: Persian translation of the Suka Saptati
116.x: The Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata of the Mughal period.

116.s: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian version of which work?
116.x: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian Panchatantra.

116.s: Who wrote Chandayan, the Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379?
116.x: Chandayan, an Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379, was written by Mulla Daud.
116.tq: Use the distinctive date and language to identify the author among premakhyan poets.
xs: **Chandayan** (Awadhi, **1379**) is by **Mulla Daud** — option **(1)** (UPPSC 2019).
**Padmavat** is by **Jayasi**, **Padmavati Katha** by **Damodar Kavi**, **Mrigavati** by **Qutban**.
xa: ⚠ **Padmavat** = Jayasi; **Padmavati Katha** = Damodar Kavi.
**Ghulam Ali**, court poet of **Tana Shah**, translated Padmavat into Urdu.

116.s: Who wrote Fawaid-ul-Fuad?
116.x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad is by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Qutban wrote Mrigavati.
xa: Fawaid-ul-Fuad = conversations (**malfuzat**) of **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
**Chandayan** (**1379**) is by **Mulla Daud**.
Padmavat is dated **1540**; one source says **15th century**.

116.s: Who wrote Mrigavati, a Sufi premakhyan?
116.x: Mrigavati is by Qutban; Chandayan is by Mulla Daud and Padmavat by Jayasi.

116.s: Ghulam Ali, who translated Padmavat into Urdu, was the court poet of which ruler?
116.x: Ghulam Ali, court poet of Tana Shah, translated Padmavat into Urdu.

116.s: The term ‘Apabhramsa’ was used in medieval Sanskrit text to denote
o: early forms of some of the modern Indian language.
116.x: Apabhramsa denotes the early forms of the modern Indian languages, which grew out of Prakrit. The notes do not cover this.

116.s: Which was the official language in the Delhi Sultanate?
116.x: Persian was the elite language of administration in the Sultanate. Urdu grew in camps and bazaars and was not the official language.

116.s: In the Qutb Shahi kingdom, which language was used among the people and in revenue records?
116.x: Telugu was used among the people and in revenue records; Persian was used at court and Dakhni Urdu in camps and bazaars.
xa: **Abdullah Qutb Shah** and **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** first issued farmans in **Telugu**.
Golconda was a Persian literary centre under **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.

116.s: Which Qutb Shahi rulers first issued farmans in Telugu?
o: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah
Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Abul Hasan Tana Shah and Kumara Kampana
Mir Momin Astarabadi and Abdullah Qutb Shah
116.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah are identified as the first Qutb Shahi rulers to issue farmans in Telugu.
116.tq: Distinguish the rulers linked with Telugu administrative usage from other Qutb Shahi figures.
xs: **Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah** first issued farmans in **Telugu** — option **(1)**.
**Mir Momin Astarabadi** was not a ruler; **Kumara Kampana** was not Qutb Shahi.
xa: **Ghulam Ali**, court poet of **Tana Shah**, translated Padmavat into Urdu.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.
**Telugu** was the language of the people and revenue records.

116.s: Addanki Gangadhara occupies an important place in Telugu literary history because he was the first poet to:
o: Dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan
Compose the first Dakhni Urdu diwan
Write a Kannada account of Warangal’s conquest
116.x: Addanki Gangadhara was the first poet to dedicate a Telugu work, Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam, to a Muslim Sultan, Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
116.tq: Match the distinctive literary distinction with the associated work and patron.
xs: **Addanki Gangadhara** was the first poet to **dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan** — option **(1)**.
The work: **Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam**, dedicated to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.
xa: **Abdullah Qutb Shah** and **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** first issued farmans in Telugu.
Reverse exchange: **Shay Akbar** translated Rangasai's **Sringaramanjari** into Sanskrit.

116.s: What is the Deccan form of Urdu known as?
116.x: Hindavi grew into Urdu in camps and bazaars; its Deccan form is Dakhni.

116.s: To whom did Addanki Gangadhara dedicate Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam?
116.x: Addanki Gangadhara was the first to dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan, Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

116.s: Which statement regarding Ferishta’s account is correct?
o: It calls Telangana ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323.
It calls Vijayanagara ‘Motupalli’ and describes its fall in 1443.
It calls Bengal ‘Tilang’ and describes its conquest in 1552.
It calls Delhi ‘Tilang’ and describes the rise of the Bahmani kingdom in 1620.
116.x: Ferishta refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323. The other options substitute incorrect places, events or dates.
116.tq: Verify the place-name and event together; a single altered detail makes a long statement false.
xs: Ferishta calls Telangana "**Tilang**" and describes the **fall of Warangal in 1323** — option **(1)**.
The other options substitute wrong places and dates.
xa: The fall of Warangal (**1323**) is also described by **Isami** and **Barani**.
Ferishta wrote **Tarikh-i-Ferishta** (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) at **Bijapur**.
He was born at **Astarabad**, **1552**.

116.s: Which group of writers is specifically associated with accounts of the fall of Warangal in 1323?
o: Kumara Kampana, Gona Budda Reddy and Kase Siddhappa
116.x: Isami, Barani and Ferishta describe the fall of Warangal in 1323.
116.tq: Use the event–chronicler association to reject writers from unrelated literary traditions.
xs: The **fall of Warangal (1323)** is described by **Isami, Barani and Ferishta** — option **(4)**.
The other groups are Telugu or Kannada poets (Tikkana, Errana, Srinatha, Kumara Kampana).
xa: Ferishta calls Telangana "**Tilang**".
**Isami's Futuh-us-Salatin** covers the Tughlaq army's victories over Warangal.
**Kumara Ramana Charitam** describes the south after the conquest of Warangal.

116.s: Who wrote Kasi Khandam?
116.x: Kasi Khandam is Srinatha's work; Errana completed the Aranya Parva and Tikkana rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.
xa: Errana's patron: **Prolaya Vema** (Reddi); Srinatha's: **Pedakomati Vema**.
**Marana** — **Markandeya Puranam** (Kakatiya era).
**Gona Budda Reddy** — **Ranganatha Ramayanam**.

116.s: Who wrote Ranganatha Ramayanam?
116.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is by Gona Budda Reddy; Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam.
xa: **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) describes the south after the fall of **Warangal**.
**Tikkana** — **Nirvachanottara Ramayanam**.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.

116.s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana render into Telugu?
116.x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

116.s: Who wrote Basava Puranam?
116.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote Basava Puranam in the Kakatiya period.

116.s: Errana of the Reddi period completed which parva of the Mahabharata?
116.x: Errana completed the Aranya Parva.

116.s: Who wrote the Nirvachanottara Ramayanam?
116.x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

116.s: Who is the author of Sringara Naishadham?
116.x: Srinatha of the Reddi period wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kasi Khandam.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
116.x: Tughluqnama is by Amir Khusrau; Ibn Battuta's work is the Rihla.

117.s: Who among the following established independent Muslim rule in Malwa?
117.x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded independent Malwa; Hoshang Shah only moved the capital to Mandu.

117.s: Which ruler unified Bengal in 1342 and made Pandua his capital?
117.x: Haji Ilyas, who assumed the title Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah, unified Bengal in 1342 and established Pandua as his capital.
117.tq: Distinguish the unifier of Bengal from the rulers connected with its monuments and later dynasty.
xs: **Haji Ilyas (Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah)** unified Bengal in **1342** with **Pandua** as capital — option **(1)**.
He founded the **Ilyas Shahi** line; **Alauddin Hussain Shah** founded the later **Hussain Shahi** line.
**Sikandar Shah** built the **Adina Mosque**; **Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah** lies in the **Eklakhi Tomb**.
xa: ⚠ **1342** Bengal (Ilyas) – **1347** Bahmani – **1394** Sharqi – **1401** Malwa – **1407** Gujarat.
Akbar annexed **Bengal** in **1576**.
Bengal chronicle: **Riyaz-us-Salatin**.

117.s: Who moved the capital of Malwa from Dhar to Mandu?
117.x: Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu; Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and Mahmud Khalji founded the Khalji line.
xa: Hoshang Shah's Tomb = **India's first marble tomb**.
Last Sultan **Baz Bahadur** was defeated by **Akbar**.

117.s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Gujarat in 1407?
117.x: Zafar Khan, as Muzaffar Shah I, founded the Gujarat Sultanate in 1407.

117.s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Malwa in 1401?
117.x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded the Malwa Sultanate.

117.s: Who shifted the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom from Gulbarga to Bidar?
117.x:
Ahmad Shah I Wali (1422–1436 CE) shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in 1425 CE. Bidar soon developed into a major centre of:
• Persian culture
• Architecture
• Literature
• Islamic learning The city remained the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom until its decline. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Capital shifted → Gulbarga → Bidar
• By → Ahmad Shah I

117.s: Who founded the Bahmani Empire?
117.x:
The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 CE by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, better known as Hasan Gangu. He revolted against the Delhi Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq and established an independent kingdom with Gulbarga as its first capital. The Bahmani Sultanate became the first independent Muslim kingdom in the Deccan and remained the principal rival of the Vijayanagara Empire for nearly two centuries. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Founder → Hasan Gangu (Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah)
• Founded → 1347 CE

117.s: The bone of contention between the Bahmani Sultanate and Vijayanagar kingdom was
117.x: The Raichur Doab, between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, was the main cause of Bahmani-Vijayanagara conflict.

117.s: Who among the following founded the Bahmani kingdom in the Deccan in the 14th century A.D.?
117.x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), who revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

117.s: Who among the following shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
117.x: Ahmad Shah I (Ahmad Shah Wali) shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar around 1424.

117.s: Besides the Doab, which of the following was a disputed zone in the Bahmani-Vijayanagara conflicts?
117.x: The Krishna-Godavari delta and Marathwada were other disputed zones; Mewar and Khandesh belonged to other regional contexts.
xa: Exam angle: "main cause of conflict" = **Raichur Doab**.
AP angle: **Telangana revolts** against the Bahmanis, quelled by Mahmud Gawan with **Velama** help.

117.s: Who was the last Sultan of the Bahmani kingdom, which ended in 1527?
117.x: The Bahmani kingdom, first ruled from Gulbarga, ended in 1527 under its last Sultan, Kalimullah.
xa: **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the capital to **Bidar**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.
Main conflict with Vijayanagara: the **Raichur Doab**.

117.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bahmani Sultanate?
o: Muhammad Shah I shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
Control of the Raichur Doab was the main cause of its conflict with Vijayanagara.
Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar.
Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
117.x: Ahmad Shah I, not Muhammad Shah I, shifted the capital to Bidar; Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.

117.s: Over control of which region were the Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars chiefly fought?
117.x: The Doab between the two kingdoms was the contested zone in the Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars.
xa: "Main cause of conflict" = the **Raichur Doab**; other zones: **Krishna-Godavari delta**, **Marathwada**.
**Mahmud Gawan** quelled the Telangana revolts (**1453** onward) with **Velama** help.
The break-up followed Mahmud Gawan's **execution in 1481**; the kingdom ended in **1527**.

117.s: Who built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid, compared to the mosque of Cordoba?
117.x: Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid with a fully covered courtyard.

117.s: Which Bahmani Sultan, a scholar-king (1397-1422), led the kingdom at its peak strength?
117.x: Firuz Shah (1397-1422) was a scholar-king under whom the Bahmanis were at peak strength.

117.s: Hasan Gangu founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347 by revolting against which Sultan of Delhi?
117.x: Hasan Gangu (Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah) revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and set up the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

117.s: Which was the first capital of the Bahmani kingdom?
117.x: Gulbarga, renamed Hasanabad, was the first Bahmani capital; Ahmad Shah I later moved it to Bidar.

117.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, was renamed Hasanabad.
2. Ahmad Shah I shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Both are true: Gulbarga was named Hasanabad, and Ahmad Shah I moved the capital to Bidar.

117.s: Which was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan?
117.x: The Bahmani kingdom, founded in 1347, was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan.

117.s: Which one among the following was not a reform measure carried out by Mahmud Gawan of Bahmani Kingdom?
o: The Kingdom was divided into eight provinces or Tarafs.
Nobles were paid salaries and were asked to maintain contingents of horses.
A tract of land, Khalisa, was set apart for the expenses of the Tarafdar.
Lands were measured and land taxes were fixed on that basis.
117.x: Gawan's reform divided the 4 tarafs into 8 provinces and put forts under central commanders to curb nobles. The notes do not mention a Khalisa land tract set apart for the Tarafdar's expenses, so option 3 is the odd one out.

117.s: With whose help did Mahmud Gawan quell the Telangana revolts?
117.x: Mahmud Gawan, the Persian Afaqi wazir of Muhammad Shah III, quelled the Telangana revolts with Velama help, not the Reddis.
xa: His letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.
Framed by rival nobles and **executed in 1481** → break-up of the kingdom.

117.s: Into how many provinces did Mahmud Gawan divide the four tarafs of the Bahmani kingdom?
117.x: To strengthen the centre and curb provincial nobles, Mahmud Gawan divided the four tarafs into eight provinces and placed forts under central commanders.
xa: **Crown (khalisa) land** was reserved in each taraf.

117.s: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar was built on which model?
117.x: The three-storeyed, tile-decorated madrasa followed a Persian (Herat/Samarkand) model; the Cordoba comparison belongs to the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
xa: **Bidriware** of Bidar: **14th century** under the Bahmanis; GI tag **2006**.
Mahmud Gawan's letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.

117.s: How did Mahmud Gawan, whose fall led to the break-up of the Bahmani kingdom, meet his end in 1481?
o: Execution after being framed by rival nobles
Assassination during a court revolt in Gulbarga
117.x: Mahmud Gawan was framed by rival nobles and executed, traditionally dated to 1481; his fall contributed to the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.
xa: Under him the kingdom had reached its **greatest extent**; Bahmanis took **Goa (1472)**.
Last Sultan **Kalimullah**; kingdom ended **1527**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.

117.s: Mahmud Gawan was the wazir of which Bahmani Sultan?
117.x: Mahmud Gawan, a Persian (Afaqi), was wazir of Muhammad Shah III, under whom the kingdom reached its greatest extent.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud Gawan:
1. He took Goa in 1472.
2. His letters are collected in the Riyaz-us-Salatin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Mahmud Gawan took Goa in 1472; his letters are the Riyaz-ul-Insha, while the Riyaz-us-Salatin is a history of Bengal.

117.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bidriware?
o: It received a Geographical Indication tag in 2006
It is metalware of a blackened zinc alloy inlaid with silver
It developed in the fourteenth century under the Vijayanagara rulers
117.x: Bidriware of Bidar developed in the fourteenth century under the Bahmanis, not the Vijayanagara rulers. It is blackened zinc-alloy metalware inlaid with silver and received a GI tag in 2006.

117.s: Who founded the Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar in 1490?
117.x: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk founded the Imad Shahi state of Berar (1490), with its capital at Ellichpur.

117.s: Which of the following pairs (Sultanate – dynasty) is correctly matched?
117.x: Golconda was ruled by the Qutb Shahis; Bijapur was Adil Shahi, Ahmadnagar Nizam Shahi, Bidar Barid Shahi and Berar Imad Shahi.

117.s:
Consider the following statements: The striking feature of the Jama Masjid in Kashmir completed by Zain-ul-Abidin include(s):
I. turret
II. similarity with Buddhist pagodas
III. Persian style
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
117.x: The Jama Masjid in Srinagar, extended by Zain-ul-Abidin, features turrets, pagoda-like roofs echoing Buddhist/Hindu traditions, and clear Persian architectural influence — all three elements together define its style.

117.s: Which among the following ruler abolished Jizya for first time?
117.x: Shahi Khan (Zain-ul-Abidin), the brother of Ali Shah, became the ruler of Kashmir in 1420 AD. He was the greatest king of Kashmir. He earned a name for his policy of religious tolerance and public welfare activities. He abolished Jizya tax on Hindus and banned cow slaughter. He was the first ruler to do so Mahabharata, Dashavatara and Rajtarangini were translated into the Persian language during his period. He was compared with Akbar due to his religious tolerance. The scriptures ‘Jain Prakash’ and Jain-Vilas’ were compiled during his rule. Also, he constructed artificial island of Zaina Lank in the middle of Wular Lake.

117.s: Ruler of Kashmir who was also known as “Akbar of Kashmir’ was-
117.x: Shahi Khan (Zain-ul-Abidin), the brother of Ali Shah, became the ruler of Kashmir in 1420 AD. He was the greatest king of Kashmir. He earned a name for his policy of religious tolerance and public welfare activities. He abolished Jizya tax on Hindus and banned cow slaughter. He was the first ruler to do so Mahabharata, Dashavatara and Rajtarangini were translated into the Persian language during his period. He was compared with Akbar due to his religious tolerance. The scriptures ‘Jain Prakash’ and Jain-Vilas’ were compiled during his rule. Also, he constructed artificial island of Zaina Lank in the middle of Wular Lake.

117.s: What was the original name of ruler of Kashmir Zainul-Abidin?
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin's original name was Shahi Khan, brother of Ali Shah.

117.s: Which Sultan was reputed to be 'Akbar of Kashmir?
117.x: In 1420 A.D. brother of Ali Shah, Shahi Khan, sat on the throne of Kashmir with the name of Zain-ul-Abidin. He was greatest ruler of Kashmir who ruled for nearly 50 years. On account of his liberal religious policy, promotion of learning, and interest in art and architecture he was called 'Akbar of Kashmir'.

117.s: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir was popularly known by which of the following titles?
o: Bud Shah and the Akbar of Kashmir
Butshikan and Lord of the East
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin was called “Bud Shah”, meaning Great King, and the “Akbar of Kashmir”.
117.tq: Match the ruler with his distinctive epithets, avoiding famous but unrelated titles.
xs: **Zain-ul-Abidin** was called **"Bud Shah" (Great King)** and the **"Akbar of Kashmir"** — option **(1)**.
**Butshikan** was **Sikandar's** epithet; **Lord of the East** (Malik-us-Sharq) was **Malik Sarwar's** title; **Shiraz-i-Hind** = Jaunpur.
xa: Original name: **Shahi Khan**; ruled **1420-1470**.
He **abolished jizya**, rebuilt temples and recalled Brahmins.

117.s: Which ruler of Kashmir abolished jizya, permitted the rebuilding of temples and called back the Brahmins?
117.x: These measures marked the conciliatory religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin.
xa: This reversed the policy of **Sikandar Butshikan**, who imposed jizya.
He had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian.
Works: **Zaina Kadal** bridge (Srinagar), **Zaina Lank** island (Wular lake).

117.s: Which of the following works was translated into Persian under Zain-ul-Abidin?
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin had the Mahabharata and Kalhana's Rajatarangini translated into Persian; Mirat-i-Sikandari and Riyaz-us-Salatin are original histories of Gujarat and Bengal.
xa: **Jonaraja** continued the Rajatarangini.
Zain-ul-Abidin = "**Akbar of Kashmir**".

117.s: Who wrote Mirat-i-Sikandari, the Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate?
117.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari was written by Sikandar bin Muhammad as a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate.
xa: It describes **Mahmud Begada's** prosperity and administration (UPPSC 2023).

119.x: Option (c) is correct: Harihara I, along with his brother Bukka, founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE. He established a new city on the south bank of the Tungabhadra River (a tributary of the Krishna River) and named it Vijayanagara. The decline of the Hoysala kingdom enabled Harihara and Bukka to expand their newly founded kingdom. By c. 1346 CE, they brought the whole of the Hoysala kingdom under their control. Bukka succeeded his brother in c.1356 and ruled till 1377 CE. During his reign, the Sultanate of Madurai was eliminated. Option (a) is incorrect: Amoghavarsha I (c.814−878 CE) was one of the most famous of the Rashtrakutas, who built a new capital city, that of Manyakheta (modern Malkhed). He was a patron of literature and was an accomplished scholar in Kannada and Sanskrit himself. He wrote the Kavirajamarga, the earliest Kannada work on poetics, and the Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit, which is considered a work of high merit and was later translated into Tibetan. Because of his religious temperament, his interest in the arts and literature and his peace-loving nature, he is often compared to emperor Ashoka and called "Ashoka of the South", and is also compared to Gupta king Vikramaditya in giving patronage to men of letters. Option (b) is incorrect: The Hoysalas ruled over parts of the present Karnataka and most of the Tamil region. The first independent ruler of the kingdom was Ballala II (1173-1220). The four dynasties of this empire are - Sangama dynasty (1336-1485 A.D.), Saluva dynasty (1485-1505 A.D.), Tuluva dynasty (1505-1570 A.D.) and Aravidu dynasty (1570-1672 A.D.).

119.s: The kingdom of Vijayanagara was founded by-
119.x: The Vijayanagara empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336. This dynasty is known as Sangama Dynasty after their father’s name. Harihara and Bukka were the feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal. After the fall of Warangal at the hands of Delhi Sultan, they shifted to Kampili and became ministers. Muhammad Tughluq invaded Kampili and arrested Harihara and Bukka. Both were forced to convert to Islam. Later, both were sent to the south to suppress a rebellion. They could not succeed, but under the influence of Saint Vidyaranya, they again reverted to Hinduism to establish the Vijayanagara Dynasty. They were inspired by their spiritual teacher Vidyaranya and Sayan, a noted commentator of Vedas. Four Dynasties ruled under this empire. (i) Sangama dynasty (1336-1485 A.D.). (ii) Saluva dynasty (1485-1505 A.D.), (iii) Tuluva dynasty (1505-1570 A.D.) and (vi) Aravidu dynasty (1570-1672 A.D.). These dynasties ruled over three hundred years. The capitals of Vijayanagara were Anegundi, Vijayanagara, Penukonda and Chandragiri respectively.

119.s: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and canalcum-aqueduct several a kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
119.x: Deva Raya I (c. 1406–1422 CE) was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire known for his contributions to irrigation, military organisation, and cultural patronage. He commissioned a massive dam across the Tungabhadra River along with a canal-cum-aqueduct system to supply water to the capital, and also constructed another dam on the Haridra River to support agriculture. The celebrated Hazara Rama Temple, a fine example of Deccan architecture, was built during his reign. His court was visited by travellers such as Nicolo Conti, who left valuable accounts of the empire. Deva Raya I strengthened the Vijayanagara army by improving cavalry forces, employing Turkic archers, and importing quality horses from Arabia and Persia. He was also a patron of Kannada literature and architecture, with the noted Jain poet Madhura associated with his court, a tradition that continued from his father Harihara II's time. Additional Information: The Vijayanagar kingdom constituted four dynasties — Sangama (c.1336–1485 CE), Saluva (c.1485–1503 CE), Tuluva (c.1503–1570 CE) and Aravidu (till the end of the 17 th century). Harihara and Bukka (c.1336–1377 CE) were founders of the Sangama dynasty of the Vijayanagar kingdom. Mallikarjuna, Vira Vijaya, and Virupaksha were rulers of the Sangama Dynasty, but historical records are unclear about their exact timelines, and their rule saw no significant accomplishments.

His masterpiece, Manu Charitramu (Svarochisha Manu Sambhavam), is regarded as one of the greatest works of Telugu literature. Because of his literary excellence, Krishnadevaraya honoured Allasani Peddana with exceptional respect, and he came to be known as the greatest poet of the Vijayanagara period. 121.x: Kandachara was the military department of the Vijayanagara empire, headed by the Senapati/Dalavai.

121.s: During the rule of Sri Krishnadevaraya, the 'Kandacharya' department looked into these matters?
121.x:
During the Vijayanagara administration, the Kandacharya was an important official connected with the military department. The Kandacharya supervised military organization, recruitment, maintenance of troops, inspection of armed forces and other defence-related responsibilities. Since the Vijayanagara Empire maintained a powerful standing army, this office occupied an important place in the administrative system. The military strength of the empire was one of the major reasons for its success against the Bahmani Sultanate and other contemporary powers. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Kandacharya – Military Department
• Period – Vijayanagara Empire

121.s: Who is the President of the Imperial Council of Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: Vijayanagara Empire had a Council of Ministers to assist the king in administration. The President of this council is the Prime Minister or Sarva Sirah Pradhani, also known as Sabha nayaka, Tantra nayaka and karyakarta.

121.s: Which one of the following statements about the Rayavachakam is correct?
o: It records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.
It records twelve departments, each headed by a Karanika.
It records only military offices under the Mahapradhani.
It records four departments, each headed by a Dalavayi.
121.x: Rayavachakam records nine departments, and each department was headed by a Samprati.
121.tq: Use the distinctive number-and-office combination as the key.
xs: The **Rayavachakam** records **nine departments**, each headed by a **Samprati** — option **(1)**.
The office was the **Rayasam**, with **Karanalu** (accountants).
xa: **Karanikas** were scribes; **Dalavayi** was C-in-C.
The Rayavachakam also lists forts: **Giri, Sthala, Jala, Vana**.
The **Kandachara** (military) department was headed by the **Dalavayi**.

121.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
121.x: The Mahapradhani was the chief minister who headed the pradhanis. Karanikas were scribes, Rayasams were secretaries and the Dalavayi was the commander-in-chief.
121.tq: Detect the office assigned to the wrong administrative level.
xs: **Mahapradhani — Village tax collector** is wrong — option **(1)**; the Mahapradhani was the **PM**, heading the **pradhanis**.
**Karanikas** = scribes, **Rayasam** = secretaries, **Dalavayi** = **C-in-C** — all correct.
xa: Example of a Mahapradhani: **Saluva Timmarusu**.
Rayasam secretaries named: **Kondamarasu**, **Ayyamarasu**.
In the village, the **Reddi** was head and collector of revenue.

121.s: Which matters did the Athavane department deal with in Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: Athavane was the revenue department; Kandachara was military and Bhandara the treasury.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (department – function) is correctly matched?
121.x: Bhandara was the treasury; Athavane was revenue, Kandachara military and Dharmasana judicial.

121.s: What was the chief minister heading the pradhanis in Vijayanagara called?
121.x: The Mahapradhani headed the pradhanis (e.g. Saluva Timmarusu); the Dalavayi was commander-in-chief.

121.s: According to the Rayavachakam, how many departments were there in the Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: The Rayavachakam records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.

121.s: Who headed the Kandachara department of the Vijayanagara administration?
121.x: Kandachara was the military department; it was headed by the Senapati or Dalavayi, the commander-in-chief.

121.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Department)
a. Kandachara
b. Athavane
c. Bhandara
d. Dharmasana
List-II (Function)
1. Treasury
2. Military
3. Justice
4. Revenue
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
121.x: Kandachara dealt with military affairs, Athavane with revenue, Bhandara was the treasury and Dharmasana the judicial department.

121.s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding foreign merchants?
o: Treat them generously and encourage imports
Confine them to a single port
Bar them from the horse trade
121.x: Amuktamalyada advises improving harbours, encouraging imports and treating foreign merchants generously.
xa: It also says **Brahmins** should command forts.
It advises building **tanks and irrigation**.

121.s: What does Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada advise the king to do regarding forest tribes?
o: Win them over rather than merely crush them
121.x: Amuktamalyada combines devotion with statecraft and advises winning over forest tribes rather than merely crushing them.
xa: "Political matters are discussed" in it (APPSC G2 **2003**).
Revenue maxim: the **bulk of revenue should go to the army**.

121.s: According to Amuktamalyada, to whom should the bulk of the king's revenue go?
121.x: Amuktamalyada advises that the bulk of revenue go to the army.

121.s: According to Amuktamalyada, who should command the forts?
121.x: Krishnadevaraya's maxim was that Brahmins should command forts.

121.s: Which of the following is correctly stated regarding the contents of Amuktamalyada?
o: It refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns and gives political advice, but does not trace a genealogy from Bukka.
It is exclusively a manual on fort construction.
It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka but not Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns.
It contains no discussion of kingship or administration.
121.x: Amuktamalyada contains political maxims on rajaniti, kingship and administration and refers to Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns, but it gives no genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2003).
121.tq: Discriminate between the work’s dynastic genealogy and the campaigns it does not record.

121.s: Who was the repair and maintenance officer of forts in the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: The parupatyagar was the local representative of the king, in charge of tax collection and the repair and maintenance of forts and public works.

121.s: What was the administrative unit of the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: A military governor called Nayaka was given Amarams for the salaries and army expenses; this is called the Amara Nayankara system.

121.s: The biggest administrative unit in the Vijayanagara Empire was
121.x: The Rajya/Mandala (province) was the largest unit of Vijayanagara provincial administration, above Nadu, Sthala and Grama, so Mandalam is correct.

121.s: Who headed a Nadu or Seema in Vijayanagara provincial administration?
121.x: A Nadu was under the Nadagauda and Parupatyagar; a Rajya under a prince or Durgadhipati, a Sthala under the Reddi/Gauda/Sthalakaranam and a village under the Ayagars.
xa: Sangama princes as governors were titled **Odeyar/Vodeyar**; the office was the **Chavadi**.
About **17 rajyams** existed under **Achyutaraya**, e.g. **Udayagiri, Chandragiri, Kondaveedu**.
**Kavalgar** kept order at the Sthala level.

121.s: Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara provincial governors is correct?
o: They could not keep their own armies
They held office for life without transfer
121.x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

121.s: What title did the Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces hold?
121.x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

121.s: Before 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of which Andhra rajya?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha governed Chandragiri before 1485; it later became a capital.

121.s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
121.x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

121.s: About how many rajyams were there under Achyutaraya?
121.x: There were about 17 rajyams under Achyutaraya.

121.s: Which officer of the nadu (sima) collected revenue and maintained forts in the Vijayanagara empire?
121.x: The Parupatyagar was the nadu/sima officer who collected revenue and maintained the forts.

121.s: Which was the most important Andhra rajya of the Vijayanagara empire, covering the Paka and Muliki districts (Nellore, Kadapa)?
121.x: Udayagiri was the most important Andhra rajya and was governed by royal princes under the first dynasty.

121.s: The Nayakas in the Vijayanagar empire were
o: Priests of large and powerful temples.
121.x: Nayakas (Amaranayakas) were military chiefs who held land (amaram) in lieu of salary, and administered it, so they were military chiefs controlling territories, not ministers, priests or ordinary cavalry.

121.s: What was the land assigned by the Vijayanagara king to military chiefs in lieu of cash salaries called?
121.x: Amaram was land granted to military chiefs, who were known as Amaranayakas, Nayaks, Palaiyagars or Poligars. The grant substituted for direct cash payment to the chiefs.
121.tq: Use the exact administrative term rather than a similar land-revenue term.
xs: Land granted to military chiefs instead of cash salaries was the **Amaram** — option **(2)**.
Holders were **Amaranayakas / Nayakas / Poligars** (also Palaiyagars), titled **Mahamandaleshwara**.
**Manyam** = tax-free lands of the **Ayagars**; **Jagir** belongs to the **Mughal** mansabdari.
xa: They paid a fixed **annual tribute (kist / kappam)**.
Krishnadevaraya had about **200 nayankaras** (Nuniz).
**Amara gramalu** collected **Durgadayam** for the army.

121.s: What title did the Vijayanagara amaranayakas hold?
121.x: Amaranayakas held the title Mahamandaleshwara and had more autonomy than the Durgadannayakas.
xa: They paid **kist / kappam** and attended the **Mahanavami** court.
The Vijayanagara amara-nayankara **evolved from the Kakatiya** system (CDX).

121.s: At which festival did Vijayanagara amaranayakas attend court with gifts?
121.x: Amaranayakas paid tribute, kept troops, horses and elephants, and attended court at Mahanavami with gifts.
xa: Local duties: keep order, maintain **forts**, fund **temples** and **irrigation**.
⚠ Kakatiya **75/77** nayakas vs Vijayanagara about **200**.
After **1565** they grew into **independent Nayaka states** (Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi).

121.s: What was the tribute paid by the Vijayanagara amaranayakas to the king called?
121.x: Amaranayakas paid tribute called Kappam and kept troops, horses and elephants for the king.

121.s: What was the principal political outcome of the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system after 1565?
o: The replacement of Nayakas by hereditary village accountants
The conversion of all amarams into Mughal jagirs
The complete abolition of regional chieftaincies
The emergence of semi-independent and later independent Nayaka states such as Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi
121.x: After 1565, semi-independent Nayaka kingdoms emerged and some became independent, including those of Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.
121.tq: Test the result of the system through its named regional examples.
xs: After **1565**, **semi-independent** and then **independent Nayaka states** arose — **Madurai, Tanjore, Keladi** — option **(4)**.
The Nayankara gave a huge army **cheaply** but bred kingdoms that **broke away after Talikota**.
xa: Amara-nayakas also became **Palegars (Poligars)**, forerunners of the **zamindars**.
The Mughal mansabdari, by contrast, was **non-hereditary** and centrally controlled.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (system – characteristic) is correctly matched?
o: Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara – Numerical zat and sawar ranks
Mughal Mansabdari – Mandalams and forts held by 75 or 77 Nayakas
Kakatiya Nayankara – Amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas
121.x: The Vijayanagara system involved amaram fiefs and about 200 Nayakas. The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 Nayakas holding mandalams and forts, and Mughal mansabdars held zat and sawar ranks.
xa: Kakatiya origin: **Prataparudra II** (APPSC **2025** key).
Vijayanagara nayakas included **Shudra** chiefs.

121.s: Who is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system?
121.x: Prataparudra II is identified as the originator of the Kakatiya Nayankara system. The Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system grew out of the Kakatiya system.
121.tq: Use the originator–system association and avoid substituting a later ruler.
xs: The Kakatiya Nayankara originated with **Prataparudra II** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025** key).
**Akbar** is linked to the Mughal **mansabdari**; the Vijayanagara system **grew out of** the Kakatiya one (CDX).
xa: Kakatiya nayakas held **a fort and a quarter of the land** and paid a fixed sum.
⚠ Kakatiya **75/77** vs Vijayanagara about **200**.

121.s: About how many nayakas held amarams under the Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system?
121.x: Vijayanagara had about 200 nayakas, against the Kakatiyas' 75 or 77.

121.s: The Kakatiya nayankara system had how many nayakas?
121.x: The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 nayakas holding mandalams and forts; Vijayanagara had about 200.

121.s: Who were polygars of South India?
121.x: Palegars (Poligars) were the amara-nayakas who administered territories and held military obligations, so they were territorial administrative and military governors, not ordinary zamindars (they were only forerunners of zamindars).

121.s: From whom did the Palegars or Poligars primarily originate?
121.x: The Amara-nayakas became the Palegars or Poligars when central authority weakened after the Battle of Talikota.
121.tq: Trace the origin of the later institution to its Vijayanagara military-administrative predecessor.
xs: The Palegars (Poligars) grew out of the **Amara-nayakas** — option **(3)**.
After **Talikota (1565)** weakened central authority, they became **hereditary** local rulers.
xa: They were **forerunners of the zamindars**.
In **Rayalaseema** they were suppressed by **Thomas Munro** with **Campbell**.
⚠ **Ayagars** were village functionaries; **Parupatyagars** were Nadu revenue officials.

121.s: The Palegars (Poligars), who became hereditary local rulers after Talikota, are regarded as the forerunners of whom?
121.x: The Palegars are regarded as forerunners of the zamindars; Ryotwari was introduced by Munro after suppressing them.
xa: Palegars arose from the **Amara-nayakas**.
Rayalaseema (the **Ceded Districts**) had a dense network of fortified poligar chiefs.

121.s: Which system did Thomas Munro introduce after suppressing the poligars of Rayalaseema?
121.x: Munro, with military officer Campbell, suppressed the poligars and then brought in the Ryotwari system.
xa: Poligars grew from **amara-nayakas** after **Talikota (1565)**.
**Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy**, Kurnool polygar, looted the **Koilkuntla** treasury.
**Kurnool Nawabs** were deposed in **1839**.

121.s: Which British officer, assisted by Campbell, crushed the Palegars of Rayalaseema?
121.x: Thomas Munro, with his officer Campbell, crushed the Palegars and then introduced the Ryotwari system.

121.s: What was the village headman called in the Vijayanagara Empire?
121.src: APPSC Junior Assistants (Dr. NTR University of Health Scienc
121.x: Officers called Reddy/Karanam/Gowda headed the stala (village group); the Parupatyagar headed the Sima.

121.s: How many Ayagars traditionally ran each village under the Ayagar system?
121.x: Each village was administered by 12 hereditary Ayagars. They included officials, artisans and service providers.
121.tq: Test the fixed numerical composition of the village institution.
xs: Each village had **12 hereditary Ayagars (Ayagandlu)** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2012**).
They included officials (**Karanam, Reddi, Talari, Purohita**) and artisans/servants.
xa: Artisans: **Kamsali** (goldsmith), **Kummari** (potter), **Vadrangi** (carpenter), **Kase** (mason), **Kammari** (blacksmith).
Servants: **Chakali** (washerman), **Mangali** (barber), **Madiga**.
Ayagar and Nayankara tenure both continued **Kakatiya** practice.

121.s: How were the Ayagars generally paid?
o: A fixed share of customs duties alone
Tax-free Manyam lands and a share of the harvest called Mera
Regular cash salaries from the royal treasury only
121.x: Ayagars received tax-free Manyam lands, also called Mirasi, Bhattu Vrutti or Jatikattu Manyalu, along with a share of the harvest called Mera. They were not paid regular cash salaries.
121.tq: Distinguish in-kind and land-based village remuneration from cash salary and Mughal jagir payment.
xs: Ayagars got **tax-free Manyam lands** and a **share of the harvest called Mera** — option **(2)**.
They drew **no cash salary**; **zat** ranks and transferable jagirs are Mughal.
xa: Manyam types: **Mirasi / Bhattuvritti / Jatikattu** manyams.
**Jodi** was a nominal tax on Ayagar and manya lands.
⚠ **Mera** = Ayagar harvest share; **Merulu** = Talari's grain gifts.

121.s: Which of the following pairs (Ayagar – function) is correctly matched?
121.x: The Talari was the village watchman. The Karanam was the accountant, the Reddi the village head and the Purohita the priest.
xa: Karanam kept village accounts, land and crop registers, and **temple accounts**.
Reddi was also collector of revenue; under the **Kakatiyas**, the village judge.
**Begari** supervised forced labour (**vetti**).

121.s: Who was the 'Kase' among the village artisans of the Vijayanagara period?
121.x: Kase was the mason or house-builder; Vadrangi was the carpenter, Kummari the potter and Chakali the washerman.
xa: **Kammari** = blacksmith; **Mangali** = barber.
There were **12 Ayagars** per village.

121.s: Who collected the grain gifts called 'Merulu' in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

121.s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
121.x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

121.s: Who supervised forced labour (vetti) in a Vijayanagara village?
121.x: The Begari supervised vetti (forced labour).

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mera was the share of the harvest given to the Ayagars.
2. Meruka was a tax on sale and purchase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Meruka was the sale and purchase tax, so both statements are correct.

121.s: What was the village head called Reddi in Andhra known as in Karnataka?
121.x: The Reddi was the village head and revenue collector of Andhra; in Karnataka he was the Gauda.

121.s: What was the chief characteristics of financial system of Vijayanagara Empire?
121.x: Land revenue (share of produce, usually 1/6, and higher on fertile land) was the mainstay of Vijayanagara finance, so Land Revenue is correct.

121.s: The Vijayanagar King who totally withdrew the marriage tax was:
121.x: Sadasivaraya Vijayanagara Empire, is Sadasivaraya, a ruler of the credited with abolishing the marriage tax that had been levied on subjects, as part of welfare-oriented measures. Such tax reforms were governance sometimes used to gain popular support and legitimacy for rulers. This act reflects the administrative practices of later Vijayanagara rulers.

121.s: What is "Meruka" a tax on?
121.x:
Meruka was a commercial tax levied on the sale and purchase of goods during the Reddy period. Trade and commerce formed an important source of state revenue, and taxes like Meruka were imposed on market transactions carried out by merchants. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Meruka – Tax on Sale and Purchase

121.s: Vijayanagara king who completely abolished marriage tax?
121.x: According to Paes and Nuniz, Sri Krishnadevaraya abolished the Kalyana Kanike (marriage tax). Sadashivaraya abolished the Mangali (barber) tax.

121.s:
Match the following taxes:
List I

a. Navidadere

b. Melivamsam

c. Manevana

d. Tudimeya
List II

I. Tax on Marriage

II. Tax on Barbers

III. Tax on Ploughs

IV. Tax Houses
121.x: Navidadere is the barbers' tax (II), and the notes also list the house tax (Maneyanna) and the marriage tax (Kalyana Kanika). That fits option 2, with Melivamsam as the plough tax (III) and Tudimeya as the marriage tax (I).

121.s: Which of the following pairs relating to land classification is correctly matched?
121.x: Bagayati denoted garden land. Nanja was wet land, Punja was dry land and Banjara was waste land.
121.tq: Use elimination through the land-classification terms.
xs: **Bagayati — garden land** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Nanja** = wet; **Punja** = dry; **Banjara** = waste — so options 1, 2 and 4 are wrong.
xa: Andhra terms: **Neerarambamu (Magani)** = irrigated, paid in grain; **Kaadarambamu (Metta)** = dry, paid in cash.
Tax rates depended on the **quality of land**.

121.s: What did Neerarambamu or Magani denote in the Andhra terminology of Vijayanagara revenue administration?
o: Garden land assessed through market tolls
121.x: Neerarambamu, also called Magani, was irrigated land and was generally taxed in grain at higher rates.
121.tq: Distinguish the two closely related Andhra land-assessment terms.
xs: **Neerarambamu (Magani)** = **irrigated land**, taxed in **grain** at a higher rate — option **(3)**.
Dry land, **Kaadarambamu (Metta)**, was taxed in **cash** at a lower rate.
xa: Andhra shares: **Sangoru (1/2)**, **Mungoru (1/3)**.
Water tax: **Neeruganti**.

121.s: How were the rights to collect market or santhalu taxes generally given in the Vijayanagara Empire?
o: Assigned permanently to village assemblies without payment
121.x: The right to collect market taxes was auctioned to Sunkandarlu.
121.tq: Identify the agency associated with the collection right rather than the tax itself.
xs: The right to collect market (**santhalu**) taxes was **auctioned to Sunkandarlu** — option **(4)**.
The **Dalavayi** was the army C-in-C, not a toll collector.
xa: Customs and excise came under the **Sunka vyavahara** department.
**Adikasu** was the tax on shops; **Meruka** on sale and purchase.
Land tax remained the **main source** of revenue.

121.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase of goods
121.x: Putrodaya kanuka was a tax on the birth of a son. Sale and purchase of goods was taxed through Meruka.
121.tq: Find the wrongly matched tax and object.
xs: **Putrodaya kanuka — Sale and purchase** is wrong — option **(1)**; it was a tax on the **birth of a son**.
Sale and purchase was taxed by **Meruka**.
**Kalyana kanika** = weddings; **Illari pannu** = houses; **Kondaju** = barbers — all correct.
xa: **Sadashiva Raya** abolished the barbers' tax **Kondaju**.
The **marriage tax** was abolished empire-wide by **Krishnadevaraya**, after **Saluva Narasimha** lifted it in some areas.

121.s: Which of the following statements regarding Siddhaya is correct?
o: It was exclusively a military title of the commander-in-chief.
It denoted a fixed levy, with varieties connected with occupations such as cotton ginning and toddy tapping.
It was the name of the royal treasury.
It referred only to a tax on sale and purchase of goods.
121.x: Siddhaya meant a fixed levy. Pinje Siddhayam was connected with cotton ginners, Eidipi Siddhayam with toddy tappers and Jati Siddhayam with castes or professions.
121.tq: Identify the general term from its occupational applications.
xs: **Siddhaya** was a **fixed levy**, with occupational forms — option **(2)**.
**Pinje Siddhayam** = cotton ginners; **Eidipi Siddhayam** = toddy tappers; **Jati Siddhayam** = castes/professions.
The treasury was **Bhandara**; tax on sale and purchase was **Meruka**.
xa: Under the **Kakatiyas**, Siddhaya was an extraordinary **war-time tax**.
**Kanika / Kanuka** = levy or present, e.g. **Kalyana kanika**.

121.s: On whom was the Vijayanagara tax Navidadere levied?
121.x: Navidadere (Kondaju) was the barbers' tax; Maneyanna was the house tax.

121.s: On what was the Vijayanagara tax Maneyanna (Illari Pannu) levied?
121.x: Maneyanna was the house tax.

121.s: What was the usual share of produce collected as land revenue in Vijayanagara?
121.x: The usual share was 1/6; fertile land paid 1/4 or 1/3.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara tax was levied on the birth of a son?
121.x: Putrodaya Kanuka was levied on the birth of a son; Kalyana Kanika was the wedding tax.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew (abolished) the marriage tax?
121.x: The marriage tax was totally withdrawn under Sadasiva Raya (APPSC Group 1 key); Krishnadevaraya is a frequent decoy.

121.s: Which tax of the Vijayanagara period was levied on sale and purchase?
121.x: Meruka was the tax on sale and purchase; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share and Merulu the Talari's grain gifts.

121.s: What were the land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period called?
121.x: Land-tax documents of the Vijayanagara period were called Adhuvanatantram.

121.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler first remitted the marriage tax?
121.x: The marriage tax was first remitted by Saluva Narasimha and later abolished under Sadasiva Raya.

121.s: What was the practice adopted by the Vijayanagar Kings to protect the inhabitants within a fortified area from starvation due to sieges by enemy armies?
o: Large granaries were built within the fortified area to store grains
Secret pathways were maintained to transport groceries into fortified areas
Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
The forts were built on hills to prevent siege by the enemy
121.x: Per NCERT (Themes in Indian History II, ch. 7), granaries were the ordinary measure against sieges, while the Vijayanagara rulers adopted the more elaborate strategy of enclosing agricultural tracts within the fortified area.

121.s: Who headed the Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara?
121.x: The standing army was under the Dalavayi; Durga Dannayakas commanded forts.
xa: Nuniz put the standing army at about **50,000**.
The other wing: **Amara-nayaka levies** — **600,000** under Achyutaraya (Nuniz).

121.s: Who was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon?
121.x: Bukka I was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon; firearms were associated with Turkish and Portuguese experts.
xa: ⚠ First cannon = **Bukka I**; **Samugaris** (gunmen) = **Saluva Narasimha**.
Cavalry was **decisive**.

121.s: Through which ports did Vijayanagara mainly import Arabian and Persian horses?
121.x: Horses came via the west-coast ports Goa, Honnavar and Bhatkal; Portuguese and Arab merchants ran the trade.
xa: Krishnadevaraya had **24,000 horses**.
Amuktamalyada urges importing **horses, elephants and gems**.

121.s: Who introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen, into the Vijayanagara military system?
121.x: Saluva Narasimha introduced the Samugaris, or gunmen. Bukka I is associated with the first use of cannon by a Vijayanagara king.

121.s: In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
121.x:
The Pradvivaka (Pradvivaka or Pradvivakudu) was the chief judicial adviser to the king in ancient and medieval Indian administration. He assisted the ruler in legal matters, interpreted Dharmashastra, advised on judicial decisions and supervised the administration of justice. His position was equivalent to that of a chief judge or legal expert in the royal court. Several ancient legal texts refer to the office of the Pradvivaka as an important component of judicial administration. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Pradvivaka – Chief Judicial Adviser
• Department – Judiciary

122.s:
According to Portuguese writer Nuniz, the women in Vijayanagara Empire were experts in which of the following areas?
1. Wrestling
2. Astrology
3. Accounting
4. Soothsaying
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
122.x: All are correct: The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled by four successive dynasties: the Sangama (c. 1336–1485 CE), Saluva (c. 1485–1503 CE), Tuluva (c. 1503–1570 CE), and Aravidu dynasties, the last continuing till the end of the 17th century. A significant understanding of the empire's history comes from the accounts of two Portuguese Medieval Indian History PMF IAS IH – 41 chroniclers, Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz. Writing in the sixteenth century, their narratives provide valuable first-hand insights. Domingo Paes recorded his observations during 1520–22, in the reign of Krishnadevaraya, while Fernao Nuniz wrote around 1535–37, during the rule of Achyuta Deva Raya. Both rulers were key figures of the Tuluva dynasty. Women in Vijayanagara society enjoyed a notable status and actively participated in political, social, and cultural life. They were engaged in activities such as wrestling, swordsmanship, the use of shields, music, and other fine arts, and some also received substantial literary education. Nuniz notes that women held diverse roles, including wrestling, astrology, and soothsaying. He also notes the presence of women officials who kept expense records in the palace and documented administrative affairs, often cross-checking these records with those kept by external scribes.

In the entertainments of the Vijayanagara kings, apart from Yakshaganam, which art form entertained the common rural people of Andhra?
124.x:
During the Vijayanagara period, several traditional performing arts flourished under royal patronage. While Yakshaganam was popular in royal courts and among elite audiences, the Leather Puppet Dance (Tholu Bommalata) was the most popular entertainment among the rural population. Tholu Bommalata is a traditional shadow puppet theatre in which colourful leather puppets are manipulated behind a white screen with the help of light. Stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas were presented through music, narration and dialogue. This art form served not only as entertainment but also as a medium for religious instruction and moral education. Andhra Pradesh continues to be one of the most important centres of Tholu Bommalata. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

126.s: Who was the king of Vijayanagara during the Rakshasa Tangadi (Tallikota) battle of 1565?
126.x: Sadashiva Raya was the nominal king while Aliya Rama Raya ruled as regent.

126.s: ............ The Vijayanagara Empire came to an end in the Battle of Talikota.
126.x: The Vijayanagara Empire came to an end in the battle of Talikota in 1565.

126.s: Son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya?
126.x: Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law was Aliya Ramaraya, whose actions led to the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasa Tangadi) on 23 January 1565.

126.s: In which year did the Talikota war take place?
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 26 January 1565 between Vijayanagara (led by Aliya Ramaraya) and an alliance of Bahmani successor kingdoms, which won.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought in –
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565, so 1565 A.D. is correct; 1526 is the First Battle of Panipat.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought between
o: Vijayanagara and combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda.
126.x: Vijayanagara faced a confederacy of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar. The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up, so option 2 is wrong.

126.s: In January 1565, the Battle of Talikota was fought between-
o: The Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccani Sultanates
The Mughal Empire and the Vijayanagara Empire
The Marathas and the Deccani Sultanates
The Bahmani Sultanate and the Vijayanagara Empire
126.x: The Battle of Talikota (1565) was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and a coalition of Deccan Sultanates including Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar and Bidar. The defeat of Vijayanagara in this battle led to the destruction of the capital Hampi and marked the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire.

126.s: The famous battle held in 1565 is –
126.x: The battle of Talikota (1565 A.D.), a watershed battle, was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates of Bijapur, Bidar, Ahmadnagar, Golconda (Barar was not included). It resulted in the defeat of Vijayanagara and ended weakening one of the greatest Indian empires originating from southern India before the Maratha Empire. Talikota is situated in Karnataka near Vijayapura district.

126.s: Who fought the Battle of Rakshashi-Thangadi (Talikota, 1565 A.D.) which ended the glory of the Vijayanagar empire?
o: Ramaraya and the Imadshahis of Berar
The Adilshahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya
Veeranarasimha and the Nizamshahis of Ahmednagar
Ramaraya and Nizam Shah of Ahmednagar
126.x: Bijapur's Adil Shahis (Ali Adil Shah) were part of the sultanate confederacy that fought Rama Raya. The other options name only one sultanate, or Berar, which stayed out.

126.s: Vijayanagara Empire was destroyed in Tallikota war of ________.
126.x: Vijayanagara was defeated at Talikota in 1565, after which Hampi was looted; so 1565 AD is correct.

126.s: Which dynasty ruled Berar, the Deccan Sultanate that stayed out of the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Berar was ruled by the Imad Shahis and stayed out; Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda organised the alliance.
Vijayanagara faced the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom (G1 **2018**).

126.s: From which Sultanate was Jagadeva Rao, whose shelter by Rama Raya helped provoke the Deccan coalition, a rebel?
126.x: Rama Raya sheltered Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda, one of the causes of the coalition.
xa: Marriage links: **Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
**Ferishta** also alleges religious insults.
Rama Raya **sacked Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.

126.s: Which region did Rama Raya acquire in 1546-47 by backing Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar?
126.x: In 1546-47 Rama Raya supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab.
xa: This **divide-and-rule** diplomacy is listed as a cause that **united the Sultans** against him.
Rama Raya had earlier served under **Golconda** and the **Bahmanis**.
He also sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.

126.s: Who was the key organiser of the Deccan Sultanates' alliance that fought at Talikota (1565)?
126.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was the key organiser of the coalition.
xa: **Robert Sewell** called it **Talikota**; **Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri** called it **Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
Date: **23 January 1565**; some notes give **26 January**.
**Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**.
⚠ **Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out of the battle.

126.s: Which statement about the aftermath of Talikota is correct?
o: Sewell held that the capital suffered no destruction.
The sack is universally held to have wiped out Vijayanagara culture.
Tirumala wrote the account of the sack in 1570.
Sewell called the sacked city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.
126.x: Sewell used the expression 'graveyard' for the sacked capital, though that assessment may be exaggerated.
xa: Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**).
**Caesar Frederick** gave an eyewitness account in **1567**.
Nayaka courts later spread **Raya gopurams** and **kalyana mandapas** across Andhra.

126.s: Which of the following pairs (Sultanate – Ruler at Talikota) is correctly matched?
126.x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah. Ahmadnagar was under Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda under Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar under Ali Barid Shah.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** was the key organiser of the alliance.
**Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
**Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out.

126.s: Who among the following was married to Chand Bibi among the marriage alliances before Talikota?
126.x: Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah, while Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
xa: Rama Raya sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.
In **1546-47** he took the **Raichur doab**.

126.s: For how long was Hampi looted after the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hampi was looted for about six months; the damage was severe but not total.
xa: Sewell's **"graveyard"** account may exaggerate.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** + coastal tracts.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s: Which historian named the Battle of 1565 'Rakshasi-Tangadi'?
126.x: Heras called it Rakshasi-Tangadi; Sewell used Talikota and Sherwani used Bannihatti.

126.s: Who beheaded Aliya Rama Raya at the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar beheaded Rama Raya; Ibrahim Qutb Shah was the alliance's main organiser.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Aliya Rama Raya:
1. He ruled as regent of Sadasiva Raya.
2. Between 1557 and 1563 he backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
3. He gave shelter to Jagadeva Rao, a rebel of Golconda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: All three are correct: Rama Raya was Sadasiva's regent, razed Ahmadnagar with Bijapur in 1557-63 and sheltered Jagadeva Rao.

126.s: Who called the Vijayanagara capital after Talikota a 'graveyard'?
126.x: Robert Sewell called the city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.

126.s: In which year was the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) fought?
126.x: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565 between Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates.

126.x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was the son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya.

126.s: Which became the second capital of the Vijayanagara Empire after 1565 AD?
126.x: After the battle of Tallikota (1565) the Aravidu rulers moved the capital to Penukonda.

126.s: What was the capital of Vijayanagara after the Battle of Tallikota?
126.x: After Rakshasa Tangadi, Tirumala Raya moved to Penugonda and founded the Aravidu dynasty with it as capital.

126.s: Which became the second capital of the Vijayanagara Empire after 1565 AD?
126.x:
After the Battle of Talikota (1565 CE) and the destruction of Hampi, the Vijayanagara rulers shifted their capital to Penukonda in presentday Andhra Pradesh. Penukonda served as the imperial capital for several decades before the capital was later shifted to Chandragiri and Vellore. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Second Capital after Talikota → Penukonda

126.s: Capital of Araveeti dynasty?
126.x: After the battle of Rakshasa Tangadi, Tirumala Raya fled to Penugonda and was crowned there, making it the capital.

126.s: Where did Sadasiva and Tirumala flee after the defeat at Talikota?
126.x: They fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II.
xa: Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.
**Sriranga Raya I** later lost **Kondaveedu** to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

126.s: In order of succession, which ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara was the Aravidu dynasty?
126.x: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara and ruled from 1570 to 1680 with seven rulers.
xa: Some notes date the empire's end to **1646**.
Founder **Tirumala** shifted the capital to **Penukonda** in **1570**.
Greatest ruler: **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**).

126.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
126.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
126.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.
xs: **Tirumala Raya** founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at **Penukonda** in **1570** — so option **(4)** is correct.

128.s: Kabuliyat and Patta was introduced by
128.x: Patta (title deed) and qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) were introduced by Sher Shah as part of his land revenue settlement, not by Shivaji, Jahangir or Aurangzeb.

128.x: Sher Shah introduced the patta and qabuliyat as instruments of direct state-peasant settlement; the other rulers listed did not.

128.x: Sher Shah Suri levied a land tax at the rate of one-third of the produce under his revenue administration, based on careful measurement and assessment.

128.x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.
xa: State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **cash or grain**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "one-fourth" is false.
**Patta** = title deed given to the cultivator; **Qabuliyat** = deed of acceptance signed by the peasant.
The system became the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.

128.s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, what was the Qabuliyat?

the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
128.x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.
128.tq: Patta given to peasant; Qabuliyat signed by peasant
xs: The **Qabuliyat** was the peasant's **deed of agreement** accepting the revenue demand, **signed by him** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Patta** was the **title deed** given to the cultivator.
**Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
xa: ⚠ **Patta** = given by the state; **Qabuliyat** = signed by the peasant.
Assessment was by the **Amin**, with shiqdar, qanungo and patwari.

128.x: The tomb of Sasaram, also known as the tomb of Sher Shah Suri, is located in the Rohtas district of present-day Bihar. The socio-political condition of the country was such that Akbar thought it was advisable to adopt independent views in religious matters. The non-Muslims constituted the majority of his Indian subjects. Without winning their confidence and active support, Akbar could not hope to establish and consolidate the Mughal rule in India. Religion had played the role of a divisive force in Indian society ever since the advent of Islam which most of its people had refused to embrace. Akbar fully understood the centrifugal tendencies of the complex Indian sociopolitical order and made a serious attempt to eliminate these by separating religion from politics. To win the goodwill of Hindus, he abolished the pilgrimage tax and Jizya. Freedom of worship, matrimonial alliances with Hindus, high civil and military positions to Hindus, translation of Hindu scriptures, establishment of Ibadatkhana, issue of infallibility decree, freedom to construct temples, land grants, considerations of Hindu sentiments, reforms in Hindu society were some measures adopted by Akbar to establish religious harmony but he had not forsaken Islam.

It contained the good points of all religions, and the basics were rational. However, his new faith proved to be a failure. It fizzled out after his death. 129.s: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with the house of :
129.x: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with Kachhwaha Rajput. He went on a pilgrimage to the Mausoleum of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer in 1562 A.D. His route laid through the Rajput state of Amber. Its ruler Raja Bihari Mal (Bharmal), with a view of safeguarding his position, offered his submission to Akbar at Sanganer and voluntarily proposed his daughter, Princess Harkhabai (Jodha) marriage with the young monarch. Akbar accepted the offer and on his return from Ajmer, married in 1562 AD. It was the first marriage of Akbar with any Rajput girl. Thus, Raja Bharmal was the first Rajput king who accepted Akbar’s supremacy of his accord. Salim (later Jahangir), heir to the throne was born of this wedlock on August 30, 1569 AD.

130.s: Zabti system was introduced by –
130.x: Zabti System was introduced for land revenue in the reign of Akbar which was measurement based assessment; revenue circles (dasturs) with per-bigha cash rates; Ain-i-Dahsala (ten year average rate). It was based on schedules of Dasturul-Amal and Zabti Khasre for land survey and land revenue determination. Most of the area was based on this system. 33. In which measures Todarmal achieved fame ? (a) Military campaign (b) Land Revenue (c) Humor (d) Painting U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1992 Ans. (b) Todarmal achieved fame in the field of land revenue. Akbar introduced the Dahsala or Zabti system of land revenue collection in 1580 A.D. to consolidate Mughal empire. The founder of this system was Todarmal under Akbar. That’s why it is known as Todarmal settlement. Under this system, the average produce of different crops, as well as the average prices prevailing over the last ten years, was calculated. Onethird of the average produce was state Share (Maal), rest two-third share was left to the cultivators (Kharaj).

One-third of that average was fixed as land revenue for state which was also called “Dahsala System”. Ain-i-Dahsala is known as Todarmal Bandobast.’
