130.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zabti — Crop-sharing between the state and peasant
Batai — Rough assessment based on past revenue records
Kankut — Yield estimated on the standing crop
Nasaq — Land measured and cash rates fixed per crop
130.x: Kankut involved estimating the yield on the standing crop. Zabti involved measurement and cash rates, Batai involved crop-sharing, and Nasaq relied on past revenue records.
130.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate swapped meanings.
xs: **Kankut — yield estimated on the standing crop** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Zabti** = land measured and cash rates fixed per crop; **Batai** = crop-sharing.
**Nasaq** = rough assessment from **past revenue records**, without fresh measurement.
xa: Kankut was used where **measurement was not practical**.
**Nasaq** was used mainly in **Bengal**.
⚠ **Batai** = crop-sharing; **Kankut** = standing-crop estimate; **Nasaq** = past records.

130.s: In which region was the Nasaq method of revenue assessment mainly used under the Mughals?
130.x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.
xa: **Kankut** estimated the yield on the **standing crop** where measurement was impractical.
**Zabti** fixed cash rates per crop per **bigha** after measuring land.
**Batai** is also called **Ghalla-bakhshi**.

130.s: In which year was Akbar's Dahsala system introduced?
130.x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.
xa: Dahsala is also called **Ain-i-Dahsala**; it was the APPSC-G2 **2017** answer.
**Bandobast** system = **Dahsala** (JPSC **2013** key).
State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **dam**.

130.s: The Dahsala was based on the average produce and prices of which years?
130.x: The Dahsala (1580) used the average of the last ten years, 1571-1580.

130.s: Where was Batai (Ghalla-bakhshi) mainly used under the Mughals?
130.x: Crop-sharing (batai) was used in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir; Nasaq was mainly in Bengal and Zabti in the core provinces.

130.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, what were the 'dasturs'?
o: Cash revenue rates per crop per bigha
Revenue circles yielding one crore dams
130.x: Under zabti, land was measured and dasturs fixed cash rates per crop per bigha.

130.s: In parts of the Deccan, on what basis was land revenue fixed under the plough method?
o: An estimate of the standing crop
130.x: In parts of the Deccan revenue was assessed by the number of ploughs.

130.s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left fallow for one or two years called?
130.x: Parauti lay fallow one or two years; Polaj was cultivated every year, Chachar fallow three or four years, Banjar five or more.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse **Parauti** (1-2 yrs) with **Chachar** (3-4 yrs).
Relief measures: **Taccavi** loans and remissions.
Golconda's classes were different: **wet, dry, garden, waste**.

130.s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left uncultivated for five years or more called?
130.x: Banjar was fallow 5+ years; Parauti 1-2 and Chachar 3-4 years.

130.s: In Akbar's classification, what kind of land was Polaj?
130.x: Polaj land was cultivated every year.

130.s: In Mughal administrative vocabulary ‘Maal’ represents–
130.x: It was related to Land Revenue.

130.s: ‘Madad-i-Mash’ indicates in Mughal administration –
o: Revenue free land granted to learned persons
130.x: Sometimes, the Mughal administration issued grants as a Madad-i-Maash to pious or otherwise worthy recipients as charity. The spirit of composite culture and harmony expressed in revenue-free grants (Madad-i-Maash), which the nobles extended to the support of saints, maintenance of religious institutions, religious places and upkeep of Mashaikhs, etc.

130.s: In the Mughal administration ‘Madad- i-Mash’ indicates
o: revenue free land given to learned persons
130.x: Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy, so option 2 is correct. It was not a tax or a military pension.

130.s: What was Mughal crown land, whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury, called?
130.x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.
xa: **Khalisa** revenue went straight to the imperial treasury; cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid from it.
A **jagir** was a right to collect revenue in lieu of salary — not ownership.
Khalisa expanded in Golconda under **Abdullah** and **Tana Shah**.

130.s: What did a jagir represent under the Mughal system?
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
130.x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.
130.tq: Apply the distinction between revenue-collection rights and ownership.
xs: A **jagir** was the **right to collect revenue in lieu of salary**, not ownership — so option **(3)** is correct.
Direct cash salaries came from **khalisa** revenue (**naqd**); revenue-free grants to scholars were **madad-i-maash**.
xa: Mansabdars held **non-hereditary**, combined civil-military ranks **paid by jagir**.
⚠ British **ICS** = purely civil, fixed salary from the treasury.
**Suyurghal** = another name for charitable revenue-free grants.

130.s: What were Mughal revenue-free grants to scholars, holy men and the needy called?
130.x: Madad-i-maash (also suyurghal) was a charitable revenue-free grant; Khalisa was crown land.

130.s: What was the principal source of income of the Mughal state?
130.x: Maal, the land revenue, was the main income of the Mughal state.

130.s: What did the term 'Suyurghal' mean in the Mughal period?
130.x: Suyurghal, like madad-i-maash, was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.

130.s:
Assertion (A) : During the time of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses.
Reason (R) : Horses had to be rested while on march and replacements were necessary in times of war.
o: Both (A) and (R) is true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
130.x: During the reign of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the Mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses. The main reason for this custom was that it was essential to give rest to the horses during the long journey and it was needed to replace horses during the war. Thus, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

130.s: Which feature distinguished Mughal mansabdars from the British ICS?
o: They were paid only fixed treasury salaries
130.x: Mansabdars held combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir; the ICS was purely civil and salaried.
xa: A **jagir** was the right to collect revenue, **not ownership**.
Cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid against **khalisa** land.
Mansabdari + **zabti-dahsala** gave a salaried, **transferable** nobility.

130.s: In which tradition did the Mughal mansabdari system have its origin?
130.x: Mansabdari was of Central Asian / Mongol military origin.

130.s: Under Akbar, to whom alone were mansabs above those of the nobles (5,000, later 7,000) given?
130.x: Noble ranks ran from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks were only for royal princes.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system:
1. Zat denoted personal rank and pay.
2. Sawar denoted the number of horsemen to be maintained.
3. Mansabs were hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
130.x: Zat was personal rank and Sawar the horsemen to be kept; mansabs were non-hereditary.

130.s: In which class was a mansabdar whose sawar rank equalled his zat rank placed?
130.x: By the sawar-zat ratio, sawar equal to zat made a mansabdar first class.

130.s: What was the range of mansab ranks for nobles under Akbar?
130.x: Nobles held mansabs from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks went only to princes.

130.s: Which type of Mughal jagir was hereditary and not transferable?
130.x: Watan jagir, the zamindar's homeland, was hereditary and not transferable.

130.s: After how many years were Tankha jagirs, given in lieu of salary, normally transferred?
130.x: Tankha jagirs were transferable every 3-4 years, which prevented local power bases.

130.s: Which of the following pairs (Jagir type – feature) is correctly matched?
o: Mashrut – conditional, tied to specified duties
130.x: Mashrut was conditional; Watan was non-transferable, In'am carried no service obligation and Tankha was in lieu of salary.

130.s: Which Mughal central minister handled military matters such as dagh, chehra and promotions?
130.x: The Mir Bakhshi was the military head in charge of dagh, chehra and promotions.

130.s: What was the Mughal Sadr-us-sudur in charge of?
130.x: The Sadr-us-sudur dealt with religious affairs, charitable grants and the Shariat.

130.s: Which of the following about Mughal central ministers is NOT correct?
o: The Mir Saman was in charge of religious affairs.
The Wakil was the highest in rank.
The Wazir handled revenue, treasury and accounts.
130.x: The Mir Saman looked after the royal household and karkhanas; religious affairs were with the Sadr-us-sudur.

130.s: Which Mughal central minister looked after the royal household and the karkhanas?
130.x: The Mir Saman was in charge of the royal household and karkhanas.

130.s: In medieval Deccan, Deshmukh was a village official, wh responsible to-
o: Collect land revenue from the peasants and to deposit it in the State treasury
Maintain law and order in the village
130.x: In the medieval Deccan administrative system, the Deshmukh was a local official responsible for collecting land revenue from villages. The Deshmukh collected revenue from peasants and forwarded it to the state treasury, functioning as an intermediary between the state administration and rural society.

130.s:
Match the following revenue officials during the reign of Akbar with their duties:
List I
List II
a. Amalguzar
I. Kept records of the revenue payable by the villages
b. Karkuns
II. Revenue Collector in-charge of a District
c. Qanungo
III. Accountant
d. Bitikchi
IV. Prepared the seasonal crop statistics
130.x: The amalguzar was the revenue collector, the qanungo kept revenue records, and the bitikchi kept records on land and produce, with the karkun preparing crop statistics. The option a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III matches this pattern.

130.s: Who was the head of a Mughal suba, served by a Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi?
130.x: The Subedar headed the suba; the Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi were the other suba officials.
xa: **Sarkar**: **Faujdar** (law and order) and **amalguzar** (revenue).
**Pargana**: **Shiqdar**, amil, qanungo.

130.s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the state generally took what share of the produce?
130.x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

130.s: Which of the following pairs (Unit – Officials) is correctly matched?
130.x: The pargana had the shiqdar, amil and qanungo. The sarkar had the faujdar and amalguzar, the town the kotwal, and the village the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.
xa: The **Faujdar** handled law and order; the **amalguzar** handled revenue.
The **Kotwal** looked after police and municipal order.
**Suba** officials: Subedar, diwan, bakhshi, sadr, qazi.

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdar — military and law-and-order duties at the sarkar level
Subahdar — governor responsible for law and order
Provincial Diwan — revenue administration and an independent check on the governor
Kotwal — maintenance of pargana land and revenue records
130.x: The Kotwal was responsible for law and order in the city. Maintenance of land and revenue records at the pargana level was the duty of the Qanungo.
130.tq: Locate the wrong administrative level attached to the official.
xs: **Kotwal — pargana land and revenue records** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Kotwal** was a **town** official for **police and municipal order**.
Pargana-level officials were the **Shiqdar**, **amil** and **qanungo**.
The **Faujdar** handled **law and order** at the **sarkar** level; the **Subedar** and **diwan** were suba officials.
xa: Sarkar revenue was handled by the **amalguzar**.
Village: **muqaddam** (headman), **patwari**, **chowkidar**.

130.s: Which Mughal official kept the land and revenue records of a pargana?
130.x: The qanungo kept pargana land and revenue records; the potdar was a treasurer.

130.s: What was the Potdar in Mughal revenue administration?
130.x: The potdar was the treasurer; the patwari was the village accountant and the amalguzar the sarkar revenue collector.

130.s: In 1580, Akbar's empire was divided into how many subas?
130.x: There were 12 subas in 1580.

130.s: Whose duty was law and order in a Mughal town?
130.x: The kotwal kept law and order in the city; the faujdar did so at sarkar level.

130.s: In Mughal revenue administration, what was the duty of the Bitikchi?
o: Collecting the revenue of the sarkar
Keeping records on land and produce
Maintaining law and order in towns
130.x: The bitikchi kept records on land and produce; the amalguzar collected revenue and the potdar was treasurer.

130.s: Who was the revenue collector of a Mughal sarkar, also charged with extending cultivation?
130.x: The amalguzar collected sarkar revenue and tried to extend cultivation.

131.s: Who among the following wives of Jahangir committed suicide?
131.x: The notes do not state which wife of Jahangir committed suicide.

131.s: Which among the following is not correctly matched? Emperor Amir
131.x: The notes do not mention Sawai Jai Singh as an amir of Jahangir, but the other pairings are not contradicted; the notes give no line settling it.

131.s: Jahangir took shelter at which of the following fort?

Of the following who had rebelled against the Mughal Emperor Jahangir?

I. Asif Khan

II. Khurram

III. Mahabat Khan

IV. Khusrau
Codes
131.x: Khusrau (1606), Khurram (1622-26) and Mahabat Khan (1626 coup) all rebelled against Jahangir. Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and a junta member, not a rebel.

131.s: In whose reign was the ‘Treaty of Chittor’ signed between Mughal and the Rana of Mewar ?
131.x: It was the reign of Jahangir in which the ‘’Treaty of Chittor’’ was signed between Mughals and Rana of Mewar in 1615 A.D. Rana accepted the allegiance of Mughal emperor and Jahangir returned Mewar and Chittorgarh to Rana which were annexed by Mughals during the reign of Akbar. 3. Who of the following was sent first by East India Company to the court of Jahangir ? (a) Sir Thomas Roe (b) Vasco-da-Gama (c) Hawkins (d) Job Chornok U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1993 Ans. (c) William Hawkins (1608-11 A.D.) was the first English ambassador of English East India Company to visit the court of Jahangir. He was sent by East India Company in 1608 AD. He stayed at the royal court for 3 years. Jahangir honoured him with mansab of 400. Sir Thomas Roe led the second delegation to visit the court of Jahangir. Sir Thomas Roe was the first ambassador sent by British King James-I to the court of Jahangir. 4. Who among the following is the envoy of British King James- I was sent to Jahangir’s court? (a) William Hawkins (b) William Finch (c) Pitra Della Villa (d) Edward Terry U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2013 Ans. (*)

131.s:
Which of the following incidents took place during the reign of Jahangir?
I. The fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev was sentenced to death.
II. Victory over Rajputs of Mewar.
III. Annexation of Kabul and Kandahar.
IV. Arrival of English East India Company to India.
131.x: During the reign of Jahangir (1605-1627) several significant events occurred. The fifth Sikh Guru Guru Arjan Dev was executed in 1606. Jahangir also concluded peace with the Rajputs of Mewar, and the English East India Company established trade relations during this period.

131.s: In which year did Jahangir's eldest son Khusrau rebel?
131.x: Khusrau rebelled in 1606; Khurram's revolt (1622-26) was the one provoked by Nur Jahan backing Shahryar.
xa: Khusrau was **blinded** and later died (**1622**) in Khurram's custody.
**Shahryar** was Nur Jahan's **son-in-law**.
**1626**: **Mahabat Khan** seized Jahangir on the **Jhelum**.

131.s: Which statement about Mewar during Jahangir's reign is correct?
o: Rana Amar Singh submitted in 1615 and Karan Singh was made a mansabdar.
Karan Singh succeeded Jahangir after Mewar's submission.
Rana Amar Singh defeated Jahangir and ended Mughal control over Mewar.
Rana Amar Singh recovered Kandahar for the Mughals.
131.x: Amar Singh of Mewar submitted to Jahangir in 1615 and his son Karan Singh was made a mansabdar, ending the long Mughal-Mewar conflict.
xa: Mewar's submission is one of the APPSC G1 **2022** "Jahangir's reign" events.
Others: **Guru Arjan Dev's** execution and the arrival of the **English EIC**.
⚠ Trap: **Kabul-Kandahar** were **not annexed** by Jahangir.

131.s: Whom did Nur Jahan support, which was the immediate political reason for Khurram's revolt?
131.x: Nur Jahan favoured Shahryar, her son-in-law, as successor. This contributed to Khurram's revolt from 1622 to 1626.
131.tq: Identify the correct heirship dispute behind a rebellion.
xs: Nur Jahan backed **Shahryar** as heir, triggering Khurram's revolt — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Shahryar** was married to her daughter; Khurram revolted **1622-1626**.
**Khusrau** had rebelled earlier (**1606**); **Dara Shikoh** and **Murad Bakhsh** were Shah Jahan's sons.
xa: The **Nur Jahan junta** ran the empire for about **ten years** and split over this succession issue.
Kandahar was lost to Persia in **1622** during the revolt.
Khurram had married Nur Jahan's niece **Arjumand Banu Begum** in **1612**.

131.s: With which place is Salim Chishti of Akbar's reign associated?
131.x: Salim Chishti lived at Sikri in Akbar's time.
n: Guru Arjan Dev was executed during the reign of Jahangir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed during the reign of Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Salim Chishti was associated with Sikri during the reign of Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
xa: **Fa-Hien** visited under **Chandragupta II**; **Hiuen-Tsang** under **Harsha**.
**Ibn Battuta** came under **Muhammad bin Tughluq**.
Arjan Dev was executed for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.

131.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hawkins — English arrival in India in 1608
Shah Abbas I — recovery of Kandahar in 1638
Guru Arjan Dev — rebellion against Khurram
Mahabat Khan — revolt of Khusrau in 1606
131.x: Hawkins reached Surat in 1608, in Jahangir's reign. B is wrong because Shah Abbas I captured Kandahar in 1622; its recovery in 1638 was under Shah Jahan, when Ali Mardan Khan surrendered it. C and D are wrong because Guru Arjan Dev backed the rebel Khusrau (not a rebellion against Khurram), and Mahabat Khan's coup was in 1626, not Khusrau's 1606 revolt.
131.tq: Start from the sure person-event pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Hawkins — English arrival in 1608** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Shah Abbas I** captured Kandahar in **1622**; its **1638** recovery under Shah Jahan came from **Ali Mardan Khan**.
**Guru Arjan Dev** backed the rebel **Khusrau**; **Mahabat Khan's** coup was in **1626**.
xa: Hawkins reached **Surat 1608**, Agra **1609**; got the title **"English Khan"**.
**Captain Best** beat the Portuguese off Surat (**1612**) → factory at **Surat (1613)**.
**Sir Thomas Roe** (**1615-1619**) won trade rights.

131.s: On the bank of which river did Mahabat Khan seize Jahangir in 1626?
131.x: Mahabat Khan's coup of 1626 seized Jahangir on the Jhelum.

131.s: Which of the following did NOT take place in Jahangir's reign?
131.x: Kabul and Kandahar were not annexed by Jahangir; Kandahar was in fact lost to Persia in 1622.

131.s: During which years did Prince Khurram revolt against Jahangir?
131.x: Khurram revolted in 1622-26 when Nur Jahan backed Shahryar as heir.

131.s: Who was the mother of Prince Khusrau, Jahangir's eldest son?
131.x: Khusrau's mother was Man Bai; Jagat Gosain was the mother of Shah Jahan.

131.s: To which Persian ruler did Jahangir lose Kandahar in 1622?
131.x: Kandahar was lost to Shah Abbas I of Persia in 1622.

131.s: What was the childhood name of Nur Jahan?
131.x: Bahu Begam According to the answer key, Nur Jahan's childhood name is given as Bahu Begam, though she is more commonly known historically as Mehrun-Nisa before she was given the title Nur Jahan by Emperor Jahangir. This appears to differ from standard historical references. Nur Jahan became one of the most powerful women in Mughal history.

131.s: Who of the following was not a member of Noorjahan’s Junta?
131.x: Nur Jahan was a cultured, educated, intelligent dominating lady and ambitious wife of Mughal emperor Jahangir. Nur Jahan’s Junta consisted a group of fiveherself, her mother Asmat Begum, her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg or Itmad-ud- Daula, her brother Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram (Son-inlaw of her brother Asaf Khan). Prince Khurram (known as Shah Jahan) had been allied with Nur Jahan during 1611- 1622, but when she swung her support to her son-in-law Shaharyar, he left her Junta and rebelled.

131.s: Who among the following was not a member of 'Nurjahan's Junta'?
131.x: The junta consisted of Nur Jahan, Asmat Begum, Ghiyas Beg (Itimad-ud-Daulah), Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram. Mahabat Khan was not a member (he later seized Jahangir in a coup).

131.s: Mehrunnisa who was known as Nur Jahan was the wife of
131.x: Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Nur Jahan, so Jahangir is correct.

131.s: Who of the following was not a member of Nur Jahan’s Junta?
131.x: Jahangir himself was not a member of the junta, which was made up of Nur Jahan, her parents, Asaf Khan and Khurram. Ghiyas Beg, Asaf Khan and Khurram were members.

131.s: Who built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah at Agra, noted for its marble inlay and regarded as a precursor of the Taj Mahal?
131.x: Nur Jahan built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah (her father, Ghiyas Beg) at Agra. Ghiyas Beg was also Jahangir's diwan, and Asaf Khan was his son, but the builder was Nur Jahan; Shah Jahan's father-in-law was Asaf Khan, not Itimad-ud-Daulah.
131.tq: Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb = Nur Jahan for her father ('Baby Taj').
xs: **Nur Jahan** built the tomb of **Itimad-ud-Daulah** for **her father** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Itimad-ud-Daulah = **Ghiyas Beg**, Jahangir's **diwan**; the tomb's **marble inlay** made it a precursor of the Taj.
**Asaf Khan** was Ghiyas Beg's son, not the builder; Shah Jahan's father-in-law was **Asaf Khan**.
xa: Nur Jahan was also a poet, pen name **"Makhfi"**.
The **Taj Mahal** holds **Mumtaz Mahal**.
Jahangir's own tomb is at **Shahdara (Lahore)**.

131.s: What was the original name of Mumtaz Mahal?
131.x: Mumtaz Mahal, born Arjumand Banu Begum, was Asaf Khan's daughter and is entombed in the Taj Mahal.
xa: She married **Prince Khurram** in **1612**.
Asaf Khan was **Nur Jahan's brother**, so Mumtaz was Nur Jahan's niece.
Asaf Khan later became **Shah Jahan's key adviser**.

131.s: Who was Nur Jahan's father, who served as Jahangir's diwan?
131.x: Ghiyas Beg was Nur Jahan's father and Jahangir's diwan; Asaf Khan was her brother.
xa: **Asaf Khan** was **Khan-i-Saman** and later Shah Jahan's key adviser.
The junta ran the empire for about **ten years**.
Nur Jahan's name on coins is a standard **"first/only"** question.

131.s: Under which pen name did Nur Jahan write poetry?
131.x: Nur Jahan was also a poet and used the pen name Makhfi.
131.tq: Identify the literary pseudonym associated with the political personality.
xs: Nur Jahan wrote poetry under the pen name **"Makhfi"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jahanara** was Shah Jahan's **daughter**; **Padshah** was a title, not her pen name.
xa: Her titles: **Nur Jahan** ("Light of the World"), later **Padshah Begum**.
She built the **tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah** (Agra), with marble inlay — a precursor of the Taj.
Born **Mehrunnisa** in **1577** at **Kandahar**.

131.s: In which year did Nur Jahan marry Jahangir?
131.x: Nur Jahan married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Padshah Begum.
xa: **Mumtaz Mahal** was Asaf Khan's daughter.
She was the widow of **Sher Afghan**.
The junta split when she pushed **Shahryar** as heir.

131.s: Which of the following emperor–diwan pairs is correctly matched?
131.x: Jahangir's diwan was Ghiyas Beg Itimad-ud-Daulah. The other correct pairs are Akbar–Muzaffar Khan, Shah Jahan–Sa'adullah Khan and Aurangzeb–Asad Khan.
131.tq: Use the ruler-office association and eliminate swapped emperor–official pairs.
xs: **Jahangir — Ghiyas Beg Itimad-ud-Daulah** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
Correct pairs: **Akbar — Muzaffar Khan**; **Shah Jahan — Sa'adullah Khan**; **Aurangzeb — Asad Khan**.
So option 1 misplaces Ghiyas Beg, and options 3 and 4 swap **Asad Khan** and **Sa'adullah Khan**.
xa: Ghiyas Beg was Nur Jahan's **father**.
His son **Asaf Khan** was **Khan-i-Saman**.
Nur Jahan built his tomb at **Agra**.

131.s: Which Mughal consort had her name placed on coins and farmans?
131.x: Nur Jahan was the only Mughal consort whose name appeared on coins and farmans.

131.s: Whose widow was Mehrunnisa (Nur Jahan) before marrying Jahangir?
131.x: Mehrunnisa was the widow of Sher Afghan; Asaf Khan was her brother.

131.s: Which member of Nur Jahan's junta was her brother and Shah Jahan's father-in-law?
131.x: Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and father of Mumtaz Mahal; Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg) was her father.

131.s: Which title did Nur Jahan later receive?

Who re-imposed Jizya ?

The Hindus were categorised into three classes for the purpose of paying tax: (i) Those with income less than 200 Dirham per annum, had to pay 12 Dirham per annum as tax. (ii ) Those with income 200 to 10,000 Dirham per annum, had to pay 24 Dirham per annum as tax. (iii) Those with income more than 10,000 Dirham per annum, had to pay 48 Dirham per annum as tax. Women, slaves, children under 14 years, beggars and unemployed persons were exempted from it. The subordinate Hindu kings and Brahmins were compelled to pay this tax. About reviving Jizya, Europian traveller wrote that his motive was to increase his treasure but it seems to be partially true.

o: Abdullah Pani — Defender of Golconda honoured by Aurangzeb
Abul Hasan Qutb Shah — Imprisoned at Bidar and Daulatabad
Abdur Razzaq Lari — Honoured as Mustafa Khan
Tana Shah — Died in 1699 and buried at Khuldabad
132.x: Abdullah Pani was the traitor who opened the gates of Golconda. Abdur Razzaq Lari was the defender who was honoured as Mustafa Khan.
132.tq: Find the swapped role in a not-correctly-matched question.
xs: **Abdullah Pani — defender honoured** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abdullah Pani** was the **traitor** who opened Golconda's gates on **21 Sept 1687**.
The defender honoured as **Mustafa Khan** was **Abdur Razzaq Lari**; the other pairs are right.
xa: **Tana Shah** was imprisoned at **Bidar**, then **Daulatabad**; died **1699**; buried at **Khuldabad**.
The fort was taken on **3 Oct 1687** → **21st suba**.
Ministers **Madanna-Akkanna** were murdered in **1686**.

132.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mughal conquest of Golconda?
o: Madanna and Akkanna were murdered in 1686.
Its last ruler, Abul Hasan Tana Shah, was exiled to Gwalior.
132.x: Tana Shah was exiled to Daulatabad, not Gwalior (where Murad Bakhsh was imprisoned).
xa: The fort fell on **3 Oct 1687** after **Abdullah Pani** opened the gates (**21 Sept 1687**).
**Abdur Razzaq Lari** defended it; honoured as **Mustafa Khan**.
**Bhakta Ramadasu** was the nephew of **Akkanna-Madanna**.

132.s: The fall of Golconda to Aurangzeb in 1687 ended the rule of which dynasty over Andhra?
132.x: Golconda fell in 1687 and Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was imprisoned, ending Qutb Shahi rule over Andhra; Golconda became a Mughal suba.
xa: **Bhakta Ramadasu** was the nephew of **Akkanna-Madanna**.
**Abdullah Pani** opened the gates; **Abdur Razzaq Lari** defended it.
Tana Shah died in **1699**; buried at **Khuldabad**.

132.s: Who was the last Adil Shahi ruler of Bijapur, defeated by Aurangzeb in 1686?
132.x: Sikandar Adil Shah was presented in silver chains and sent to Daulatabad when Bijapur fell in 1686.

132.s: Which traitor opened the gates of Golconda fort to the Mughals in 1687?
132.x: Abdullah Pani opened the gates; Abdur Razzaq Lari was the loyal defender.

132.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of which Golconda ministers?
132.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Akkanna–Madanna, the ministers murdered in 1686.

132.s: Where was Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) finally kept after the fall of Golconda?
132.x: Tana Shah was imprisoned at Bidar, then Daulatabad; Gwalior was where Murad Bakhsh was held.

132.s: Which event is associated with Shivaji's visit to Agra in 1666?
o: He was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.
He began the campaign from Jinji.
He was insulted, placed under house arrest and escaped in fruit baskets.
He captured Sirhind from Wazir Khan.
132.x: During his 1666 visit to Agra, Shivaji was insulted and placed under house arrest, from which he escaped in fruit baskets.
132.tq: Identify the distinctive incident associated with a specific year and place.
xs: In **1666** at **Agra**, Shivaji was **insulted**, put under **house arrest**, and **escaped in fruit baskets** — so option **(3)** is correct.
His **Chhatrapati** coronation was at **Raigad** in **1674**.
**Sirhind** belongs to Banda Singh's story, not Shivaji's.
xa: **1700-07**: **Tarabai** (Rajaram's widow) raided Mughal territory in her son's name.
The Marathas split into the **Satara** line and Tarabai's **Kolhapur** line.
**Prince Akbar** fled to **Sambhaji**.

132.s: Why was the prolonged 27-year Deccan war described as the 'Deccan Ulcer'?
o: prevented the annexation of Bijapur and Golconda
drained the Mughal treasury through prolonged warfare
strengthened the Mughal treasury through continuous tribute
132.x: The 27-year Deccan war drained the Mughal treasury and was therefore called the 'Deccan Ulcer', in comparison with Napoleon's Spanish Ulcer.
132.tq: Infer the consequence of a prolonged policy from the descriptive historical term.
xs: The **27-year** Deccan war **drained the treasury** — the **"Deccan Ulcer"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was compared to **Napoleon's Spanish Ulcer**.
Bijapur and Golconda were in fact annexed (**1686-87**), and the Maratha war went on till his death.
xa: Phase IV (**1687-1707**): war against the **Marathas** till death.
Aurangzeb spent **25-27** years camped in the Deccan.
He died in **1707** at **Ahmednagar**.

132.s: Where was Sambhaji captured before his execution in 1689?
132.x: Sambhaji was captured at Sangameshwar and executed in March 1689.

132.s: Who led the Maratha war against Aurangzeb from 1700 as regent for her infant son Shivaji II?
132.x: Tarabai, Rajaram's widow, led the war from 1700 as regent for Shivaji II.

132.s: From which fort did Rajaram resist the Mughals after becoming Chhatrapati in 1689?
132.x: Rajaram resisted from Jinji and died at Sinhagad in 1700.

132.s: Where did the Maratha Chhatrapati Rajaram die in 1700?
132.x: Rajaram, who resisted from Jinji, died at Sinhagad in 1700.

132.s: The given map refers to the kingdom of :
o: Akbar at the time of capture of Khandesh in 1601
Akbar at the time of his death in 1605
Aurangzeb at the time of capture of Hyderabad
Aurangzeb at the time of his death in 1707
132.x: The given map shows the extent of the kingdom of Aurangzeb at the time of his death in 1707 A.D. it included Bijapur and Golconda.

132.s: Where was Aurangzeb, who died at Ahmednagar in 1707, buried?
132.x: He was buried in a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad, where Tana Shah was also buried.
xa: Tana Shah was imprisoned at **Bidar**, then **Daulatabad**, and died in **1699**.
Aurangzeb spent his last **25-27** years camped in the Deccan.
**Golconda** fell on **3 Oct 1687** and became the **21st suba**.

132.s: Where did Aurangzeb die in 1707?
132.x: Aurangzeb died at Ahmednagar in 1707 and was buried at Khuldabad.

132.s: Which last Golconda ruler is also buried at Khuldabad, the burial place of Aurangzeb?
132.x: Tana Shah (Abul Hasan Qutb Shah) died in 1699 and was buried at Khuldabad, where Aurangzeb also lies.

133.s:
Read the statements
(A) and
(B) below and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: (A) Not all the mansabdars were military officers. (B) Those who held high civil posts under the Mughals were also mansabdars and were graded accordingly.
133.x: The Mansabdari system was the administrative system of the Mughal Empire which was introduced by Akbar. The system was common to both the military and the civil department. Abul Fazl has mentioned 66 grades of Mansabdars but in practice only 33 categories were prevalent.

133.s: The Mansabdari System introduced by Akbar was borrowed from the system followed in –
133.x: The Mansabdari system introduced by Akbar was borrowed from Mongolia. This type of military division was implemented in the Mongolian (Central Asia) army under the leadership of Genghis Khan. However, the Mansabdari System was widely new. Nevertheless, originally, it was based on the Mongolian military division.

133.s: In medieval India, Mansabdari system was introduced mainly for :
133.x: Akbar introduced a well-organised system in the military and civil service of the empire which came to be known as Mansabdari system. Very soon, this system became the main basis of the military and civil administration of the Mughals. The main intention to introduce Mansabdari was to provide a clean and better administration.

133.s: Military system in the reign of Akbar was based on :
133.x: It was essential to have a well-organised army for expansion of empire and maintenance of peace and order, Akbar reformed many loopholes of a military system for this purpose. He revived the practice of Chehra (descriptive image of each soldier maintained) and Dagh (branding of horses) in 1573-74 A.D. After this action, he organised soldiers by Mansabdari system in 1574-75 A.D. Mansab means rank or position. Mansabdar means the official who had a rank or designation in the royal army. This was based on the decimal system.

133.s: Who was responsible for the smooth functioning of the Mughal Mansabdari system?
133.x: Mir Bakshi was responsible for the smooth functioning of the Mughal Mansabdari system. The Mansabdari system was the administrative system introduced by Akbar in Mughal Empire. The word 'Mansab' is of Arabic origin meaning rank or position. Hence Mansabdari was a system of ranking the government officials and determining their civil & military duties, along with their renumeration. The recruitment and promotion of the Mansabdars was in the hands of the Emperor who could also dismiss them at will. Mostly the recruitment of the Mansabdars was done on the recommendation of Mir Bakshi.

133.s:
Consider the following observations relating to the reign of the Mughal Emperor Akbar

I. Akbar strengthened his control on the nobility and the army by introducing the Mansabdari system.

II. Under the Mansabdari system, every officer was assigned a rank (Mansab).

III. The ranks were divided into Zat, Sawar and Chehra.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
133.x: Akbar introduced mansabdari to grade nobles and army, giving each officer a rank, so I and II are right. The ranks were zat and sawar; Chehra is a descriptive roll, not a rank, so III is wrong.

133.s:
Assertion (A) The Mansabdari system was existing during Mughal period.
Reason (R) Mansabdars were selected on the basis of qualification.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

133.s:
With reference to Mansabdari system, which of the statements is/are correct?

I. Mansabdari system was the official nobility of the state, started by Akbar.

II. A Mansabdari was hereditary.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
133.x: Mansabdari was introduced by Akbar as the graded official nobility, so I is true. Mansabs were not hereditary, as rank and jagir ended with the holder, so II is false.

133.s:
Which of the following statements about ‘Mughal Mansab’ system are correct?

I. ‘Zat’ rank was an indicator of a Mansabdar’s position in the imperial hierarchy and the salary of the Mansabdar.

II. ‘Sawar’ rank indicated the number of horsemen the Mansabdar was required to maintain.

III. In the seventeenth century, Mansabdars holding 1000 or above ‘Sawar’ rank were designated as nobles (Umara).
Codes
133.x: Zat is the personal rank fixing status and salary, and sawar is the number of cavalrymen to be maintained, so I and II are correct. The notes do not support III.

133.s: What did a mansab denote under Akbar's Mansabdari system?
133.x: A mansab was a rank serving military and civil administration, not a hereditary office.
xa: "Mansab" is **Arabic** for **rank/position**; model from **Central Asia** (Mongol decimal grading).
The **Mir Bakhshi** ran the system (JPSC **2023**).
**Not all mansabdars were military officers**; high civil post-holders were graded the same way.

133.s: What normally happened to ranks and jagirs under the Mansabdari system?
o: Ended with the death of the holder
Passed to the holder's eldest son
133.x: Mansabs were not hereditary; ranks and jagirs normally ended with the holder's death.
xa: One grading served **both army and civil service** (BPSC **2019** "more than one").
The **Mir Bakhshi** ran the system.
Mansabdari was introduced by **Akbar**.

133.s: What was payment to a mansabdar in cash known as?
133.x: Mansabdars were paid in cash (naqd) or by non-hereditary assignment of land revenue (jagir).
xa: A jagir was **not a property right**, only the right to collect revenue.
**Tankhwah** jagirs were **transferable**; **Watan** jagirs were hereditary and not transferred.
**Khalisa** = crown land whose revenue went to the treasury; not a jagir.

133.s: What kind of rank was the mansab, on which the Mughal central administration rested?
133.x: Every officer held a mansab, a combined military-cum-civil rank, which is why the Mughal state was essentially military.
xa: The mansab fused **nobility, army and bureaucracy** into one graded service.
**Mir Bakhshi** was head of **military and intelligence**.
⚠ Contrast: the British **ICS** was purely civil with fixed cash salaries.

133.s: What was the range of mansab ranks under the Mansabdari system?
133.x: Ranks ran from 10 to 10,000, the highest reserved for princes.

133.s: According to Abul Fazl, how many mansab grades existed in theory?
133.x: Abul Fazl gives 66 grades in theory, of which 33 existed in practice.

133.s: Who introduced the Mansabdari system in Mughal India?
133.x: Akbar introduced the mansabdari system, giving every army and civil officer a rank (mansab).

133.s: From where was the model of the Mughal mansabdari system borrowed?
o: Central Asia (Mongol decimal grading of the army)
133.x: The mansabdari model came from Central Asia, from the decimal army grading of Genghis Khan's Mongols.

133.s: Which one of the following is not true about the Mughal Mansabdari System ?
o: They got conditional or Mashut rank
Their ‘Sawar’ rank could exceed the ‘Zat’ rank
All civil and military officers were given mansabs
133.x: Mansab meant rank or status. Mansabdars or officeholders were divided into 33 classes and were paid in cash according to their respective grades. There were exceptions to this rule, particularly when the mansabdar was serving in a difficult terrain amidst the rebels. In such cases, the state often increased the sawar rank without altering the zat rank. Obviously, the system was not a static one. It changed to meet the circumstances. Thus, reform was the use of conditional rank (Mashrut), which meant an ‘increase of sawar rank for a temporary period. So, option (c) is the correct answer.

133.s: What did 'sawar' denote in the Mughal Mansabdari system?
133.x: Sawar indicated the number of cavalrymen to be maintained; zat was personal rank and status.
xa: Horse rule: every **10** sawars to bring **20** horses (**10-20-30** norm).
Class depends on the **sawar-zat** ratio (equal, half or more, less than half).
Jahangir's **du-aspa sih-aspa** raised sawar without raising zat.

133.s: Which of the following pairs regarding classes of mansabdars is correctly matched?
o: First class – Sawar less than half of zat
First class – Sawar half of zat
Third class – Sawar equal to zat
Second class – Sawar half of zat
133.x: Second-class mansabdars had sawar equal to half of zat. First class had sawar equal to zat and third class had sawar less than half of zat.
xa: ⚠ **Zat** = personal rank and pay; **Sawar** = cavalry to maintain.
Mansabs ranged from **10 to 10,000** under Akbar.
Payment: cash (**naqd**) or **jagir**.

133.s: With the reign of which Mughal emperor was the conditional increase in sawar rank known as mashrut associated?
133.x: Aurangzeb introduced mashrut, a temporary increase in the sawar rank connected with a specific assignment.
133.tq: Distinguish similar mansab innovations by linking each to its emperor.
xs: **Mashrut** (conditional) increase belongs to **Aurangzeb** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was a **temporary extra increase in sawar rank** tied to a specific assignment.
⚠ **Du-aspa sih-aspa** = **Jahangir**; **month-scale** = **Shah Jahan**.
xa: **Mashrut jagir** = jagir given on conditions of service.
Under Aurangzeb, mansabdars grew sharply while **paibaqi** shrank → **jagirdari crisis**.
Shah Jahan let mansabdars maintain only **1/5 to 1/3** of sawar strength.

133.s: Under Shah Jahan, what was a jagir yielding half its assessed revenue called?
133.x: A half-yield jagir was shashmaha and a quarter-yield jagir sihmaha.
xa: Pay was scaled down when the actual yield (**hasil**) fell below the estimate (**jama**).
⚠ **Du-aspa sih-aspa** = Jahangir; **mashrut** = Aurangzeb.
The **chakla** (group of parganas) also dates from Shah Jahan's time.

133.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the du-aspa sih-aspa arrangement?
o: It raised the zat rank of the mansabdar.
Part of the sawar rank was counted double.
133.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa counted part of the sawar rank twice for trusted mansabdars without raising their zat.

133.s: Under Shah Jahan's month-scale, how much did a 'sihmaha' jagir yield?
o: A quarter of its assessed revenue
133.x: Sihmaha meant a quarter-yield; shashmaha meant half-yield.

133.s:
Consider the following statements about zat and sawar:
1. Zat denoted personal rank, status and salary.
2. The sawar rank could exceed the zat rank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Zat was the personal rank; under the system the sawar could not exceed the zat.

133.s: Which Mughal emperor introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system?
133.x: Jahangir introduced du-aspa sih-aspa, under which part of a mansabdar's sawar rank was counted double without raising his zat.

133.s: Under the mansabdari system, how many horses had to be kept for every 10 sawars?
133.x: The horse rule required 20 horses for every 10 sawars (cavalrymen).

133.s:
Consider the following statements: Ahadis were those troopers who
I. offered their services singly.
II. did not attach themselves to any chief.
III. had the emperor as their immediate colonel.
IV. attached themselves to Mirzas. Of these statements:
o: I, III and IV are correct
I, II and III are correct
133.x: Only statements I, II and III are correct: Ahadis (special imperial troopers) were elite imperial cavalrymen recruited individually and placed directly under the Mughal emperor's command. Unlike mansabdari troops, they were not attached to any jagirdar or provincial chief and could not be transferred through intermediaries. Serving as the emperor's personal contingent, they functioned as his immediate household cavalry, responsible for his security and campaign requirements.

133.s: The troops raised by the Emperor but not paid directly by the state and placed under the charge of Mansabadars were known as
133.x: Dakhili troops were state-paid troops placed under mansabdars, so Dakhili is correct. Walashahi (the option spelled Balashahi) refers to the emperor's bodyguard.

133.s: What were gentlemen troopers recruited and paid directly by the Mughal emperor called?
133.x: Ahadis were recruited directly by the emperor; Tabinan were mansabdars' contingents, dakhili state-paid troops under mansabdars, Walashahi the bodyguard.
xa: Ahadis were paid by the state, under **their own bakhshi**.
The **bulk** of the army = **mansabdars' cavalry contingents**.
Head of the army: **Mir Bakhshi**.

133.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Mughal army is NOT correct?
o: The entire army consisted exclusively of ahadis recruited directly by the emperor.
The bulk of the army consisted of the cavalry contingents of mansabdars.
Artillery and infantry supplemented the cavalry arm.
Mansabdars’ contingents could be paid through cash or jagir assignments.
133.x: The Mughal army was not composed exclusively of ahadis. Its bulk consisted of mansabdars’ cavalry contingents, supplemented by infantry and artillery, with different categories of state and personal troops.
133.tq: Reject the absolute claim created by the word ‘exclusively’.
xs: **"The entire army consisted of ahadis"** is NOT correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The **bulk** was **mansabdars' cavalry contingents**, paid via **naqd** or **jagir**.
**Artillery and infantry** supplemented the cavalry.
xa: Other components: **Dakhili** (state-paid, under mansabdars), **Tabinan** (mansabdars' own), **Walashahi** (bodyguard).
Musters were held periodically under the **Mir Bakhshi**.
**Dagh** and **chehra** checked horses and troopers.

133.s: What were state-paid troops placed under mansabdars in the Mughal army called?
133.x: Dakhili were state-paid troops under mansabdars; tabinan were the mansabdars' own contingents.

133.s: What were the mansabdars' own contingents in the Mughal army known as?
133.x: Tabinan were the mansabdars' own contingents; ahadis were the emperor's own troopers.

133.s: What did 'dagh' refer to in Mughal military administration?
133.x: Dagh was horse branding; chehra was the descriptive roll and tashiha the muster check.

133.s: What did the Mughal term 'tashiha' mean?
133.x: Tashiha was the muster check, alongside dagh (branding) and chehra (descriptive roll).

133.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal muster terms:
1. Chehra was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
2. Akbar revived the dagh and chehra.
3. Walashahi was the emperor's bodyguard.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: All three are correct: chehra was the descriptive roll, Akbar revived dagh and chehra, and walashahi was the bodyguard.

133.s: During Aurangzeb’s reign, whose duty was to see that people lived their lives in accordance with the ‘shariat’?
133.x: The notes do not mention the Muhtasib. He was the officer who enforced conduct according to the shariat, unlike the Ahadis, mansabdars or the Walashahi bodyguard.

133.s: The head of the military department under the recognised central machinery of administration during Akbar’s reign was
133.x: The Mir Bakhshi headed the military department, handling the army, mansabdars and intelligence. The Diwan handles revenue and the Mir Saman the household.

133.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mughal central ministers?
o: Wazir or Diwan – finance and revenue
Mir Bakhshi – military pay, mansabs and intelligence
Mir Saman – religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
Sadr-us-Sudur – religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
133.x: The Mir Saman supervised the royal household and karkhanas; religion and charity were under the Sadr-us-Sudur.

133.s: What did the authority of the Wakil largely become under Akbar?
133.x: Although the Wakil had traditionally been the chief adviser or regent, the office became largely symbolic under Akbar.
133.tq: Test the change in the practical importance of a central office.
xs: Under Akbar the **Wakil's** authority became largely **symbolic** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Wakil (vakil-us-saltanat) was chief adviser/regent; **Bairam Khan** held it in the regency, after which Akbar reduced it.
xa: Real finance power passed to the **Wazir/Diwan**.
Military power lay with the **Mir Bakhshi**.
Sultanate ministries (**Wazir**, **Diwan-i-Arz**) fed the Mughal model.

133.s: Under which official did Mughal intelligence, run through waqia-navis, khufia-navis and harkaras, come?
133.x: Intelligence was under the Mir Bakhshi.
xa: The Mir Bakhshi also ran **recruitment, pay and musters**.
**Muhtasib** = public morals.
**Mustaufi** = auditor.

133.s: Which Mughal central official supervised the royal household and the karkhanas?
133.x: The Mir Saman supervised the royal household and karkhanas.

133.s: Who was the Mughal chief justice who administered the Sharia?
133.x: The Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief justice under the Sharia.

133.s: Who were the 'waqia-navis' in the Mughal espionage system?
133.x: Waqia-navis were news-writers; khufia-navis wrote secret reports and harkaras were runners/spies.

133.s: The term 'Chakla' has been used in Medieval Indian History sources. This was
o: Territorial unit between Subah and Paragnah, but not
133.x: Chakla was an administrative division between subah and Paragnah (but not Sarkar) in the Indian subcontinent during Mughal Period, especially during Shah Jahan's rule.

133.s: How many subahs were there by the end of Akbar's reign?
133.x: Akbar had 12 subahs in 1580 and 15 by the end of his reign; Aurangzeb had 21.
xa: The **Subahdar** handled law and order; the provincial **Diwan** handled revenue.
The subah also had a **Bakhshi**, **Sadr** and **Qazi**.
⚠ **Chakla** sits between pargana and sarkar.

133.s: In a Mughal province, which official managed revenue and acted as an independent check on the governor?
133.x: The provincial Diwan managed revenue and checked the Subahdar, who handled governance and law and order.
xa: Other subah officials: **Bakhshi**, **Sadr**, **Qazi**.
Pargana: **Shiqdar** (military/police).
Village: **Muqaddam**, **Patwari**.

133.s: Above which unit did the pargana stand immediately in the Mughal administrative hierarchy?
133.x: The order from lowest to highest was village, pargana, sarkar and subah, so the pargana stood just above the village.

133.s: Who kept land records and revenue papers in a Mughal sarkar?
133.x: The Bitikchi kept land records and revenue papers; the Khazanadar was the treasurer.

133.s: Who was the head of the patwaris at the pargana level?
133.x: The Qanungo headed the patwaris and kept records; the Karkun was a clerk.

133.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
133.x: The Kotwal handled town police and markets; the Shiqdar was the pargana executive and the Khazanadar the treasurer.

133.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tashiha — verification and muster of troops and horses
Chehra — descriptive roll of a trooper
Dagh — preparation of revenue papers by the assistant to the amalguzar
133.x: Dagh was the branding of horses to prevent substitution. Preparation of revenue papers and accounts was the duty of the Bitikchi.
133.tq: Find the one pair that belongs to a different administrative function.
xs: **Dagh — preparing revenue papers** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dagh** was the **branding of horses** to stop substitution.
The others are right: **Tashiha** = muster/verification; **Chehra** = descriptive roll of a trooper.
xa: Dagh was used earlier by **Alauddin** and **Sher Shah**.
Failure to present the required sawars at musters → **pay cuts**.
Musters were held under the **Mir Bakhshi**.

133.s: Which of the following is the correct ascending order of Mughal administrative units?
133.x: From smallest to largest the units were village, pargana, sarkar and subah (province).

133.s: Who was in charge of military command and law and order in a Mughal sarkar?
133.x: The faujdar headed the sarkar's military and kept law and order; the kotwal policed towns.

133.s: Who was the executive and police officer at the pargana level in Mughal administration?
133.x: The Shiqdar headed the executive and police work of a pargana; the Faujdar worked at the sarkar level.

133.s: Who was the village accountant in Mughal administration?
133.x: The Patwari was the village accountant; the Qanungo was head of the patwaris at pargana level.

133.s: Which one of the following pairs of term and meaning is not correctly matched?
o: Khalisa – Villages whose income went directly to the state treasury.
Inam – Land allotted to learned and religious man
Jagir – Territorial assignment given to Mansabdars in lieu of salary.
133.x: Mauza means a village, not rebellious territory, so this pair is wrong. Khalisa (crown land) and jagir (assignment in lieu of salary) are correctly matched.

133.s: What were madad-i-maash grants generally?
o: Transferable assignments made to cavalrymen in lieu of salary

134.s: With reference to medieval India, which one of the following is the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size?
134.x: The hierarchical order based on size is Paragana – Sarkar – Suba. The Mughal Empire was divided into several Subas (provinces), each administered by a Subedar (or Nizam) and a Diwan. During Akbar's reign, there were 15 Subas, which later increased to 22 under Aurangzeb. Each Suba was further divided into Sarkars, each under the charge of a Fauzdar (administrative head) and an Amal (revenue collector). The Sarkars were subdivided into Paraganas, administered by a Shiqdar (executive officer) and assisted by Amils in revenue collection. At the paragana level, there were also three semi-hereditary officials: the Qanungo (keeper of revenue records), the Chaudhuri (responsible for revenue collection), and the Qazi. A number of villages (gramas) together formed a pargana, and each village was managed by a Muqaddam (headman) and a Patwari (accountant)

135.s: Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were
135.x: During the medieval period, the Indian trading classes were large in number, widely spread throughout the country, and well organised. Seth, bohra traders specialised in long-distance trade, while local traders were called banik. Another class of traders, known as banjaras, specialised in carrying bulk goods and used to travel long distances with their goods on the backs of oxen (their caravans were called Tanda). Interestingly, the trading community did not belong to one caste or religion. For instance, the Gujarati merchants included Hindus, Jains, and Muslims, Oswals, Maheshwaris, and Agarwals came to be called the Marwaris, while in South India, the Chettis on the Coromandel coast and the Muslim merchants of Malabar formed important trading communities.

(a) Wellesley (b) Warren Hastings (c) Lord Cornwallis (d) Lord Dufferin U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1991 Ans. (c) The Permanent Settlement (1793 AD) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis. This system was launched in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Varanasi (U.P.) etc. It is also known as Istimarari Maalguzari, Bishwedari etc. The Permanent Settlement stood on the following features - It recognized the landlords as the proprietors of the land. It also recognized the rights of a hereditary successor or lawful successors of the landlords. The government believed that these landlords would remain faithful to the British. The landlords were given the right to transfer or sell their land. All the rights of the landlords depended on their payment of the fixed revenue on the fixed date at the treasury of the government. All their rights ended if they failed to pay. This was one reason for increased litigation. An increase in intermediaries between farmers and landlords was another reason for increased litigation. The total amount of revenue to be paid by each landlord for his Zamindari was fixed once and for all. It was agreed that the tax rate would not increase in the future.

Consider the following statements:

138.x: European painting was introduced at the Mughal court through Portuguese Jesuit missionaries, not Danish merchants; statements a and b are correct.

138.s: The Mughal School of Painting formed the spinal column of the various schools of Indian miniature art. Which one of the following painting styles was not affected by Mughal painting?
138.x: The Mughal School of Painting significantly influenced several regional schools of Indian miniature painting, including the Pahari, Rajasthani, and Kangra styles, which adopted elements such as refined brushwork, naturalism, and courtly themes. However, the Kalighat style, which developed in 19 th century Bengal around the Kalighat temple in Kolkata, evolved independently as a popular folk art tradition and was not shaped by Mughal painting traditions.

138.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under:
138.x: Mughal painting reached its zenith under Jahangir, whose personal patronage encouraged refined portraiture, naturalistic animal studies, and fine detailing. Under Shah Jahan, greater emphasis was placed on architecture. Hence, the peak of Mughal painting falls during Jahangir's reign.

138.s: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait?
138.x: Jahangir (c. 1605–1627 CE) presided over the zenith of Mughal painting. He patronised several distinguished artists, including Abul Hasan, Bishan Das (renowned as a master of portraiture), Madhu, Anant, Manohar, Govardhan, and Ustad Mansur, who specialised in animal painting. During his reign, the use of the halo or divine light behind the emperor's head became a prominent artistic feature. The artistic focus also shifted from illustrated manuscripts to muraqqas—albums of miniature paintings and calligraphic works. Stylistically, Jahangir favoured naturalism, incorporating elements of Persian painting while placing strong emphasis on portraiture.

138.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under :
138.x: The Mughal painting reached its zenith under the reign of Jahangir. Earlier, the paintings were concerned with the contents of manuscripts, but Jahangir freed it from this bondage. Farrukh Beg, Daulat, Mansur, Abul Hasan, etc. were such painters who had inscribed their names in a golden word in the history of Mughal painting with their talent. Ustad Mansur and Abul Hasan was an excellent painter of Jahangir’s reign. Emperor Jahangir bestowed both Nadirul-Asra (Ustad Mansur) and Nadir-ul-Zaman (Abul Hasan). Ustad Mansur was specialized in depicting plants and animals while Abul Hasan was a portrait artist.

138.s: The Mughal School of Painting formed the spinal cord of the various Schools of Indian miniature art. Which one of the following painting styles was not affected by Mughal painting?
138.x: The Mughal schools of painting from the Mughal court spread to various regional centres and gave rise to Pahari, Rajasthani school of painting but Kalighata school of painting was Indigenous and not affected by Mughal painting.

138.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under :
138.x: Mughal painting reached its zenith (golden period) under Jahangir, with naturalism, portraits and albums. Akbar's period built the atelier and Shah Jahan's was formal and gold-heavy, so they are not the peak.

138.s: Jahangir mainly patronized which of the following arts?
138.x: Jahangir (1605-27) had an artistic inclination. During his reign, Mughal painting developed further as Jahangir was fascinated with art, science and architecture from a young age. He showed a leaning towards painting and had an atelier of his own. His interest in portraiture led to much development in this art form. The art of Mughal painting reached great heights during Jahangir’s reign. His interest in painting also served his scientific interest in nature. Painter Ustad Mansur became one of the best artists to document the animals and plants which Jahangir either encountered on his military expeditions or received as donations. Jahangir maintained a huge aviary and kept a record of every specimen and organized experiments. He patronized the European and Persian arts.

Painter Ustad Mansur became one of the best artists to document the animals and plants which Jahangir either encountered on his military expeditions or received as donations. Jahangir maintained a huge aviary and kept a record of every specimen and organized experiments. He patronized the European and Persian arts.

138.x: Tansen was given the title by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior. He was a court musician in the darbar of Raja Ramachandra of Bandavagarh (Rewa). When Akbar heard of his prodigious talent, he sent a 'firman' to the king asking for Tansen and made him one of the Navaratnas in his court. Akbar gave him the title of 'Mian'. Tansen composed numerous dhrupads dedicated to deities such as Ganesha, Shiva, Parvati, and Rama, as well as compositions for his royal patrons. A major collection of his works, Kalpadruma, includes around 300 of his dhrupads composed in the Gauhar Bani style. Tansen is also known for composing in his favourite ragas, including Multani, Bhairavi, and Todi. He is credited with creating several new ragas, such as the night raga Darbari Kanhra, morning raga Mian Ki Todi, midday raga Mian Ki Sarang, and the seasonal raga Mian Ki Malhar. His descendants and disciples are called Seniyas.

The Asaf Jahi Dynasty was founded by Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan, popularly known as Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, in 1724 CE. Initially appointed as the Mughal Governor of the Deccan by Emperor Farrukhsiyar, he defeated Mubariz Khan in the Battle of Shakar Kheda (1724) and established an independent state with Hyderabad as its centre. The Asaf Jahi rulers governed Hyderabad until 1948, when Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union after Operation Polo. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

• Established → 1724

142.s: Prem Vatika, poems on the life of Krishna, was composed by:
142.x: Raskhan was a 16 th-century Sufi poet devoted to Krishna. His poetry reflects India's composite culture, blending Islamic roots with Vaishnava bhakti. Surdas wrote Sur Sagar in Braj Bhasha, and Kabir composed Bijak, emphasising Nirguna (formless) Brahman rather than Saguna.

142.s: Prem Vatika, poems on the life of Krishna, was composed by :

Choose the correct pair of the following:
Which of the following statements regarding the Bhakti Movement is not correct?
o: Nimbarka propounded the philosophy of Dvaitadvaita
143.x: The renowned saint of the Bhakti Movement tradition, Madhvacharya, was a proponent of Dvaita (Dualism) philosophy. His central doctrine is "Dvaitavada", which states that the individual soul (ātman), the material world, and the Supreme Being (Paramatma) are distinct and fundamentally different from each other. Madhvacharya followed the Saguna Bhakti tradition, not the Nirguna Bhakti stream. He considered Lord Vishnu as the supreme deity and strongly advocated his worship. Thus, statement (c) is incorrect, while other statements are correct.

143.s: Who among the following is not related to the Philosophy of Vedanta?
143.x: Abhinav Gupta is not related to the philosophy of Vedanta. The thesis of Vedanta philosophy has an enormous impact on Hindu thought and culture. Shankaracharya (8th century), Ramanuja (11th century) and Madhava (13th century) were the giant scholars of Vedantic School, who gave varying interpretations of Vedanta philosophy.

143.s: “Shuddha Advaitvad” was propounded by –
143.x: Shuddha Advaitavada is the “purely non-dual” philosophy propounded by Shri Vallabhacharya, the founder and guru of the Vallabha Sect. Vallabhacharya was the son of Telugu Brahmin Shri Lakshmana Bhatta of Somyaji clan, who is said to have developed the views of Vishnuswami into Shuddha Advaita or pure non-dualism.

143.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched? Bhakti Saint Philosophy
143.x: Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism). Kevaladvaita/Advaita belongs to Shankara, not Ramananda or Chaitanya, and Avadhuta is not Shankara's philosophy.

143.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
143.x: Dvaitadvaita was founded by Nimbarka. Vallabhacharya founded Shuddhadvaita or Pushtimarga.
143.tq: Distinguish closely named philosophical schools by their founders.
xs: Pair **(1)** is NOT correct: **Dvaitadvaita** belongs to **Nimbarka**, not Vallabhacharya.
**Vallabhacharya** taught **Shuddhadvaita** (pure non-dualism).
**Madhva — Dvaita**, **Ramanuja — Vishishtadvaita**, **Shankara — Advaita** are correct.
xa: ⚠ Advaita = Shankara; Vishishtadvaita = Ramanuja; Dvaita = Madhva; Dvaitadvaita = Nimbarka; Shuddhadvaita = Vallabha.
Shankara = Advaita was asked in **APPSC-G1 2012**.

143.s: Which one of the following statements about Madhvacharya is correct?
o: He centred his teaching on devotion to Radha-Krishna.
He taught that God and souls are eternally distinct.
He identified his philosophy with pure non-dualism.
He propounded Nirguna devotion as the central path.
143.x: Madhvacharya’s Dvaita philosophy maintains that God, identified with Vishnu, and individual souls are eternally distinct. His devotional emphasis is Saguna bhakti.
143.tq: Catch the reversed or swapped teaching associated with a confusable acharya.
xs: **Madhvacharya** taught that **God and souls are eternally distinct** — option **(2)**.
This is **Dvaita** (dualism), with **Saguna** devotion to **Vishnu**.
**Radha-Krishna** = Nimbarka; **pure non-dualism** = Vallabha; ⚠ "Madhva propounded **Nirguna** bhakti" is wrong (RPSC **2024**).
xa: His centre: **Udupi** Krishna Matha.
Disciple **Narahari Tirtha** spread Dvaita in Andhra-Kalinga from **Srikurmam**.

143.s: Which of the following correctly describes Vallabhacharya's teaching?
o: Dvaita, with exclusive emphasis on ritual sacrifice
Shuddhadvaita, with Pushtimarg and Vatsalya bhakti
Vishishtadvaita, with rejection of Krishna worship
Advaita, with salvation through knowledge alone
143.x: Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita or pure non-dualism. He advocated Pushtimarg, the path of grace, Vatsalya bhakti towards child Krishna and householder life for devotees.
143.tq: Combine school, path and devotional emphasis to identify the precise option.
xs: Vallabhacharya taught **Shuddhadvaita**, with **Pushtimarg** and **Vatsalya bhakti** — option **(2)**.
Pushtimarg = "**path of grace**"; vatsalya bhakti to **child Krishna**; **householder life** for devotees.
xa: He set up **84** Pushtimarg centres.
Pushtimarga = Vallabhacharya (APPSC-G1 **2018**).

143.s: Who was Ramananda's principal object of devotion?
143.x: Ramananda worshipped Rama; child Krishna was the focus of Vallabha.
xa: Ramananda **replaced Vishnu worship with devotion to Rama**.
**Chaitanya**'s deity: **Krishna**.

143.s: Which acharya's tradition worshipped child Krishna along with Radha-Krishna?
143.x: Vallabha worshipped child Krishna and Radha-Krishna; Ramananda worshipped Rama, Chaitanya Krishna and Nimbarka Radha-Krishna.
xa: Chaitanya founded **Gaudiya Vaishnavism**.
Nimbarka's centre: **Brindavan**.

143.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Acharya — Teaching emphasis
o: Vallabhacharya — Rejection of householder life for devotees
Ramanuja — Salvation through intense devotion to Vishnu
Madhvacharya — God and souls are identical
Nimbarka — Exclusive emphasis on Vedic ritual
143.x: Ramanuja taught that salvation is attained through intense devotion or prapatti to Vishnu. Madhva upheld the eternal distinction between God and souls, while Vallabha accepted householder life for devotees.
143.tq: Use the teaching-emphasis comparison and reject reversed philosophical positions.
xs: **Ramanuja — salvation through intense devotion (prapatti) to Vishnu** — option **(2)**.
**Vallabha** accepted **householder life** for devotees; **Madhva** held God and souls **eternally distinct**.
xa: For Ramanuja the best means of salvation is **devotion**, not Vedas, logic or meditation (UPSC **2022**).
**Nimbarka** emphasised devotion to **Radha-Krishna**.

143.s: Which one of the following sequences indicates the correct chronological order?
143.x: The correct chronological order is Adi Shankaracharya (8 th century CE) → Ramanuja (11 th–12 th century CE) → Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (15 th–16 th century CE).

143.s: Who among the following was the first Bhakti Saint to use Hindi for the propagation of his message?
143.x: Ramananda was born in 1299 A.D. at Prayag (Prayagraj) in an orthodox Kanyakubja Brahmin family. He got an education in Prayag and Varanasi. Swami Ramananda changed the spiritual landscape of northern India. He propagated the worship of Rama and Sita among the masses.

143.s: Which one of the following sequences indicates the correct chronological order?
143.x: The correct chronological order is – Shankaracharya (8th Century), Ramanuja (1017-1137 A.D.)- Chaitanya (1486- 1533 A.D.).

143.s: Which of the following acharyas came earliest?
143.x: The order is Ramanuja, Nimbarka (12th-13th century), Ramananda and then Vallabhacharya, so Ramanuja was the earliest.

143.s: Which exponent of monism (Advaita) is regarded as a forerunner of the Bhakti cult?

⚠ **Nimbarka** was **not** a contemporary of Akbar (UPSC **2019**).
**Shankara (788-820)** and **Ramanuja (1017-1137)** lived centuries apart; **Madhva** belongs to the **13th c.**

143.x: Shankara was the forerunner (knowledge); Ramanuja was the first true exponent of Bhakti (devotion).

143.x: Sriperumbudur was the birthplace of Ramanuja; Shankaracharya is linked to Kaladi and Madhva to Udupi.
xa: Nimbarka's school: **Dvaitadvaita**; deity **Radha-Krishna**.
Kaladi lies in **Malabar, Kerala**.

143.s: Which was Madhva's main centre?
143.x: Madhva's main centre was the Udupi Krishna Matha; Ramanuja's was Srirangam, Nimbarka's Brindavan and Ramananda's Varanasi.
xa: **Vallabha** preached Krishna bhakti in **Gujarat**, Varanasi and Braj.
Shankara's **Sringeri** head **Vidyaranya** was the Vijayanagara-era proponent.

143.x: Nimbarka's centre was Brindavan; Udupi was Madhva's.

143.x: Ramananda was born at Prayag and made Varanasi his centre.

143.s: Where was Shankaracharya born?
143.x: Shankaracharya was born at Kaladi in Kerala.

143.s: Where was Vallabhacharya born, by tradition?

143.s: Kabir was disciple of –
143.x: Kabir was prominent among 12 disciples of Ramananda. He was born to a widow Brahmin near Varanasi, and his upbringing was done by a weaver couple Neeru and Neema.

143.s: ‘Let no man ask a man’s sect or caste’ whose dictum was this?”

143.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Ramananda’s social teaching?
o: He restricted Rama worship to Kanyakubja Brahmins.
He upheld Brahmin supremacy as essential to devotion.
He accepted caste but rejected Vaishnavism.
He rejected caste distinctions and Brahmin supremacy.
143.x: Ramananda rejected caste and Brahmin supremacy. His dictum was “Let no man ask a man’s sect or caste,” and he is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright.
143.tq: Test the reformer’s central social message against extreme and reversed alternatives.
xs: **Ramananda rejected caste and Brahmin supremacy** — option **(4)**.
His saying: "**Let no man ask a man's sect or caste.**"
xa: He was the **first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright**.
Disciples included **Padmavati** (a woman) and **Pipa** (a Rajput ruler).

143.s: What was the background of Pipa, a disciple of Ramananda?
143.x: Pipa was a Rajput ruler of Gagron; Kabir was a weaver, Raidas a shoemaker and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.

143.x: Ramananda had 12 disciples, Kabir being one of them.

143.s: Who was the woman disciple of Ramananda?
143.x: Padmavati was Ramananda's woman disciple.

143.s: What was the philosophy of Vidyaranya Swamy?
143.x: Vidyaranya, who blessed Harihara and Bukka, followed Advaita.

143.s: Vallabhacharya visited the court of which ruler, where he refuted Shaiva propositions and defeated Vyasaraya?
143.x: Vallabhacharya visited the court of Krishnadevaraya, refuted Shaiva propositions and defeated the Dvaita scholar Vyasaraya, also known as Vyasa Tirtha.
143.tq: Match the religious debate with the correct ruler’s court.
xs: Vallabhacharya visited the court of **Krishnadevaraya** — option **(4)**.
There he **refuted Shaiva propositions** and **defeated** the Dvaita scholar **Vyasaraya** (Vyasa Tirtha).
xa: ⚠ Vallabha **defeated** Vyasaraya; Vyasa Tirtha = **royal guru** of Krishnadevaraya.

143.s: Vyasa Tirtha, royal guru to Saluva Narasimha and Krishnadevaraya, was a scholar of which school?
143.x: Vyasa Tirtha was a Dvaita scholar and author of Nyayamrita.

143.s: Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhva, spread which philosophical doctrine in Andhra-Kalinga from Srikurmam?
143.x: Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhva, spread Dvaita in Andhra-Kalinga, beginning from Srikurmam.
143.tq: Separate the disciple, doctrine and regional centre in a teacher–philosophy question.
xs: **Narahari Tirtha**, a disciple of **Madhva**, spread **Dvaita** from **Srikurmam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Madhva's school is **Dvaita**; **Advaita** is Shankaracharya's and **Vishishtadvaita** is Ramanuja's.
xa: All three are schools of **Vedanta** (Uttara Mimamsa), founded by **Badarayana**.
⚠ **Kumarila Bhatta** belongs to Purva Mimamsa, not Vedanta.
Vedanta holds **Brahman** the only reality.

143.s: The world's second tallest statue in the sitting pose of Ramanuja was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India at Hyderabad recently. Which one of the following statements correctly represents the teachings of Ramanuja
o: The best means of salvation was devotion.
Vedas are eternal, self-existent and wholly authoritative.
Logical arguments were essential means for the highest bliss.
Salvation was to be obtained through meditation.
143.x: Ramanuja spoke of universal salvation through devotion to God, compassion, humility, equality, and mutual respect, which is known as the Sri Vaishnavam Sampradaya. The philosophy propounded by Ramanuja was Vishishtadwaita or qualified monism. Vishishtadvaita signifies non-dualism of a qualified whole but is characterised by multiplicity. In other words, it believes in "all diversity subsuming to an underlying unity" (qualified monism). Ramanuja emphasised devotion to a personal God, identified with Vishnu, who is both immanent (present within the world) and transcendent (beyond it). He held that liberation (moksha) is attained through loving devotion (bhakti) combined with divine grace. Srirangam Ranganatha temple in Tamil Nadu is associated with his tradition. His greatest contribution is the propagation of the concept of "vasudhaiva kutumbakam", which translates as "all the universe is one family"

143.s: In Andhra, Sri Vaishnavism was patronised by the Palnati Haihayas and which other dynasty?
143.x: The Velanati Cholas and the Palnati Haihayas patronised Sri Vaishnavism in Andhra.
xa: It inspired **Brahmanayudu's Veera Vaishnava** movement in Palnadu.
It gave **Panchamas temple entry**.

143.s: Whom does the Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorate?
143.x: The Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorates Ramanuja and his message of spiritual and social equality.
143.tq: Use the monument–person association rather than confusing neighbouring Bhakti teachers.
xs: The **Statue of Equality** at Hyderabad honours **Ramanuja** — option **(4)**.
It is the world's **second-tallest sitting statue**, inaugurated by the PM (UPSC **2022**).
xa: Ramanuja gave **Panchamas temple entry**.
He taught any eager student **without the customary long wait**.

143.s: Ramanuja is credited with installing which deity at Tirupati?
143.x: Ramanuja is credited with ordering temple worship at Tirumala and installing Govindaraja at Tirupati.

143.s: Ramanuja is held to be an incarnation of whom?
143.x: Ramanuja, called Ilaya Azhwar, is held to be an incarnation of Adisesha/Lakshmana.

143.s: Which movement of Palnati Brahmanaidu in Andhra was inspired by Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita?
143.x: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita inspired Palnati Brahmanaidu's Veera Vaishnava movement, with its common dining (Chapakudu).

143.s: To which group did Ramanuja give temple entry?
143.x: Ramanuja gave the Panchamas temple entry.

143.s: By which name is Ramanuja also called?
143.x: Ramanuja is called Ilaya Azhwar and held to be an incarnation of Adisesha.

145.s: Who is the foremost composer of Carnatic music?
145.x:
Saint Thyagaraja (1767–1847) is regarded as one of the greatest composers of Carnatic music and is revered as a member of the Carnatic Trinity, along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. He composed thousands of devotional Kritis, most of them dedicated to Lord Rama. His compositions are known for their profound devotion, musical excellence and philosophical depth, making them central to the Carnatic music tradition. Although Annamacharya composed over 32,000 Sankirtanas in praise of Lord Venkateswara and is regarded as the Padakavita Pitamaha, the title of the foremost composer of Carnatic music is associated with Saint Thyagaraja. His annual Thyagaraja Aradhana at Tiruvaiyaru continues to attract musicians from across the world. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Foremost Composer of Carnatic Music – Saint Thyagaraja
• Carnatic Trinity – Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri
• Devotional Deity – Lord Rama

146.x: The ten maqamat begin with Tauba (repentance) and end with Riza (submission), passing through Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja and Tawakkul. Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr and Shukr are intermediate stages, and 'Riza and Tauba' reverses the order.
xs: The maqamat begin with **Tauba** (repentance) and end with **Riza** (submission) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr** are intermediate stages; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: The **10 stages**: Tauba → **Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja, Tawakkul** → Riza.
